content.value:
Vākyapadīya transcribed by Somadeva Vasudeva (start - 3.7) and Yves Ramseier
	(3.8 - end), based on the Rau 1977 edition.

The electronic text below is in a lossless transliteration using the Latin alphabet.
      The transliteration scheme used is the IAST (
The International Alphabet of Sanskrit Transliteration

). IAST differs in
      small ways from ISO 15919, but is preferred by most working Sanskrit scholars.
      Conversion of this file to ISO 15919 can be achieved by performing the following
      replacements throughout the file:

Text division separates words with spaces ("ity evam" not "ityevam"), where sandhi
      permits.

children.translated_text: <s>Brahmakāṇḍa</s> (<s>Brahmakāṇḍa</s>)
The beginningless and endless <s>Brahman</s> (<s>Brahman</s>), the imperishable essence of speech (<s>śabda-tattva</s>),
manifests as the condition of meaning, from which proceeds the process of the world
That which is taught as one alone, owing to reliance on distinct powers,
though not separate from the powers, appears as if separate
In whom the six modifications—birth and the rest—have taken refuge in the power of time, with its implanted divisions,
the sources of the differentiations of existence
Of the one universal seed, of whom indeed this manifold existence
abides in the forms of the enjoyer and the object-to-be-enjoyed, and also in the form of enjoyment
The <s>Veda</s> (<s>Veda</s>), the means of attaining and the imitation (anukāra) of that (Brahman), has been transmitted by the great seers,
though one, it is taught along many paths, as though separate, separately
Because multiplicity has many paths, and ritual action has parts and sub-parts in one place,
the measured capacity of words is seen in its branches (<s>śākhā</s>)
The variously formed smṛtis, having purposes seen and unseen,
have been devised by knowers of the <s>Veda</s> relying on those very (Vedic) marks (liṅgas)
Depending on that, and born of their own constructions, the expository discourses (arthavādas),
the doctrines of the monists and dualists likewise have come forth in many forms
Therein truth is declared to be purity, and knowledge alone as the single-path scripture,
appropriately identified with the form of <s>Praṇava</s> (the syllable Oṃ), which is non-contradictory to all doctrines
Of that ordainer of the worlds, the varieties of learning, bound to limbs and sub-limbs,
are displayed as causes of the cultivation of knowledge

children.text: āsannaṃ brahmaṇas tasya tapasām uttamaṃ tapaḥ
children.translated_text: Nearest to His <s>Brahman</s>, the highest asceticism among austerities,

children.text: prathamaṃ chandasām aṅgam āhur vyākaraṇaṃ budhāḥ
children.translated_text: the wise declare grammar to be the first limb of the <s>Chandas</s> (Veda as metrical scripture)
For the division of attained forms, that supreme essence of speech,

children.text: yat tat puṇyatamaṃ jyotis tasya mārgo+ayam āñjasaḥ
children.translated_text: which is that most holy light—this is its straightforward path
Words alone are the foundation of the true principles of practical engagement,
and an apprehension of the realities of words does not exist without grammar
Therefore this is the door to liberation, the therapy for the impurities of speech,
the purifier of all knowledges, the over-knowledge (adhividyā) is made manifest
Just as all the kinds of real entities are grounded in word-forms,

children.text: tathaiva loke vidyānām eṣā vidyā parāyaṇam
children.translated_text: so too in the world, among the sciences, this science is the final resort
This is the first station of words among the stages of the ladder to success,
this is that straight royal pathway for those seeking liberation
Here, having reversed prior error, one beholds solely

children.text: chandasyaś chandasāṃ yonim ātmā chandomayīṃ tanum
children.translated_text: the metres, the womb of the metres, and the self, a body made of metre
The highest form of speech, in which distinctions have subsided,

children.text: yad asminn eva tamasi jyotiḥ śuddhaṃ vivartate
children.translated_text: the pure light that manifests even in this very darkness
Having transcended the derivative, the perception of gross activity,
having passed beyond light and darkness, the radiance which they worship
Where the causes of speech, like signs for the memory of syllables,
shine, through a union with the prior Word (<s>śabda</s>), like reflections
In which, of the <s>Atharvans</s> and <s>Aṅgirases</s> and of the <s>Sāman</s>, the <s>Ṛc</s> and the <s>Yajus</s>,
the high and low sounds, separately situated, are comprehended
That which, though one, is divided in many ways by differences of procedure,
by approaching that grammar, the supreme <s>Brahman</s> is realized
The eternal relations of word and meaning are taught there by the great seers,
the authors of the sūtras, with their ancillary systems, and of the bhāṣyas
Those entities that are to be separated out, and those that have established characteristics,

children.text: anvākhyeyāś ca ye śabdā ye cāpi pratipādakāḥ
children.translated_text: and those words that are to be expounded, and also those that are denotative
Standing in the relations of effect and cause, and of fitness (yogya-bhāva),

children.text: dharme ye pratyaye cāṅgaṃ saṃbandhāḥ sādhvasādhuṣu
children.translated_text: the connections that are parts in dharma and in affixes, in correct and incorrect forms

children.text: te liṅgaiś ca svaśabdaiś ca śāstre+asminn upavarṇitāḥ
children.translated_text: They are described in this treatise by signs and by their own words,

children.text: smṛtyartham anugamyante ke cid eva yathāgamam
children.translated_text: only some are followed according to tradition, for the sake of memory
Approved (sādhu) forms, established from the tradition of the learned, are instruments of dharma,
but the disapproved (asādhu), when there is no difference in conveying the meaning, are the opposite

children.text: nityatve kṛtakatve vā teṣām ādir na vidyate
children.translated_text: Whether eternal or made, no beginning is known for them,
as with living beings; and this stability is said to be the eternality of convention

children.text: nānarthikām imāṃ kaś cid vyavasthāṃ kartum arhati
children.translated_text: No one is entitled to establish this convention as purposeless,
therefore the memory regarding correctness is bound down by the learned

children.text: na cāgamād ṛte dharmas tarkeṇa vyavatiṣṭhate
children.translated_text: And dharma does not stand established by reasoning apart from tradition

children.text: ṛṣīṇām api yaj jñānaṃ tad apy āgamapūrvakam
children.translated_text: Even the knowledge which belongs to the seers (<s>ṛṣis</s>), that too is preceded by tradition (<s>āgama</s>)
And the paths of <s>Dharma</s>, which stand established as not delimited,

children.text: na tāṃl lokaprasiddhatvāt kaś cit tarkeṇa bādhate
children.translated_text: no one invalidates them by reasoning, because they are established in the world
Because of the difference of states, place, and times, among powers that are distinct,
the ascertainment of entities by inference is exceedingly difficult

children.text: nirjñātaśakter dravyasya tāṃ tām arthakriyāṃ prati
children.translated_text: For a substance whose power has been ascertained, with regard to this or that causal efficacy,
that power is impeded when there is a relation with a particular (other) substance
A meaning that has been inferred even with effort by skilled inferers,
is established differently by others who are yet more adept
For others, the unsayable (recognition) arises only from practice,
the cognition of the nature of a gem and of counterfeit silver, for those skilled in it, is not inferential
The accomplishments of the <s>pitṛs</s>, <s>rakṣas</s>, and <s>piśācas</s>, born of karma, stand established
transcending perception and inference
For those whose manifestation of light has arisen, whose minds are untroubled,
knowledge of past and future is not distinct from perception
They behold with the seer’s eye (<s>ārṣa-cakṣus</s>) entities that are beyond the senses and not apprehensible,

children.text: ye bhāvān vacanaṃ teṣāṃ nānumānena bādhyate
children.translated_text: the statement of those men is not invalidated by inference

children.text: yo yasya svam iva jñānaṃ darśanaṃ nātiśaṅkate
children.translated_text: Whoever, with regard to someone, does not greatly suspect his direct seeing as his own knowledge,

children.text: thitaṃ pratyakṣapakṣe taṃ katham anyo nivartayet
children.translated_text: him, being established on the side of perception, how could another turn back

children.text: idaṃ puṇyam idaṃ pāpam ity etasmin padadvaye
children.translated_text: “This is meritorious, this is sinful” — in this very pair of words,
for human beings down to the <s>Caṇḍāla</s>, the utility of scripture is small

children.text: caitanyam iva yaś cāyam avicchedena vartate
children.translated_text: And this tradition (<s>āgama</s>), which proceeds without interruption as if consciousness itself,

children.text: āgamas tam upāsīno hetuvādair na bādhyate
children.translated_text: sitting near it, is not refuted by doctrines of reasons
Like a blind man running on a rough path by the touch of the hand,
for one who relies chiefly on inference, a downfall is not hard to come by

children.text: tasmād akṛtakaṃ śāstraṃ smṛtiṃ ca sanibandhanām
children.translated_text: Therefore, the unmade treatise (<s>śāstra</s>) and the tradition (<s>smṛti</s>) endowed with foundations,
having been resorted to, are undertaken by the learned; the recollection concerning correctness is its subject
In words that are instrumentally causal, the knowers of words know two words:
one is the occasioning cause of words, the other is employed with regard to the meaning
The word, undivided, arises as the revealer of the meaning out of the divided (sounds),
there the word, whose nature is the form of the meaning, attains a coalescence

children.text: ātmabhedaṃ tayoḥ ke cid astīty āhuḥ purāṇagāḥ
children.translated_text: Some, the reciters of ancient lore, say that there is a difference of self between those two,
others declare a difference, even though (word and meaning) are not different, due to a difference of cognition
Just as the fire latent in the arani-sticks is the cause of another illumination,

children.text: tadvac chabdo+api buddhisthaḥ śrutīnāṃ kāraṇaṃ pṛthak
children.translated_text: so too the word, abiding in the intellect, is separately the cause of hearings

children.text: vitarkitaḥ purā buddhyā kva cid arthe niveśitaḥ
children.translated_text: Formerly pondered by the intellect and in some respect set into an object,
it is supported by sound that has issued forth from the instruments (of speech)

children.text: nādasya kramajātatvān na pūrvo na paraś ca saḥ
children.translated_text: Because sound arises in sequence, it is neither prior nor posterior,
the non-sequential appears to be manifold through a sequential form
Just as a reflection elsewhere, through the operation of water,
seems to follow its activity, so does that property in regard to <s>sphoṭa</s> and the like

children.text: ātmarūpaṃ yathā jñāne jñeyarūpaṃ ca dṛśyate
children.translated_text: Just as in cognition the form of the self is seen, and the form of the knowable,

children.text: artharūpaṃ tathā śabde svarūpaṃ ca prakāśate
children.translated_text: so in the word both the form of the object and its own nature are made manifest
The resolve called “word” (<s>śabda</s>), which has, as it were, assumed the condition of an egg (a germinal whole),

children.text: vṛttis tasya kriyārūpā bhāgaśo bhajate kramam
children.translated_text: its function, of the nature of activity, shares out the sequence in parts
Just as a form, the object of a single cognition, is fashioned upon the cloth,
so too in the word a triad of other forms is seen

children.text: yathā prayoktuḥ prāg buddhiḥ śabdeṣv eva pravartate
children.translated_text: Just as beforehand the speaker’s intention operates precisely in words,

children.text: vyavasāyo grahītṝṇām evaṃ teṣv eva jāyate
children.translated_text: so the determination of the receivers is produced precisely in them
In certain objects to be denoted, which have become subordinate to the object (meaning),
the people do not apprehend (the words) as accomplishing their purpose, because they are for the sake of another

children.text: grāhyatvaṃ grāhakatvaṃ ca dve śaktī tejaso yathā
children.translated_text: Graspability and the capacity-to-grasp—two powers, as with light—
so too for all words these two are present separately
An object is not made manifest by words that have not obtained the condition of being related to a subject-matter,
nor by their mere existence are they manifesters of objects that have not been apprehended
Therefore, because their forms are not known, one says “What does it say,”
and likewise, in an object manifest to the senses, its own form is not grasped (by the senses themselves)
Two properties of the word, grasped as distinct and extracted as separate,
go without contradiction to be the cause in works that involve differentiation
Just as words like “growth” (<s>vṛddhi</s>) and the rest are bound up with their own natures,
so they enter into relation with technical designations through words signified by the affix <s>ādeś</s> etc.
Likewise this word “agni” is bound to the word “agni,”
by the hearing of “agni” it attains relation with that which is denoted by the word “agni”

children.text: yo ya uccāryate śabdo niyataṃ na sa kāryabhāk
children.translated_text: Any word that is uttered does not, as a rule, partake of being an effect
In causing another to apprehend, its power is not obstructed

children.text: uccaran paratantratvād guṇaḥ kāryair na yujyate
children.translated_text: Because, while being uttered, it is dependent, the quality is not conjoined with the effects
Therefore, a relation of the effects with those meanings is posited
Whatever commonness (<s>sāmānya</s>) is resorted to between the standard and the thing to be compared,
of that, in the similes, a different property is distinguished
A quality (<s>guṇa</s>) that is taught as a cause of excellence, independently,
its preeminence is understood from the very quality in which it is grounded
The word which is established in the capacity of denoter of that,

children.text: tasyāpy uccāraṇe rūpam anyat tasmād vivicyate
children.translated_text: even of it, upon utterance, another form is discerned from that
Prior to connection with the name-bearer (<s>saṃjñin</s>), a name (<s>saṃjñā</s>) has the character of a form-word (<s>rūpa-padārthikā</s>),

children.text: ṣaṣṭhyāś ca prathamāyāś ca nimittatvāya kalpate
children.translated_text: and it is posited as the occasion for the genitive and the nominative
Because of triply having meaningfulness, the nominative is prescribed with respect to a name-word,

children.text: asyeti vyatirekaś ca tadarthād eva jāyate
children.translated_text: and the exclusion ‘of this’ arises from that very meaning

children.text: svaṃ rūpam iti kaiś cit tu vyaktiḥ saṃjñopadiśyate
children.translated_text: But some say: ‘its own form’—an individual is denoted by the name,

children.text: jāteḥ kāryāṇi saṃsṛṣṭā jātis tu pratipadyate
children.translated_text: effects are connected with the class (<s>jāti</s>), but the class is apprehended

children.text: saṃjñinīṃ vyaktim icchanti sūtre grāhyām athāpare
children.translated_text: Some desire, in the sūtra, the individual name-bearer that is to be grasped, while others,
the individual, made known by the class, stands in places

children.text: kāryatve nityatāyāṃ vā ke cid ekatvavādinaḥ
children.translated_text: Some, whether on the view of being an effect or of eternality, are proponents of oneness,

children.text: kāryatve nityatāyāṃ vā ke cin nānātvavādinaḥ
children.translated_text: some, whether on the view of being an effect or of eternality, are proponents of manyness
Even though there is a difference of words, the oneness of phonemes (<s>varṇa</s>) is not annulled,

children.text: vākyeṣu padam ekaṃ ca bhinneṣv apy upalabhyate
children.translated_text: and in sentences a single word is observed even among differing (contexts)

children.text: na varṇavyatirekeṇa padam anyac ca vidyate
children.translated_text: There is no word other than phonemes, nor is there any other besides them,

children.text: vākyaṃ varṇapadābhyāṃ ca vyatiriktaṃ na kiṃ ca na
children.translated_text: and a sentence is in no way distinct from phonemes and words

children.text: pade na varṇā vidyante varṇeṣv avayavā na ca
children.translated_text: In a word, phonemes are not found; nor are there parts in phonemes,

children.text: vākyāt padānām atyantaṃ pravibhāgo na kaś ca na
children.translated_text: nor is there any absolute division of words from a sentence
Relying on divergent views, common practice is accommodated,

children.text: tatra yan mukhyam ekeṣāṃ tatrānyeṣāṃ viparyayaḥ
children.translated_text: what is primary for some is, in that very place, the reverse for others
They declare, for the <s>sphoṭa</s>, which is of indivisible time and follows not the times of sound,
a diversity of functions due to differences of the conditions of apprehension
Because of differences of natural constitution in short, long, and protracted,
the time of the natural sound is, by extension, said to be the time of the word

children.text: śabdasya grahaṇe hetuḥ prākṛto dhvanir iṣyate
children.translated_text: The natural sound is accepted as the cause in the apprehension of the word,
the altered (sound) is understood to have the condition of being the occasion of differences of state
After the manifestation of the word, the altered sounds take on a diversity of functions,

children.text: dhvanayaḥ samupohante sphoṭātmā tair na bhidyate
children.translated_text: but the <s>sphoṭa</s>-self is not divided by them
Whether it is only the sense-organ whose disposition is produced, or only the word, or both—
these are the three theses of those who teach manifestation, concerning sounds
The disposition of the sense-organ alone is produced by concentration, collyrium, and the like,
but the disposition of the object is for the cognition of its odor

children.text: cakṣuṣaḥ prāpyakāritve tejasā tu dvayor api
children.translated_text: When the eye operates by contact, but by the light both have it,

children.text: viṣayendriyayor iṣṭaḥ saṃskāraḥ sa kramo dhvaneḥ
children.translated_text: the disposition of object and sense-organ is accepted; such is the sequence of sound
The apprehension of sound is accepted as without division of the form of <s>sphoṭa</s>,

children.text: kaiś cid dhvanir asaṃvedyaḥ svatantro+anyaiḥ prakalpitaḥ
children.translated_text: by some, sound is conceived as unapprehended and independent by itself by others
Just as a recitation-section (<s>anuvāka</s>) or a verse (<s>śloka</s>) attains endurance,

children.text: āvṛttyā na tu sa granthaḥ pratyāvṛtti nirūpyate
children.translated_text: by repetition; but that does not make the book—repetition is what is determined
By means of impressions (<s>pratyaya</s>) that are ineffable, and likewise suited to apprehension,
when the word is illuminated by sound, its own nature is ascertained
When the reverberations (<s>nāda</s>) have implanted the seed, together with the final sound,
when repetition has matured, the word is ascertained in the intellect

children.text: asataś cāntarāle yāñ śabdān astīti manyate
children.translated_text: That weakness of the apprehender whereby, in the interval of non-existence, he thinks ‘there are words,’

children.text: pratipattur aśaktiḥ sā grahaṇopāya eva saḥ
children.translated_text: that is itself the means of apprehension
Either an imitation of the distinctions by cognition, or a constant perturbation of speech,
or speech whose form is pervaded by sequence; cognition is grounded upon the knowable
[Without the knowable, cognition does not stand in usage,
and with speech that has not obtained sequence, no object at all is denoted]
Just as the non-grasping of the first number is a means for apprehending
the other numbers in their difference, so too the hearing of another word
Those which are, each individually, revealers—distinct in phonemes, sentences, and words—
their powers, even in absolute difference, are as if intermingled

children.text: yathaiva darśanaiḥ pūrvair dūrāt saṃtamase+api vā
children.translated_text: Just as, on account of prior perceptions, or from afar, or even in darkness,
altering the object, one decides it otherwise,
so too, when a sentence is being manifested by the causes of sentence-manifestation,
the intellect first proceeds in the form of partial apprehension
Just as, with respect to alteration, there is a fixed sequence between milk and seed,
so indeed, for apprehenders, there is a determined order in the intellect

children.text: bhāgavatsv api teṣv eva rūpabhedo dhvaneḥ kramāt
children.translated_text: Even within those very parts, the difference of form of sound is due to sequence,
or else, in what is partless, the positing of division into parts is an expedient
The universal, which is made manifest by many particulars, is remembered as <s>sphoṭa</s> (burst/manifestive expression),

children.text: kaiś cid vyaktaya evāsyā dhvanitvena prakalpitāḥ
children.translated_text: by some, the particulars themselves of this are contrived as its sounds
While the word is unmodified, the sound, modified by causes,
assumes the role of an occasion in apprehension, like a revealer of light
Nor is manifestation, with regularity, established in impermanent things,

children.text: āśrayair api nityānāṃ jātīnāṃ vyaktir iṣyate
children.translated_text: even with transient substrates, the manifestation of eternal universals is accepted

children.text: deśādibhiś ca saṃbandho dṛṣṭaḥ kāyavatām api
children.translated_text: And relation with place and the like is observed even for bodies,
yet, even when there is a diversity of place, there is no difference between sound and word
Just as suitability is fixed between the apprehender and the apprehendable,
so too, even in the relation of manifested and manifesting, for <s>sphoṭa</s> and the like
And in the world, for perceptions of similars, a determinate cause that makes manifest
is something situated corresponding to each individual substance
And the object to be made manifest follows the aspects of difference of the revealers,
as is directly seen in reflectors, given the differences among oil, water, and the like
Where there are opposed dimensions—such as diamond, mirror-surface, and the like—
there cannot arise entities of the same form as mountains and the like
Therefore, in phonemes, sentences, words, and the like whose times are not distinct,
the time of functioning and their own time are not divided by the differences of reverberation (<s>nāda</s>)
That which is generated by conjunction and disjunction by the instruments,

children.text: sa sphoṭaḥ śabdajāḥ śabdā dhvanayo+anyair udāhṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: that is <s>sphoṭa</s>; the sounds produced from sound are presented by others as reverberations (<s>dhvani</s>)

children.text: alpe mahati vā śabde sphoṭakālo na bhidyate
children.translated_text: Whether the word is small or great, the time of the <s>sphoṭa</s> does not differ,
but the stream of sound has the nature of accumulation and diminution

children.text: dūrāt prabheva dīpasya dhvanimātraṃ tu lakṣyate
children.translated_text: From afar, as it were a mere radiance of a lamp, only reverberation (<s>dhvani</s>) is observed,

children.text: ghaṇṭādīnāṃ ca śabdeṣu vyakto bhedaḥ sa dṛśyate
children.translated_text: and in the sounds of bells and the like, that difference is seen as manifest
Due to the impact upon the substratum, even in accumulation, the long and protracted (quantities) are distinct,

children.text: kampe tūparate jātā nādā vṛtter viśeṣakāḥ
children.translated_text: but when the vibration ceases, the reverberations (<s>nāda</s>) that have arisen serve as distinctions of functioning
Even when the instrument’s vibration is not steady, other reverberations (<s>dhvani</s>)
arise from <s>sphoṭa</s> itself, like one flame from another flame
By some it is held that the cognition of air-atoms attains the status of sound,

children.text: kaiś cid darśanabhedo hi pravādeṣv anavasthitaḥ
children.translated_text: for the diversity of views in the doctrines is unsettled
[Having acquired action through effort, following the will of the speaker,
the air, struck at the articulatory places, attains soundness (the condition of being sound),
by the potency of its cause, having the property of increase of speed,
even solid forms are divided through aggregation and conjunction,
the atoms, because of omnipotence, have the function of combination and division,
transforming into the forms of shadow, heat, darkness, and sound,
when their own power is made manifest, being set in motion by effort,
the ultimate atoms called ‘sound’ accumulate like clouds,
or else this inner knower, established in the self of subtle speech,
for the manifestation of its own form, transforms into sound,

children.text: sa manobhāvam āpadya tejasā pākam āgataḥ
children.translated_text: that, having assumed the state of mind and come to ripeness through fire,
enters the air, the <s>Prāṇa</s>, and then is emitted,
the air, having attained the status of the substrate of the principle of the internal organ,
being pervaded by its property, transforms precisely by fire,
dividing the knots of itself by various forms that are auditory,
the <s>Prāṇa</s> manifests the phonemes and itself is dissolved in the phonemes,

children.text: ātmā buddhyā samarthyārthān mano yuṅkte vivakṣayā
children.translated_text: the self, by means of intellect, yokes the mind to meaning-objects for the sake of capability with intention to speak,

children.text: manaḥ kāyāgnim āhanti sa prerayati mārutam]
children.translated_text: the mind strikes the body-fire and that impels the wind]
The sound whose operation is unceasing, because of its subtlety is not apprehended,

children.text: vyajanād vāyur iva sa svanimittāt pratīyate
children.translated_text: like air by a fan, it is inferred from its own cause

children.text: tasya prāṇe ca yā śaktir yā ca buddhau vyavasthitā
children.translated_text: And the power of that, which resides in <s>Prāṇa</s> and which is established in the intellect,
when it transforms in the articulatory places, this attains differentiation
The power, resting in sounds alone, is the bond of this universe,
by whose eye this cognitive flash (<s>pratibhā</s>) of the form of difference is displayed
Since the differentiation of sounds and the like is explained and shaped by sound,
therefore all provisions concerning objects rest solely upon sound
Those versed in the <s>Āmnāya</s> (sacred transmission) know this as the transformation of sound,

children.text: chandobhya eva prathamam etad viśvaṃ pravartate
children.translated_text: from the <s>chandas</s> (Vedic meters) indeed this universe first proceeds
Having divided himself manifold, that <s>Chandasyah</s> (<s>Prajāpati</s>, Lord of meter) entered it in many ways,
by measures that are made of <s>chandas</s> (meter), manifold indeed he entered that

children.text: sādhvī vāg bhūyasī yeṣu puruṣeṣu vyavasthitā
children.translated_text: Wherever virtuous speech is more abundantly established in persons,

children.text: adhikaṃ vartate teṣu puṇyaṃ rūpaṃ prajāpateḥ
children.translated_text: in them abides in greater measure the meritorious form of <s>Prajāpati</s> (Lord of creatures)

children.text: prājāpatyaṃ mahat tejas tatpātrair iva saṃvṛtam
children.translated_text: The great <s>prājāpatya</s> (pertaining to <s>Prajāpati</s>) splendor, as if enveloped by its vessels,
when bodies are differentiated, hastens to its own source among the learned

children.text: yad etan maṇḍalaṃ bhāsvad dhāma citrasya rādhasaḥ
children.translated_text: This radiant circle, the abode of variegated potency,
having attained that condition, dissolves into knowledge
All prescriptions of what is to be done in the world rest upon sound,
which even a child, by a prior-laid impression, apprehends
The arrangement of the instruments, the upward movement of <s>Prāṇa</s> (vital breath),

children.text: sthānānām abhighātaś ca na vinā śabdabhāvanām
children.translated_text: and the striking of the articulatory places—[none occur] without the cultivation of sound

children.text: na so+asti pratyayo loke yaḥ śabdānugamād ṛte
children.translated_text: There is no cognition in the world that is without accompaniment by sound,

children.text: anuviddham iva jñānaṃ sarvaṃ śabdena bhāsate
children.translated_text: all knowledge appears, as it were, pierced through by sound
If the eternal speech-formedness of awareness were to depart,

children.text: na prakāśaḥ prakāśeta sā hi pratyavamarśinī
children.translated_text: manifestation would not manifest; for it is indeed reflexive-apprehension
She is the binder of all sciences, arts, and skills,
by whose dominion whatever comes forth is analyzed into its entities

children.text: saiṣā saṃsāriṇāṃ saṃjñā bahir antaś ca vartate
children.translated_text: This designation of those who transmigrate operates both outside and inside,
and consciousness, not transgressing that mere-that (its own minimal unit), is present in all species
In practical operations speech coordinates all embodied beings,
and when that departs, this one is seen senseless, like a wooden post or a wall
Through the revolving surge of discerning distinctions, having gained the appropriation of forms,

children.text: āmnātā sarvavidyāsu vāg eva prakṛtiḥ parā
children.translated_text: in all the transmitted sciences speech alone is taught as the supreme <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature)
Remaining without overstepping unity, bound by the eye of speech and by speech itself,
separate partitions of speech—cows and the like—appear distinctly
They, who have six doors, six abodes, six awakenings, six imperishables,

children.text: te mṛtyum ativartante ye vai vācam upāsate
children.translated_text: surpass death—those indeed who worship <s>Vāc</s> (Speech)

children.text: pravibhāge yathā kartā tayā kārye pravartate
children.translated_text: As the agent, having made a division, proceeds by it in action,
so, without division, that same [speech] stands as the very condition of action
Having partitioned the Self by the Self, having created entities of diverse kinds,
the Lord of all, all-formed, proceeds as the enjoyer in dream

children.text: svamātrā paramātrā vā śrutyā prakramyate yathā
children.translated_text: Whether by one’s own measure or by another’s measure, as the usage of hearing determines,

children.text: tathaiva rūḍhatām eti tayā hy artho vidhīyate
children.translated_text: just so it becomes established; for by that usage the meaning is ordained
Even when the ground is entirely not-as-such, through reliance upon audition (scriptural wording),
a determination of the form of a thing is perceived, as in the firebrand-circle and the like

children.text: api prayoktur ātmānaṃ śabdam antar avasthitam
children.translated_text: They even declare the self of the speaker, the word abiding within,

children.text: prāhur mahāntam ṛṣabhaṃ yena sāyujyam iṣyate
children.translated_text: to be the great Bull, union with whom is sought

children.text: tasmād yaḥ śabdasaṃskāraḥ sā siddhiḥ paramātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore that cultivation of sound is the accomplishment of the Supreme Self,
and the knower of the principle of its operation enjoys that <s>Brahman</s>-nectar
Having surpassed the functioning of <s>Prāṇa</s> and being established in the principle of speech,
by the yoga of sequential dissolution, contracting the self into the Self,

children.text: vācaḥ saṃskāram ādhāya vācaṃ jñāne niveśya ca
children.translated_text: having placed the refinement of speech, and having inserted speech into knowledge,

children.text: vibhajya bandhanāny asyāḥ kṛtvā tāṃ chinnabandhanām
children.translated_text: and having divided its bonds, making it one whose bonds are cut,
having approached the inner light, having grasped the cutting of the knots,
he proceeds, having severed the knots, into oneness with the causal light

children.text: na jātv akartṛkaṃ kaś cid āgamaṃ pratipadyate
children.translated_text: No one ever apprehends a scripture that is authorless;
when the seeds of all scriptures perish, the triad (the <s>Veda</s>) alone remains established

children.text: astaṃ yāteṣu vādeṣu kartṛṣv anyeṣv asatsv api
children.translated_text: When the disputations have set, and the authors, being others, even if non-existent,
the world does not transgress the dharma declared by <s>Śruti</s> and <s>Smṛti</s>

children.text: jñāne svābhāvike nārthaḥ śāstraiḥ kaś ca na vidyate
children.translated_text: In innate knowledge there is no use whatsoever for treatises,

children.text: dharmo jñānasya hetuś cet tasyāmnāyo nibandhanam
children.translated_text: but if dharma is the cause of knowledge, then its foundation is the sacred transmission (<s>Āmnāya</s>)
And reasoning, not opposed to the <s>Veda</s> and treatise, is the eye of those who do not see,
for from mere form alone the meaning of a sentence does not stand independently
Non-intention with respect to what exists, being-for-another’s-sake, the manifestation of meaning through a sign—
thus the rule, manifold, is analyzed through reasoning

children.text: śabdānām eva sā śaktis tarko yaḥ puruṣāśrayaḥ
children.translated_text: That power of words alone is reasoning, which is grounded in persons,
and that rule, accompanied by words, is unbound in matters lacking scripture
If the great circle of cups of fig-wood color,

children.text: pītaṃ na gamayet svargaṃ kiṃ tat kratugataṃ nayet
children.translated_text: though drunk, does not lead to heaven, how should that which is contained in the rite lead [there]?
Just as forms and the like are seen, each possessed of capacity toward their respective objects,
so too words are seen in such matters as poison-removal and the like

children.text: yathaiṣāṃ tatra sāmarthyaṃ dharme+apy evaṃ pratīyatām
children.translated_text: As their efficacy there is thus, so let it be understood in dharma as well,
therefore, by the virtuous, it should be spoken by the virtuous to those who desire prosperity
Everyone apprehends things whose results are unseen from scripture

children.text: viparītaṃ ca sarvatra śakyate vaktum āgame
children.translated_text: And the reverse, moreover, can be stated everywhere in scripture,
On the ground of knowing what is correct (sādhutva) and of expertise, this is the <s>Smṛti</s> (tradition) of grammar,
without interruption among the cultured; this is a compendium of <s>Smṛti</s> grounded in the learned,

children.text: vaikharyā madhyamāyāś ca paśyantyāś caitad adbhutam
children.translated_text: Of <s>Vaikharī</s> (articulate), <s>Madhyamā</s> (middle), and <s>Paśyantī</s> (seeing)—this is the marvel,
the supreme state of the <s>Trayyā</s> <s>Vāc</s> (Speech of the threefold <s>Veda</s>), manifold in the divisions of many fords (paths),

children.text: gaur iva prakṣaraty ekā rasam uttamaśālinī
children.translated_text: Like a cow, a single one flows forth, bearing excellent savor,
as <s>Bhāratī</s> (Goddess of Speech), the cow fair-smiling, in divine and non-divine form,
Behold the difference of these two, subtle and vibrating,
between <s>Prāṇa</s> and <s>Apāna</s> one alone constantly stands for all,

children.text: anyā tv apreryamāṇaiva vinā prāṇena vartate
children.translated_text: while another, indeed, operates without being impelled, even without <s>Prāṇa</s>,

children.text: jāyate hi tataḥ prāṇo vācam āpyāyayan punaḥ
children.translated_text: for from that there is born <s>Prāṇa</s> again, replenishing speech,
Being replenished by <s>Prāṇa</s>, that very one thus becomes the basis of practical transaction,

children.text: sarvasyocchvāsam āsādya na vāg vadati karhi cit
children.translated_text: yet, though it reaches everyone’s exhalation, speech does not speak at any time,
The sounding one, having produced a sound, and the unsounding one, operate,

children.text: tayor api ca ghoṣiṇyā nirghoṣaiva garīyasī
children.translated_text: and of those two, even though the sounding is there, the unsounding is the weightier,
When the places (articulatory points) are opened and the breath is released, with the phonemes taken up,
<s>Vaikharī vāk</s> (articulate speech) of speakers, grounded in the operation of <s>Prāṇa</s>,
merely follows the sequence whose material is intellect, having the form of an order,
transcending the operation of <s>Prāṇa</s>, <s>Madhyamā vāk</s> proceeds,
But <s>Paśyantī</s> is undivided, with all sequence withdrawn,
subtle speech that does not depart, whose own-form’s light is within,
Though always being filled with nectar, by adventitious impurities,
like the last digit of the moon, she is not utterly overwhelmed,
When she is seen in her own-form, entitlement (adhikāra) ceases,

children.text: puruṣe ṣoḍaśakale tām āhur amṛtāṃ kalām
children.translated_text: in the man possessing sixteen parts they call her the immortal digit,
Having come into the form of what has been influenced, by disturbances that cling,
<s>Vaikharī</s>, like pure <s>Sattva</s> (lucidity), is not scattered by the qualities (<s>Guṇa</s>s),
As established by division and non-division being effected,
to those who know the natures of things, the powers of words are seen,
They declare the <s>Śruti</s> (revealed text) to be beginningless, un-delimited, authorless,

children.text: śiṣṭair nibadhyamānā tu na vyavacchidyate smṛtiḥ
children.translated_text: but <s>Smṛti</s>, though being set down by the learned, is not delimited,
The designation, for what unfolds from the undivided, is in <s>Śruti</s> like in a dream,

children.text: bhāvatattvaṃ tu vijñāya liṅgebhyo vihitā smṛtiḥ
children.translated_text: but <s>Smṛti</s> is enjoined after knowing the true nature of things from indicators (liṅgas),
The impurities that are situated with respect to body, speech, and intellect—
their purifications are through the sciences of therapy, characteristics, and the inner self (<s>adhyātma</s>),

children.text: śabdaḥ saṃskārahīno yo gaur iti prayuyukṣyate
children.translated_text: A word devoid of refinement that one would apply as ‘cow’ (<s>gauḥ</s>),
they regard as an <s>apabhraṃśa</s> (corruption), though lodged in a particular meaning,
Words like ‘asva’, ‘goṇī’, and the like are correct in another domain,
and due to difference of occasion, correctness is established everywhere,
In the correct ones, by inference, the causes of the arising of cognition,
having approached identity, are revealers of the word-meaning,

children.text: na śiṣṭair anugamyante paryāyā iva sādhavaḥ
children.translated_text: They are not followed by the learned, like synonyms that are correct,

children.text: te yataḥ smṛtiśāstreṇa tasmāt sākṣād avācakāḥ
children.translated_text: since they are [established] by the treatise on <s>Smṛti</s>, therefore they do not directly denote,
Just as a child under instruction mis-speaks, saying ‘ambvaṃbv,’

children.text: avyaktaṃ tadvidāṃ tena vyaktau bhavati niścayaḥ
children.translated_text: by that which is indistinct to those who know the matter, a certainty is produced about the distinct,
Thus, when a corruption is employed where a correct form ought to be used,
by that, some meaning, removed from the correct, is expressed,
Through transmission, corruptions have gained currency among inferior utterers,

children.text: prasiddhim āgatā yena teṣāṃ sādhur avācakaḥ
children.translated_text: whereby for them the correct [form] does not denote,
This divine speech is intermingled by those unable to utter,
but in this debate, for those who see impermanence, there is an error of intellect,
Since both are without interruption, with the intention of a different word,
a word that is other, when employed, is not the denoter of the meaning
Thus is completed the Brahma-Section in the Vākyapadīya composed by <s>Bhartṛhari</s>
Vākyakāṇḍa
The verb, the aggregate of words, the universal present in the aggregate,
the one partless word, sequence—these are the recollective syntheses of intellect,

children.text: padam ādyaṃ pṛthak sarvaṃ padaṃ sāpekṣam ity api
children.translated_text: ‘The word is primary,’ ‘each [word] separately,’ ‘every word is relational’—also thus,

children.text: vākyaṃ prati matir bhinnā bahudhā nyāyadarśinām
children.translated_text: with respect to the sentence, the opinions of the logicians are variously diverse,
What is prescribed in the treatise for the arrangement of prosodic suppressions and the like—
by that, having members that expect (one another), not everything has the same definition,
A sentence is said to be [that] whose members are mutually expectant, distinct, not containing alien-expectant words,
being action-primary with qualifiers, or a single meaning,

children.text: saṃbodhanapadaṃ yac ca tat kriyāyā viśeṣakam
children.translated_text: And the vocative word is a determiner of the action,
‘Go, <s>Devadatta</s>!’—there is prosodic suppression (nighāta) in that case accordingly
Just as even a single <s>ktvānta</s> (absolutive) is a specifier of a <s>tiṅanta</s> (finite verb),
so they say that a <s>tiṅanta</s> there is a specifier of a <s>tiṅanta</s> as well
Just as the one single revealer of all meanings is articulated in divisions,
so too, in conformity with the differences in what is seen, there is comprehension of sentence-meaning
Just as, of a single variegated figure, by means of demonstrations of difference,
descriptions are made with distinct marks such as ‘blue,’ and the like,
so likewise, for a single sentence wholly without mutual expectancy,
a describing by other words is accompanied by ones that do have expectancy
Just as in a word the base, suffix, and the like are separated,
so in a sentence the extraction (apoddhāra) of words is justifiable
Sameness-of-form with other phonemes is seen in the parts of phonemes,
and parts of words stand as if they were same-formed with other words
Bulls, water, and barley are combined with parts that are meaningless,
but co-presence and absence (anvaya–vyatireka) are the basis of practical usage
There is no division of the word; how then will there be division of the meaning?
by divisions, the uninformed apprehend mere procedural differences

children.text: brāhmaṇārtho yathā nāsti kaś cid brāhmaṇakambale
children.translated_text: Just as there is no ‘<s>brāhmaṇa</s>-meaning’ in any ‘<s>brāhmaṇa</s>-blanket,’
so too words like <s>Devadatta</s> and the like in a sentence would be meaningless
The meaning of the universal, once concealed, does not stand in a particular,
once taken up, whence the abandonment? Once ceased, where should it stand?

children.text: aśābdo yadi vākyārthaḥ padārtho+api tathā bhavet
children.translated_text: If the sentence-meaning is non-verbal, then the word-meaning would be so as well,

children.text: evaṃ sati ca saṃbandhaḥ śabdasyārthena hīyate
children.translated_text: and if that is the case, the relation of word to meaning is impaired
Certain particularizing words, being imitations (counterparts) of the universal,
are manifested in cognizers through relation to other words

children.text: teṣāṃ tu kṛtsno vākyārthaḥ pratibhedaṃ samāpyate
children.translated_text: But for those, the entire sentence-meaning is concluded with distinction apportioned,
the success of the meaning for cognizers is through what is manifest and what suggests

children.text: sa vyaktaḥ kramavāñ śabda upāṃśu yam adhīyate
children.translated_text: That manifest word, when one studies it sotto voce, is sequential,
but the intellect, wherein it stands spread out, is non-sequential
Just as even with a specific kind of ‘lifting up’ no difference of action is grasped,
on repetition the universal is manifested by actions such as revolving and the like
Thus in phoneme, sentence, and word, the same hearing with manifest and suggestive is obtained,
the reality, though absolutely distinct, is apprehended as if same-formed

children.text: nityeṣu ca kutaḥ pūrvaṃ paraṃ vā paramārthataḥ
children.translated_text: And in the eternal, how could there be earlier or later in the ultimate sense?

children.text: ekasyaiva tu sā śaktir yad evam avabhāsate
children.translated_text: it is the power of the one alone by which it thus appears

children.text: ciraṃ kṣipram iti jñāne kālabhedād ṛte yathā
children.translated_text: As in the cognition ‘long’ and ‘short,’ apart from a difference of time,
they appear at different times—the same property of short and long [applies to measures]

children.text: na nityaḥ kramamātrābhiḥ kālo bhedam ihārhati
children.translated_text: Time, being eternal, does not merit difference by mere measures of sequence here,
in the absence of measures that delimit, what sort of sequence would there be?

children.text: tābhyo yā jāyate buddhir ekā sā bhāgavarjitā
children.translated_text: The cognition that arises from them is one, devoid of parts,
for it, by its own power, though itself one, apprehends sequence as if divided
Because of the adherence of the scratch of sequence, whatever seed is deposited therein,
for that, the definition of ‘one reality or many’ does not hold fast
But at the time of contemplation (bhāvanā), this sequential capacity becomes non-sequential,
whereby a meaning, with distinctions set aside, is apprehended as possessed of distinctions

children.text: padāni vākye tāny eva varṇās te ca pade yadi
children.translated_text: If the words in a sentence are just those very phonemes, and those are in a word,
then in phonemes there would be a division of phoneme-parts, like ultimate atoms

children.text: bhāgānām anupaśleṣān na varṇo na padaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: From the non-coalescence of the parts, there would be neither phoneme nor word,
since those would be unnameable, what else should be named?

children.text: yad antaḥśabdatattvaṃ tu bhāgair ekaṃ prakāśitam
children.translated_text: But that inner word-principle, one, made manifest by parts,

children.text: tam āhur apare śabdaṃ tasya vākye tathaikatām
children.translated_text: others call that the ‘word,’ and likewise its unity in the sentence
Likewise, by parts of meaning, their internal meaning is made manifest,
these two—word and meaning—are differences of this very Self, abiding as non-distinct
The status of revealer and revealed, the form of effect and cause,
belong always to that inner-measure Self of the principle of the word
For in that very one, existence and non-existence, the capacities, are equally established,
in the non-sequential that appears as sequential, the ground of practical usage
By making the cognition of assurance (saṃpratyaya) the means of proof for positing word-meanings,
upon accumulation and abandonment of word-meanings, meaninglessness would ensue
By the word ‘king,’ the meaning ‘king’ is apprehended in a different form,
in usage, a word other than the finite verb is employed, similar to the finite verb
As, when one says ‘horse-eared,’ it is understood even without ‘horse,’

children.text: kaś cid eva viśiṣṭo+arthaḥ sarveṣu pratyayas tathā
children.translated_text: so too, with all affixes, only a particularized meaning is apprehended
Given the presence of a different meaning in sentences and the positing of similarity,
for some, word-hood by convention (rūḍhi) is adopted only within the treatise

children.text: upādāyāpi ye heyās tān upāyān pracakṣate
children.translated_text: Even adopting means which indeed are to be abandoned, they declare them as means
and a fixed rule regarding means does not necessarily stand firm

children.text: arthaṃ kathaṃ cit puruṣaḥ kaś cit saṃpratipadyate
children.translated_text: Some person somehow apprehends a meaning,

children.text: saṃsṛṣṭā vā vibhaktā vā bhedā vākyanibandhanāḥ
children.translated_text: the distinctions are grounded in the sentence, whether conjoined or separated

children.text: so+ayam ity abhisaṃbandho buddhyā prakramyate yadā
children.translated_text: When the relation ‘this-one and that-one’ is initiated by the intellect,

children.text: vākyārthasya tadaiko+api varṇaḥ pratyāyakaḥ kva cit
children.translated_text: then, in regard to the sentence-meaning, even a single phoneme is, at times, a bringer-to-cognition
Just so far as a meaning is denoted by a bare word alone,
so far, of that meaning located in a sentence, they call that [word] the denoter

children.text: saṃbandhe sati yat tv anyad ādhikyam upajāyate
children.translated_text: But whatever surplus arises when there is relation,
that they call the sentence-meaning, which rests upon multiple words
And that, though situated in multiple words, is brought to completion as a single specific content,
like a class in a collection, others conceive it as number
Yet others know universality as conformable to all distinctions,
and that, through connection with another meaning, assumes the form of distinction
Its wavering—since it expects distinctions—
relation, delimiting that, by establishing it in the particular, cuts it off

children.text: kāryānumeyaḥ saṃbandho rūpaṃ tasya na vidyate
children.translated_text: Relation is to be inferred from effect; it has no [own] form,
being utterly of the nature of non-being, therefore they posit it
When the effect is determinate, the means is determinate; an action has a determinate instrument,
by mere proximity that rule becomes manifest
There, the noun operates as qualified, with expectancy,
as being to-be-accomplished, it looks to the verb as its occasion

children.text: santa eva viśeṣā ye padārtheṣu vyavasthitāḥ
children.translated_text: The specificities that truly exist, established in the word-meanings,

children.text: te kramād anugamyante na vākyam abhidhāyakam
children.translated_text: are followed in sequence; the sentence is not the denoter

children.text: śabdānāṃ kramamātre ca nānyaḥ śabdo+asti vācakaḥ
children.translated_text: And besides the mere sequence of words, there is no other word that is an indicator,

children.text: kramo hi dharmaḥ kālasya tena vākyaṃ na vidyate
children.translated_text: for sequence is a property of <s>kāla</s> (time); therefore a sentence does not exist

children.text: ye ca saṃbhavino bhedāḥ padārtheṣv avibhāvitāḥ
children.translated_text: And the distinctions which are possible in the word-meanings but not made explicit,

children.text: saṃnidhāne vyajyante na tu varṇeṣv ayaṃ kramaḥ
children.translated_text: are manifested upon contiguity; but this sequence does not belong to phonemes
And the designation ‘word’ and the term ‘sentence,’ which are situated merely in the sequence of phonemes and of words,

children.text: padākhyā vākyasaṃjñā ca śabdatvaṃ neṣyate tayoḥ
children.translated_text: their word-hood is not admitted

children.text: samāne+api tu śabdatve dṛṣṭaḥ saṃpratyayaḥ padāt
children.translated_text: Yet, even if there were the same word-hood, an experienced assurance arises from the word,

children.text: prativarṇaṃ tv asau nāsti padasyārtham ato viduḥ
children.translated_text: but such [assurance] is not per phoneme; therefore they know the word’s meaning

children.text: yathā sāvayavā varṇā vinā vācyena kena cit
children.translated_text: Just as phonemes, being with parts or without some distinct denotatum,

children.text: arthavantaḥ samuditā vākyam apy evam iṣyate
children.translated_text: are meaningful when assembled, so too is a sentence accepted
They say that uttered in sequence they are either meaningless, because of being liable to fall away, or meaningful by the word-meaning,
while the sentence-meaning has a distinct characteristic
On the supposition of the eternity of aggregates or of a <s>jāti</s> (class),
they say that the sentence, being invariable, has a unitary meaning
Those who speak of the sentence imagine distinctions preceded by non-difference,
but those who regard the word take non-differences to be preceded by distinctions
And the status of being the basis of words is described according to differences of functions,

children.text: padānāṃ saṃhitā yoniḥ saṃhitā vā padāśrayā
children.translated_text: the coalescence of words is the source, or coalescence rests upon words

children.text: padāmnāyaś ca yady anyaḥ saṃhitāyā nidarśakaḥ
children.translated_text: And if there is another tradition of words as an indicator of coalescence,

children.text: nityas tatra kathaṃ kāryaṃ padaṃ lakṣaṇadarśanāt
children.translated_text: how could a word there be a product, being established by the perception of characteristics?
Just as the apprehension of a word-meaning is not cognized with regard to each phoneme,
so, with words, the determination of sentence-meaning is not cognized [piecewise]
The sentence-meaning settles into the words that co-occur,
just so the word-meaning [settles] into the phonemes that co-occur

children.text: sūkṣmaṃ grāhyaṃ yathānyena saṃsṛṣṭaṃ saha gṛhyate
children.translated_text: As that which is subtle, though to be grasped, is grasped together with something conjoined to it,

children.text: varṇo+apy anyena varṇena saṃbaddho vācakas tathā
children.translated_text: so a phoneme, bound with another phoneme, is an indicator

children.text: padasyoccāraṇād artho yathā kaś cin nirūpyate
children.translated_text: Just as, from the utterance of a word, some meaning is determined,

children.text: varṇānām api sāṃnidhyāt tathā so+arthaḥ pratīyate
children.translated_text: so, from the proximity of phonemes, that very meaning is apprehended

children.text: prāptasya yasya sāmarthyān niyamārthā punaḥ śrutiḥ
children.translated_text: If, for something already obtained by capacity, a further Vedic statement for restriction occurs,
and by that, if the universal is entirely overruled in a specific way
then, since “one should sacrifice” yields a substance as obtained, defined by capacity,

children.text: vrīhiśrutyā nivarteta na syāt pratinidhis tathā
children.translated_text: it should be set aside by the mention of ‘rice,’ nor would a substitute be appropriate
Therefore the word ‘rice’ should posit ‘rice-ness’ as additional,

children.text: dravyatvam aviruddhatvāt prāptyarthaḥ san na bādhate
children.translated_text: while ‘substance-hood,’ being non-contradictory and for the sake of obtaining, is not overruled
And when ‘substance-hood,’ which accompanies it, is thus delimited and set apart,
the non-appearance there of other specifics is due to their impossibility

children.text: na ca sāmānyavat sarve kriyāśabdena lakṣitāḥ
children.translated_text: Nor are all specifics indicated by an action-word as with a universal,

children.text: viśeṣā na hi sarveṣāṃ satāṃ śabdo+abhidhāyakaḥ
children.translated_text: for the word does not denote all specifics that exist
Just as whiteness and the like, though present as qualities, are there not intended,
so too there is non-intention of those distinctions that accompany ‘substance-hood’

children.text: asaṃnidhau pratinidhir mā bhūn nityasya karmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Let there not be a substitute, in the absence [of the specified item], for what is a permanent action,

children.text: kāmyasya vā pravṛttasya lopa ity upapadyate
children.translated_text: but for a desired or already undertaken [action] the omission is reasonable
The action is indeed particularized by which the sentence-meaning is conceived,

children.text: dravyābhāve pratinidhau tasya tat syāt kriyāntaram
children.translated_text: and when there is a substitute in the absence of the substance, that would be a different action for it

children.text: nirjñātārthaṃ padaṃ yac ca tadarthe pratipādite
children.translated_text: And as for a word whose meaning has not been understood, when its object is conveyed,

children.text: pikādi yad avijñātaṃ tat kim ity anuyujyate
children.translated_text: what, then, is asked about that which is unknown, such as ‘cuckoo’ and the like?
And that which, obtained by capacity, is attached to the meaning of the individual,
the <s>śruti</s> (Vedic text) itself, by way of an adjunct, overrules the [inferential] marks and sentences

children.text: aprāpto yas tu śuklādiḥ saṃnidhānena gamyate
children.translated_text: But that which, like ‘white’ and the like, is not already obtained is grasped by proximity,
and that which is obtained by effort in a sentence is distinct from the property of <s>śruti</s>

children.text: abhinnam eva vākyaṃ tu yady abhinnārtham iṣyate
children.translated_text: If the sentence is indeed non-differentiated when a non-differentiated meaning is accepted,

children.text: tat sarvaṃ śrutibhūtatvān na śrutyaiva virotsyate
children.translated_text: then, since all would be of the status of <s>śruti</s>, it would not be opposed by <s>śruti</s> itself
And the aggregate of sentences which is for the establishment of a single meaning,
there, even though the members have mutual expectancy, the sentence-meaning is not present

children.text: prāsaṅgikam idaṃ kāryam idaṃ tantreṇa labhyate
children.translated_text: This is an incidental result; this is obtained by system,
this is [due to] differences of recurrence; here there are accumulations of overrulings

children.text: ūho+asmin viṣaye nyāyyaḥ saṃbandho+asya na bādhyat
children.translated_text: Here conjectural adjustment is legitimate; its relation is not overruled,
this is an extension of the general, and here the particular is extended

children.text: arthitvam atra sāmarthyam asminn artho na bhidyate
children.translated_text: Here ‘need’ is the capacity; in this, the meaning is not divided,
this jurisdiction is obtained from scripture; its exclusion is in a different action

children.text: iyaṃ śrutyā kramaprāptir iyam uccāraṇād iti
children.translated_text: This is obtained in sequence by <s>śruti</s>; this is [obtained] from utterance,

children.text: kramo+ayam atra balavān asmiṃs tu na vivakṣitaḥ
children.translated_text: here sequence is strong, but in this [other case] it is not intended
This, being connected with the subsequent auxiliaries, is not productive for the auxiliaries,
this is productive for them; here this is not bound by immediate succession

children.text: idaṃ pradhānaṃ śeṣo+ayaṃ viniyogakramas tv ayam
children.translated_text: This is the principal; this is the remainder; and this is the order of application,
this directly assists it; this, from a distance, specifies
Here the difference is a difference of the operation of powers, but here the result differs,
this difference of cognition is from relation; there, difference is not intended
This is a non-relational negation; but here this is an exceptive negation,

children.text: idaṃ gauṇam idaṃ mukhyaṃ vyāpīdaṃ guru laghv idam
children.translated_text: this is secondary; this is primary; this pervades; this is weighty; this is light
Its relation of subordinate and principal is determined by difference; in many ways this is to be distinguished,
this is restricted; for this, here fitness arises
From what is seen in another sentence, difference is inferred by an indicatory mark,
this word-meaning is separated by removing words
Thus the properties in sentences that are grounded on word-meanings,

children.text: te sarve na prakalperan padaṃ cet syād avācakam
children.translated_text: all these would not be established if a word were non-denotative
Even when the sentence-meaning is undivided, by the difference of powers, when separated out,
it is not contrary to what was said, by division among other sentences
Just as a single fragrance is conceived as diversified
in flowers and the like, so too in a sentence a difference of meaning is expressed
And as, in the cases of a <s>gavaya</s> (wild ox) and a <s>narasiṃha</s> (man-lion), without a prior single cognition,
one grasps a portion only of another <s>jāti</s> (class) as similar

children.text: aprasiddhaṃ tu yaṃ bhāgam adṛṣṭam anupaśyati
children.translated_text: But what portion is not established and is unseen, which one does not observe,
a dull person takes that much indistinctness to be everywhere
Likewise, by connection with ‘cuckoo’ and the like, in a sentence utterly distinct,
he takes the cognition only of something similar to be the meaning of what is non-existent

children.text: ekasya bhāge sādṛśyaṃ bhāge bhedaś ca lakṣyate
children.translated_text: Similarity is observed in a part of one thing, and difference in a part,
and the manifestation that is without parts is grasped only by a mind that is without parts
Just so, similarity is determined in a part and difference in a part,
even in the absence of parts, for sentences whose properties are utterly distinct
When the forms of words perish, how could there be the supposition of a delimiter?
And when the delimiter is not apprehended in a word, how could the meaning be distinguished?
As if a conjunction of forms, their arrangement is in the word elsewhere,
for diverse forms, that form, by rule, is not taken as another
When, in that non-difference, the conjunction of differences occurs,
a form is distinguished as not other than another form

children.text: śāstre pratyāyakasyāpi kva cid ekatvam āśritam
children.translated_text: In the [grammatical] system, even of what makes known, unity is assumed in some cases,

children.text: pratyāyyena kva cid bhedo grahaṇagrāhyayoḥ sthitaḥ
children.translated_text: and in some cases difference is posited between the apprehender and the apprehended

children.text: ū ity abhedam āśritya yathāsaṃkhyaṃ prakalpitam
children.translated_text: Relying on the non-difference denoted by ‘ū’, a one-to-one sequence is conceived,

children.text: lṛluṭor grahaṇe bhedo grāhyābhyāṃ saha kalpitaḥ
children.translated_text: and, in the taking of <s>lṛ</s> and <s>luṭ</s>, difference is posited along with the things to be apprehended

children.text: yasyety etad aṇo rūpaṃ saṃjñinām abhidhāyakam
children.translated_text: ‘yasya’—this is the form of the affix <s>aṇ</s>, which denotes those bearing a name,
for there is no possibility of taking, by means of what is already cognized

children.text: ū ity etad abhinnaṃ ca bhinnavākyanibandhanam
children.translated_text: And ‘ū’—this is non-different, yet it is grounded upon different sentences

children.text: bhedena grahaṇaṃ yasya pararūpam iva dvayoḥ
children.translated_text: Whose apprehension, by difference, is as if the other’s form in the case of two,
and the prolongation’s (<s>pluta</s>) increase belonging to the base, and likewise the aggregate of accents,

children.text: vyudasyatā punar bhedaḥ śabdeṣv atyantam āśritaḥ
children.translated_text: when set aside, again, difference is utterly relied upon in words
Just as, in half-<s>ṛc</s> and the like, there is difference of form in words, successively,
so too, from the system (<s>tantra</s>), even where there is one word, there is a different audition for different ones
In the domain of <s>saṃhitā</s> (phonetic conjunction), the phonemes, unchanged in their own form,
seem to go to being another word, because of the acceptance of another power
By alteration of the senses and the like, it is seen with regard to things to be grasped,

children.text: ātmatyāgād ṛte bhinnaṃ grahaṇaṃ sa kramaḥ śrutau
children.translated_text: apart from the relinquishment of their own nature, the distinct apprehension—that is sequence in audition
From the difference of the act of denotation, even when the words are unaltered,
the very same form, by utter difference, manifests as one

children.text: ṛco vā gītimātraṃ vā sāma dravyāntaraṃ na tu
children.translated_text: The <s>ṛc</s> or merely the chant is not a different substance as <s>sāman</s>,

children.text: gītibhedāt tu gṛhyante tā eva vikṛtā ṛcaḥ
children.translated_text: but by difference of chant, those very <s>ṛc</s>-verses are apprehended as modified
By a means for the consolidation of audition, for those different ones that have a single principal,
their correctness in the treatise is said to be by instrumental utterance (<s>antra</s>)
Having taken even a single audition, though there are differences of form,

children.text: tantreṇoccāraṇaṃ kāryam anyathā te na sādhavaḥ
children.translated_text: utterance by the system (<s>tantra</s>) is to be done; otherwise they are not correct
And for sentences that are of the same form, not established by the treatise,
from utterance by the system (<s>tantra</s>), one correct form is obtained
The multiplicity of forms of one (thing) is due to acceptance of pipe and the like (<s>nālikā</s> etc.),

children.text: yathā tathaiva tantrāt syād bahūnām ekarūpatā
children.translated_text: so too, from the system (<s>tantra</s>), there would be unity of form for many
Just as the occurrence, separately, of sentences that are identical in words,
so, in the absence of another sentence, these would have separateness of meaning
The denoted is the meaning of the word; the meaning of the sentence is the intended purpose,

children.text: yasya tasya na saṃbandho vākyānām upapadyate
children.translated_text: of whichever it is, that connection of sentences is not tenable
There, only the verb-members look to one another,
and the connection, being bound to the verb-members, is then apprehended
Repetition or restatement pertains to the positing of particulars of word-meanings,
but the meaning, completed in each, abides in co-present (constituents)
When the sentence-meaning is unvariegated, the alternatives rest upon the injunction (<s>bhāvanā</s>),
in this topic many doctrines of the predecessors are accepted
By habituation, every word is held by others to be a cause of intuition (<s>pratibhā</s>),
in the conveying of the real meaning for children and for animals

children.text: anāgamaś ca so+abhyāsaḥ samayaḥ kaiś cid iṣyate
children.translated_text: And that habituation, without transmission, is by some held to be convention (<s>samaya</s>),

children.text: anantaram idaṃ kāryam asmād ity upadarśakaḥ
children.translated_text: as an indicator, ‘this is to be done immediately after that’
‘There is a meaning for all words’—this is the mark of what makes understand (<s>pratyāyin</s>),
they say it is on a par with unprecedented duty, deities, and heaven, with respect to cows and the like
But the grasp of shapes due to seeing usage and habituation,

children.text: na sa śabdasya viṣayaḥ sa hi yatnāntarāśrayaḥ
children.translated_text: that is not the domain of the word, for it relies on a different effort

children.text: ke cid bhedāḥ prakāśyante śabdais tadabhidhāyibhiḥ
children.translated_text: Some say that differences are manifested by words that denote them,

children.text: anuniṣpādinaḥ kāṃś cic chabdārthān iti manyate
children.translated_text: and hold that some word-meanings do not effect production

children.text: jāteḥ pratyāyake śabde yā vyaktir anuṣaṅgiṇī
children.translated_text: For a word that makes known a <s>jāti</s> (class), the particular that adheres after it,
the class-word does not rely upon differences that belong to that particular
Nor does the denoter make known the shapes of pots and the like,
since it is directed merely to the thing, its course is not intermediate

children.text: kriyā vinā prayogeṇa na dṛṣṭā śabdacoditā
children.translated_text: Without an action, no performance is seen that is prompted by a word,

children.text: prayogas tv anuniṣpādī śabdārtha iti gamyate
children.translated_text: but usage, not itself producing, is understood to be the word-meaning

children.text: niyatās tu prayogā ye niyataṃ yac ca sādhanam
children.translated_text: But those usages that are fixed, and the means that is fixed,
their being denoted by words is followed by others
A collection is the denoted, or else an unvariegated cumulation,

children.text: asatyo vāpi saṃsargaḥ śabdārthaḥ kaiś cid iṣyate
children.translated_text: or even an unreal relation—some hold this to be the word-meaning

children.text: asatyopādhi yat satyaṃ tad vā śabdanibandhanām
children.translated_text: What is true by reason of an unreal adjunct, that is held to be dependent on words,

children.text: śabdo vāpy abhijalpatvam āgato yāti vācyataṃ
children.translated_text: or else the word, having attained the state of ‘uttered toward’ (<s>abhijalpatva</s>), comes to have denotability

children.text: so+ayam ity abhisaṃbandhād rūpam ekīkṛtaṃ yadā
children.translated_text: When, by the relation ‘this here is that’, the form is unified
of the word with the meaning, they call that word ‘uttered toward’ (<s>abhijalpa</s>)
When the two have non-distinct identity, usage is unfailing,

children.text: kiṃ cid eva kva cid rūpaṃ prādhānyenāvatiṣṭhate
children.translated_text: some one form, somewhere, stands forth as principal
In common usage a word, having attained the status of the form of the object, operates,
but in the treatise the twofoldness of form is distinguished by intention

children.text: aśakteḥ sarvaśakter vā śabdair eva prakalpitā
children.translated_text: From incapacity, or from omnipotence, a fixed assignment of action and the like
for a single meaning is constructed by words alone
Whatever meaning is the object of cognition, grounded in an external thing,

children.text: sa bāhyaṃ vastv iti jñātaḥ śabdārtha iti gamyate
children.translated_text: that, known as the external thing, is understood to be the word-meaning
The knowables are endowed with forms, based upon recollection of particulars
These (knowables) appear; but mere consciousness (<s>saṃvinmātra</s>) is otherwise than this
Just as the sense-faculty, coming into conjunction, displays (objects) with variety,
so indeed the apprehension of the meaning from the word is manifold
Even when the speaker has set forth in one way, with the understanders being diverse,
the word-meaning is partitioned, in conformity with their own cognitions

children.text: asminn api dṛśye+arthe darśanaṃ bhidyate pṛthak
children.translated_text: Even with regard to this very visible object, the seeing is separately differentiated,

children.text: kālāntareṇa caiko+api taṃ paśyaty anyathā punaḥ
children.translated_text: and even one and the same person, at another time, sees it differently again
And even for one single word, because the conditions are unsettled,
by one or by many, the meaning is imagined in many ways
Therefore, for those whose reality has not been seen, perception or utterance,
being faulty and much-trickling (full of many pretexts), is indeed ever unsettled

children.text: ṛṣīṇāṃ darśanaṃ yac ca tattve kiṃ cid avasthitam
children.translated_text: And whatever vision of the seers (<s>ṛṣi</s>-s) is in any respect fixed regarding the reality,

children.text: na tena vyavahāro+asti na tac chabdanibandhanam
children.translated_text: by that there is no transactional usage, nor is it grounded in words

children.text: talavad dṛśyate vyoma khadyoto havyavāḍ iva
children.translated_text: As a reflection on the ground, the sky is seen; as fire in the firefly, the oblation-eater (<s>havyavāt</s>/<s>hutāśana</s>) is seen,

children.text: naiva cāsti talaṃ vyomni na khadyote hutāśanaḥ
children.translated_text: yet there is no ground in the sky, nor is there the fire of oblations in the firefly

children.text: tasmāt pratyakṣam apy arthaṃ vidvān īkṣeta yuktitaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, even with regard to an object that is perceptible, the learned person should examine by reasoning,

children.text: na darśanasya prāmāṇyād dṛśyam arthaṃ prakalpayet
children.translated_text: and should not, on account of the authority of (mere) seeing, construct the object that is seen
As, for things whose realities cannot be named, in ordinary dealings there is a naming,

children.text: vyavahāre samākhyānaṃ tat prajño na vikalpayet
children.translated_text: that the wise person should not reify by conceptual construction
When there is non-grasping of separations of the things, it is precisely <s>pratibhā</s> (intuition) that arises,

children.text: vākyārtha iti tām āhuḥ ē̃ padārthair upapāditām
children.translated_text: they call that the sentence-meaning, presented by the word-meanings

children.text: idaṃ tad iti sānyeṣām anākhyeyā kathaṃ ca na
children.translated_text: ‘This is that’—and how should it not be unnameable for others?

children.text: pratyātmavṛtti siddhā sā kartrāpi na nirūpyate
children.translated_text: established as operating only for one’s own self, it is not determined even by the agent (speaker)
Unreflected, it effects, as it were, a coalescence of the meanings,
having, as it were, attained universal-form-ness, it functions as an object
Whether generated directly by the word, or along with a following from cultivation (<s>bhāvanā</s>),

children.text: itikartavyatāyāṃ tāṃ na kaś cid ativartate
children.translated_text: in the ‘what-is-to-be-done’ (<s>itikartavyatā</s>) no one oversteps it
The whole world follows that as a means of valid cognition,
undertakings are set in motion, even among animals, by its power
Just as, from the maturations of particular substances, powers such as intoxication are seen to arise without effort,
so too is <s>pratibhā</s> for those endowed with that (maturation)
Who alters the natural functioning of the voice of the male cuckoo in spring?
and how are creatures and the like instructed in making nests and so on?
Who is the prompter for deer and birds in actions such as eating, delight, aversion, swimming, and the like,
which are well known as connected with their species-lineage?
This arises indeed from tradition (<s>āgama</s>) accompanied by cultivation (<s>bhāvanā</s>),
and tradition is distinguished by closeness and remoteness (of association)
They know <s>pratibhā</s> to be sixfold: produced by (1) nature, (2) covering, (3) practice, (4) yoga, (5) the unseen (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>), (6) having a qualifier,
or, produced by the unseen, and characterized as specifically qualified
Just as the word ‘cow’ is applied to an object marked by substances that are conjoined,

children.text: gośabdo na tv asau teṣāṃ viśeṣāṇāṃ prakāśakaḥ
children.translated_text: but it is not a revealer of the particular properties of those (substances)
Even when the word operates with respect to cows and the like that are compounded of shape, color, and parts,

children.text: śabdaḥ pravartamāno+api na tān aṅgīkaroty asau
children.translated_text: it does not adopt those (shape, color, and parts)
A word is applied to an object qualified by configuration, color, and parts,
but no operation of it is observed with respect to that object’s parts
For someone in the world it is difficult to see all the parts,

children.text: kaiś cit tv avayavair dṛṣṭair arthaḥ kṛtsno+anumīyate
children.translated_text: but from certain parts that are seen, the whole object is inferred
Likewise, for <s>jāti</s> (class), the lotus, and the like—qualities that are concomitant,
having a permanent relation—we observe their determination by scent
The denoter operates without dependence on number, measure, or configuration,

children.text: bindau ca samudāye ca vācakaḥ salilādiṣu
children.translated_text: and denotes both the drop and the aggregate, in the case of water and the like
Where there is a determination limited by a conditioning such as refinement (<s>saṃskāra</s>), as in oil and the like,
a word truly states a part, because it pertains to something that resides in the parts
When an expression is employed as connected with a certain meaning,
upon the departure of that meaning its usage ceases

children.text: yāṃs tu saṃbhavino dharmān antarṇīya prayujyate
children.translated_text: But the words that are employed by including properties that are possible (to be present),

children.text: śabdas teṣāṃ na sāṃnidhyaṃ niyamena vyapekṣate
children.translated_text: do not invariably require the presence of those properties
As is observed in the variation of hairiness, dewlap, and the like,

children.text: gośabdo na tathā jāter viprayoge pravartate
children.translated_text: the word ‘cow’ does not operate when there is the separation from the class
Therefore, when there is a cognition from the word of a possible object,
that whose separation has not been seen is grasped as being related

children.text: vācikā dyotikā vā syur dvitvādīnāṃ vibhaktayaḥ
children.translated_text: The case-endings of duality and the like may be vocalic (expressive) or indicative (dyotic),
or else the aggregate of a numbered object may be the denotatum
Or, without the expression of number, or with a difference of number attached,

children.text: arthān svarūpabhedena kāṃś cid āhur gavādayaḥ
children.translated_text: some say that objects such as cows are (distinguished) by difference in their own natures
Those words whose powers are known to be fixed by an eternal connection,
their meanings are apportioned by conjunction and disjunction (anvaya-vyatireka)
And so long as an assumption of those two (conjunction and disjunction) is possible without deviation,

children.text: niyamas tatra na tv evaṃ niyamo nuṭśabādiṣu
children.translated_text: there is restriction there; but not so is there restriction in words like the affix <s>nuṭ</s>
Where denotation is possible, an indicating function (lakṣaṇā) is posited,
for the powers of words are fixed in relation, being dependent (on contextual factors)
The conjunction of meaning (with form) is observed in ku-, su-, and upa-,
hence it is inferred that only the compound (saṃghāta) conveys a distinct meaning
Secondary derivations (anvākhyāna) diverge in the tasks of word-analysis (śabda-vyutpatti),

children.text: bahūnāṃ saṃbhave+arthānāṃ nimittaṃ kiṃ cid iṣyate
children.translated_text: when many meanings are possible, some cause is assumed
Names such as <s>Vairavāsiṣṭha</s>, <s>Giriśa</s>, and likewise <s>Ekāgārika</s>, etc.,

children.text: kaiś cit kathaṃ cid ākhyātā nimittāvadhisaṃkaraiḥ
children.translated_text: have been explained by some in some manner, with mixtures of limits and causes
Just as the designation of a path by trees, ant-hills, and mountains
is not at odds (with usage), so for cows and the like together with diverse concomitants
And otherwise, those who discern differences of condition make designations,
fixing upon a single part for things like the <s>kiṃśuka</s> (Butea monosperma), etc.

children.text: kaiś cin nirvacanaṃ bhinnaṃ girater garjater gameḥ
children.translated_text: Some propose a different etymology from gir- (‘to swallow/engulf’), garj- (‘to roar’), or gam- (‘to go’),

children.text: gavater gadater vāpi gaur ity atrānudarśitam
children.translated_text: or from gov-/gad-, saying ‘gauḥ (cow)’—this is adduced here

children.text: gaur ity eva svarūpād vā gośabdo goṣu vartate
children.translated_text: Either the word ‘gauḥ’ functions among cows just by its own form (svarūpa),

children.text: vyutpādyate na vā sarvaṃ kaiś cic cobhayatheṣyate
children.translated_text: or nothing at all is derived (etymologically); and some accept both ways
And instruction in general terms in the treatise is adopted for the sake of concision,
while specific differentiations teach the properties of another (item) as if it were a different <s>jāti</s> (class)

children.text: arthāntare ca yad vṛttaṃ tat prakṛtyantaraṃ viduḥ
children.translated_text: And what occurs with respect to a different meaning they know as a different base (prakṛti),

children.text: tulyarūpaṃ na tad rūḍhāv anyasminn anuṣajyate
children.translated_text: that which is of the same form is not, in established usage, attached to something else
The two roots iji and ji are distinct, each restricted to a different domain,

children.text: kaiś cit kathaṃ cid uddiṣṭau citraṃ hi pratipādanam
children.translated_text: yet by some they have been specified in some way—exposition is indeed manifold
Accordingly one should treat vāla-, vāya-, etc., like jitvarī and the like,
