children.text: bhedābhedābhyupagame na virodho+asti kaś ca na
children.translated_text: for on admitting difference and non-difference there is no contradiction at all
For the sake of establishing the aḍ-class and the like, a separate positing is made,

children.text: dhātūpasargayoḥ śāstre dhātur eva tu tādṛśaḥ
children.translated_text: but in the grammar concerning roots and preverbs, it is the root alone that is of that sort

children.text: tathā hi saṃgrāmayateḥ sopasargād vidhiḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus, in the case of saṃgrāmayate and the like, the rule is remembered as requiring a preverb,
and such specific actions, in a complex (saṃghāta), proceed accordingly
In this way, the inner-ness (antaraṅgatva) of operations belongs to roots and preverbs,

children.text: sādhanair yāti saṃbandhaṃ tathābhūtaiva sā kriyā
children.translated_text: the action stands related to the instruments, and it is precisely such
When the meaning is established as fit for usage, it becomes divisible, being specified,
but prior to connection with the instruments the action does not at all arise
Just as, from the progression toward a future union of the root with its instruments,

children.text: dhātutvaṃ karmabhāvaś ca tathānyad api dṛśyatām
children.translated_text: root-hood and the status of ‘action’ are seen, so let other (cases) be observed
Just as, at the time of the seed, by the connection (with them), lac-juice and the like,
through transformations of color and so on, render service to the fruits
So too, by the connection established in cognition, for root and preverb,
a difference that has been internalized becomes manifest at the stage of the word

children.text: kva cit saṃbhavino bhedāḥ kevalair anidarśitāḥ
children.translated_text: Some differences that are possible are left unexpressed by the roots alone,
but in connection with a preverb they are made manifest by pra-, ni-, rā-, and the like

children.text: sa vācako viśeṣāṇāṃ saṃbhavād dyotako+api vā
children.translated_text: It (the preverb) either denotes specificities, or else, because of possibility, it indicates; or again,
it is employed as an auxiliary for the imposition of power upon the root

children.text: sthādibhiḥ kevalair yac ca gamanādi na gamyate
children.translated_text: And whatever going and the like is not grasped by roots like sthā (‘to stand’) taken alone,
there, from the twofold inference, the preverb is said to be a property of that (action)
In non-usage and in over-extension, wherever a different action is observed,
the root, as denoter of that, together with those two, is semantically idle
Likewise, some elements that are self-meaning, functioning within another compound,
when conjoined with something semantically idle, merely reiterate the base-meaning
Some particles (<s>nipāta</s>) are indicators (dyotaka) in establishing distinct meanings,

children.text: āgamā iva ke cit tu saṃbhūyārthasya sādhakāḥ
children.translated_text: while some, like <s>āgama</s> (augment), combine and serve to accomplish the meaning

children.text: upariṣṭāt purastād vā dyotakatvaṃ na bhidyate
children.translated_text: Whether preceding or following, their status as indicators does not differ,
even when they are employed among entirely different meanings

children.text: cādayo na prayujyante padatve sati kevalāḥ
children.translated_text: Items like ‘ca’ are not employed by themselves when they are words (i.e., as independent padas),
and an affix, even though denotative, is not employed by itself
But in combined denotation there is no separation,
and a non-existent state is denoted by finite-verb words (tiṅ-padas)
Even in combined denotation, for those that denote a qualified meaning,

children.text: guṇaiḥ padānāṃ saṃbandhaḥ paratantrās tu cādayaḥ
children.translated_text: The relation of words is through qualities (<s>guṇa</s>), but the ad-classes and the like are dependent

children.text: janayitvā kriyā kā cit saṃbandhaṃ vinivartate
children.translated_text: Having generated some connection, an action withdraws,

children.text: śrūyamāṇe kriyāśabde saṃbandho jāyate kva cit
children.translated_text: when the word for action is heard, in some cases the connection arises
There, the genitive case is prescribed, word by word, for the cessation of a compound,
and a <s>kāraka</s> is cited for the sake of showing; indeed, it is enjoined
And that connection, once arisen, when the finite-verb word is absent,
is, here and there, restricted by what is called <s>karmapravacanīya</s> (‘governing a patient’)
That by which there is an implicature of a finite-verb word is fitted out with the <s>kāraka</s> case-endings,

children.text: yujyate vir yathā tasya likhāv anupasargatā
children.translated_text: just as in the case of vira, for him there is ‘writing’ without a preverb

children.text: tiṣṭhater aprayogaś ca dṛṣṭo+apraty ajayann iti
children.translated_text: And the non-usage of tiṣṭhati is seen in ‘he conquered without the preverb’,

children.text: sunv abhīty ābhimukhye ca kevalo+api prayujyate
children.translated_text: and sunu, abhi, and in the sense of ‘facing toward’ (<s>ābhimukhya</s>), even alone, are employed
The status of being <s>karmapravacanīya</s> is prescribed upon connection with an action,
for the sake of the cessation of ṣatva and the like, for items like <s>sva</s> and the rest, which have an alien property
When, in delimiting the connection of cause and caused, a refusal has been made,
then, from the outset, the third case, characterized as the cause, is overridden

children.text: kriyāyā dyotako nāyaṃ na saṃbandhasya vācakaḥ
children.translated_text: This does not indicate the action, nor does it denote the relation,
nor does it implicate a finite-verb word; rather, it differentiates the relation
A complex of meaningless items, and likewise a meaningful (one) together with meaningless,

children.text: varṇānāṃ padam arthena yuktaṃ nāvayavāḥ pade
children.translated_text: a word (pada) is composed of phonemes connected with meaning, but the parts are not words
The complex of words that are connected with meaning is again divided,
through the cognition of a different meaning and through the loss of relation
In the distinction between meaningful and meaningless, they do not attain relation,
but some say ‘they do attain it’, citing hut and the like as examples
From meaningful items there arises a complex with a specified meaning,
but some say ‘it does not arise’, in cases like compounds that express only their own meaning and the like

children.text: ke cid dhi yutasiddhārthā bhede nirjñātaśaktayaḥ
children.translated_text: For some, having conjoined established meanings, the powers are ascertained in distinction,
while for some, by concomitance and its reversal (presence-with, absence-without), the powers are posited
Only in the sense of the teaching is the meaningfulness of phonemes shown;

children.text: ātvādīnāṃ hi śuddhānāṃ laukiko+artho na vidyate
children.translated_text: for pure items like ā, etc., a worldly meaning does not exist
And the meaning of primary and secondary derivatives (<s>kṛt</s> and <s>taddhita</s>), when taken alone, is non-worldly,

children.text: prāg vibhaktes tadantasya tathaivārtho na vidyate
children.translated_text: and prior to a case-ending the same is true of something ending in them: its meaning does not exist
That meaning which is more fully manifested, which is observed in stems ending in affixes,
is adopted, in accordance with the topic of meaningfulness, as being of just that kind

children.text: ātmabhedo na cet kaś cid varṇebhyaḥ padavākyayoḥ
children.translated_text: If there is no distinct self-nature from phonemes to words and sentences,
then, by mutual dependence of power, even a phoneme would be a denoter

children.text: varṇena kena cin nyūnaḥ saṃghāto yo +abhidhāyakaḥ
children.translated_text: A complex which is denotative, though lacking some phoneme,

children.text: na cec chabdāntaram asāv anyūnas tena gamyate
children.translated_text: if there is no different word, is understood by that very absence as not lacking

children.text: sa tasmin vācake śabde nimittāt smṛtim ādadhat
children.translated_text: That person, in the word which is the denoter of that (meaning), establishing recollection on the basis of a cause,
apprehends the meaning by the word, as if directly, though separated

children.text: padavācyo yathā nārthaḥ kaś cid gaurakharādiṣu
children.translated_text: Just as a meaning to be denoted by a word is, in some cases like ‘cow-donkey’ and the rest,

children.text: saty api pratyaye+atyantaṃ samudāye na gamyate
children.translated_text: not at all grasped in the aggregate despite the affix being present
When the essence of meaning is apprehended as if conjoined with word-meanings,
then the seeing of the individual word-meanings there is in just that way unhelpful
And when, in the functions of aggregate and constituents, their meanings are different,
simultaneous difference and conjunction, being incompatible, come along as attachments
And who would posit adhyāhāra and the like as having only the purpose of instrumentality,
and how could a meaning of an un-employed word exist in a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound?
Nor is there determination of meaning by constituents like ‘prajñu’, ‘saṃjñvā’, and the rest,
therefore, one and the same aggregate alone is the basis of a specified meaning

children.text: gargā ity eka evāyaṃ bahuṣv artheṣu vartate
children.translated_text: ‘Gargā’—this one single (word) operates in many meanings,
and a complex having the designation ‘dvandva’ is a denoter of many (things)
As in the case of the ‘one remainder’, bhujya and the like stand each individually,
so also, in the meaning denoted by a dvandva, the action is distributed severally
And as for the expecting of the sense of a dvandva-word by the pronoun ‘tad’,
that too, with the form of the (members) being excluded, is of the same form as a pronoun

children.text: yathā ca khadiracchede bhāgeṣu kramavāṃś chidiḥ
children.translated_text: And just as, in the cutting of khadira-wood, the act of cutting is sequential in the parts,
so too, in the parts of the sense of a dvandva-word, there is the observation of sequence
As, with respect to a part of an aggregate, they consider the special actions to follow the aggregate,
so that sequence applies to a member of a dvandva
For one expounding a function that presupposes the sentence, to those unlearned,
the primacy, by reason of the difference of the word-meanings within the function, has been pointed out
Because of the non-difference of the denotatum, in a <s>nañ</s>-compound the primacy is varied,

children.text: prādhānyaṃ bahudhā bhāṣye doṣās tu prakriyāgatāḥ
children.translated_text: and in many ways in the commentary; but the defects belong to the procedure
And, in the alternative of ‘abandoning one’s own meaning’ (<s>jahatsvārtha-vikalpa</s>), for one who wishes the relinquishment of all meanings,
the total abandonment of the meaning of a <s>bahuvrīhi</s>-word has been shown
In the tradition, in some cases the meaning of the base (<s>prakṛti</s>) is expressed by the affix (<s>pratyaya</s>),
and when the base has been set aside, the meaning of the affix too is expressed by roots (<s>dhātu</s>)

children.text: yam artham āhatur bhinnau pratyayāv eka eva ta
children.translated_text: The very meaning which two different affixes convey—one single (meaning) indeed, that (is conveyed),

children.text: kva cid āha pacantīti dhātus tābhyāṃ vinā kva cit
children.translated_text: and in some cases the root says ‘they cook’, while in other cases it does so without those two
And those meanings of affixes which are dependent on recollection from explanatory restatement (<s>anvākhyāna-smṛti</s>)—
those have been designated as meanings of the base, being cited by a different recollection
Because of established usage, precisely in accordance with what is in use, it is expressed in the tradition;
for they consider the exposition of the purport of the tradition to be for practical usage
In the traditions, through differences of procedure (<s>prakriyā</s>), only ignorance is being described,
but an option not grounded in scripture ceases of itself by knowledge
Just as a result, not bound to the causes and incapable of a narrative account,
so too knowledge is inexpressible, yet is indicated as a means of instruction

children.text: yathābhyāsaṃ hi vāg arthe pratipattiṃ samīhate
children.translated_text: For speech, according to habituation, strives for apprehension with respect to an object,
and, beginningless like a nature, a false habituation stands established
The unlearned imagines a composite thing in the atom (<s>paramāṇu</s>),
and likewise again imagines the composite as constituted by other parts
From the perception of pot and the like the common world, being delimited, arrives at a conclusion,

children.text: samārambhāc ca bhāvānām ādimad brahma śāśvatam
children.translated_text: and from the initiation of entities, (arrives at) the eternal <s>Brahma</s> possessed of a beginning
The expedients for those learning—children—are persuasive devices,

children.text: asatye vartmani sthitvā tataḥ satyaṃ samīhate
children.translated_text: standing on a false path and thence aiming at the true
Otherwise, having first grasped the words, one apprehends the meaning in one way,

children.text: punar vākye tam evārtham anyathā pratipadyate
children.translated_text: and again, in the sentence, one apprehends that very meaning in a different way

children.text: upāttā bahavo+apy arthā yeṣv ante pratiṣedhanam
children.translated_text: Even when many meanings are introduced, in those cases where, at the end, a negation is made,

children.text: kriyate te nivartante tasmāt tāṃs tatra nāśrayet
children.translated_text: they are turned back; therefore one should not rely on them there
And the sentence ‘the tree is not’ has the mark of qualified absence (<s>viśiṣṭābhāva</s>),

children.text: nārthe na buddhau saṃbandho nivṛtter avatiṣṭhate
children.translated_text: the relation does not stand either in the object or in the cognition, because it has been negated
And if, in the apprehension of a cutting-off, ‘it exists’ is ascertained,

children.text: aśabdavācyā sā buddhir nivartyeta sthitā katham
children.translated_text: that cognition would be unexpressible by word; how would it remain once negated?

children.text: atha yaj jñānam utpannaṃ tan mithyeti nañā kṛtam
children.translated_text: Or, if the cognition that has arisen is made false by the negative particle <s>nañ</s>,
then, in this difference of the operation of <s>nañ</s>, how would there be cognition of absence?
And if the operation of <s>nañ</s> proceeds without a basis, there would be a prior operation (of it);

children.text: athādhāraḥ sa evāsya niyamārthā śrutir bhavet
children.translated_text: but if that very (negated entity) is its basis, the scripture would be for the purpose of restriction
Or, it might be a reiteration for the purpose of indicating restriction; as it may be,

children.text: kaś cid evārthavāṃs tatra śabdaḥ śeṣās tv anarthakāḥ
children.translated_text: there, only some one word is meaningful, while the rest are meaningless
And a contradictory connection is produced by things like examples and the like cited out of place,
one apprehends the sentence-meaning differently when the sentence is completed
And in sentences where praise and blame predominate, the meaning is not such as is
imagined by dividing up the words
But if indeed the meaning, not yet combined, is present in the words,
that is a means for the sentence-meaning, in conveying a single (meaning)

children.text: pūrvaṃ padeṣv asaṃsṛṣṭo yaḥ kramād upacīyate
children.translated_text: What was previously uncombined in the words and is gradually accumulated,
because of being like a broken-then-tied garland, they know that as more specifically qualified

children.text: ekam āhur anekārthaṃ śabdam anye parīkṣakāḥ
children.translated_text: Some examiners say one word has many meanings,
and the universality of one word is differentiated by difference of occasioning factors
Transcending simultaneity, it settles in alternation,
by meaning or by context, or by syntactic connection (<s>yoga</s>), or by another word
Just as a mass having dewlap and the rest is denoted by the word ‘cow’,

children.text: tathā sa eva gośabdo vāhīke+api vyavasthitaḥ
children.translated_text: so that very word ‘cow’ is fixed also in the case of a <s>Vāhīka</s>
And for that very word, possessing all powers and many properties,
because of difference of established usage there arises <s>gauṇa</s>-ness (secondary usage) and primariness
One mantra, in just this way, (applies) to the self, to the deity, and to the rite,
without confusion, the one word bearing all meanings, its powers being distinct

children.text: gotvānuṣaṅgo vāhīke nimittāt kaiś cid iṣyate
children.translated_text: Some accept, in the case of a <s>Vāhīka</s>, the accompaniment of cow-ness due to an occasioning factor,
the mere sense being transposed, while the word is fixed in its own meaning
Likewise, the very form (own-form) of words is connected to all meanings,

children.text: arthamātraṃ viparyastaṃ svarūpe tu śrutiḥ sthitā
children.translated_text: the mere sense being transposed, while the scripture (heard form) is fixed in the form
And they who observe the paths of difference say that the oneness of the secondary and primary words,
because of similarity of form, exists despite absolute difference
And similarly, the alternative in the <s>Sāmidhenī</s> is connected in repetition,

children.text: mantrāś ca viniyogena labhante bhedam ūhavat
children.translated_text: and mantras, by application, obtain distinction along with optional modification

children.text: tāny āmnāyāntarāṇy eva paṭhyate kiṃ cid eva tu
children.translated_text: Only some among those are indeed recited as alternative traditions,

children.text: anarthakānāṃ pāṭho vā śeṣas tv anyaḥ pratīyate
children.translated_text: or there is the recitation of what is pointless, while the remainder is understood as other
The own-form of the word is taught by others in the recitation, but the meaning,
though there is absolute difference among all, belongs, by their connection, to those that have it
One <s>Sāvitrī</s> (Gayatri-verse) of refinement is employed in the rite, another in other rites,

children.text: anyā japaprabandheṣu sā tv ekaiva pratīyate
children.translated_text: another in sequences of muttered recitation (<s>japa</s>); yet that very one is apprehended as one
For one who desires the functioning of words in the self-form of meaning, from their own form,
the functioning of the sentence-form with respect to the sentence-meaning is independent of anything else
For those by whom the many-meaningedness of a single word is recognized,
their projection of primary and secondary (<s>gauṇa</s>) depends on success and failure
That which, being dependent on meaning and context, or together with other words,

children.text: yuktaḥ pratyāyayaty arthaṃ taṃ gauṇam apare viduḥ
children.translated_text: is appropriately connected and makes known the meaning, some others know that as secondary (<s>gauṇa</s>)
That whose own meaning is well-known as grasped upon mere pure utterance,
is to be understood as primary, resting solely on the form

children.text: yas tv anyasya prayogeṇa yatnād iva niyujyate
children.translated_text: But that which, through the use of something else, as if by effort, is made to be applied,
they consider that unestablished, being fixed on a secondary meaning
Even when operating in its own meaning, that upon which a word relies for meaning,

children.text: nimittaṃ tatra mukhyaṃ syān nimitti gauṇa iṣyate
children.translated_text: that occasioning factor is primary there, while the occasioned is considered secondary

children.text: purārād iti bhinne+arthe yau vartete virodhini
children.translated_text: In the opposed senses of ‘formerly’ and ‘near’ (<s>purā</s> and <s>ārāt</s>), which are mutually contrary,
their determination too depends on meaning and context
When the extraction of word-meanings from the sentence-meaning is posited,
with what other word would a connection, for any one (word), be reasonable?

children.text: yac cāpy ekaṃ padaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ caritāstikriyaṃ kva cit
children.translated_text: And that single word which is observed somewhere to have completed an action,

children.text: tad vākyāntaram evāhur na tad anyena yujyate
children.translated_text: they say that is itself another sentence; it is not to be joined with another

children.text: yac ca ko+ayam iti praśne gaur aśva iti cocyate
children.translated_text: And when, in the question ‘Who is this?’ one says ‘a cow’, ‘a horse’,

children.text: praśna eva kriyā tatra prakrāntā darśanādikā
children.translated_text: there, the very question is the action that has commenced, on account of the seeing and so on
Neither an excess of properties nor a deficiency serves as the instigator,

children.text: ādhikyam api manyante prasiddher nyūnatāṃ kva cit
children.translated_text: yet, due to familiarity, they sometimes suppose excess and sometimes deficiency
Where a genus is employed even without the genus-word,

children.text: saṃbandhisadṛśād dharmāt taṃ gauṇam apare viduḥ
children.translated_text: because of a property similar to and connected with (that genus), some others know that as secondary
And where, as if by inversion of the meaning, they seem to take it as if a different meaning,

children.text: manyante sa gavādis tu gauṇa ity ucyate kva cit
children.translated_text: there, the use beginning with ‘cow’ is sometimes said to be secondary
Fixed as instruments, endowed with form-power,
as are known in actions the plow, the sickle, the pestle, and the like

children.text: kriyāntare na caiteṣāṃ vibhavanti na śaktayaḥ
children.translated_text: And these do not flourish with respect to another action, nor do their powers,

children.text: rūpād eva tu tādarthyaṃ niyamena pratīyate
children.translated_text: but their suitability for that (particular action) is understood invariably from form alone
Just so, by form and power, having arisen and being established,
a word has fixed suitability for that (meaning), though its power is employed elsewhere
Where its capacity is ascertained from mere hearing,

children.text: taṃ mukhyam arthaṃ manyante gauṇaṃ yatnopapāditam
children.translated_text: they consider that meaning primary, while that which is produced by effort is secondary
In the affixal sense of <s>-cvi</s> with words like ‘<s>go</s>’, ‘<s>yuṣmat</s>’, ‘great’ (<s>mahat</s>), when, from one’s own meaning, they stand in another meaning,
the state of being that other meaning is seen there even of what is primary
Greatness and whiteness the base form apprehends,
yet, when that is regarded as distinct, it serves to establish secondariness
Words like ‘<s>Agni</s>’, ‘<s>Soma</s>’, whose word-forms are their very referents,
when used by proper names (<s>saṃjñā</s>), in those unfamiliar cases there is secondariness

children.text: agnidattas tu yo+agniḥ syāt tatra svārthopasarjanaḥ
children.translated_text: But where ‘<s>Agni</s>’ is ‘given by <s>Agni</s>’ (<s>Agnidatta</s>), there the word ‘Agni’,
being subordinated to its own meaning and functioning in the meaning of ‘given’, is understood as secondary
Due to difference of occasioning factors, in the already-begun operation of word-derivation,
in forms like ‘<s>Hariścandra</s>’ there is an established presence and absence of the augment <s>suṭ</s>
A word which has obtained an internal refinement, as in ‘<s>ṛṣi</s>’ and the like, when joined with another,
there, the internal refinement does not get removed with respect to the external meaning
Even when the meaning is entirely opposed, as the meaning is determined,
the word is employed as primary, according to the current ascertainment
Even though the determination of the reality of meaning depends on cognition,

children.text: na sarvaḥ pratyayas tasmin prasiddha iva jāyate
children.translated_text: not every cognition in that matter arises as if established
The seeing of water in a mirage is comparable to the seeing of water in water,

children.text: bhedāt tu sparśanādīnāṃ na jalaṃ mṛgatṛṣṇikā
children.translated_text: but because of difference in touch and so on, the mirage is not water
By that distinctive effect which is well-known in the case of rope and snake,
there is discrimination of difference between the two, though the seeing is similar
And whatever is seen as the cause of the inversion of a well-known meaning,

children.text: yas tasmāl lakṣyate bhedas tam asatyaṃ pracakṣate
children.translated_text: the difference that is inferred from that, they declare that false

children.text: yac ca nimnonnataṃ citre sarūpaṃ parvatādibhiḥ
children.translated_text: And that which, in a picture, is the low and the high, similar in form to mountains and the like,

children.text: na tatra pratighātādi kāryaṃ tadvat pravartate
children.translated_text: there, obstruction and the like are not operative; in just that way, activity proceeds
Just as the continuous sequence of touch with the hand is unbroken in the case of a wheel,

children.text: na tathālātacakrasya vicchinnaṃ spṛśyate hi tat
children.translated_text: not so with a firebrand-circle; for that is touched as interrupted
And just as, by embankments and rampart-like coverings, touch is blocked,

children.text: nagareṣu na te tadvad gandharvanagareṣv api
children.translated_text: so in cities; but in cities of <s>Gandharva</s> (illusory cities) it is not so
Whatever extent of result is accomplished by real deer, cattle, and the like,

children.text: tāvān na mṛnmayeṣv asti tasmāt te viṣayaḥ kanaḥ
children.translated_text: that extent does not exist in clay-made ones; therefore their domain is but a particle
A great region is covered by well-known mountains and the like,
but a reflection is seen as existing in a small intervening space
And just as griefs due to causes like death are real,

children.text: na te svapnādiṣu svasya tadvad arthasya sādhakāḥ
children.translated_text: those do not, in dreams and the like, effect their own (real) object; similarly, they do not accomplish the object
What, due to differences of place, time, and the senses, is seen otherwise,

children.text: yathā prasiddhir lokasya tathā tad avasīyate
children.translated_text: is ascertained according to the world’s established practice

children.text: yac copaghātajaṃ jñānaṃ yac ca jñānam alaukikam
children.translated_text: And cognition that is due to impairment, and cognition that is non-ordinary,
with those two there is no transaction, for words are founded on worldly usage
Just as, in regard to pots and the like, a lamp, being employed for one object,
makes manifest something else also because of proximity
So too, in connected objects, a word which is employed for one,

children.text: tasmāt prayojakād anyān api pratyāyayaty asau
children.translated_text: from that prompting object makes others also known
Just as kindling by aranis, prepared for the sake of fire,
produces smoke as well, unintended, though there is a single instrument

children.text: tathā śabdo+api kasmiṃś cit pratyāyye+arthe vivakṣite
children.translated_text: So too, when a word, with some particular denotatum intended,
manifests an un-intended object as well because of proximity
Just as, when something is absolutely conjoined, it cannot be abandoned,

children.text: tathā śabdo+api saṃbandhī pravivektuṃ na śakyate
children.translated_text: so too a word, being related, cannot be precisely distinguished (from its associates)
Even when there is the presence of objects and their manifestation,
the prompting object of the word is grasped, though the form is the same
In some cases, the subordination or predominance of qualities and substrates is not intended,

children.text: kva cit sāṃnidhyam apy eṣāṃ pratipattāv akāraṇam
children.translated_text: in some cases even their proximity is not a cause in comprehension

children.text: yac cānupāttaṃ śabdena tat kasmiṃś cit pratīyate
children.translated_text: And that which, though not taken up by the word, is grasped in some context,

children.text: kva cit pradhānam evārtho bhavaty anyasya lakṣaṇa
children.translated_text: in some cases the principal meaning is the substrate, while the other is an indicator

children.text: ākhyātaṃ taddhitārthasya yat kiṃ cid upadarśakam
children.translated_text: Whatever finite verb serves to indicate something of the sense of a taddhita-affix,
there an inversion of the relation of quality and principal is observed
In specification, the proximity of gender and number is not the cause,
the measure even when not expressed is understood as a means of proof in the cases of half and short

children.text: hrasvasyārdhaṃ ca yad dṛṣṭaṃ tat tasyāsaṃnidhāv api
children.translated_text: And what is observed as the half of the short, even in its absence,
is expressed just so, because it serves as the characteristic of the short

children.text: dīrghaplutābhyāṃ tasya syān mātrayā vā viśeṣaṇam
children.translated_text: By long and protracted lengths, or by mora, there can be its qualification,

children.text: jāter vā lakṣaṇāya syāt sarvathā saptaparṇavat
children.translated_text: or it may be for the characterization of the genus; in every way, as with the seven-leaved (plant, i.e., as an example-name)

children.text: gantavyaṃ dṛśyatāṃ sūrya iti kālasya lakṣaṇe
children.translated_text: ‘Let it be gone’, ‘Let the sun be seen’—in the characterization of time,

children.text: jñāyatāṃ kāla ity etat sopāyam abhidhīyate
children.translated_text: ‘Let time be known’: this is stated along with a means (of recognition)
In ‘He pierces without a bow’, there is shown in particular

children.text: sāmānyam āśrayaḥ śakter yaḥ kaś cit pratipādakaḥ
children.translated_text: some indicator which presents the general as the locus of a power

children.text: kākebhyo rakṣyatāṃ sarpir iti bālo+api coditaḥ
children.translated_text: A child too, when instructed ‘Let the ghee be protected from the crows’,

children.text: upaghātapare vākye na śvādibhyo na rakṣati
children.translated_text: in a sentence aimed at warding off harm, does not protect it from dogs and the like
In washing of bowls, and likewise the cleaning of their place,
though unspoken in form, is understood because of belonging to the same undertaking
From sentence, from context, from purpose, from propriety, from place and time,

children.text: śabdārthāḥ pravibhajyante na rūpād eva kevalāt
children.translated_text: word-meanings are distinguished, not from form alone
Association and disjunction, co-occurrence and opposition,
purpose, context, indicator, the presence of another word,

children.text: sāmarthyam aucitī deśaḥ kālo vyaktiḥ svarādayaḥ
children.translated_text: capacity, propriety, place, time, particularity, accent and the like,
are causes of recollecting distinctions when word-meaning is not delimited
Even on the view of difference, because of resemblance, words of different meanings, for comprehenders,
attain fixed manifestation by means of context and the like
Words that are similar in form to nouns and verbs, but are grounded in a different operation,

children.text: śabdā vākyasya teṣv artho na rūpād adhigamyate
children.translated_text: the sentence-meaning in them is not grasped from form
That which is for the sake of undertaking and cessation, praise and blame-contrivance,
the skilled interpreter attempts that, though it is not literally true
The action being enjoined, with seen and unseen purposes,

children.text: stūyate sā stutis tasya kartur eva prayojikā
children.translated_text: that praise is the praise, which serves as the motive for the very agent of that
Just as, by the designation ‘tiger’ and the like, a child is turned back
so too, though it be untrue, some ‘negative consequence’ (<s>pratyavāya</s>) is declared
Even without having established an injunction in the case of such a ‘negative consequence’ (<s>pratyavāya</s>),

children.text: śāstreṇa pratiṣiddhe+arthe vidvān kaś cit pravartate
children.translated_text: some learned person proceeds toward an object prohibited by scripture
Even with an injunction among snakes, by means of proven spells, herbs, and the like,

children.text: nānyathā pratipattavyaṃ na dato gamayed iti
children.translated_text: one should not understand otherwise: ‘Do not let (it) bite; do not let (him) go’—thus
In some places, a true account of reality is made within praise and blame,

children.text: tatrāpi ca pravṛttiś ca nivṛttiś copadiśyate
children.translated_text: and there too both undertaking and cessation are instructed
The form of all word-meanings is the basis for sentence-meaning,

children.text: sāpekṣā ye tu vākyārthāḥ padārthair eva te samāḥ
children.translated_text: but those sentence-meanings which are dependent are the same as the word-meanings themselves

children.text: vākyaṃ tad api manyante yat padaṃ caritakriyam
children.translated_text: They even consider that to be a sentence, which is a word endowed with an accomplished action,
since a duality is observed for sentence and the rest even without an action-word
Where, in the verb-word, a fixed instrument is understood,

children.text: tad apy ekaṃ samāptārthaṃ vākyam ity abhidhīya
children.translated_text: that too, being single and having a completed sense, is said to be a sentence
A cognition separated by words, which relies on an unuttered word,
is called an inference; it is a cause for the ascertainment of that word’s meaning

children.text: apare tu padasyaiva tam arthaṃ pratijānate
children.translated_text: But others maintain that even of the single word itself that meaning is determined,
established without connection to another word

children.text: yasminn uccarite śabde yadā yo+arthaḥ pratīyate
children.translated_text: Whatever meaning, when a word is uttered, is apprehended at that time,

children.text: tam āhur arthaṃ tasyaiva nānyad arthasya lakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: that they call its meaning; there is no other definition of meaning
Thus, in words that are for the sake of an action-meaning, the action of the bases is understood;
and in constructions without initial markers, the sense of ‘gone’ and the like is apprehended

children.text: tāni śabdāntarāṇy eva paryāyā iva laukikāḥ
children.translated_text: Those are merely other words, like worldly synonyms,
yet by meaning and context their own sense is constrained

children.text: pratibodhābhyupāyās tu ye taṃ taṃ puruṣaṃ prati
children.translated_text: But the means of bringing about understanding, with respect to each particular person,
are not necessarily words connected with the knowable thing

children.text: asatyāṃ pratipattau vā mithyā vā pratipādane
children.translated_text: Even when there is no apprehension, or when there is a false presentation,

children.text: svair arthair nityasaṃbandhās te te śabdā vyavasthitāḥ
children.translated_text: those several words are fixed in constant connection with their own meanings

children.text: yathāprakaraṇaṃ dvāram ity asyāṃ karmaṇaḥ śrutau
children.translated_text: According to the context, in the hearing of ‘door’ as the object of an action,

children.text: badhāna dehi vety etad upāyād avagamyate
children.translated_text: ‘Bind! Give!’—this is grasped by means (of instruction)
There, a word that functions as an instrument and depends upon existence,
does not denote the principal thing-to-be-effected
It merely reveals its own meaning and, being dependent, withdraws,

children.text: arthas tu tasya saṃbandhī prakalpayati saṃnidhim
children.translated_text: while its correlated meaning supplies the proximity (i.e., the connection)
Because the for-the-sake-of-another is indeterminate, there is no proximity of word from word,

children.text: nārthāc chabdasya sāṃnidhyaṃ na śabdād arthasaṃnidhiḥ
children.translated_text: nor proximity of word from meaning, nor proximity of meaning from word
The verb, as if having lost its (own) form, being (merely) implicated by a word denoting the object,
would attain primacy if there were simultaneous existence of state and being
But those (opponents) describe for this verb a noun-like form,
and partition usage by agreement and difference (anvaya-vyatireka)

children.text: na cāpi rūpāt saṃdehe vācakatvaṃ nivartate
children.translated_text: Nor, when there is doubt from form, is denotative capacity annulled,

children.text: ardhaṃ paśor iti yathā sāmarthyāt tad dhi kalpate
children.translated_text: as, ‘half of the beast’—by capacity (sāmarthya), that is established
If every ‘being-word’ is pure, being grounded in production (<s>bhāvanā</s>),

children.text: saṃsarge ca vibhakto+asya tasyārtho na pṛthag yadi
children.translated_text: and in combination it is inflected, if its meaning is not distinct (therefrom)
then the verb is action-primary, and nouns are being-primary:
all this contradicts the fourfold classification of words

children.text: vākyasya buddhau nityatvam arthayogaṃ ca laukikam
children.translated_text: Seeing the sentence’s eternality in cognition, and the worldly conjunction with meaning,
<s>Audumbarāyaṇa</s> says: the fourfold (division) does not exist

children.text: vyāptimāṃś ca laghuś caiva vyavahāraḥ padāśrayaḥ
children.translated_text: Usage, which is pervading and also light (economical), is grounded in words,

children.text: loke śāstre ca kāryārthaṃ vibhāgenaiva kalpitaḥ
children.translated_text: and in the world and in the śāstra, for the sake of action, it is posited precisely by division
For the comprehenders in the world, there are no established practices arising from conjunction with meaning,

children.text: tasmād alaukiko vākyād anyaḥ kaś cin na vidyate
children.translated_text: therefore there is no other sentence, apart from the worldly one

children.text: anyatra śrūyamāṇaiś ca liṅgair vākyaiś ca sūcitāḥ
children.translated_text: Being indicated by marks heard elsewhere and by sentences,
their own senses are apprehended, unnoticed because of identity of form

children.text: utsargavākye yat tyaktam aśabdam iva śabdavat
children.translated_text: What is omitted in a general rule-sentence, being wordless as it were yet like a word,

children.text: tad bādhakeṣu vākyeṣu śrutam anyatra gamyate
children.translated_text: when heard in sentences that override (it), is understood elsewhere

children.text: brāhmaṇānāṃ śrutir dadhni prakrāntā māṭharād vinā
children.translated_text: Among the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s, the usage with ‘curds’ is established, except for the <s>Māṭhara</s>,
and the <s>Māṭhara</s>, because of the connection with ‘buttermilk’, there declares the correctness-as-it-is
Even in the connection of many verbs, in rule and exception,

children.text: ekam eveṣyate kaiś cid bhinnarūpam iva sthitam
children.translated_text: some hold it to be one sentence only, though it stands as if of different form

children.text: niyamaḥ pratiṣedhaś ca vidhiśeṣas tathā sati
children.translated_text: When that is so, restriction and prohibition, and the remainder of an injunction,

children.text: dvitīye yo lug ākhyātas taccheṣam alukaṃ viduḥ
children.translated_text: the elision (lug) that is in the second verb—they know that remainder as non-elided
Being without expectation (of anything further) and completed, they are primary with respect to one another,
how, since they do not render service to one another, could there be sentence-unity?
Because, through a specifying injunction, there is a need for a sentence-remainder, it is inferred,
therefore, as with what is to be enjoined, so too in the case of what is to be terminated, the mutual regard (vyapekṣā) is the same

children.text: saṃjñāśabdaikadeśo yas tasya lopo na vidyate
children.translated_text: Where there is a single part of a technical term (<s>saṃjñā</s>), there is no elision of that,

children.text: viśiṣṭarūpā sā saṃjñā kṛtā ca na nivartate
children.translated_text: for that <s>saṃjñā</s>, having a qualified form, once established, does not cease

children.text: saṃjñāntarāc ca dattāder nānyā saṃjñā pratīyate
children.translated_text: Nor, from another <s>saṃjñā</s>, is a further <s>saṃjñā</s> like “datta-” apprehended,
how would the word “datta-” express one bearing the <s>saṃjñā</s> named <s>Devadatta</s>?
Some think that, like a composite whole, there is an equal relation with all parts,
for the forms of words, by all the <s>saṃjñā</s>-givers

children.text: varṇānām arthavattvaṃ tu saṃjñānāṃ saṃjñibhir bhavet
children.translated_text: But the letters would have significatory capacity by the <s>saṃjñā</s>-bearers (saṃjñins),
a connected part does not hold good where <s>saṃjñā</s> and <s>saṃjñin</s> are distinguished
If, for a <s>saṃjñin</s>, there is simultaneous connection with all forms,
then there is no possibility of making that known from parts sharing (only) a portion of the form

children.text: ekadeśāt tu saṃghāte keṣāṃ cij jāyate smṛtiḥ
children.translated_text: Yet from a single part, in a complex, memory arises for some,

children.text: smṛtes tu viṣayāc chabdāt saṃghātārthaḥ pratīyate
children.translated_text: and from the remembered item, which is the word, the meaning of the complex is apprehended

children.text: ekadeśāt smṛtir bhinne saṃghāte niyatā katham
children.translated_text: How could memory, arising from a single part, be determinate in a distinct complex,
and how, when it is apprehended, would the word be the designator of the meaning?

children.text: ekadeśasarūpās tu tais tair bhedaiḥ samanvitāḥ
children.translated_text: Words, which are partial-form-similar and associated with various differences,
not fully realized (anuniṣpādin), are held to be established within <s>saṃjñā</s>s
Because they are common, they are doubtful; by capacity (sāmarthya) they have a determinate locus,

children.text: teṣāṃ ye sādhavas teṣu śāstre lopādi śiṣyate
children.translated_text: among those, whatever are valid, for them in the śāstra elision and the like are taught
When there is equal non-completion, “jye-, drā-, ghā-” are invalid,

children.text: na hy anvākhyāyake śāstre teṣu dattādivat smṛtiḥ
children.translated_text: for in the śāstra of explanatory recital (<s>anvākhyāyika</s>) there is no memory of them like “datta-” and the like

children.text: kṛtaṇatvāś ca ye śabdā nityāḥ kharaṇasādayaḥ
children.translated_text: And the words which are made as “kṛtaṇa-” and the like are eternal, like “kharaṇa-” and so on,
because they are taught for a single substance, they call those valid

children.text: gotrāṇy eva tu tāny āhuḥ saṃjñāśaktisamanvayāt
children.translated_text: But they say those are only lineages (<s>gotra</s>s), because of association with <s>saṃjñā</s>-power,
in those, dependence on a mark (nimitta) is not necessarily admitted for the own-meaning

children.text: vyavahārāya niyamaḥ saṃjñānāṃ saṃjñini kva cit
children.translated_text: For practical usage there is a restriction of <s>saṃjñā</s>s to the <s>saṃjñin</s> in some cases,

children.text: nitya eva tu saṃbandho ḍitthādiṣu gavādivat
children.translated_text: but the connection is eternal, in “ḍittha-” and the like, as with “go-” and the rest
Because of being constructed, the non-eternality of the connection is reasonable,

children.text: saṃjñāyāṃ sā hi puruṣair yathākāmaṃ niyujyate
children.translated_text: for in the <s>saṃjñā</s> that (connection) is applied by persons as they wish
Just as children make <s>saṃjñā</s>s like “sweet” upon sand-drawings,

children.text: saṃjñāḥ kriyante sarvāsu saṃjñāsv eṣaiva kalpanā
children.translated_text: so exactly is this convention of <s>saṃjñā</s>s everywhere
And in this śāstra concerning <s>vṛddhi</s> and the rest, the characterization is by delimitation of power (śakti),
for the connection is uncontrived, like that of qualifier and qualified

children.text: saṃjñā svarūpam āśritya nimitte sati laukikī
children.translated_text: In the worldly domain, a <s>saṃjñā</s>, relying on its own form, in some cases proceeds when there is a mark present,

children.text: kā cit pravartate kā cin nimittāsaṃnidhāv api
children.translated_text: and in some cases even in the absence of the mark’s presence
Also in the śāstra there is a great <s>saṃjñā</s> bound up with its own form,
the inference of the mark is apprehended when the mark is present

children.text: āvṛtter anumānaṃ vā sārūpyāt tatra gamyate
children.translated_text: There, by recurrence there is inference, or from similarity it is inferred,
or there is inference from word-difference, or a grasp of power-difference
In some places, because of difference of object, the artificial (arrangement) is fixed,
regarding number, the one object of determination belongs to both

children.text: viṣayaṃ kṛtrimasyāpi laukikaḥ kva cid uccaran
children.translated_text: Even the worldly, uttering in some cases, extends the object of the artificial (usage) from afar into comprehension,

children.text: vyāpnoti dūrāt saṃbuddhau tathā hi grahaṇaṃ dvayoḥ
children.translated_text: for thus there is apprehension for both
In dvandva compounds where a single member remains, some assert, with capacity as the criterion,
that the abiding of actions is with respect to each (member) as its own support
Eating is completed, in each individual, by the twofold form of result,

children.text: anyathā hi vyavasthāne na tadarthaḥ prakalpate
children.translated_text: for otherwise, if the determination were different, that purpose would not be accomplished
And all apprehend, individually, the act of eating, which has the form of taking food and the like and has satisfaction as its result,

children.text: pratyekaṃ pratipadyante na tu nāṭyakriyām iva
children.translated_text: but not, as it were, a theatrical action
Like water for the feet, that stands by division through capacity,

children.text: bhujiḥ karoti bhujyarthaṃ na tantreṇa pradīpavat
children.translated_text: the “eating-act” performs for the sake of what is to be eaten, not, like a lamp, by means of a device (tantra)
But a single action like “seeing” and the like, with suchlike object-functions,
even without repetition, may have as its support the aggregate
When, in observation of practices and the like, the agents have distinct forms of operation,
their distinct seeing, having come together, accomplishes the intended result
Because the target is established in the world, and because, in the śāstra, the mark is shown,
the <s>vṛddhi</s>-designation is completed distinctly in those who seek, in taking and the like
Because the taking of a hundred is primary in “punishment consisting of a hundred acts,”
even when there is a difference of qualities among the agents, the countable objective is not differentiated
Because the injunction pertains precisely to the aggregate (<s>saṅgha</s>), as in the case of an action, in the establishing (of meaning)
there, by a device (<s>tantra</s>) there is a connection between the compounded and the practiced <s>saṃjñā</s>s,

children.text: lakṣaṇārthā śrutir yeṣāṃ kāṃ cid eva kriyāṃ prati
children.translated_text: For those whose Vedic text (<s>śruti</s>) is intended for indication (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>) with regard to only some particular action,

children.text: tair vyastaiś ca samastaiś ca sa dharma upalakṣyate
children.translated_text: by them, whether taken separately or taken together, that <s>dharma</s> is indicated

children.text: vṛṣalair na praveṣṭavyam ity etasmin gṛhe yathā
children.translated_text: Just as, with respect to the rule “low-borns (<s>vṛṣala</s>) must not enter” concerning this house,
both the entry of each individual and the entry of them as an aggregate is prohibited,
but when there is a prohibition-teaching regarding joint pursuit of gain and the like,
since there is no prohibition separately, activity (individually) is not opposed
Because <s>ṇatva</s> (retroflexion) is for the sake of characterization of usage, so too with <s>aṭ</s>, <s>kup</s>, <s>vāṅ</s> and the rest,

children.text: pratyekaṃ vā samastair vā ṇatvaṃ na pratiṣidhyate
children.translated_text: neither for each separately nor for them together is <s>ṇatva</s> prohibited
When the root “bhuj-” (to enjoy/eat) is undertaken for the sake of favoring the eaters,
it does not favor them if there is no oneness of place, time, and the like
For that which, despite differences of recipients’ vessels and the like, is taught as non-plural for a single one,
or conversely, for that which is different, its unity is posited
And even when they act in a collected group, being specified as distinct,

children.text: svaṃ svaṃ bhojyaṃ vibhāgena prāptaṃ saṃbhūya bhuñjate
children.translated_text: each eats his own apportioned food, having obtained it by division
Because there is no scope for <s>vīpsā</s> (distributive iteration), because of conflict with a different number,
and because a double completion is not possible, the “hundred” stands with respect to the aggregate
Where “bhuj-” remains along with others by dvandva and <s>ekaśeṣa</s> (one-member remainder),
there too, because the point is characterization (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>-arthatva), the sentence is completed in two ways

children.text: vākyāntarāṇāṃ pratyekaṃ samāptiḥ kaiś cid iṣyate
children.translated_text: Some hold that each sentence among the other sentences has its own completion,
thus there is a collective grasping of sentences connected by a different form
Or, the sentences that express differences are not the denotata of the sentence as such,
but when that one is uttered, it apprehends differences and other (things) in that way
For those whose entire sentence-meaning is completed per distinction,

children.text: teṣāṃ tadānīṃ bhinnasya kiṃ padārthasya sattayā
children.translated_text: then, what is the status of a distinct word-meaning (as independently existing)?

children.text: atha tair eva janitaḥ so+artho bhinneṣu vartate
children.translated_text: Or else, if that meaning is produced precisely by those (words), and persists among distinct (instances),

children.text: pūrvasyārthasya tena syād virodhaḥ saha vā sthitiḥ
children.translated_text: then, with the prior meaning, there would be either conflict or coexistence
If there is coexistence, there would be mutual opposition between qualified and unqualified,
and if there is abandonment (of one), the relation would become inconstant, while the meaning would be forfeited
One common denotandum, fixed with respect to each word,
is the meaning-principle in the aggregate and in the members, designating by proximity

children.text: yathā sādhāraṇe svatvaṃ tyāgasya ca phalaṃ dhane
children.translated_text: Just as, for what is common, ownership and the fruit of relinquishment pertain to wealth,
and the satisfaction is undivided, so too is the relation to the meaning for those who have that (commonality)
When there is meaningfulness of letters with that very meaning in that which possesses it,
there is not unity in the aggregate that persists by difference
With a single lamp, all perceive the common wealth,
just so, with a single <s>sup</s> (nominal ending), the number is denoted

children.text: nārthavattā pade varṇe vākye caivaṃ viśiṣyate
children.translated_text: Meaningfulness is not, in this way, differentiated among word, letter, and sentence,

children.text: abhyāsāt prakramo+anyas tu viruddha iva dṛśyate
children.translated_text: but because of habitual practice, a different precedence appears as if opposed

children.text: viniyogād ṛte śabdo na svārthasya prakāśakaḥ
children.translated_text: Apart from assignment (<s>viniyoga</s>), a word is not a revealer of its own meaning,
they explain the relation of expression and expressed as proceeding through the channel of utterance
Just as an eye, when directed, is fitted for seeing,
so too a word, when aimed (properly connected), becomes a denoter of the meaning
A relation of instrument and object is observed to be independent of an action,
therefore there is a rule of expression between the expresser and the expressed
Where there are many single-wordings, all capable of producing the same meaning,
the word stands there where the speaker intends

children.text: āmnāyaśabdān abhyāse ke cid āhur anarthakān
children.translated_text: Some say that, in recitational usage, the canonical words (<s>āmnāya-śabda</s>) are meaningless,
and that they function only as bare forms in conveying to others
Those who see unity, however, regard them, by connection with the act of expression,
as the very ones that convey meaning, due to differences of injunction
They say that for these, which operate with varietal usage, the ultimate multiplicity remains,
as with senses like the eye and the rest, because of convergence on a single class

children.text: prayogād abhisaṃdhānam anyad eṣu na vidyate
children.translated_text: Apart from usage, there is no other intentional coordination in these,

children.text: viṣaye yataśaktitvāt sa tu tatra vyavasthitaḥ
children.translated_text: for the intention is fixed there according to the capacity in the object
Cognition pertains precisely to the multiplicity itself, by means of context of meaning and the like,

children.text: na jātv arthāntare vṛttir anyārthānāṃ kathaṃ ca na
children.translated_text: never is there operation upon a different meaning, and by no means upon other meanings
And that which is a sentence in the form of words, being tied to existence,

children.text: kāmaṃ vimarśas tatrāyaṃ na vākyāvayave pade
children.translated_text: this examination properly belongs there, not to the word as a member of the sentence
Just as, with meaningless letters, a specified meaning is denoted,
so too with words that, taken by themselves, are meaningless, a specified meaning is denoted
And whatever cognition arises, in the interval, regarding the individual word-meanings,
that is the means of apprehension, due to the determining of the sequence and its bounds

children.text: pūrvair arthair anugato yathārthātmā paraḥ paraḥ
children.translated_text: Attended by the prior meanings, each successive one has the true nature appropriate to the meaning,
and the connection that has been initiated is just so with other meaning-entities as well

children.text: aṅgīkṛte tu keṣāṃ cit sādhyenārthena sādhane
children.translated_text: But when, for some, an instrumental (means) meaning is accepted in regard to what is to be accomplished,
then the further statement (śruti) about the means serves precisely the purpose of prescribing a basis
Because there is no restriction regarding the basis, there is no exclusion (to a particular locus),

children.text: sāmarthyāt saṃbhavas tasya śrutis tv anyanivṛttaye
children.translated_text: its possibility is from capacity, while the statement serves for the exclusion of the other
An action, distinct from another action, has fixed basis and means,
for the apprehenders the differentiation already proceeds, being the causes of comprehension
But the undividedness, from words that possess sequence, though they lack word-internal sequence,

children.text: prakāśate tadanyeṣāṃ vākyaṃ vākyārtha eva ca
children.translated_text: is made manifest; and for others, both the sentence and sentence-meaning are just that

children.text: svarūpaṃ vidyate yasya tasyātmā na nirūpyate
children.translated_text: That which has a self-form (intrinsic form), its essence is not to be delineated,

children.text: nāsti yasya svarūpaṃ tu tasyaivātmā nirūpyate
children.translated_text: but that which does not have an intrinsic form—just that one’s essence is delineated
Some say that the determination of form, for the other (i.e., the meaning), is wordless,
and a memory of the nature of a manifestation of meaning arises from words
Otherwise, from the connection with fire, one imagines oneself to be burned as ‘I am burned,’
otherwise, by the word ‘burning,’ the meaning ‘burning’ is apprehended
Just as, for the senses, whose real natures are separately situated and which follow upon separate objects,

children.text: indriyāṇāṃ yathā kāryam ṛte dehān na kalpate
children.translated_text: their function is not conceived apart from bodies,
so too, for all words that are established with separate meanings,
when separated from sentences, there is no meaningfulness
What is grasped, in things-of-meaning that are compounded, is of the nature of connection,
and here no separate entity is posited, since there is the observation of a non-word-meaning (apadārtha)

children.text: darśanasyāpi yat satyaṃ na tathā darśanaṃ sthitam
children.translated_text: And what is true of perception is that perception is not thus situated,
the entity, by means of the form of connection, is delineated as being without that form
Because an object is denoted as being conjoined with existence, or as standing in the nature of cessation,
therefore a sentence is employed
Without a connection to an action, the meaning of a word is not apprehended,

children.text: satyo vā viparīto vā vyavahāre na so+asty ataḥ
children.translated_text: therefore, whether true or false, it does not exist in usage

children.text: sad ity etat tu yad vākyaṃ tad abhūd asti neti vā
children.translated_text: As for the sentence ‘this is existent,’ it is not understood as ‘was,’ ‘is,’ or ‘is not,’
without a connection to the denotation of an action
When the meaning, denoted by a finite verb, is bound up with an instrument (means),
without the denotation of existence, expectation is not resolved

children.text: prādhānyāt tu kriyā pūrvam arthasya pravibhajyate
children.translated_text: But due to primacy, the action is first distinguished with respect to the meaning,
the subsidiaries impelled by what is to be accomplished, and its result being the motivator thereof
The speaker himself intends the status of end-and-means,
and undertakes the construction of the connection of the meaning
‘He does the cooking-action’—thus it is denoted as an object (karman),
but ‘cooking’ as a form of instrument (means) is apprehended as what is to be accomplished
Whichever aspect, by which assistance, is intended by speakers,
that, due to the all-capacity of the meaning, is accordingly fixed
Sometimes the relation is denoted in cases where there is a remote functioning,

children.text: āśliṣṭo yo+anupaśliṣṭaḥ sa kadā cit pratīyate
children.translated_text: sometimes that which is conjoined is apprehended as not conjoined
For the discriminating, there is separateness of the compounded and (yet) connection,
unity of the manifold and multiplicity in the reverse case
Because of the all-formedness of the meaning, or because of its selflessness, this is established,
and because (the meaning) is of the nature of extremely extended potency, the reliance is indeed on the word alone
A word designates the entity, not the assistance (function of aiding),

children.text: na svaśaktiḥ padārthānāṃ saṃspraṣṭuṃ tena śakyate
children.translated_text: by that, the own-power of the word-meanings cannot be directly touched
Conjunction, being a property of what is related, is denoted by its own word,
but relation, namely <s>samavāya</s> (inherence), is understood as a being-related

children.text: lakṣaṇād vyavatiṣṭhante padārthā na tu vastutaḥ
children.translated_text: The word-meanings are fixed by indication (lakṣaṇā), not by reality as such,

children.text: upakārāt sa evārthaḥ kathaṃ cid anugamyate
children.translated_text: by assistance, that very meaning is somehow followed

children.text: vākyārtho yo+abhisaṃbandho na tasyātmā kva cit sthitaḥ
children.translated_text: The sentence-meaning, which is connection, has its essence nowhere established,
in usage they call that the very self of the word-meanings

children.text: padārthe samudāye vā samāpto naiva vā kva cit
children.translated_text: Whether in the word-meaning or in the aggregate, it is never completed anywhere,
its essence is distinguished according to the differentiation in the forms of the word-meanings
For the purpose of restatement, that difference which is the basis of apprehension,
because of the member that has expectation in the difference, by that another is described
The division of the one, having manifold powers, is apprehended,
for the oneness-of-meaning of the sentence is apprehended even by a measure (a single mark)

children.text: saṃpratyayārthād bāhyo+arthaḥ sann asan vā vibhajyate
children.translated_text: From the content of the present cognition, the external object is divided as being or non-being
Objectified as external, the division is characterized as the extraction/ascertainment of powers (śakti),
The powers, determined by the very nature of the meaning of the affix (pratyaya-artha), are not fixed (once-for-all),

children.text: anyatra ca tato rūpaṃ na tāsām upalabhyate
children.translated_text: and apart from that, their form is not apprehended
Even when there are many finite-verb forms (<s>tiṅ</s>-endings) that have mutual expectancy, there is sentence-unity,
and the exclusion (paryudāsa) of the accent-fall (nighāta) from one <s>tiṅ</s> with respect to other <s>tiṅ</s> is thus meaningful

children.text: ekatiṅ yasya vākyaṃ tu śāstre niyatalakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: In the śāstra, the rule is fixed that a sentence is that which has a single finite verb (<s>eka-tiṅ</s>),
but for that, by including non-<s>tiṅ</s> elements, the meaning does not arise from a splitting of the sentence
Again, in cases where there are other <s>tiṅ</s>-ended forms joined, or whether well-joined or not,

children.text: mṛgaḥ paśyata yātīti bhedābhedau na tiṣṭhataḥ
children.translated_text: in ‘the deer—see!—goes,’ difference and non-difference do not hold
Where, by capacity (sāmarthya), one expects what pertains to the sense of ‘what ought to be done’ (<s>itikartavyatā</s>),
that is called complete in meaning which has expectancy characterized as not of a word (aśabda-lakṣaṇa)
But in mere non-supplementary explanation of what is established (tattva-anvākhyāna), whatever meaning gets attached,
even without employing that, the sentence of the scripture (<s>śruti</s>) is completed
“While pacing, study here; reciting, perform the pacing,”
although there is no difference in purposive relation (tādarthya), a difference in words is apprehended
Differences of action that have results, being grounded in distinct actions,
though innumerable in their sequential prescriptions, are illustrated by a single verb
When the differences have been removed, the entire action is denoted by the action-verb,
for in the scripture (<s>śruti</s>) it is impossible to construct a detailed partition of differences
“Kings are to be sacrificed to with the <s>Aśvamedha</s>; Brāhmaṇas sit at the <s>Sattra</s>”:

children.text: brāhmaṇā iti nākhyāta- rūpād bhedaḥ pratīyate
children.translated_text: from forms that are not finite verbs, difference is not apprehended

children.text: sakṛc chrutā saptadaśasv anāvṛttāpi yā kriyā
children.translated_text: An action once heard, even when not repeated in the seventeen <s>Prājāpatya</s> rites,
by their capacity, attains difference
In Devadatta and the like, the eating (bhuj-) is established individually,
or the sentence, being independent in each case, is apprehended with difference

children.text: uccāraṇe tu vākyānām anyad rūpaṃ na gṛhyate
children.translated_text: In utterance, however, no other form of sentences is grasped,

children.text: pratipattau tu bhinnānām anyad rūpaṃ pratīyate
children.translated_text: but in apprehension, another form, as different, is cognized
A sentence of comprehensive apprehension (eka-grahaṇa-vākya) is expressed in general,

children.text: kartarīti yathā tac ca paśvādiṣu vibhajyate
children.translated_text: as, for example, “(he is) the agent,” and that is divided among cattle and the like

children.text: yady ākāṅkṣā nivarteta tadbhūtasya sakṛc chrutau
children.translated_text: If expectancy were to cease when such a thing has been heard once,

children.text: naivānyenābhisaṃbandhaṃ tad upeyāt kathaṃ ca na
children.translated_text: then how indeed would it not attain connection with something else as well?
Therefore, a single form, with many meanings, is the matrix for subsequent specification,
it is the source of the division-sentences, as if established as not other than they

children.text: kva cit kriyā vyaktibhāgair upakāre pravartate
children.translated_text: In some cases, an action proceeds by means of individual parts (instances) for assistance,

children.text: sāmānyabhāga evāsyāḥ kva cid arthasya sādhakaḥ
children.translated_text: in others, the general part alone is the accomplisher with respect to the meaning

children.text: kālabhinnāś ca ye bhedā ye cāpy uṣṭrāsikādiṣu
children.translated_text: And the differences that are separated by time, and those in <s>uṣṭrāsikā</s> and the like,

children.text: prakrame jātibhāgasya śabdātmā tair na bhidyate
children.translated_text: at the outset, the word-nature of the class-part is not divided by them
When there are differences in those of single number, actions distinguished by class and so on,
are applied with difference, upon a single hearing of that word
As the eating, breaking, cutting, and transformations in regard to dice, etc., are distinct,
though there is no difference in the time of usage, they are each established according to their respective differences
The dice (<s>akṣa</s>), the strings, and the board—means, similarity of form,

children.text: eṣāṃ kramo vibhaktānāṃ tannibaddhā sakṛc chrutiḥ
children.translated_text: the sequence of these separated elements is fixed, with a single hearing tied to that

children.text: dvāv apy upāyau śabdānāṃ prayoge samavasthitau
children.translated_text: Both means of words, too, are equally present in usage,

children.text: kramo vā yaugapadyaṃ vā yau loko nātivartate
children.translated_text: sequence or simultaneity, which the world does not transgress

children.text: krame vibhajyate rūpaṃ yaugapadye na bhidyate
children.translated_text: In sequence the form is divided, in simultaneity it is not divided,
but the action, even in simultaneity, follows the form of sequence

children.text: bhedasaṃsargaśaktī dve śabdād bhinne iva sthite
children.translated_text: The two powers—of difference and of combination—are, as it were, set as distinct from the word,
and even in simultaneity, when there is usage with many, the hearing is differentiated
When a single meaning, though not different, is intended by a difference of form,
the aggregate is supported by the property of its members

children.text: bhedanirvacane tv asya pratyekaṃ vā samāpyate
children.translated_text: But in the specification of differences, this is completed either individually,
or the hearing, being distinct in expression, stands in sentence-differentiation
There, either with a singular ending, the word ‘die’ (<s>akṣa</s>) is employed,
or, individually, the division is made into multiplicity, according to the hearing

children.text: dviṣṭhāni yāni vākyāni teṣv apy ekatvadarśinām
children.translated_text: And in those sentences that are two-staged (dviṣṭhāni), even there for those who see unity,
the own-power of the one that has many powers is apportioned
Or, when two utterly distinct ones, the usage has the characteristic of a ‘board’ (tantra),
there the means is the combination, which is diversified among the apprehenders
Words previously grasped as different, but of equal sound later,
by the ‘board’ (tantra), the hearers, taught by the speaker, apprehend
Even when there is intention of one alone, the other is not produced,
without any purposeful connection, the word, in the form of power, becomes manifest

children.text: anekā śaktir ekasya yugapac chrūyate kva cit
children.translated_text: The one has many powers, in some cases heard simultaneously,
and <s>Agni</s> is employed, even in one locus, for both illumination and burning
Even when a sentence, once heard, has a meaning divided by the power of repetition,

children.text: liṅgād vā tantradharmād vā vibhāgo vyavatiṣṭhate
children.translated_text: the differentiation is established either by an indicatory mark (<s>liṅga</s>) or by the property of the ‘board’ (<s>tantra</s>)
In the designation called <s>saṃprasāraṇa</s> (vowel-glide substitution), by two indicatory marks, of both phoneme and sentence,

children.text: pravibhāgas tathā sūtra ekasminn eva jāyate
children.translated_text: there likewise arises, in a single <s>sūtra</s>, the partition
Likewise, in the case of the duplication rule “<s>dvirvacane ac</s>,” by the ‘board’-means (<s>tantra</s>-method), which is without a single, fixed feature,
the instruction by means of <s>ekaśeṣa</s> (the ‘one-remainder’ device) is exhibited in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> itself
For the most part, grammarians who relish concision and possess only a little learning,
having reached the collection (of doctrines), when the compendium has set, as it were, into a cloak
Then, when the master <s>Pātañjala</s>, a seer of the sacred fords (tīrthas),
composed the Great Commentary (<s>Mahābhāṣya</s>), a compilation of all the seed-principles of reasoning,
since in that (work), due to its depth, there is no footing for one who has not prepared his understanding,
it appears level and smooth, yet for those of untrained mind no firm certitude is established
By the <s>Vaijisaubha</s>, <s>Haryakṣa</s>, and the like—followers of dry dialectic—
when the venerable scripture was thrown into confusion, with the cloak of a compendium as a counter-guise,
the <s>Vyākaraṇa-āgama</s> that fell away from the disciples of <s>Patañjali</s>,
in time came to be maintained in the southern lands merely as a text (book) alone
Having obtained the tradition from <s>Parvata</s>, by those who follow the seed-principles of the <s>Bhāṣya</s>,
it was then led into a branching multiplicity again by teachers such as the <s>Cāndra</s>-ācāryas

children.text: nyāyaprasthānamārgāṃs tān abhyasya svaṃ ca darśanam
children.translated_text: Having studied those paths of the <s>Nyāya</s>-foundation and also our own viewpoint,
our teacher composed this compendium of the tradition (<s>āgama-saṃgraha</s>)

children.text: vartmanām atra keṣāṃ cid vastumātram udāhṛtam
children.translated_text: Here only the bare substance of some of the paths has been indicated,
an inquiry will be undertaken, with a sharper (more exact) eye, in the third book
Discriminating insight is obtained by means of distinct scriptural viewpoints,

children.text: kiyad vā śakyam unnetuṃ svatarkam anudhāvatā
children.translated_text: but how much can be brought to light by one who merely runs after his own reasoning?

children.text: tat tad utprekṣamāṇānāṃ purāṇair āgamair vinā
children.translated_text: For those who imagine this and that, without the ancient scriptures,
and who have not attended upon the elders, learning does not become very propitious
Thus the Chapter on Sentences (<s>Vākya-kāṇḍa</s>) in the work called <s>Vākyapadīya</s>, composed by <s>Bhartṛhari</s>, is completed
Padakāṇḍa
3.1. Exposition of <s>Jāti</s> (genus, universal)

children.text: dvidhā kaiś cit padaṃ bhinnaṃ caturdhā pañcadhāpi vā
children.translated_text: Some divide the word in two, or into four or even five,
or else they extract (its parts) from sentences, like base and affix and the like

children.text: padārthānām apoddhāre jātir vā dravyam eva vā
children.translated_text: In the extraction of the meanings of words, either the <s>jāti</s> (universal) or the substance alone,
are set forth as the two meanings of all words, and they are eternal
For some, by association, <s>jāti</s> is a mark of power (capacity),
in cases like <s>khadira</s> and the like where there is no power, a powerful one is put in its stead
Dependence (bondage), whose result is lack of autonomy, remains like means of valid cognition and the like,
therefore, even when there is designation of <s>jāti</s>, that which is without power is not apprehended

children.text: saṃśleṣamātraṃ badhnātir yadi syāt tu vivakṣitaḥ
children.translated_text: If what is intended were merely a binding together (a mere conjunction),
then the indicatory sign would rest on the support of power—the injunction being like that of proof and the like
One’s own <s>jāti</s> is first denoted by all words,
thereafter an ascription-imagination upon forms that are the kinds of meaning

children.text: yathā rakte guṇe tattvaṃ kaṣāye vyapadiśyate
children.translated_text: Just as the reality of the red quality is indicated as ‘brownish’,
and, through contact with what is conjoined, it is apprehended even in cloth and the like,
so, because of the relation of word and meaning, the <s>jāti</s> abides in the word,
and, in the designation of the kinds of meanings, it is assumed for the function of a <s>jāti</s>
When there is sole remainder of the <s>jāti</s>-word, that is taken to be the <s>jāti</s> of <s>jātis</s>,
in the phrase ‘word-<s>jātis</s>’, that <s>jāti</s> is among the word-<s>jātis</s>
That <s>jāti</s> which, in the words ‘word-<s>jāti</s>’, has a characteristic distinct from the words,
that <s>jāti</s> remains as ‘word-<s>jāti</s>’ without transgression
Even when there is designation of an object-<s>jāti</s>, all denoters of <s>jāti</s>,
since they are established as having the characteristic of an activity, are the meanings of words

children.text: jātau padārthe jātir vā viseṣo vāpi jātivat
children.translated_text: Whether it is a <s>jāti</s> in the meaning of the word, or a particular possessing <s>jāti</s>,

children.text: śabdair apekṣyate yasmād atas te jātivācinaḥ
children.translated_text: since they are regarded by words, therefore they are denoters of <s>jāti</s>

children.text: dravyadharmā padārthe tu dravye sarvo+artha ucyate
children.translated_text: In the meaning of a word, being a property of substance, every object is called a substance,
and, because of being the locus of the properties of substance, therefore every object is considered a substance
Or, <s>jāti</s> may be the property of recurrence in all <s>jātis</s>,
in a particular, the generality of the exclusion-property is taken to be <s>jāti</s>
When, by a difference of properties of what is conjoined, ‘places’ are imagined,
even in those places there is a generality belonging to even <s>Ākāśa</s> (space)
Just as pots and the like, which have no place (of their own), have ‘places’ that are related,
so too the ‘places’ of <s>Ākāśa</s>, which itself has no place, are its conjuncts
A cognition whose support is distinct things persists in things conjoined,
but in inhering substrates, the apprehension of difference is discontinued
Therefore, the ‘places’ that belong to conjunction are imagined to be secondary (metaphorical),
because, through non-discrimination, primariness is ascribed to inherential (samavāyin) ‘places’

children.text: anupravṛttirūpā yā prakhyā tām ākṛtiṃ viduḥ
children.translated_text: That prominence which has the form of continued recurrence is known as the <s>ākṛti</s> (form, generic form),

children.text: ke cid vyāvṛttirūpāṃ tu dravyatvena pracakṣate
children.translated_text: but some declare that which has the form of exclusion to be a substance (<s>dravya</s>)

children.text: bhinnā iti paropādhir abhinnā iti vā punaḥ
children.translated_text: Whether, due to an external condition, they are said to be distinct, or again to be non-distinct,
this manifoldness arises only where entities, whose nature is being, are intermingled (conjunct)

children.text: naikatvaṃ nāpi nānātvaṃ na sattvaṃ na ca nāstitā
children.translated_text: There is neither unity nor plurality, neither existence nor non-existence,
among the real natures of entities when they are not intermingled
On the determination that the very self is constituted by all powers, as one only,
the positing of a difference of selves for entities would be purposeless
Therefore, all powers, beginning with substance and the rest, having distinct characteristics,

children.text: saṃsṛṣṭāḥ puruṣārthasya sādhikā na tu kevalāḥ
children.translated_text: are efficacious for human purpose only when conjoined, not when isolated
And just as the completeness that is the very self of the senses and the like is apprehended,
so too, even in the intermixture of relation-with-a-relatum, it is apprehended

children.text: na tad utpadyate kiṃ cid yasya jātir na vidyate
children.translated_text: Nothing whatsoever is produced of which there is no <s>jāti</s> (universal),
the <s>jāti</s> is the instigator of the causes for the manifestation of the self (its own locus)
Having taken their stand in causes—both eternal and non-eternal—<s>jātis</s>,

children.text: kva cit kāryeṣv abhivyaktim upayānti punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: at certain times enter into manifestation in effects, again and again

children.text: nirvartyamānaṃ yat karma jātis tatrāpi sādhanam
children.translated_text: In an action being carried out, the <s>jāti</s> too is an instrument there,
for the deposition (fixing) of its own substrate; thus it is the instigator of activity

children.text: vidhau vā pratiṣedhe vā brāhmaṇatvādi sādhanam
children.translated_text: In injunction or in prohibition, that which effects <s>brāhmaṇatva</s> (Brahmanhood) and the like,
is a <s>saṃkhyā-jāti</s> (numerical universal), a differentiator, dependent upon and residing in particulars
Just as, by waters and the like, what is manifest is called ‘the face’ itself,
so too, by substances that have made it manifest, the <s>jāti</s> itself is denoted
As the difference that resides in the senses, even without the grasping by the senses,
though unseen in the objects of the senses, is contrived for a difference of cognition,
so, through the grasping of the self-nature, for some, even without particulars,
they become the occasions (conditions) for differences of cognition of the universal

children.text: satyāsatyau tu yau bhāgau pratibhāvaṃ vyavasthitau
children.translated_text: But the two factors—truth and untruth—being fixed in their respective statuses,

children.text: satyaṃ yat tatra sā jātir asatyā vyaktayaḥ smṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: that which is true there is the <s>jāti</s>, and the particulars are considered untrue
Because of the diversity of the relatum (the ‘possessor of relation’), the very existence (being) itself, differing in cows and the like,

children.text: jātir ity ucyate tasyāṃ sarve śabdā vyavasthitāḥ
children.translated_text: is called <s>jāti</s>; upon that, all words are fixed

children.text: tāṃ prātipadikārthaṃ ca dhātvarthaṃ ca pracakṣate
children.translated_text: They declare that to be both the meaning of the base (<s>prātipadika</s>) and the meaning of the verbal root (<s>dhātu</s>),

children.text: sā nityā sā mahān ātmā tām āhus tvatalādayaḥ
children.translated_text: that is eternal; that is the great self; the forms in -tva, -tā, and the like are said of that
That very thing, having attained sequence in particulars, is called action,

children.text: kramarūpasya saṃhāre tat sattvam iti kathyate
children.translated_text: and when the form of sequence is dissolved, that is called existence (being)
That very thing, in the transformations of entities, assumes six states,
and thus appears, successively, by its own powers
Sequence too is its very self; and here there is the intuition of time,
as if standing divided into the forms of prior and posterior and the like
On the admission of disappearance, that very thing is the non-existence of entities,
and when, after sequence has been established, disappearance occurs, it is apprehended as perishing

children.text: pūrvasmāt pracyutā dharmād aprāptā cottaraṃ padam
children.translated_text: Having fallen away from the prior property and not yet attained the later state,
in the interval, because of a substrate of differences, birth is spoken of

children.text: āśrayaḥ svātmamātrā vā bhāvā vā vyatirekiṇaḥ
