children.translated_text: The substrate may be either nothing but its own self, or entities distinct (from it),
or its own powers; these are the causes for the perception of difference of existence
In the manifestation among earth and the like, it does not depend upon configuration (arrangement),
the <s>jāti</s>, having an uninterrupted substrate, remains even in a non-eternal substrate
Some declare the entire <s>jāti</s> to have an indestructible substrate,
and they are settled that there is no simultaneity of universal dissolution of everything
When, for those who see unity, the differences are dissolved into <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature),
the <s>jātis</s> resort to their own substrates as the existence of substances
Properties such as <s>brāhmaṇatva</s> (Brahmanhood) are established in all living beings,

children.text: abhivyaktāḥ svakāryāṇāṃ sādhakā ity api smṛtiḥ
children.translated_text: and there is also a tradition that, when manifest, they are efficacious for their respective functions

children.text: citrādiṣv apy abhivyaktir jātīnāṃ kaiś cid iṣyate
children.translated_text: Some accept manifestation of <s>jātis</s> even in paintings and the like,

children.text: prāṇyāśritās tu tāḥ prāptau nimittaṃ puṇyapāpayoḥ
children.translated_text: but, when they are supported by living beings, the occasion for their attainment is merit and demerit

children.text: jñānaṃ tv asmadviśiṣṭānāṃ tāsu sarvendriyaṃ viduḥ
children.translated_text: But knowledge, for those distinguished like us, they understand to be the all-sense (a universal organ),
through habituation, as in the case of connoisseurs with the specificities of gems, silver, and the like
That reality of difference which is grounded in the fragrance of the lily and the like as a <s>jāti</s>,
is not expressed in the world by means of words for entities, because of impermanence
But <s>jātis</s> like ‘man-lion’ and the like are designated by non-own-words (nonstandard words),
and another <s>jāti</s> exists in component-parts that are similar in form; in those, usage (scriptural utterance) is established
In the delimitation of the state of <s>jāti</s> (universal), number or mere numerosity is intended,
even in separation, because of conjunction, it is admitted to be contributory (instrumental) for benefit
Definition is the operation upon word-refinement (semantic conditioning of a word) for the accomplishment of the result,
and, even with equality of Vedic expression, the powers of number, action, and the like are observed

children.text: na vinā saṃkhyayā kaś cit sattvabhūto+artha ucyate
children.translated_text: No entity that has being is spoken of without number,

children.text: ataḥ sarvasya nirdeśe saṃkhyā syād avivakṣitā
children.translated_text: therefore, in the designation of everything, number would be unexpressed (i.e., not specially intended)

children.text: ekatvaṃ vā bahutvaṃ vā keṣāṃ cid avivakṣitam
children.translated_text: Unity or plurality, for some cases, is not intended,

children.text: tad dhi jātyabhidhānāya dvitvaṃ tu syād vivakṣitam
children.translated_text: for that is for the denotation of the <s>jāti</s> (universal), whereas duality would be intended

children.text: yady etau vyādhitau syātāṃ deyaṃ syād idam auṣadham
children.translated_text: “If these two should be diseased, this medicine should be given,”

children.text: ity evaṃ lakṣaṇe+arthasya dvitvaṃ syād avivakṣitam
children.translated_text: thus, in such a characterization of the object, duality would be unintentional
For what is denoted by words like ‘one, etc.,’ its being an ancillary part in actions is accepted,

children.text: saṃkhyāyāḥ khanati dvābhyām iti rūpād dhi sāśritā
children.translated_text: for number is dependent on a form such as “he digs with two (spades/hands)”
In the case “one should sacrifice with (a) beast,” where even a refinement (sacramental conditioning) is possible,
just as a <s>jāti</s> (universal), so unity is understood as instrumental (a means)

children.text: liṅgāt tu syād dvitīyādes tad ekatvaṃ vivakṣitam
children.translated_text: But from an indicatory mark (liṅga), the second and the rest would be (understood); thereby unity is what is intended,
and when there is a single referent, that indicator pertains to <s>jāti</s> and number
The injunction is, in fact, of a beast that is not enjoined elsewhere as such for the first time,

children.text: kriyāyām aṅgabhāvaś ca tat tv etasmād vivakṣitam
children.translated_text: and its status as an auxiliary in the action—that indeed is what is intended here

children.text: grahās tv anyatra vihitā bhinnasaṃkhyāḥ pṛthak pṛthak
children.translated_text: But the <s>Grahās</s> (graha-offerings), enjoined elsewhere, have different numbers, each separately,
endowed with distinctions such as “nine for the <s>Prājāpatya</s>,” and the like

children.text: aṅgatvena pratītānāṃ saṃmārge tv aṅgināṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: For those (items) apprehended as auxiliaries, how would the number, with respect to the specification in the sweeping (procedure),

children.text: nirdeśaṃ prati yā saṃkhyā sā kathaṃ syād vivakṣitā
children.translated_text: be intended for the principals again

children.text: nānyatra vidhir astīti saṃskāro nāpi cāṅgitā
children.translated_text: Since there is no injunction elsewhere, there is no refinement nor principal-hood,

children.text: hetuḥ saṃkhyāvivakṣāyā yatnāt sā hi vivakṣitā
children.translated_text: the reason for the intention regarding number is deliberate effort; for it is indeed intended

children.text: saṃmārjane viśeṣaś ca na grahe kva cid āśritaḥ
children.translated_text: And the special rule in sweeping is not dependent on any graha whatsoever,

children.text: vihītās te ca saṃskāryāḥ sarveṣām āśrayas tataḥ
children.translated_text: and those (grahas), though enjoined, are to be refined (sacramentally processed); hence they are the support for all

children.text: pratyāśrayaṃ samāptāyāṃ jātāv ekena cet kriyā
children.translated_text: When, upon the attainment of the own-substratum, if the action is with one <s>jāti</s> (universal),

children.text: paśunā na prakalpeta tat syād eva prakalpanam
children.translated_text: it should not be instituted with a beast; that institution would be just that (i.e., already accomplished)

children.text: ekena ca prasiddhāyāṃ kriyāyāṃ yadi saṃbhavāt
children.translated_text: And when the action is established with one (beast), if another is possible,
taking an additional beast should be undertaken; taking (one more) would not be purposeless
Just as, in the case of the rite for a woman who already has conceived, conception-rite is purposeless,
so, when established with one, an additional beast is purposeless
Since the purpose is accomplished to that extent, there is no transgression of unity,

children.text: ke cid icchanti na tv atra saṃkhyāṅgatvena gṛhyate
children.translated_text: some desire (another beast), but here number is not taken as an auxiliary

children.text: dvitīyādi tu yal liṅgam uktanyāyānuvādi tat
children.translated_text: But the indicator that is ‘second,’ etc., follows the reasoning already stated,
hence, not-number is understood as instrumental, like a <s>jāti</s> (universal)
When, by concomitance and difference, the acceptance of number is in place,

children.text: yuktaṃ yat sādhanatvaṃ syān na tv anyārthopalakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: it is proper that it be a means (instrumental), and not a mere indicator of some other purpose
When a padārtha (item denoted by a word) is instrumental, its capacity is not diminished,
therefore, the operation-character of number is inferred by that indicator
Because the <s>apūrva</s> (novel result) is what is enjoined, its primacy is ascertained,
and because what is enjoined (as subsidiary) is for the sake of something else, its residual (subsidiary) status is understood
Since the sweeping is what is enjoined, whereas the graha is enjoined elsewhere,

children.text: vidhivākye śrutā saṃkhyā lakṣaṇāyāṃ na bādhyate
children.translated_text: the number heard in an injunctive sentence is not overridden by the function of definition
In another injunctive sentence, the number concerning the beast is not contradictory,
therefore he (the sacrificer), possessed of a quality (i.e., along with the specified quality), is understood as being with unity
When an action is prescribed with the connection to a known substance,
the quality is desired for that (action), and is understood as with the substance

children.text: kaś cid eva guṇo dravye yathā sāmarthyalakṣaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Only a certain quality in a substance is characterized by capacity,
thus the substratum too, of a quality, is obtained as characterized by capacity

children.text: tayos tu pṛthagarthitve saṃbandho yaḥ pratīyate
children.translated_text: But when those two have distinct meanings, the relation that is understood,

children.text: na tasminn upaghāto+asti kalpyam anyan na cāśrutam
children.translated_text: in that there is no impairment; nothing else is to be imagined, nor is anything unheard (introduced)
The connection with the action that is obtained from the Vedic wording for those two,
and from the sentences regarding substratum and possessor, the restriction is established
There, in the absence of the substance and the quality, there would be an option between them severally,
for the relation obtained from the Veda is strong, on account of the sentence-character

children.text: yadā tu jātiḥ śaktir vā kriyāṃ praty upadiśyate
children.translated_text: But when a <s>jāti</s> (universal) or a power is prescribed with regard to an action,
then, by capacity, substance and quality are supplied there

children.text: jātīnāṃ ca guṇānāṃ ca tulye+aṅgatve kriyāṃ prati
children.translated_text: And when <s>jātis</s> and qualities have equal status as auxiliaries with respect to the action,
qualities are supplied as substitutes, not the <s>jātis</s> of goats and the like

children.text: vyaktiśakteḥ samāsannā jātayo na tathā guṇāḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>vyaktiśakti</s> (power of the particular) being closer, the <s>jātis</s> are not so (close) as qualities are

children.text: sākṣād dravyaṃ kriyāyogi guṇas tasmād vikalpate
children.translated_text: Because the substance is directly fit for the action, therefore the quality is optionally chosen
By parity (of reasoning), in the absence of either (member), some accept an option,

children.text: atadguṇo+ataś chāgaḥ syān meṣo vā tadguṇo bhavet
children.translated_text: thus, a goat lacking that quality could be (taken), or a ram possessing that quality could be
The operation of number that is grounded in a <s>jāti</s> (universal) is observed,

children.text: saṃkhyāviśeṣam utsṛjya kva cit saiva pravartate
children.translated_text: and, abandoning a specific number, that very (universal) sometimes operates
A generality that has the status of a subsidiary (parāṅga) is appropriately connected with the number of substances,

children.text: svārthaṃ pravartamānaṃ tu na saṃkhyām avalambate
children.translated_text: but when it operates for its own purpose, it does not depend on number
In the passage “Let him sacrifice with a beast,” here, where there is the mention of the beast for the sake of the sacrificing,
the action becomes principal when its purpose is accomplished with a single beast

children.text: yāvatāṃ saṃbhavo yasya sa kuryāt tāvatāṃ yadi
children.translated_text: If one is capable (of obtaining) as many as are possible for him, let him do (so) to that extent; if so,

children.text: ālambhanaṃ guṇais tena pradhānaṃ syāt prayojitam
children.translated_text: by that, the principal is made to rely on qualities and thus is brought about by them
But where, in the context of “while the web is being swept,” there is a mention of an action with regard to the graha,
we do not at all attend there to the taking of a specific number
In the subsequent sentence being taught, the taking of “one” that has been made,
even when a specific number remains in the rest, clearly shows that indicator
As the Vedic wording that has fallen (i.e., occurs) in the rule for compounding and affixation,
is justified strictly by the reasoning that (those) qualities are dependent
Even with regard to the quality, it is not accepted for the establishment of another principal,

children.text: saṃkhyā kartā tathā karmaṇy aviśiṣṭaḥ pratīyate
children.translated_text: and number is understood, with respect to the agent as well as the action, as non-specific
Where a further Vedic wording, whose purpose is restriction, is set down concerning something otherwise applicable,
but a separation is enjoined from a collection of like-forms (a homogeneous aggregate)
Upon cessation (of that restriction), because its purpose has been accomplished, number is there not intended,
one (term) there, meaningful, is established as denoting the aggregate
In the prescription of the affix, of the principal, or also of the compound,
when a non-intention of number is established, there is in every way favoring (inclusiveness) with respect to the quality
Similarity, which has the form of non-difference, and powers that are of the very nature (of the thing),
their being denotable as synonyms of <s>jāti</s> (universal) is also set forth
Even if, with the desire to obtain a staff, one obtains a staff,

children.text: na tasmād eva sāmarthyāt sa daṇḍīti pratīyate
children.translated_text: from that very capacity he is not apprehended as “a staff”
Nor does cognition proceed as “one who has desire” from a mere occasioning by desire,

children.text: tasmāt saty api sāmarthye buddhir arthāntarāśrayā
children.translated_text: therefore, even when capacity exists, the cognition rests on a different object
Either as an intrinsic nature or as something not expressible (by a word), capacity would have to be posited,

children.text: sarvasyānte yatas tasmād vyavahāro na kalpate
children.translated_text: but since at the end it would belong to everything, no practical usage would be possible

children.text: yadā bhedān parityajya buddhyaika iva gṛhyate
children.translated_text: When, abandoning differences, something is grasped by the intellect as if it were one,

children.text: vyaktyātmaiva tadā tatra buddhir ekā pravartate
children.translated_text: then the cognition operates there as of a particular (vyakti) alone
When something, shot through with forms of difference, is taken as if one,
then a cognition of a collection arises from many, by an apprehension of a group
When, with a will to express togetherness, bound to a single cognition,
a collection, whose members’ joints are tied (i.e., whose parts are connected), is denoted
A single (entity), due to the completion of each respective action, though accompanied by differences,
in a <s>dvandva</s> (copulative compound) is then approached under the divisions of duality and the like
In a once-only operation there is unity; in repetition, it attains the nature of similarity,
of distinct particulars, through the elimination of difference
As “again engaged,” so a distinct cognition is apprehended,
and the object, though of a excluded form (distinct), is likewise grasped as such in truth
And for all that are of like form, there are no words that introduce difference,
nor is difference determined
As for the particularities that are fixed as the objects of knowledge, word, and meaning,
because they are hard to determine, there is the view of the oneness of knowledge and the like

children.text: jñāneṣv api yathārtheṣu tathā sarveṣu jātayaḥ
children.translated_text: And just as in knowledges with respect to objects, so in all <s>jātis</s> (universals),
there is the perception of conjunction; and these establish the object
The generality exists only in the knowable and is helpful to knowledges,

children.text: na jātu jñeyavaj jñānaṃ pararūpeṇa rūpyate
children.translated_text: never is knowledge, like the knowable, shaped in the form of another
Just as light is not illuminated by another illumination,
so the form of knowledge is not apprehended by another knowledge
Nor would the power of knowledge be competent, in determining a generality inherent in the self,
to cognize some other thing already known

children.text: ayaugapadye jñānānām asyety agrahaṇaṃ na ca
children.translated_text: And in the non-simultaneity of cognitions, there is no non-apprehension such as “of this,”
for memory arises in accordance with the apprehension, after the apprehension has occurred
The cognition “pot-knowledge” is a knowledge distinct from pot-knowledge (as an object),

children.text: ghaṭa ity api yaj jñānaṃ viṣayopanipāti tat
children.translated_text: and the cognition that is “pot,” too, is that which resorts to an object
Because, in the form of the object, the form of knowledge is not grasped,
and because its own form, distinct from the form of the object, is not determined,
thus ends the section on the <s>jāti</s> (universal)
3.2 Designation of Substance

children.text: ātmā vastu svabhāvaś ca śarīraṃ tattvam ity api
children.translated_text: <s>Ātmā</s> (self), existent, own-nature, and body, and also “principle,”

children.text: dravyam ity asya paryāyās tac ca nityam iti smṛtam
children.translated_text: are synonyms of substance, and that is remembered as eternal
The real (satya), by means of unreal forms, is ascertained;
by words whose qualifying conditions are unreal, only the real is denoted
As, with a non-permanent condition, “the house of <s>Devadatta</s>,”
grasped by the word “house,” is denoted as pure (house) alone

children.text: suvarṇādi yathā yuktaṃ svair ākārair apāyibhiḥ
children.translated_text: Just as gold, etc., fitted with its own forms that are perishable,
comes rightly to be denoted by names like “earring,” while what is expressible is purely that (gold) alone
And through the delimitation by forms, universality with respect to all objects is secured,
just as the capacity of the eye and the like is (secured) by lenses and the like

children.text: teṣv ākāreṣu yaḥ śabdas tathābhūteṣu vartate
children.translated_text: The word that operates with respect to those forms as they are,
being of the nature of reality, is also said to be eternal

children.text: na tattvātattvayor bheda iti vṛddhebhya āgamaḥ
children.translated_text: “There is no difference between reality and non-reality”—such is the transmission from the elders;
they take “non-reality” to be precisely reality not examined
That which is unconstructed (avikalpita) assumes the form of construction (vikalpa), indeed reality itself;

children.text: na cātra kālabhedo+asti kālabhedaś ca gṛhyate
children.translated_text: and here there is no division of time, yet division of time is apprehended
Just as the absolute non-occurrence of the properties of the object in knowledge (as such),

children.text: tadātmeva ca tat siddham atyantam atadātmakam
children.translated_text: so it is established that knowledge is of the nature of that (object), and absolutely not of a different nature
So too, the absolute non-occurrence of modification-forms in reality;

children.text: tadātmeva ca tat tattvam atyantam atadātmakam
children.translated_text: and that reality is of the nature of that (unmodified), absolutely not of a different nature

children.text: sat yam ākṛtisaṃhāre yad ante vyavatiṣṭhate
children.translated_text: What, upon the dissolution of configurations, in the end remains standing as the real,

children.text: tan nityaṃ śabdavācyaṃ tac chabdāt tac ca na bhidyate
children.translated_text: that is eternal, denotable by the word; that and the word are not different

children.text: na tad asti na tan nāsti na tad ekaṃ na tat pṛthak
children.translated_text: It is not that that exists, not that it does not exist; it is not one, not separate;

children.text: na saṃsṛṣṭaṃ vibhaktaṃ na vikṛtaṃ na na cānyathā
children.translated_text: not conjoined, divided, not modified, nor otherwise

children.text: tan nāsti vidyate tac ca tad ekaṃ tat pṛthak pṛthak
children.translated_text: That is not (so), it is (so); that is one, that is separate, separate;

children.text: saṃsṛṣṭaṃ ca vibhaktaṃ ca vikṛtaṃ tat tad anyathā
children.translated_text: it is conjoined and divided; it is modified; this and that, otherwise
Its form as the relation of word and meaning is seen as one;

children.text: tad dṛśyaṃ darśanaṃ draṣṭā darśane ca prayojanam
children.translated_text: that seen, the seeing, the seer, and the purpose in the seeing
When modification is removed, gold is the real, as in an earring;
when modification is removed, so they speak of the highest <s>prakṛti</s> (primordial nature)

children.text: vācyā sā sarvaśabdānāṃ śabdāś ca na pṛthak tataḥ
children.translated_text: That is what is expressible by all words, and the words are not apart from that;

children.text: apṛthaktve ca saṃbandhas tayor nānātmanor iva
children.translated_text: and in non-difference, the relation is as if of two whose natures are not many

children.text: ātmā paraḥ priyo dveṣyo vaktā vācyaṃ prayojanam
children.translated_text: The self is supreme, dear, hateful; speaker, what is to be spoken, the purpose—
opposed forms of the one mind, as in a dream
Likewise, in that which is unborn, eternal, devoid of before-and-after,
there is apprehended the character of birth and the like, which is opposed,
thus ends the designation of substance
3.3 Designation of Relation

children.text: jñānaṃ prayoktur bāhyo+arthaḥ svarūpaṃ ca pratīyate
children.translated_text: Knowledge, the external object of the user (of words), and the own-nature, are apprehended;
the relation among these is established by uttered words

children.text: pratipattur bhavaty arthe jñāne vā saṃśayaḥ kva cit
children.translated_text: For the understander there sometimes arises doubt regarding the object or the knowledge,
but when the intrinsic natures are apprehended, there is no deviation

children.text: asyāyaṃ vācako vācya iti ṣaṣṭhyā pratīyate
children.translated_text: “This is the denoter of that, that is the denoted”—this is understood by the genitive,

children.text: yogaḥ śabdārthayos tattvam apy ato vyapadiśyate
children.translated_text: and therefore the connection (<s>yoga</s>) of word and meaning, even the reality of it, is designated
There is no denotation, by its own function, that can denote relation,
because of its absolute dependence, its form is not to be specified
From the (fact of) assistance, wherever that property exists, it is followed;

children.text: śaktīnām api sā śaktir guṇānām apy asau guṇaḥ
children.translated_text: that is the power of powers, and that indeed is the quality of qualities
But for the two, property and possessor of property, the “word-ness” concerns conjunction and inherence (<s>saṃyoga</s>, <s>samavāya</s>),
and for those two as well, determinate conditioning factors exist, for the sake of assistance

children.text: kā cid eva hi sāvasthā kāryaprasavasūcitā
children.translated_text: For there is only some particular state, indicated by the production of an effect,

children.text: kasya cit kena cid yasyāṃ saṃyoga upajāyate
children.translated_text: in which, for someone, with something, conjunction arises

children.text: nirātmakānām utpattau niyamaḥ kva cid eva yaḥ
children.translated_text: In the origination of things devoid of self, there is only some restriction,
and by that very (restriction) there is non-deviation, which is effected when there is no difference in attainment
By which an entity’s self is determined as the self of another entity,
and because oneness and manifoldness (there) are not ascertained as reality
that power, called inherence (<s>samavāya</s>), aiding the powers,
transcending difference and non-difference, is established in another way
“Relation supports the dharma of all categories, surpassing all characteristics,”
so runs the transmission from the predecessors
And, having been made a “category,” it is accepted everywhere by others;

children.text: saṃbandhas tena śabdārthaḥ pravibhaktuṃ na śakyate
children.translated_text: therefore relation, being the word-meaning, cannot be divided

children.text: samavāyāt sva ādhāraḥ svā ca jātiḥ pratīyate
children.translated_text: From inherence (<s>samavāya</s>) are apprehended its own substrate and its own <s>jāti</s> (universal)

children.text: ekārthasamavāyāt tu guṇāḥ svādhāra eva ye
children.translated_text: But from inherence in a single entity (<s>ekārtha-samavāya</s>), the qualities are indeed only in their own substrate,
namely <s>dravyatva</s> (thing-hood), <s>sattā</s> (existence), and <s>saṃyoga</s> (conjunction), whose own supports are bound (to them),

children.text: tatpradeśavibhāgāś ca guṇā dvitvādayaś ca ye
children.translated_text: and the divisions of that locus as well are qualities; and those such as duality (<s>dvitva</s>) and the like,

children.text: ke cit svāśrayasaṃyuktāḥ ke cit tatsamavāyinaḥ
children.translated_text: some (qualities) are conjoined with their own substrate; some are inhered-in by that (substrate),
and others are inhered-in within what is conjoined and what is inhered (therein), so too others (beyond that),

children.text: svāśrayeṇa tu saṃyuktaiḥ saṃyuktaṃ vibhu gamyate
children.translated_text: but the all-pervading (entity) is known as conjoined through those that are conjoined with its own substrate,
no relation of inherence is seen there other than that
And because relation is not differentiated, there would be no restriction here,
therefore such a relation is not posited between word and meaning
Just as, by obtaining an unseen function (<s>adṛṣṭa-vṛtti</s>), the self has conjunction somewhere,
so also elsewhere that same sequence, called the union of owner and owned, in non-difference,
but the attainment called inherence (<s>samavāya</s>), which surpasses the property of what is expressible,

children.text: prayoktā pratipattā vā na śabdair anugacchati
children.translated_text: the utterer or the understander does not follow by means of words

children.text: avācyam iti yad vācyaṃ tad avācyatayā yadā
children.translated_text: If what is to be expressed as “inexpressible” were to be decided, by its inexpressibility, as “expressible,”

children.text: vācyam ity avasīyeta vācyam eva tadā bhavet
children.translated_text: then at that time it would indeed be expressible

children.text: athāpy avācyam ity evaṃ na tad vācyaṃ pratīyate
children.translated_text: But if, conversely, it is not apprehended as what is to be expressed by saying “it is inexpressible,”
then the very condition intended for it is not ascertained
And of that whose inexpressibility is said to be “thus,” “otherwise,” or “in every way,”

children.text: tatrāpi naiva sāvasthā taiḥ śabdaiḥ pratiṣidhyate
children.translated_text: even there that condition is in no way negated by those words
For when a doubtful object, in the form of doubt, is fixed as a remainder,
so long as its own nature is not eliminated, no other doubt proceeds
And when, in the knowledge of determination, determination proceeds as determination,
then the knowledge stands firm in its own function

children.text: sarvaṃ mithyā bravīmīti naitad vākyaṃ vivakṣyate
children.translated_text: The sentence “I say that everything is false” is not intended,

children.text: tasya mithyābhidhāne hi prakrānto+artho na gamyate
children.translated_text: for when its meaning is asserted to be false, the purport already set in motion is not apprehended
Nor does what has proceeded as the signifier have expressibility,

children.text: pratipādyaṃ na tat tatra yenānyat pratipadyate
children.translated_text: for there is not, there, that to be conveyed, by which something else would be comprehended
“The thesis is unsupportable” is not what is being stated here,

children.text: yathā tathāsya dharmo+api nātra kaś cit pratīyate
children.translated_text: and likewise, none of its properties is perceived here

children.text: vyāpārasyāparo yasmān na vyāpāro+asti kaś ca na
children.translated_text: Because there is no other operation of operation, nor any operation at all,

children.text: virodham anavasthāṃ vā tasmāt sarvatra nāśrayet
children.translated_text: one should therefore not resort anywhere to contradiction or to infinite regress
Just as the fitness of the senses in their own objects is beginningless,

children.text: anādir arthaiḥ śabdānāṃ saṃbandho yogyatā tathā
children.translated_text: so too the relation of words with objects is beginningless, being fitness (<s>yogyatā</s>)

children.text: asādhur anumānena vācakaḥ kaiś cid iṣyate
children.translated_text: By some it is held that the signifier is invalid by inference,
or, if there is no distinction of signifier-ness, there would be a rule of merit and demerit (<s>puṇya</s>, <s>pāpa</s>)
The relation, in the word “relation,” is fitness with respect to fitness,
made by me as the cognition of fitness, like the union of mother and son and the like

children.text: śabdaḥ kāraṇam arthasya sa hi tenopajanyate
children.translated_text: The word is the cause of the object, for indeed the object is produced by it,

children.text: tathā ca buddhiviṣayād arthāc chabdaḥ pratīyate
children.translated_text: and thus the word is apprehended from the object as the content of cognition

children.text: bhojanādy api manyante buddhyarthe yad asaṃbhavi
children.translated_text: Even eating and the like they consider impossible with respect to the object of cognition,

children.text: buddhyarthād eva buddhyarthe jāte tad api dṛśyate
children.translated_text: yet that too is seen to arise from the object of cognition, within the object of cognition
Even in impermanent things, permanence is maintained in the form of what is denotable,

children.text: anityatvaṃ svaśaktir vā sā ca nityān na bhidyate
children.translated_text: or impermanence is its own power, and that does not differ from the permanent
By the word there is a saṃskāra (impression/formation) of the object, with seen and unseen purposes,
how could that be effected without relation
It is not necessary that, in what is denotable, such an impression be so constituted,

children.text: dṛśyate na ca saṃbandhas tathābhūto vivakṣitaḥ
children.translated_text: and such a relation as that is not seen to be intended
When there is the status of being a cause of a cognition, relation is reasonable,
since, for the word with respect to the object, there, relation is inferred to exist

children.text: nitye+anitye+api vāpy arthe puruṣeṇa kathaṃ ca na
children.translated_text: How could there be relation, whether the object is permanent or impermanent,
by words whose relation has not been made; it cannot be effected by a person
In the designation of the meanings of words, the being of some other (entity) is figurative,
serving, in all conditions, for all of them, as the revealer of the form of the self
Just as a substance like crystal, through supports of different forms,
by the conjunction with its own power, attains a relation as if of that very form,

children.text: tadvac chabdo+api sattāyām asyaṃ pūrvaṃ vyavasthitaḥ
children.translated_text: so too a word, previously established in existence (<s>sattā</s>),
enters into relation through properties that are non-contradictory and contradictory
Thus, in neganda (things to be negated), for the construction of negation,
negation proceeds by figurative dependence on what is supported

children.text: ātmalābhasya janmākhyā satā labhyaṃ ca labhyate
children.translated_text: The acquisition of the self is termed birth; and what exists is obtainable and is obtained,

children.text: yadi saj jāyate kasmād athāsaj jāyate katham
children.translated_text: if what exists is born, why; and if what does not exist is born, how

children.text: sato hi gantur gamanaṃ sati gamye pravartate
children.translated_text: For the going of one who exists proceeds when the goal exists

children.text: gantṛvac cen na janmārtho na cet tadvan na jāyate
children.translated_text: If, like the goer, then the meaning of birth would not exist; if not, then, like that, it is not born
But by figurative usage (<s>upacāra</s>), the agent is spoken of, for the sake of initiating designation (<s>abhidhāna</s>)

children.text: punaś ca karmabhāvena tāṃ kriyāṃ ca tadāśrayām
children.translated_text: and again, in the capacity of being a patient (<s>karmabhāva</s>), that action and its substrate are (spoken of)
Therefore, in this way, only figurative existence (<s>upacāra-sattā</s>) is what the cases (such as) the lâ-affixes indicate,

children.text: janmanā tu virodhitvān mukhyā sattā na vidyate
children.translated_text: but primary existence (<s>mukhyā sattā</s>) is not admitted, because it would be opposed by birth
Bearing himself by himself, he is designated as ‘he exists,’

children.text: antarbhāvāc ca tenāsau karmaṇā na sakarmakaḥ
children.translated_text: and, because of inclusion (i.e., reflexive containment), therefore he is not, by the action, transitive (<s>sakarmaka</s>)

children.text: prāk ca sattābhisaṃbandhān mukhyā sattā kathaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: And before the connection with existence (<s>sattā</s>), how could there be primary existence,

children.text: asaṃś ca nāsteḥ kartā syād upacāras tu pūrvavat
children.translated_text: and if it is absent, there would be no agent; but figurative usage is as before
Therefore, among different properties, in those that are incompatible, there is a non-contradictory (existence),
resorted to by those various words merely for the manifesting of incompatibility
As a figurative (existence), which is of non-different time with respect to the objects and yet established in different times,
a cause of the application of all words, for all,

children.text: etāṃ sattāṃ padārtho hi na kaś cid ativartate
children.translated_text: no entity at all surpasses this existence (<s>sattā</s>) as its referent,

children.text: sā ca saṃpratisattāyāḥ pṛthag bhāṣye nidarśitā
children.translated_text: and this has been shown separately, distinct from present-existence (<s>saṃprati-sattā</s>), in the commentary
The practice (of speech) proceeds by determining a region, or a part of a region, or from elsewhere,
or by inversion, or by absence
Just as, owing to the defect of an organ, a cognition arises as if there were a superimposition of the measure,
so indeed is the notion that arises from an indicative mention (<s>uddeśa</s>) with respect to objects
Relying on a cognition with an appearance whose object is not entire, the word conveys the object
in another form, not in its own form explicitly determined
Standing on the common worldly path of description and designation,

children.text: jñānaṃ praty abhilāpaṃ ca sadṛśau bālapaṇḍitau
children.translated_text: both child and learned person are alike with respect to cognition and utterance
The purity of cognition, being of the form of all objects and without dependence (on an external support),

children.text: tato+apy asya parāṃ śuddhim eke prāhur arūpikām
children.translated_text: and beyond even that purity, some declare for it a higher, formless (<s>arūpika</s>) purity
For the perturbation of cognition is its following upon external forms,

children.text: kāluṣyam iva tat tasya saṃsarge vyatibhedajam
children.translated_text: and that is its impurity, arising from contact as a diversification

children.text: yathā ca jñānam ālekhād aśuddhau vyavatiṣṭhate
children.translated_text: And just as cognition, from the sketch (outline), remains in impurity,
so too the object, being connected with a support, is drawn away from its own nature

children.text: evam arthasya śabdasya jñānasya ca viparyaye
children.translated_text: Thus, in the mutual inversion of object, word, and cognition,
being and non-being, without difference, follow upon worldly usage
Just as, relying on being, its non-being is followed,
so, relying on non-being, its being too is followed
Non-being does not become being, being does not come to unreportability (<s>anupākhyatā</s>),
being and non-being, imagined as not other than a single self
Since non-being is unreportable, a cause is not a prover of it,

children.text: sopākhyasya tu bhāvasya kāraṇaṃ kiṃ kariṣyati
children.translated_text: but what will a cause accomplish for being, which is reportable

children.text: tasmāt sarvam abhāvo vā bhāvo vā sarvam iṣyate
children.translated_text: Therefore either all is non-being, or all is being, is accepted,

children.text: na tv avasthāntaraṃ kiṃ cid ekasmāt satyataḥ sthitam
children.translated_text: but there is no other status that stands established in a single reality

children.text: tasmān nābhāvam icchanti ye loke bhāvavādinaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore those in the world who are advocates of being do not desire non-being,
nor do those who are advocates of non-being take being as the mark of reality
And in the absolutely non-dual, where everything has a single mark by its own nature,
only in conceptual constructions are boundaries observed as manifold
For just as four states are imagined in what is inexpressible,
so too this duality, dependent on being and non-being, is imagined

children.text: avirodhī virodhī vā sann asan vāpi yuktitaḥ
children.translated_text: Whether non-contradictory or contradictory, existent or non-existent, by reasoning,
whether sequential or non-sequential, non-being does not become coherent

children.text: avirodhī virodhī vā sann asan vāpi tattvataḥ
children.translated_text: Whether non-contradictory or contradictory, existent or non-existent, in reality,

children.text: kramavān akramo vāpi tena bhāvo na vidyate
children.translated_text: whether sequential or non-sequential, therefore being is not found

children.text: abhāve triṣu kāleṣu na bhedasyāsti saṃbhavaḥ
children.translated_text: In non-being there is no possibility of difference in the three times,
and even if there were being, without that (difference), tri-temporality does not stand firm
The abandonment of the truth of the self is not reasonable from something else,

children.text: ātmatattvaṃ tu parataḥ svato vā nopakalpate
children.translated_text: but the truth of the self is not constituted from another or from itself

children.text: tattve virodho nānātva upakāro na kaś ca na
children.translated_text: In reality there is no contradiction, no multiplicity, no assistance whatsoever,
and when reality and non-reality are abandoned, worldly usage subsides

children.text: yatra draṣṭā ca dṛśyaṃ ca darśanaṃ cāvikalpitam
children.translated_text: Where the seer, the seen, and the seeing are undivided,
the Veda-knowers of the three ends of the Veda hold, only that object has reality

children.text: sāmānyaṃ vā viśeṣaṃ vā yasmād āhur viśeṣavat
children.translated_text: Because they say that the universal or the particular has the particular as its nature,

children.text: śabdās tasmād asatyeṣu bhedeṣv eva vyavasthitāḥ
children.translated_text: therefore words are established only in differences that are unreal

children.text: na hy abhāvasya sadbhāve bhāvasyātmā prahīyate
children.translated_text: For in the existence of non-being, the nature of being is not abandoned,
nor, in the non-existence of non-being, is the nature of being produced
The existence of the Śābaleya is not a defeater of the Báhuleya,
nor is a Báhuleya posited on the ground that ‘the Śābaleya does not exist’

children.text: abhāvo yadi vastu syāt tatreyaṃ syād vicāraṇā
children.translated_text: If non-being were an entity (<s>vastu</s>), then this examination would apply there,

children.text: tataś ca tadabhāve+api syād vicāryam idaṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: and then, even when that (non-being) were absent, this would again have to be examined

children.text: avastu syād atitaṃ yad vyavahārasya gocaraḥ
children.translated_text: What has gone past, which is the scope of worldly usage, would be a non-entity,

children.text: tatra vastugato bhedo na nirvacanam arhati
children.translated_text: there, a difference grounded in an entity does not deserve articulation
There is no footing for a word in a wordless object; for a cause there is no availability,

children.text: atha ca prāgasadbhāvaḥ kāraṇe sati dṛśyate
children.translated_text: and yet a prior existence is observed when the cause is present

children.text: kā tasya prāgavastheti vastvāśritam idaṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: What, then, is its prior state of being?—this again depends upon an entity,

children.text: prāg avastheti na hy etad dvayam apy asty avastuni
children.translated_text: but ‘a prior non-state’—neither of these two exists with respect to a non-entity
Nor, later, is there any basis for the statements ‘it is’ or ‘it is not’,

children.text: alaṃ syād apadasthānam etad vācaḥ pracakṣate
children.translated_text: this placement of speech in what lacks a word is rejected as useless, they declare

children.text: atyadbhutā tv iyaṃ vṛttir yad abhāgaṃ yad akramam
children.translated_text: But truly astonishing is this procedure, that of things which were formerly non-existent,
the inner reality of their own nature becomes manifest, though they have no parts and no sequence
Indeed, the entire worldly domain is posited by a construction of thought (<s>vikalpa</s>),
and ordinary transaction is prescribed as if by primary denotations of word-objects
Therefore those who maintain eternality attribute to it a power of being,

children.text: bhāvam eva kramaṃ prāhur na bhāvād aparaḥ kramaḥ
children.translated_text: and they declare sequence to be nothing but being; there is no sequence apart from being

children.text: kramān na yaugapadyasya kaś cid bhedo+asti tattvataḥ
children.translated_text: From sequence there is, in truth, no difference belonging to simultaneity,

children.text: yathaiva bhāvān nābhāvaḥ kaś cid anyo+avasīyate
children.translated_text: just as, from beings, no distinct non-being is ascertained

children.text: kālasyāpy aparaṃ kālaṃ nirdiśanty eva laukikāḥ
children.translated_text: Worldly people also indicate another time of time itself,
but by indication alone, separation is not thereby established
Projecting in thought a support, one does not gain a footing in non-being,

children.text: avastuṣv api notprekṣā kasya cit pratibadhyate
children.translated_text: and even with respect to non-entities, no one’s imaginative supposition is constrained
Therefore, by a division of powers, the single object, of the nature of being-and-non-being,
is eternal, and, in being denotable by words, appears multiform
And the worldly transaction is with word-objects that are conceptual constructs,
while in the treatise the word-object, for the sake of practical purpose, is analytically distinguished
Thus ends the specification of relation
3.4 Specification of predominant substances (<s>bhūyo-dravya</s>)
Having arisen from a form of combination, and extracted from the form of cognition,
they are separated in the treatise from the meaning of the sentence, like the meanings of base and affix
Being instrumental to correctness, and of the nature of what is inferred from the treatise,

children.text: ke cit padārthā vakṣyante saṃkṣepeṇa yathāgamam
children.translated_text: certain <s>padārthas</s> (categories/word-objects) will be stated briefly, according to the tradition
Where a pronoun is employed to mark an entity (<s>vastu</s>),

children.text: dravyam ity ucyate so+artho bhedyatvena vivakṣitaḥ
children.translated_text: that referent is called substance (<s>dravya</s>), intended as capable of differentiation
Thus ends the specification of predominant substances
3.5 Specification of qualities (<s>guṇa</s>)

children.text: saṃsargi bhedakaṃ yad yat savyāpāraṃ pratīyate
children.translated_text: Whatever, in a co-occurrent, is apprehended as differentiating and operative,
its being a quality (<s>guṇatva</s>) is stated in the treatise on account of its dependence
A quality that is taken up for what is not itself denoted as a substance,
is a differentiator for the sake of designation; its intensification is what is expressed
For nothing whatever that is principal attains prominence without a cause of difference,
nor does a word arrive at denotability
Not all causes of difference that exist in the principals,
are expressed by words of particularity, which signify exclusion
If, there, a particular were engaged in marking the entity,
its prominence, for lack of a rule, would have an unascertained cause
And everything is necessarily, in every respect, drawn out by rule,
by a co-occurrent condition, whether inferior or superior

children.text: nāpekṣate nimittaṃ ca prakarṣe vyāpṛtaṃ yadi
children.translated_text: And if, in prominence, it does not require a condition,

children.text: dravyasya syād upādānaṃ prakarṣaṃ praty anarthakam
children.translated_text: then the taking of substance would be purposeless with respect to prominence
Therefore a quality, being operative, depends upon its own prominence,
it indeed differentiates the substance-nature, instating its own prominence
Just as a formless substance is designated by another’s form,
so too the non-prominent is encompassed by the prominent as regards quality
Thus ends the specification of qualities
3.6 Specification of direction (<s>dik</s>)

children.text: dik sādhanaṃ kriyā kāla iti vastvabhidhāyinaḥ
children.translated_text: Direction, instrument, action, time—these, as denoters of entity (<s>vastu</s>),
are, as forms of power, utterly unsettled among the word-objects
That which is the cause of exclusion for what is to be delimited and what delimits,

children.text: ṛjv ity evaṃ yato+anyena vinā buddhiḥ pravartate
children.translated_text: since, as ‘straight’, cognition proceeds without reference to something else
The manifestation of the class-differences of actions, which has a locus,

children.text: sā svair upādhibhir bhinnā śaktir dig iti kathyate
children.translated_text: being distinguished by its own limiting adjuncts, is called ‘power’ as direction (<s>dik</s>)
In the higher-and-lower of shapes, resting upon differentiation of place,

children.text: tata eva prakalpete kramarūpe tu kālataḥ
children.translated_text: thereby they are constructed; but as regards sequence, by time

children.text: ākāśasya pradeśena bhāgaiś cānyaiḥ pṛthak pṛthak
children.translated_text: By the region of <s>ākāśa</s> (space) and by other distinct parts, each separately,
that (direction) is thereby posited as the condition for conjunctions and disjunctions

children.text: diśo vyavasthā deśānāṃ digvyavasthā na vidyate
children.translated_text: There is an ordering of directions; there is no fixed ordering of places as directions
For indeed the powers (<s>śakti</s>) of entities (<s>bhāva</s>) are efficacious through helpful influence
Among entities whose forms are turned away (i.e., opposed), ‘direction’ is denoted as ‘east’

children.text: pūrvabuddhir yato dik sā samākhyāmātram anyathā
children.translated_text: Because prior cognition is what (grounds) direction, that is merely a convention of naming; otherwise,

children.text: svāṅgād vyavasthā yā loke na tasyāṃ niyatā diśaḥ
children.translated_text: The arrangement in the world that is from one’s own limb (i.e., body) has no fixed directions

children.text: pratyaṅmukhasya yat paścāt tat purastād viparyaye
children.translated_text: What is behind one who faces west is in front of him when the orientation is reversed
A rule of place-arrangement does not stand fast within directions

children.text: rūḍham apy aparatvena pūrvam ity abhidhīyate
children.translated_text: Even what is established by usage is called ‘east’ in a secondary (relative) sense
Therefore, since it is spoken with masculine gender, a masculine-like status is not established

children.text: asminn arthe na śabdena prasavaḥ kva cid ucyate
children.translated_text: In this matter, no ‘birth/production’ is stated anywhere by the word

children.text: dikśakter abhidhāne tu niyataṃ diśi darśanam
children.translated_text: But when the power of direction is what is denoted, then the seeing is fixed in a direction,
just as, for the genitive (<s>ṣaṣṭhī</s>), in determining possession of life
By shadow and light, the parts of mountains and the like are constructed (distinguished),
but for entities that do not have those properties, a division into parts is not posited
For the partless atom, a ‘part’ of direction is prescribed,
they call that initial capacity the power of constructing parts

children.text: adeśāś cāpy abhāgāś ca niṣkramā nirupāśrayāḥ
children.translated_text: And entities are without place and without parts, without egress and without substrate,
yet, due to the form of conjunction (relational contact), a differentiation of powers is posited
The partless nature is alike for the atom and for the pot,

children.text: bhāgaḥ śaktyantaraṃ tatra parimāṇaṃ ca yat tayoḥ
children.translated_text: a ‘part’ there is a distinct power in them, and that (distinctness) which is measure for those two

children.text: yataḥ prakalpate bhedo bhedas tatrāpi dṛśyate
children.translated_text: Wherever a construction of difference is made, difference is also observed there
They consider as most improper a difference that ceases without being observed

children.text: sarvatra tasya kāryasya darśanād vibhur iṣyate
children.translated_text: Because this effect (of direction) is seen everywhere, it is held to be pervasive (all-pervading),

children.text: vibhutvam etad evāhur anyaḥ kāyavatāṃ vidhiḥ
children.translated_text: and they say that this very pervasiveness is its nature; a different rule obtains for embodied things
Like consciousness, the conceptual construction of direction and time stands in the world,

children.text: prakṛtiṃ prāṇināṃ tāṃ hi ko+anyathā sthāpayiṣyati
children.translated_text: for who would otherwise establish that nature of living beings?
If the natural order were reversed, there would be a confusion of worldly practices,

children.text: tasmāt tyajann imān bhāvān punar evāvalambate
children.translated_text: therefore, abandoning these (alternative) entities, one again relies upon (the established ones)

children.text: tasyās tu śakteḥ pūrvādi- bhedo bhāvāntarāśrayaḥ
children.translated_text: But the differentiation into east and the rest of that power is dependent upon other entities,
by that differentiation, direction, being distinct, is instituted merely for the sake of difference
And, as a delimitation, in the connection of dependence, there is a rule characterized by direction,

children.text: pūrvam as yeti ṣaṣṭhy eva dṛṣṭā dharmāntarāśraye
children.translated_text: indeed ‘it goes to the east’ is seen with the genitive alone, when there is a different locus of the property
The reversal of east and the others is unperceived when delimiters are confused,

children.text: ṛjv etad asyety etac ca liṅgaṃ na vyatikīryate
children.translated_text: and ‘straight’ and ‘it is this one’s’—these marks are not intermingled
Or a property of the internal organ appears outside in this way,

children.text: asyāṃ tv antarbahirbhāvaḥ prakriyāyāṃ na vidyate
children.translated_text: but in this procedure there is no internal–external status

children.text: ekatvam āsāṃ śaktīnāṃ nānātvaṃ veti kalpane
children.translated_text: In the supposition ‘are these powers one or many?’,
having recognized that it falls upon what is not an entity, one should not, in truth, take hold of it
In realities whose truth is beyond alternative construction (<s>vikalpa</s>),
those worldly usages that rest on convention are to be followed there
There is no oneness without manyness, nor the other without oneness,

children.text: paramārthe tayor eṣa bhedo+atyantaṃ na vidyate
children.translated_text: in the ultimate, this difference of the two is not absolutely found

children.text: na śaktīnāṃ tathā bhedo yathā śaktimatāṃ sthitiḥ
children.translated_text: Nor is there such a difference of powers as is the condition of the powerful (substances),

children.text: na ca laukikam ekatvaṃ tāsām ātmasu vidyate
children.translated_text: nor does worldly oneness belong to them in their own natures

children.text: naikatvaṃ vyavatiṣṭheta nānātvaṃ cen na kalpayet
children.translated_text: Oneness would not be established if one did not posit manyness,

children.text: nānātvaṃ cāvahīyeta yady ekatvaṃ na kalpayet
children.translated_text: and manyness would be diminished if one did not posit oneness
Thus ends the specification of direction
3.7 Specification of means (<s>sādhana</s>)
The capacity, in the completion of actions that are conjoined with their own substrate and likewise in another substrate,
is known as the means (<s>sādhana</s>)
Because the powerful (i.e., those possessing <s>śakti</s>) are numerous by conjecture, and the universe has manifold properties,

children.text: sarvadā sarvathā bhāvāt kva cit kiṃ cid vivakṣyate
children.translated_text: since entities always exist in every way, at times something particular is intended
And the practice regarding means depends upon the fixation in cognition,

children.text: sann asan vārtharūpeṣu bhedo buddhyā prakalpyate
children.translated_text: the distinction between real and unreal forms (of the object) is constructed by cognition
When, by a unity aimed at by cognition, a speaker groups the <s>Pañcāla</s>-s with the <s>Kuru</s>-s,
then, when he divides them again, the loss (of that unity) is apprehended
And those aspects of form that are furnished by words and have come into the scope of cognition,
he regards as means, as if they were perceptible, like <s>Kaṃsa</s> and the others
And having superimposed the form of the operation of cognition, the denoters,
construct differentiations of powers in the objects
In the manifest referent, the instrumentality of an action generated by word and the like,
is thus established as posited in the form of cognition
Both independence and dependence, and the form of sequence, were shown,
and even in entities devoid of striving, there is a dependence upon construction
All powers (<s>śakti</s>-s) and all powerful entities are, for those who speak of conjunction (relational contact),
entities; in those, with words not their own, instrumentality (<s>sādhanatva</s>) is determined
When the pot is the object of seeing, magnitude and the like are the means (<s>sādhana</s>),
when form is the object of seeing, <s>rūpatva</s> (form-ness) and the like are the means
The powerful entities, such as taste and so on, by their own universals and particulars,
are, in the world, grasped with fixity; those powers are (grasped) along with such substrates
The connection of sense-organ, object, mind, and agent is, in certain cases, the means,

children.text: yad yadā yadanugrāhi tat tadā tatra sādhanam
children.translated_text: whatever, whenever, in relation to whatever, is a supporter (promoter), that, then and there, is the means
But when denoted by their own words, that (entity) is said by the property (its own qualifier),
whereas the assistance (instrumentality) is apprehended only by case-endings and the like
The entities adopt the status of cause (occasion) for the sake of assistance (upakāra),

children.text: natir āvarjanety evaṃ siddhaḥ sādhanam iṣyate
children.translated_text: thus, ‘bending’ and ‘attracting’—such is the established means (<s>sādhana</s>) that is accepted

children.text: sa tebhyo vyatirikto vā teṣām ātmaiva vā tathā
children.translated_text: That (means) is either distinct from them, or else it is just their own self likewise,
adopting distinctness, it is posited as instrumentality
A showing (presentation) is (the means) in requesting, while a determination (decision) is immediately (the means) in resolving,
and the determination, at the outset of undertaking, is posited as instrumentality

children.text: pūrvasmin yā kriyā saiva parasmin sādhanaṃ matā
children.translated_text: The very action that is prior is regarded as the means in the subsequent (action),

children.text: saṃdarśane tu caitanyaṃ viśiṣṭaṃ sādhanaṃ viduḥ
children.translated_text: but in showing (perception), a qualified consciousness is known as the means
In mere production alone, agency (doership) is present for every <s>kāraka</s> (semantic role),
given an orientation to differences of operation, the possibility of instrumentality and the like arises

children.text: putrasya janmani yathā pitroḥ kartṛtvam ucyate
children.translated_text: As, at the birth of a son, agency is ascribed to the parents,

children.text: ayam asyām iyaṃ tv asmād iti bhedo vivakṣayā
children.translated_text: with the differentiation intended as ‘this is his, this is hers, and this is from him’
The agents of qualities and actions, whose powers are eclipsed by the agent (principal doer),

children.text: nyaktāyām api saṃpūrṇaiḥ svair vyāpāraiḥ samanvitāḥ
children.translated_text: even when eclipsed, being furnished with their own complete operations,
are known by instrumentality and the like, which track the differences of action,

children.text: svātantryam uttaraṃ labdhvā pradhāne yānti kartṛtām
children.translated_text: and, having obtained a later independence, they attain agency in the principal (role)

children.text: yathā rājñā niyukteṣu yoddhṛtvaṃ yoddhṛṣu sthitam
children.translated_text: Just as, when warriors are commissioned by the king, the state of ‘being fighters’ resides in the fighters,

children.text: teṣu vṛttau tu labhate rājā jayaparājayau
children.translated_text: yet in their performance the king obtains victory and defeat,
so, when all (subsidiary factors) are commissioned by the agent and act toward one purpose,
agency, subsequent to instrumentality and the rest, is not incompatible

children.text: anāśrite tu vyāpāre nimittaṃ hetur iṣyate
children.translated_text: But when an operation is not (yet) grounded (in a substrate), the cause is held to be a <s>nimitta</s> (occasion),
and in the definitions they understand a definition as the limiting condition up to what is grounded
A cause whose scope is substance and the like is the <s>kāraka</s> with a fixed action,
the agent, depending upon another agent, is held to be the cause in respect of the action

children.text: kriyāyai karaṇaṃ tasya dṛṣṭaḥ pratinidhis tathā
children.translated_text: For the action, the instrument is its representative (substitute) that is observed,

children.text: hetvarthā tu kriyā tasmān na sa pratinidhīyate
children.translated_text: but the action has the purpose of the cause; therefore that (cause) is not represented (by another)
By contrariety and conformity (inverse and direct correlation), the cause establishes the object,
its being-for-that (tādarthya), through conformity, follows from its causality
Everywhere, a natural power persists as long as the substance exists,
but at the time of action, from the substrate, it becomes operative as a helper
The power of a wall is in covering, of these others (e.g., axe, etc.) in rending,

children.text: sarvadā sa tu san dharmaḥ kriyākāle nirūpyate
children.translated_text: and that property, though always existing, is determined at the time of action
Just as the nooses of the <s>Vāruṇa</s>-s, which are conjoined to their own limbs,
become manifest for those intent on victory, so the powers of substances
When, by its own sharpness, heaviness, hardness, and shape, a sword,

children.text: chedyaṃ prati vyāpriyate śaktimān gṛhyate tadā
children.translated_text: is engaged with what is to be cut, then the powerful entity is apprehended

children.text: prāṅ nimittāntarodbhūtaṃ kriyāyāḥ kaiś cid iṣyate
children.translated_text: Some hold as the means something prior that arises on the disappearance of another occasion,

children.text: sādhanaṃ sahajaṃ kaiś cit kriyānyaiḥ pūrvam iṣyate
children.translated_text: others hold the innate means, others (hold) earlier actions different from the (present) action

children.text: pravṛttir eva prathamaṃ kva cid apy anapāśritā
children.translated_text: In some cases, the very first activity, even ungrounded (in a prior factor),
draws along the powers, in a single substrate, like a current

children.text: apūrvaṃ kālaśaktiṃ vā kriyāṃ vā kālam eva vā
children.translated_text: Some say ‘the unseen (<s>apūrva</s>), or the power of time, or the action, or time itself’,

children.text: tam evamlaksanam bhāvam ke cid āhuh katham ca na
children.translated_text: or ‘that very thing with such-and-such a mark is the entity’—how indeed would it not be so? (they argue)
The six powers are eternal; in other things they possess both difference and non-difference,
and, for the accomplishment of action, they are present in things like a class (universal)
By distinctions such as form of substance and the like, they appear as if without limit,

children.text: dṛśyante tattvam āsāṃ tu ṣaṭ śaktīr nātivartate
children.translated_text: but their reality does not exceed six powers
Because of the difference of occasions (<s>nimitta</s>-s), a single power is apprehended as divided,
they say that agency, sixfold, is the foundation of its activity

children.text: tattve vā vyatireke vā vyatiriktaṃ tad ucyate
children.translated_text: Whether in the (ultimate) reality or in distinction from it, that (view) is called distinct,
the world, whose means of knowledge is word, is followed by the scripture
But in the highest truth there is no oneness having the characteristic of separateness,
rather, as the form of separateness-and-oneness, reality itself is made manifest

children.text: yat pṛthaktvam asaṃdigdhaṃ tad ekatvān na bhidyate
children.translated_text: That separateness which is not doubtful is not sundered by oneness,

children.text: yad ekatvam asaṃdigdhaṃ tat pṛthaktvān na bhidyate
children.translated_text: and that oneness which is not doubtful is not sundered by separateness

children.text: dyauḥ kṣamā vāyur ādityaḥ sāgarāḥ sarito diśaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Dyauḥ</s> (heaven), earth, wind, the sun, the oceans, the rivers, the directions,
are outwardly situated portions of the principle of the internal organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa-tattva</s>)
As having the form of temporal segmentation, that very one abides as one,

children.text: sa hy apūrvāparo bhāvaḥ kramarūpeṇa lakṣyate
children.translated_text: for that existence, being without prior-and-subsequent (<s>apūrva</s>-apara), is marked as sequence
For indeed, even without negative concomitance, when negative concomitance and positive concomitance are absent,
the positive concomitance of objects like a tree is observed; therefore a distinct meaning of the case-ending (<s>vibhakti-artha</s>) is posited
The common factor is the <s>kāraka</s>; for it, the first-and-following seven (case-relations) are sources of differentiation,
the six, by differentiation such as action-name (<s>karman</s>, etc.), while the remaining distinction is the seventh (locative)
<s>karmādhikāraḥ</s> (Section on the object of action)

children.text: nirvartyaṃ ca vikāryaṃ ca prāpyaṃ ceti tridhā matam
children.translated_text: What is to be produced and what is to be modified and what is to be obtained—these are held to be threefold,
among these, the most-desired object is the action; but another (class) is imagined as fourfold

children.text: audāsīnyena yat prāpyaṃ yac ca kartur anīpsitam
children.translated_text: What is to be obtained with indifference, and what is not desired by the agent,

children.text: saṃjñāntarair anākhyātaṃ yad yac cāpy anyapūrvakam
children.translated_text: what is not denoted by other technical names, and what moreover is unprecedented (having no prior instance),
Whether present or not present, the <s>prakṛti</s> (substrate/natural basis) is a transformer;
what does not rely on it is declared to be ‘to-be-produced’ (nirvartya)

children.text: prakṛtes tu vivakṣāyāṃ vikāryaṃ kaiś cid anyathā
children.translated_text: But when <s>prakṛti</s> is intended, some call it ‘to-be-modified’ (vikārya) otherwise;

children.text: nirvartyaṃ ca vikāryaṃ ca karma śāstre pradarśitam
children.translated_text: both ‘to-be-produced’ and ‘to-be-modified’ action are exhibited in the śāstra

children.text: yad asaj jāyate sad vā janmanā yat prakāśyate
children.translated_text: What is generated as non-existent or as existent, or what is made manifest by birth,

children.text: tan nirvartyaṃ vikāryaṃ ca karma dvedhā vyavasthitam
children.translated_text: that action is established twofold as ‘to-be-produced’ and ‘to-be-modified’
Partly arising from the cutting off of the substrate, like ash from wood and the like,
partly by the arising of a different property, like the transformation of gold and the like

children.text: kriyākṛtā viśeṣāṇāṃ siddhir yatra na gamyate
children.translated_text: Where the accomplishment of particulars is not apprehended as made by the activity,

children.text: darśanād anumānād vā tat prāpyam iti kathyate
children.translated_text: from perception or from inference that is called ‘to-be-obtained’ (prāpya)
Acquisition of particularity is found everywhere by perception and the like,
for some, the success of manifestation of that is in objects such as the field of sight
Approach to appearance (apprehension), manifestation, and firmness—thus are the action’s,
the particulars of what is to be obtained are fixed upon the accomplishment of the activity
In what is to be produced and the like, having first experienced independence,
the action is then completed in the operation of other agents
Even when the discrimination of that operation exists, established in its own operation,
the action, being enjoined, at times obtains rules that rely on the śāstra
An action whose sending (impulsion) has ceased remains in its own part of activity,
when the actionhood is ceasing, it is established in its own agency
They know those as merely other roots, like pac, sidhi, and so on,
despite difference, because of similarity of form, there is the supposition of oneness
In a part and in a collection, activities such as ‘cook’ (pac) proceed by their own nature,
endowed with a similar form
Nyagbhāvanā and nyagbhavana are understood with the root ruh ‘to grow’ as pure,
nyagbhāvanā and nyagbhavana are also accepted with the ṇyant (causative) form

children.text: avasthāṃ pañcamīm āhur ṇyante tāṃ karmakartari
children.translated_text: They call the fifth state, in causatives (ṇyant), that [state] where the object is the agent,
because the sending (impulsion) of the root has ceased, the affix ṇi is said in the primary meaning

children.text: bravīti pacater arthaṃ sidhyatir na vinā ṇicā
children.translated_text: He says that the meaning of pac (‘to cook’) is of siddhi (‘to accomplish’) not without the causative,

children.text: sa ṇyantaḥ pacater arthe prākṛte vyavatiṣṭhate
children.translated_text: thus the causative (ṇyant), in the meaning of pac, stands in the primary sense

children.text: keṣāṃ cid devadattāder vyāpāro yaḥ sakarmake
children.translated_text: For some, the operation of <s>Devadatta</s> and the like, which is transitive,
is intended even without <s>Devadatta</s> and the like, in regard to things like a mat
An action whose sending has ceased acts as the motivator of its own agent,
when there is relation to another sending, in the causative (ṇyant) it is denoted by ‘le’
Where, in things like ‘similar’, the object’s agency is apprehended,
there, in the falling-into or causing-to-fall-into (āpatty-āpādana), objecthood is with respect to the action

children.text: kutaś cid āhṛtya padam evaṃ ca parikalpane
children.translated_text: By bringing a word from somewhere, and by such a construction,
there could be the status of making a locus for the object for those denoting perception and the like
Where there is the perception of a particular, there the activity is determined,

children.text: kriyāvyavasthā tv anyeṣāṃ śabdair eva prakāśyate
children.translated_text: but for others, the determination of activity is made known only by words
For time, being, path, and place, when conjoined with other activities included within them,
objecthood arises in all the intransitives

children.text: ādhāratvam iva prāptās te punar dravyakarmasu
children.translated_text: Having attained, as it were, the status of substratum, then again, in substance-actions,
time and the like, of a different class, proceed to subsequent objecthood

children.text: atas taiḥ karmabhir dhātur yukto+adravyair akarmakaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, by those actions the root, being joined with non-substances and being intransitive,

children.text: lasya karmaṇi bhāve ca nimittatvāya kalpate
children.translated_text: in the ‘karmaṇi’ and ‘bhāva’ senses of the affix ‘las’ is assumed to have the status of occasion (<s>nimitta</s>)
And every unexpressed object (of action) is apprehended as of a different class
By the difference in the specification of the verb-meaning, that indeed is said to be the most desired (nepsitatama),
What is called the principal object (pradhāna-karma) is that which is the instigator (prayojaka) of the action,

children.text: tatsiddhaye kriyāyuktam anyat tv akathitaṃ smṛtam
children.translated_text: for the accomplishment of that, something else, connected with the action, is remembered as unexpressed (akathita)
As in duhy- and the like, and in nay- and the like, objecthood rests on the unexpressed,
but when the finite verb is not employed, by rule the remainder (śeṣa) is accepted
For duhy- and the like, whose causative sense (ṇij-artha) is included within them, objecthood is established by the preceding (discussion),
and likewise the rule for the causative (ṇijanta)
Just as for the instrument (karaṇa) there is no reliance on superiority within its own class,

children.text: karmaṇo+api svakakṣyāyāṃ na syād atiśayas tathā
children.translated_text: so too for the object (karma), within its own class, there should not be excess

children.text: karmaṇas tv āptum iṣṭatva āśrite+atiśayo yataḥ
children.translated_text: But since superiority is grounded in the desirability of attaining the object,
therefore, relying on that, there is an absolute distinction from the former object

children.text: ṇijante ca yathā kartā sakriyaḥ san prayujyate
children.translated_text: And as in the causative (ṇijanta) the agent (kartṛ), being active, is employed,

children.text: na duhyādau tathā kartā niṣkriyo+api prayujyate
children.translated_text: not so in duhy- and the like is the agent, even when inactive, employed

children.text: bhedavākyaṃ tu yan ṇyante nīduhiprakṛtau ca yat
children.translated_text: But the sentence of distinction that is in the causative (ṇyanta) and that which is in the bases nī- and duhi-,
because of the difference of the word, has no contact with that verb-root
Just as one single ablative (apādāna) is shown in the śāstra in distinct ways,
so too one and the same object (karma) is taught in distinct ways

children.text: nirvartyo vā vikāryo vā prāpyo vā sādhanāśrayaḥ
children.translated_text: Whether to be produced, or to be modified, or to be attained, as the locus of the means,
because only actions have the status of something to be accomplished, it is designated as already-formed (siddha-rūpa)
Just as, with respect to what is harmful, from greediness the agent’s desire arises,
so too, with respect to poisons and the like, from fear and the rest, he sets about
Where, between principal and non-principal, of substance and of action, separately,
the power (śakti) resides in a quality (guṇa) as its substratum, there the principal follows it
Power whose scope is the principal is expressed by an affix (pratyaya),

children.text: yadā guṇe tadā tadvad anuktāpi prakāśate
children.translated_text: when it belongs to a quality, then likewise, even if unexpressed, it becomes manifest

children.text: pacāv anuktaṃ yat karma ktvānte bhāvābhidhāyini
children.translated_text: The object which is unexpressed with pac- (‘cook’), when at the end of ktvā the affix denotes a state (bhāva),

children.text: bhujau śaktyantare+apy ukte tat taddharma prakāśate
children.translated_text: in bhuj- (‘enjoy/eat’), even when another power is stated, that property manifests

children.text: iṣeś ca gamisaṃsparśād grāme yo lo vidhīyate
children.translated_text: And the lopa (elision) which is prescribed in the village (grāma) because of the contact of iṣ- (‘desire’) with gam- (‘go’),
there, by the very desirer (iṣiṇa) the non-enjoyment (nirbhoga) of the action of going is effected

children.text: paktvā bhujyata ity atra keṣāṃ cin na vyapekṣate
children.translated_text: In the expression ‘having cooked, it is eaten,’ in that context he does not expect, for some,
‘he cooks the porridge’—that one is inferred from implication
Likewise, the object which is firmly intended that is denoted in a finite-verb ending (tiṅ-anta),
even though, at the end of ktvā, there is an adverbial sense (adhikaraṇa), they do not desire the locative there

children.text: yan nirvṛttāśrayaṃ karma prāpter apracitaṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: That object whose substratum has been completed, not accumulating again for attainment,
being distinguished by falling under the domain of something edible and the like, that is intended
Because of the inclusion of the function of the root in another sense, within the root-meaning,
on account of established usage and because it is not intended to be expressed, an action without an object (akarmika) [occurs] for the object

children.text: bhedā ya ete catvāraḥ sāmānyena pradarśitāḥ
children.translated_text: These four distinctions have been shown in general,
they are then further divided in many ways according to differences such as occasion (nimitta) and so on
Thus ends the section on the object (karma)
The section on the instrument (karaṇa) [begins]
When, immediately after the completion of the action,

children.text: vivakṣyate yadā tatra karaṇatvaṃ tadā smṛtam
children.translated_text: that by whose operation it is intended to be expressed, then it is remembered as instrumentality (karaṇatva)

children.text: vastutas tad anirdeśyaṃ na hi vastu vyavasthitam
children.translated_text: In reality that is indescribable as a thing, for the thing is not fixed,

children.text: sthālyā pacyata ity eṣā vivakṣā dṛśyate yataḥ
children.translated_text: since the intention ‘it is cooked in the pot’ is observed

children.text: karaṇeṣu tu saṃskāram ārabhante punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: But with respect to instruments they repeatedly initiate refinement (saṃskāra),
and particular modes of application too, for the establishment of the principal

children.text: svakakṣyāsu prakarṣaś ca karaṇānāṃ na vidyate
children.translated_text: Within their own classes there is no superiority of the instruments,
but their characterization there is, as it were, a superiority derived from dependence on something else
Even though independent, the prompters (prayoktṛs) render service from a distance,
for everyone’s activity is mediated by the instrument

children.text: kriyāsiddhau prakarṣo+ayaṃ nyagbhāvas tv eva kartari
children.translated_text: This is the preeminence in the success of the action, while lowness (nyagbhāva) is indeed in the agent,

children.text: siddhau satyāṃ hi sāmānyaṃ sādhakatvaṃ prakṛṣyate
children.translated_text: for when success is present, it is the generality—being a means—that is exalted

children.text: asyādīnāṃ tu kartṛtve taikṣṇyādi karaṇaṃ viduḥ
children.translated_text: But as for things like a sword and the like, in agency they know sharpness and so on to be the instrument,
and when sharpness and the like are independent, the nature is established as twofold

children.text: ātmabhede+api saty evam eko+arthaḥ sa tathā sthitaḥ
children.translated_text: Even when there is a difference of selves in this way, the one meaning remains thus established,
therefore, because of its being based upon that, even amid difference, agency is a disqualifier
And just as instrumentality is apprehended through contact (saṃnidhāna),
so too, even without contact, it is apprehended because the action is accomplished

children.text: stokasya vābhinirvṛtter anirvṛtteś ca tasya vā
children.translated_text: They declare the well-known instrumentality of smallness and the like, either because of the completion of a small portion,
or because of the non-completion of that same [portion]

children.text: dharmāṇāṃ tadvatā bhedād abhedāc ca viśiṣyate
children.translated_text: It is specified by difference and non-difference of the properties that inhere in it,
just as it is divided by the particular delimitation of the scope of the action
Thus ends the section on the instrument (karaṇa)
The section on the agent (<s>kartr</s>)
Because, prior to anything else, he acquires power from another, and also because of the bringing about of lowness (subordination),
since the activity depends on that [other], and because those who have set about acting are caused to desist,
because the substitute (representative) is not perceptible, and because distinct perception is seen,

children.text: ārād apy upakāritve svātantryaṃ kartur ucyate
children.translated_text: even when help is rendered from afar, independence is predicated of the agent

children.text: dharmair abhyuditaiḥ śabde niyamo na tu vastuni
children.translated_text: By properties that have arisen in the word there is restriction, not in the thing;
when there is the intention to express the agent’s property, the agent is understood from the word
For one and the same entity, through determinations in cognition and when difference is imagined,
agenthood, instrumentality, and objecthood arise
Prior to production, non-existence depends upon a state of cognition,
being not distinguished from an existent other, one becomes the agent from the time of birth (arising)
When a cause is established in the condition of an effect,
having obtained the word ‘effect,’ it comes to be as an effect
Just as the coiling (kuṇḍalī-bhāva) of a snake, or the completeness of busy (engaged) things,
so indeed some declare the very form of birth (origin) for existents
That effect which proceeds from causes whose source has been differentiated,
its own class-nature (species) is established even as a particular (individual) of that

children.text: bhāveṣv eva padanyāsaḥ prajñāyā vāca eva vā
children.translated_text: The placing of words is only upon existents, or upon cognition, or upon speech alone;

children.text: nāstīty apy apade nāsti na ca sad bhidyate tataḥ
children.translated_text: ‘it is not’—even without a word it is not; nor is the existent thereby divided
Cognition and word operate with things as they are,

children.text: teṣām anyena tattvena vyavahāro na vidyate
children.translated_text: there is no usage of them with some other reality

children.text: ākāśasya yathā bhedaś chāyāyāś calanaṃ yathā
children.translated_text: Just as the division of space, just as the movement of a shadow,

children.text: janmanāśāv abhede+api tathā kaiś cit prakalpitau
children.translated_text: so too, despite the non-difference of birth and destruction, some have imagined them
Just as the non-existence of space is defined by a material form as its opposite (i.e., by form),
so likewise the non-existence of form relies upon the non-existent (immaterial) space
Just as, by their relevant operations directed to that purpose, what is action in essence is designated,
by the apprehension of non-difference this is the sequence of effect and cause

children.text: vikāro janmanaḥ kartā prakṛtir veti saṃśaye
children.translated_text: When there is doubt whether the transformation is the agent’s or the nature’s (substrate’s),
the cognition of the observers is distinguished by observations of signs (indicia)

children.text: kḷpi saṃpadyamāne yā caturthī sā vikārataḥ
children.translated_text: When the dative (caturthī) is employed with ‘becoming’ (<s>saṃpadyamāna</s>), that [is] by reason of transformation,
in ‘in the lump of gold’ denoting the substrate, the statement relies upon the earrings (as the emergent form)
