children.text: vākye saṃpadyateḥ kartā saṅghaś cvyantasya kathyate
children.translated_text: In the sentence, the agent of ‘becoming’ is called the aggregate when [the parts] are assembling,
in usage [we say] ‘they become an aggregate’; thus, the independence of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>-s

children.text: atvaṃ saṃpadyate yas tvaṃ na tasmin yuṣmadāśrayā
children.translated_text: He who becomes ‘you-ness’ (atvaṃ saṃpadyate) is not, in that, dependent upon ‘you’ (the addressee);
there is activity of the person, he is prescribed as the natural (original) one
Not abandoning the prior state while touching the later property,
as if the very nature of the thing were congealed, it is said to be being born

children.text: savyāpārataraḥ kaś cit kva cid dharmaḥ pratīyate
children.translated_text: Some property is apprehended as more pervaded by activity in certain cases,
and the powers of entities, though possessed of difference, are conjoined
In the contrary case, the person’s functioning with a reversed object would be inferred,

children.text: gamyeta sādhanaṃ hy atra savyāpāraṃ pratīyate
children.translated_text: for here the means would be apprehended as indeed possessed of activity

children.text: tvam anyo bhavasīty eṣā tatra syāt parikalpanā
children.translated_text: ‘You become other than you’—such an imagining would occur there,

children.text: rājñi bhṛtyatvamāpanne yathā tadvad gatir bhavet
children.translated_text: as when a servant attains kingship; similar would be the course
Upon the accomplishment of action by supposition (consideration), being resorted to as agent,
in an action to be accomplished by oneself, he is the instigator of the means
In mere application there is subordination, but on account of independence it is indeed established,
he becomes not distinguished from others who are independent and free from doubt
All, indeed, proceed from causes (occasions) for the sake of their own nature,
and conformity to intention is even for the manifestation of one’s own purpose
Thus ends the section on the agent (<s>kartr</s>)
The section on the cause (<s>hetu</s>)
When, commanding and requesting, one performs, and also carries out things suitable thereto,
the agent himself attains, as prescribed in the treatise, the designation ‘cause’ (<s>hetu</s>)

children.text: dravyamātrasya tu praiṣe pṛcchyāder loḍ vidhīyate
children.translated_text: But when the injunction is of mere substance, the optative/imperative (<s>loṭ</s>) is prescribed for asking and the like,

children.text: sakriyasya prayogas tu yadā sa viṣayo ṇicaḥ
children.translated_text: when the domain is of one possessing activity, then the causative (<s>ṇic</s>) is the operation
In commanding, because of independence with respect to property and action, he, having gone into the state of object (karmatā),
by rule, on account of the designation ‘object’ (<s>karman</s>), is expressed by his own function

children.text: kriyāyāḥ prerakaṃ karma hetuḥ kartuḥ prayojakaḥ
children.translated_text: The object that impels the action is the cause (<s>hetu</s>); the instigator is the agent,
and with regard to the object, by the apprehensions of the arising of action, refinement (<s>saṃskāra</s>), and attainment
Thus ends the section on the cause (<s>hetu</s>)
The section on the recipient (<s>saṃpradāna</s>)
Because the agent is not denied, the desired object in the act of relinquishment is an accessory,
and through prompting and consent it attains the status of recipient (<s>saṃpradāna</s>)
When there is the designation ‘object’ (<s>karman</s>) in the sense of cause, or else when it is an auxiliary (<s>śeṣa</s>) factor,
in objects such as desire, purpose, and the like, it is termed ‘recipient’ by the treatise

children.text: bhedasya ca vivakṣāyāṃ pūrvāṃ pūrvāṃ kriyāṃ prati
children.translated_text: And when differentiation is intended, with respect to each preceding action,
because the part belonging to another has the status of object (<s>karman</s>), the taking of the action is not performed
But when, in an aggregate of actions, oneness is intended,
then, by connection with the action, the object (<s>karman</s>) is figuratively designated by its own name
And the intention of difference and non-difference is fixed by the very nature (of things),
therefore, in the case where motion-meaning is the object (<s>gatyartha-karmatva</s>), deviation is not observed

children.text: vikalpenaiva sarvatra saṃjñe syātām ubhe yadi
children.translated_text: If, everywhere, both designations were by mere option,

children.text: ārambheṇa na yogasya pratyākhyānaṃ samaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: then the rejection of the connection (yoga) would not be on a par with the initiation
In what is to be abandoned, of the form of relinquishment, and in what is to be attained, the perception of contact (connection),

children.text: āsthitaṃ karma yat tatra dvairūpyaṃ bhajate kriyā
children.translated_text: that object (<s>karman</s>) which is established there causes the action to assume a dual form
Thus ends the section on the recipient (<s>saṃpradāna</s>)
The section on the source/ablative (<s>apādāna</s>)
The <s>apādāna</s> is said to be threefold: (1) that which has a specified domain, (2) that which has an adopted (taken up) domain,
and (3) that which has an action as its object of expectation

children.text: saṃyogabhedād bhinnātmā gamir eva bhramir yathā
children.translated_text: Because of a difference of conjunction, the mover is of a distinct nature from the spinner, as,
though having a fixed limit, departure too is conjoined with a non-fixed (object)

children.text: dravyasvabhāvo na dhrauvyam iti sūtre pratīyate
children.translated_text: It is understood in the sūtra that ‘the nature of a substance is not fixity’,

children.text: apāyaviṣayaṃ dhrauvyaṃ yat tu tāvad vivakṣitam
children.translated_text: but what is intended as ‘fixity’ is, for the time being, fixity with respect to the domain of departure

children.text: saraṇe devadattasya dhrauvyaṃ pāte tu vājinaḥ
children.translated_text: In the moving, fixity belongs to <s>Devadatta</s>; in the falling, to the horse,
that which is pervaded by departure—they declare its non-fixity

children.text: ubhāv apy adhruvau meṣau yady apy ubhayakarmaje
children.translated_text: Both rams are indeed non-fixed, even if they are born of a twofold action,

children.text: vibhāge pravibhakte tu kriye tatra vivakṣite
children.translated_text: when separation is intended—division being effected with respect to the action
A distinct boundedness (limit) dependent on the other ram’s action, separately for each ram,

children.text: meṣayoḥ svakriyāpekṣaṃ kartṛtvaṃ ca pṛthak pṛthak
children.translated_text: and, dependent on each one’s own action, agency also, separately for each ram

children.text: abhedena kriyaikā tu dvisādhyā ced vivakṣitā
children.translated_text: But if a single action, though one, is intended as to be accomplished by two,

children.text: meṣāv apāye kartārau yady anyo vidyate+avadhiḥ
children.translated_text: the two rams are agents in departure, provided there is another limit

children.text: gatir vinā tv avadhinā nāpāya iti gamyate
children.translated_text: Indeed, it is concluded that there is no departure without a limit of motion,

children.text: vṛkṣasya parṇaṃ patatīty evaṃ bhāṣye nidarśitam
children.translated_text: as is illustrated in the commentary by ‘the leaf of the tree falls’
Difference and non-difference, separateness, and persistence—being mutually opposed—

children.text: yugapan na vivakṣyante sarve dharmā balāhake
children.translated_text: are not all intended simultaneously, with respect to all properties, in a hailstorm
In ‘he pierces with a bow,’ since instrumentality would not obtain without the intention of departure,

children.text: karaṇatvaṃ yato nāsti tasmāt tad ubhayaṃ saha
children.translated_text: therefore those two (the instrument and the departure) are together (to be intended)

children.text: ekaiva vā satī śaktir dvirūpā vyavatiṣṭhate
children.translated_text: Or, a single power, though one, stands established as twofold,
there, between the two designations, the one is overridden by the superior cause, the other (by the inferior)

children.text: nirdhāraṇe vibhakte yo bhītrādīnāṃ ca yo vidhiḥ
children.translated_text: In determination, in separation, and in the rules regarding fear and the like,
the <s>apādāna</s> requiring an adopted or an expected (limit) is taught for the understanding of the unlearned
Thus ends the section on the source/ablative (<s>apādāna</s>)
The section on the locus (<s>adhikaraṇa</s>)
That which, not directly, bears the action, being separated from agent and object,
and assists in the accomplishment of the action, is called ‘locus’ (<s>adhikaraṇa</s>) in the treatise
And the identity of adhesion (upāśleṣa) in sesame-seed, ether, and pot, etc.,
yet the modes of assistance differ for things conjoined and for things co-inherent
Indestructibility of heaviness, independence in constraint,
delimitation by a particular direction—such are causes of difference
Some, by positing differentiation of place, hold that space alone,
is the primary capacity as substrate for all things in conjunction

children.text: idam atreti bhāvānām abhāvān na prakalpate
children.translated_text: The designation ‘this is here’ for entities is not posited for non-entities,
they declare that that designation has space as its cause
Actions are divided by time; all forms are by space,
and this much difference, indeed, is bound up with non-difference

children.text: yady apy upavasir deśa- viśeṣam anurudhyate
children.translated_text: Even though ‘to fast’ (<s>upavas</s>) follows a particular place,
yet, by the rule governing the application of words, it relies upon time itself
Therefore, even when ‘dwelling’ (<s>vas</s>) is not employed, place is the locus (<s>adhikaraṇa</s>),
and the action ‘to fast’ (<s>upavas</s>) is remembered as unexpressed, such as a three-night rite
Thus ends the section on the locus (<s>adhikaraṇa</s>)
The section on the remainder/accessory (<s>śeṣa</s>)
A relation other than the <s>kāraka</s>-s, presupposing the action and the <s>kāraka</s>-s,
is denoted, whether the action is heard (explicit) or unheard (implicit)
Though it is twofold, because it exists for the sake of another, it is distinguished among the secondary factors (<s>guṇa</s>),
and, being denoted there, it is also applied even with respect to the principal
The restriction of cause (nimitta) for relation is not grasped from the word alone,
but, by the words called <s>karmapravacanīya</s>-s, that specific usage is secured
And when the instruments are specified, while the action is being heard again,
the genitive is prescribed, word by word, for the cessation of the compound
When the participle (<s>niṣṭhā</s>) relates to the object (<s>karman</s>), the genitive is prohibited,
and, with the genitive having the mark of a <s>śeṣa</s>, a compound is not admitted there
When, of something designated otherwise, a distinctness arises elsewhere,

children.text: vyatirekaḥ sa dharmau dvau labhate viṣayāntare
children.translated_text: that separation obtains two properties in a different domain

children.text: prādhānyaṃ svaguṇe labdhvā pradhāne yāti śeṣatām
children.translated_text: Having gained primacy in its own attribute, it goes to the state of <s>śeṣa</s> (accessory) with respect to the principal,
therefore, in co-association and in its own association, its being-principal is not diminished
Thus ends the section on the remainder/accessory (<s>śeṣa</s>)
They understand vocative address (<s>saṃbodhana</s>) to be merely the turning-toward of one who is established,
for the object itself, once made present to one’s regard, is employed in actions

children.text: saṃbodhanaṃ na vākyārtha iti pūrvebhya āgamaḥ
children.translated_text: “Vocative is not the sentence-meaning”—such is the tradition from the predecessors,
the meanings of the case-endings, by designation, are extracted apart from the sentence-meaning
From the statement concerning the case-meaning in the <s>avyayībhāva</s> (indeclinable compound), let this be inferred:
the case-meaning is other than the substance, and that is expressed by the indeclinable

children.text: dravyaṃ tu yad yathābhūtaṃ tad atyantaṃ tathā bhavet
children.translated_text: But a substance, whatever it is like, remains entirely such,
and even in connection with an action, its nature as substance is not lost

children.text: tasmād yat karaṇaṃ dravyaṃ tat karma na punar bhavet
children.translated_text: Therefore, that which is an instrument and a substance does not become an object (<s>karman</s>) again,
otherwise the otherness of everything would result from its substantial nature
Thus ends the introduction to means/instruments (<s>sādhana</s>)
3.8: Introduction to action (<s>kriyā</s>)
As long as what is established or not established is spoken of as to-be-accomplished,
because it has the form of a sequence based on supports, that is apprehended as ‘action’ (<s>kriyā</s>)
By the relation of effect and cause, “it sounds”—thus the sequence based on supports; but

children.text: dhvaniḥ kramanivṛttau tu dhvanir ity eva kathyate
children.translated_text: when the sequence ceases, it is spoken of simply as “sound”

children.text: śvete śvetata ity etac chvetatvena prakāśate
children.translated_text: In the expression “in the white, whiteness,” this is manifested as “by whiteness,”
and, because it has the form of a sequence based on supports, designation proceeds
A cluster with parts that function as attributes (<s>guṇa</s>), whose births are sequential,
is called ‘action’ (<s>kriyā</s>) through a conceptualized non-difference in intellect
That cluster, being what belongs to that, is completed into sub-kinds within clusters,
then, upon the differentiation, there is the possibility of temporal difference

children.text: kramāt sadasatāṃ teṣām ātmāno na samūhinām
children.translated_text: By sequence they (the parts) are existent or non-existent, not the cluster-holders,
they enter into relation, through eye and the like, with truly existent objects

children.text: yathā gaur iti samghātaḥ sarvo nendriyagocaraḥ
children.translated_text: Just as the total aggregate “cow” is not wholly an object of the senses,
but, of what is apprehended in parts, a form is determined in the intellect
When by the senses there is attainment otherwise, with factors that introduce aspects of difference,
a form of actions is imagined like a firebrand-circle
And just as the parts of ‘cooking’ are water-pouring and the like,
so too the parts of water-pouring and the like are to be known as further others
And that which is understood as having reached the limit of withdrawal,
with respect to that single thing, the word ‘action’ is not employed in isolation
Thus, with earlier and later parts establishing the sequence, that one (complex) also,
though superimposed upon the non-existent, is denoted by finite verbs

children.text: kālānupāti yad rūpaṃ tad astīty anugamyate
children.translated_text: That form which follows time is apprehended as “it is,”

children.text: paritas tu paricchinnaṃ bhāva ity eva kathyate
children.translated_text: but, circumscribed all around, it is spoken of simply as ‘being’ (<s>bhāva</s>)
Because common usage is established, this is not a mere positing of attribute,
for metaphor rests upon the possibility of the primary sense
Because of subsequently imposed capacities, or distributively for cluster-holders,
they are marked as many-formed, being non-sequential as if sequential

children.text: anantaraṃ phalaṃ yasyāḥ kalpate tām kriyām viduḥ
children.translated_text: That is known as action (<s>kriyā</s>) whose result is brought about immediately after,
being the principal; by contextual fitness, other things then receive its designation
When the cause for the undertaking of an action is present, whatever exertion is for the sake of that,
one should employ without further regard, determining it by “he goes,”

children.text: satsu pratyayarūpo+asau bhāvo yāvan na jāyate
children.translated_text: As long as that existent, of the form of a causal condition, has not arisen,

children.text: tāvat pareṣāṃ rūpeṇa sādhyaḥ sann abhidhīyate
children.translated_text: until then, being to-be-accomplished in the form of another, it is spoken of
But when it is accomplished, the expectation of the means ceases because the end has been attained,

children.text: na kriyāvācināṃ tasmāt prayogas tatra vidyate
children.translated_text: therefore, at that point, there is no use of words denoting action
And it, not overreached by prior or posterior, being one, is of a non-sequential nature,
it is, by the property of prior and posterior, tracked for the sake of that

children.text: asan nivartate tasmād yat sat tad upalabhyate
children.translated_text: Hence, the non-existent ceases, and what is existent is apprehended,

children.text: tayoḥ sadasatoś cāsāv ātmaika iva gṛhyate
children.translated_text: and of these two, existent and non-existent, it is grasped as if it were a single self
Others say action (<s>kriyā</s>) is a universal (<s>jāti</s>) that resides in many particulars,
unaccomplished in the form of a particular, it is apprehended as if to be accomplished

children.text: ante yā vā kriyābhāge jātiḥ saiva kriyā smṛtā
children.translated_text: Or, the universal that is in the final part of an action—that very thing is remembered as the action,
and before the completion of the particular, that is apprehended as if coming-into-being
Or, the existence of agents and objects, qualified by their own activities;
or, action (<s>kriyā</s>) is the co-inherent existence in the distinctions of activity

children.text: antye vātmani yā sattā sā kriyā kaiś cid iṣyate
children.translated_text: Or, the existence which is in the final self is what some accept as action (<s>kriyā</s>),

children.text: bhāva eva hi dhātvartha ity avicchinna āgamaḥ
children.translated_text: for indeed the meaning of the verbal root is just being (<s>bhāva</s>)—such is the uninterrupted tradition

children.text: buddhiṃ tajjātim anye tu buddhisattām athāpare
children.translated_text: Others, however, assert “intellect” (<s>buddhi</s>) or its universal (<s>jāti</s>), and still others the existence-status of intellect (<s>buddhi-sattā</s>),
as a form withdrawn in the existents, they profess as action (<s>kriyā</s>)
By yet others, manifestation and withdrawal (appearance and disappearance), birth and destruction,
are posited, among the six modifications of being (<s>bhāva-vikāra</s>), as conventional
By these two, there is an inclusive grasp of all activities without distinction,
and resemblance to the substrate is called ‘abiding’ (<s>sthiti</s>), being precisely birth
Since, for what is coming-to-be, there is nothing other than birth; and even in destruction there is non-referentiality of the subject,
therefore, among the modifications of being, one single existence (<s>sattā</s>) stands firm

children.text: *pūrvabhāgas tu yaj jātāt taj janmety apadiśyate
children.translated_text: Only that prior part of what has arisen is indicated as ‘birth,’
when causal efficacy is intended in the form of an order relying on a substrate
In this way, the referent is denoted by finite-verbal words (<s>ākhyāta-śabda</s>),
while nominal words (<s>nāma-śabda</s>) operate as if gathering up the sequence

children.text: phalaṃ phalāpadeśo vā vastu vā tadvirodhi yat
children.translated_text: The result, or the designation as result, or the thing that is contrary to that,

children.text: tad anyad eva pūrveṣāṃ nāga ity apadiśyate
children.translated_text: that alone, different from what precedes, is indicated by “not yet” (<s>nāga</s>)

children.text: naivāsti naiva nāstīti vastuno grahanād vinā
children.translated_text: “It neither is nor is-not”—without the apprehension of a thing,
is not conceived; by another’s form, another thing is tracked
The being and non-being of pots and the like—even without touching with the hand—

children.text: kaś cid vedāprakāśe+api prakāśe tata eva vā
children.translated_text: someone knows, whether in the non-manifestation to the senses, or indeed in manifestation, from that very (ground)

children.text: vyāpi saukṣmyaṃ kva cid yāti kva cit saṃhanyate punaḥ
children.translated_text: The pervader sometimes attains subtlety, and elsewhere is again condensed,

children.text: akurvāṇo+atha vā kiṃ cit svaśaktyaivaṃ prakāśate
children.translated_text: doing nothing at all or doing something, it is manifested by its own power
The seeing of the reality that is of all forms, as if in sequence,

children.text: bhāgair iva prakḷptiś ca tāṃ kriyām apare viduḥ
children.translated_text: and a construction as if by parts—that, others know as action (<s>kriyā</s>)
Existence (<s>sattā</s>), by the conjunction of its own power, is established as all-formed,

children.text: sādhyā ca sādhanaṃ caiva phalaṃ bhoktā phalasya ca
children.translated_text: and as the end (<s>sādhya</s>) and the means (<s>sādhana</s>), indeed as the result and the enjoyer and of the result

children.text: kriyām anye tu manyante kva cid apy anapāśritām
children.translated_text: Others, however, take action (<s>kriyā</s>) to be, in some cases even without reliance (on a substrate),
an un-failing activity in the unity of purpose of means and end
Being first universal, it is divided previously, part by part,
then, in the form of operation (<s>vyāpāra</s>), it stands precisely as the end

children.text: prakṛtiḥ sādhanānāṃ sā prathamaṃ tac ca kārakam
children.translated_text: The nature (<s>prakṛti</s>) of the means is that (universal); and that is the ‘instrument’ (<s>kāraka</s>) first,
after that, the otherness of operations (<s>vyāpāra</s>) is described by some
When many factors are present, only some are indeed helpful,

children.text: saṃsarge kaś cid esāṃ tu prādhānyena pratīyate
children.translated_text: and in their conjunction, one among them is apprehended as principal
There, because of being an end (<s>sādhyatva</s>), the operations, with the means accomplished,
are denoted predominantly by finite verbs, and are also impelled by the result
Through unity and recurrence, in the reconciliation of difference and non-difference,
numbers are there ascertained—the actions of countables and of parts
How can there be a connection with means for an accomplished thing like ‘cooking,’

children.text: sādhyatve vā tiṅantena kṛtāṃ bhedo na kaś cana
children.translated_text: or, if it is to be accomplished, no distinction is made by the finite-verb
If, in that matter, the finite verb is the basis for the connection with the <s>kārakas</s> (semantic roles),

children.text: ṣaṣṭhvāḥ sā lena saṃbandhe vyudastā kartṛkarmanoḥ
children.translated_text: then, with the genitive case marking connection, the agent and object are excluded
A single denotation and a single referent cannot at once bear a double property;

children.text: na saṃbhavati siddhatve sa sādhyaḥ syāt kathaṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: in the state of accomplishment, it is not possible—how then would it be to-be-accomplished again

children.text: etāvat sādhanaṃ sādhyam etāvad iti kalpanā
children.translated_text: “So much is the means, so much the end”—such a positing

children.text: śāstra eva na vākye+asti vibhāgaḥ paramārthataḥ
children.translated_text: is only in the treatise; in the sentence there is no division in ultimate truth
In the finite-verbal word, by parts, the functioning with end and means

children.text: prakalpitā yathā śāstre sa ghañādisv api kramaḥ
children.translated_text: is constructed, just as that sequence is (constructed) also in the <s>ghaṅ</s> and similar affixes
There, as to-be-accomplished, action (<s>kriyā</s>) depends upon the verbal-root form,

children.text: sattvabhāvas tu yas tasyāḥ sa ghañādinibandhanaḥ
children.translated_text: but the being-status (<s>sat-bhāva</s>) of that is dependent on the <s>ghaṅ</s> and the like
Fixed in the word ‘relative’ (<s>bandhu</s>) in the form of identity-in-relationship and difference,
a collection is the state of relatives; and that is denoted by the suffix

children.text: tatra yam prati sādhyatvam asiddhā taṃ prati kriyā
children.translated_text: There, the action is with respect to him for whom the ‘to-be-accomplished’-ness is not accomplished,

children.text: siddhā tu yasmin sādhyatvaṃ na tam eva punaḥ prati
children.translated_text: but as for him in whom the ‘to-be-accomplished’-ness is accomplished, not again with respect to that very one

children.text: rājñaḥ putrasya napteti na rājñi vyatiricyate
children.translated_text: “Grandson of the king’s son” is not distinguished in the king,
the sense of ‘son’ is the primacy, and that does not depart from it
“The deer runs”—“he sees”: the forms of end and means,
thus, through difference of object, are justified for ‘movement’
For the meanings of the <s>laṝ</s>, <s>ktá</s>, <s>khal</s>, and likewise of indeclinable-forming affixes,
and of the established <s>niṣṭhā</s>, <s>ghaṅ</s> and the like—the verbal root is the expresser of the to-be-accomplished
Because of the non-attainment of the to-be-accomplished, “this very one thus” does not receive support (from itself),

children.text: tiṅantair antareṇevam upamānaṃ tato na taiḥ
children.translated_text: therefore the comparison, without finite verbs, is not by those (alone)

children.text: sādhanatvaṃ prasiddhaṃ ca tiṅkṣu saṃbandhināṃ yataḥ
children.translated_text: Since the status of ‘means’ is well-established in the finite-verb forms as connected,

children.text: tenādhyāropa eva syād upamā tu na vidyate
children.translated_text: therefore it would be only a superimposition; but a comparison is not found
And in cases where they are deficient yet intended to be complete, comparison is prescribed,

children.text: kriyā caivāśraye sarvā tatra tatra samāpyate
children.translated_text: and action (<s>kriyā</s>), indeed, in each locus, is everywhere brought to completion
By the very reason by which “the swan flies” is stated,

children.text: ātau tasya samāptatvād upamārtho na vidyate
children.translated_text: since, at the start, that (flying) is complete, the import of comparison does not obtain
For actions (<s>kriyā</s>) that are of different classes (<s>jāti</s>), similarity is not to be ascertained,

children.text: siddheś ca prakrame sādhyam upamātum na śakyate
children.translated_text: and when the procedure is established, what is to be accomplished cannot be compared
Just as “the forest (is) trees,” on the basis of the support of difference-and-non-difference,

children.text: arthātmā bhidyate bhāve sa bāhyābhyantare kramaḥ
children.translated_text: the very nature of the object/meaning is divided in the state of being; there is that sequence, external and internal

children.text: sāmānye bhāva ity atra yal liṅgam upalabhyate
children.translated_text: Where “being” is in the universal, whatever mark is apprehended,

children.text: bhedānāṃ anumeyatvān na tat teṣu vivakṣyate
children.translated_text: since differences are to be inferred, that is not intended with respect to them
Because, in designation, the purpose has been achieved, the mark is not intended for being,
and because of the prescribing of comparison—what is other than being in the ‘cook’ and similar (forms)
As for what pertains to the ‘being’ (bhava) of ‘cook’ and the like, so much is here taught,

children.text: na ca liṅgam pacādināṃ bhavatau samavasthitam
children.translated_text: and the mark of ‘cook’ and the like is not established in the ‘being’

children.text: ekaś ca so+arthaḥ sattākhyaḥ katham cit kaiś cid ucyate
children.translated_text: And that one single meaning, called existence (<s>sattā</s>), is somehow said by some,
and its marks are diversified, like the differences of ‘cook’-form and the like
Just as “teacher” and “maternal uncle” are both predicated of one,
so, through difference of relations, the very nature of the object is (rendered) manifold: that is the prescription concerning the states of being-a-cooker and being-a-<s>bhāva</s>
3.9: Delineation of Time (<s>kāla-samuddeśa</s>)
Some declare time (<s>kāla</s>) apart from operation (<s>vyāpāra</s>),

children.text: nityam ekaṃ vibhu dravyaṃ parimāṇaṃ kriyāvatām
children.translated_text: an eternal, one, all-pervading substance, a measure for things that have action
Measures like diṣṭi, prastha, suvarṇa, and the like are devised for differences of form (extent),

children.text: kriyābhedāya kālas tu saṃkhyā sarvasya bhedikā
children.translated_text: but time is for difference of actions (<s>kriyā</s>), number being the differentiator of all

children.text: utpattau ca sthitau caiva vināśe cāpi tadvatām
children.translated_text: And, in origination, in continuance, and also in dissolution, of those that have (such states),
they say time alone, existing with a differentiated nature, is the instrumental cause
They speak of it as the stage-manager of this world-machine,
by whose restraints and permissions the universe is apportioned

children.text: yadi na pratibadhnīyāt pratibandhaṃ ca notsṛjet
children.translated_text: If it did not restrain, and did not also release restraint,
the states would be intermingled, devoid of before-and-after
Its nature is manifoldly divided by differences that rest upon other properties,

children.text: na hi bhinnam abhinnaṃ vā vastu kiṃ cana vidyate
children.translated_text: for there is no thing whatsoever that is either (wholly) different or (wholly) non-different

children.text: naiko na cāpy aneko+asti na śuklo nāpi cāsitaḥ
children.translated_text: It is not one, nor indeed many; not white, nor again black,

children.text: dravyātmā sa tu saṃsargād evaṃrūpaḥ prakāśate
children.translated_text: but as a substance-nature it appears thus only through conjunction (with others)

children.text: saṃsargināṃ tu ye bhedā viśeṣās tasya te matāḥ
children.translated_text: And the differentiations—the specific features—of the conjuncts are regarded as its (apparent) differences,

children.text: sa bhinnas tair vyavasthānāṃ kālo bhedāya kalpate
children.translated_text: and being differentiated by them, time is devised for the differentiation of states
From a relation to a particular time, acquisition of activity is conceived,
and it is established as the cause for the conjunction of powers
The regulations of birth and manifestation are dependent upon application,
and because of being ever dependent on a substratum, continuance is preceded by regulation

children.text: sthitasyānugrahas tais tair dharmaiḥ saṃsargibhis tataḥ
children.translated_text: For what is abiding, there is favoring by those various properties with which it is conjoined;
for the self (entity), restraint is obscuration, and ‘abandonment’ as well
But here the operation of time is determined as counter-positional,

children.text: kāla eva hi viśvātmā vyāpāra iti kathyate
children.translated_text: for time itself, the soul of the universe, is said to be operation (<s>vyāpāra</s>)
By it, for bodies (forms) that are different, accumulations and diminutions separately
are observed, through transformation that is the associate of all differences
Through activities resembling the entrainment of a water-machine’s whirling,

children.text: sa kalāḥ kalayan sarvāḥ kālākhyāṃ labhate vibhuḥ
children.translated_text: that all-pervading (reality), apportioning all moments (<s>kalā</s>), attains the designation ‘time’ (<s>kāla</s>)

children.text: pratibhaddhāś ca yās tena citrā viśvasya vṛttayaḥ
children.translated_text: And the varied modes of the universe that are restrained by it,

children.text: tāḥ sa evānujānāti yathā tantuḥ śakuntikāḥ
children.translated_text: those it alone permits, as a thread (permits) the puppets
When powers have attained ripeness through connection with a particular time,
action (<s>kriyā</s>) is manifested by the eternal act called ‘application’ (<s>prayoga</s>)
And in that, the manifestation of the result is produced, prompted by the class (<s>jāti</s>),

children.text: kuto+apy adbhutayā vṛttyā śaktibhiḥ sā niyamyate
children.translated_text: and by some wondrous function from somewhere, that is governed by the powers

children.text: tatas tu samavāyākhyā śaktir bhedasya bādhikā
children.translated_text: Then the power called <s>samavāya</s> (inherence), being a blocker of difference,

children.text: ekatvam iva tā vyaktīr āpādayati kāraṇaiḥ
children.translated_text: brings about, as it were, unity in those manifestations, by means of the causes

children.text: athāsmān niyamād ūrdhvaṃ jātayo yāḥ prayojikāḥ
children.translated_text: Next, those classes (<s>jāti</s>) which, beyond this regulation, are purposive for us,

children.text: tāḥ sarvā vyaktim āyānti svacche chāyā ivāmbhasi
children.translated_text: all attain manifestation, like clear reflections on water
Then, because of conformity to the causes, and proceeding from causes,
qualities (<s>guṇa</s>) arise there as the causes of the manifestation of their own class

children.text: āśrayāṇāṃ ca nityatvam āśritānāṃ ca nityatā
children.translated_text: And the permanence of the substrates, and the permanence of what is supported,

children.text: tā vyaktīr anugṛhṇāti sthitis tena prakalpate
children.translated_text: that sustains the manifestations, and thus continuance is instituted
Just as there is dependence at the arising of the non-eternal, so also in its continuance,
it is created only for destruction—they recognize a state that is not self-governed
When established, it is favored by entities that are in conjunction with it in their own operations,

children.text: naiṣāṃ sattām anudgṛhya vṛttir janmavatāṃ smṛtā
children.translated_text: its activity for those that are born is said to occur without sustaining their existence
The time-power called ‘old age’ (<s>jarā</s>), which opposes other powers,

children.text: sā śaktīḥ pratibadhnāti jāyante ca virodhinaḥ
children.translated_text: blocks the powers, and antagonistic ones arise

children.text: prayojakās tu ye bhāvāḥ sthitibhāgasya hetavaḥ
children.translated_text: But those entities that are instigators, the causes of the portion of continuance,

children.text: tirobhavanti te sarve yata ātmā prahīyate
children.translated_text: all of them disappear, since the self-principle is discarded
Just as, by a wondrous mode of operation, there emerges an exit that is without any binding cause,
so the self-principle of this (composite) is abandoned, all becomes footless (i.e., without support)
For two actions that are ultimate (i.e., not leading to further result), each bearing diverse purposes,
how could there be delimitation without a single connector?
As on a balance or in the hand there is a disposition of diverse substances,
heaviness would be measured only by time; so too the course of action

children.text: jahāti sahavṛttāś ca kriyāḥ sa samavasthitāḥ
children.translated_text: And he (time), while remaining the same, abandons actions that coexist with him,
as rice abandons water; thereby he attains the designation ‘annual’ (<s>hāyana</s>)
By the constraint and permission (i.e., inhibition and allowance), that perpetual operation of his,
being divided by that, he assumes the form of sequence
Through difference of agents, in those things for which he is instrumental, there occur accumulation and diminution,

children.text: samatvaṃ viṣamatvaṃ vā sa ekaḥ pratipadyate
children.translated_text: he alone, being one, assumes equality or inequality
Just as, from difference of action, in one (substrate) the designation ‘carpenter’ and the like proceeds,
so, from difference of action, in one (substrate) the designation ‘season’ and the like arises

children.text: ārambhaś ca kriyā caiva niṣṭhā cety abhidhīyate
children.translated_text: Beginning, action indeed, and completion—thus they are spoken of,
owing to superimposition of other properties, differing as real and unreal

children.text: yāvāṃś ca dvyaṇukādīnāṃ tāvān himavato+apy asau
children.translated_text: And as great in the <s>dyad</s> (<s>dvyaṇuka</s>) and the rest, so great even in <s>Himavat</s> is he,

children.text: na hy ātmā kasya cid bhettuṃ pracetuṃ vāpi śakyate
children.translated_text: for the self of anything cannot be split or expanded

children.text: anyais tu bhāvair anyeṣāṃ pracayaḥ parikalpyate
children.translated_text: Yet by other entities, the accumulation of others is conceived,

children.text: śanair idam idaṃ kṣipram iti tena pratīyate
children.translated_text: hence this is apprehended as ‘slow here, swift there’

children.text: asataś ca kramo nāsti sa hi bhettuṃ na śakyate
children.translated_text: And of the non-existent there is no sequence, for that cannot be split,
and even of the existent, that which is the essence of self remains just so
And being the adjunct of action (<s>kriyā</s>), the states of ‘past’, ‘future’, and ‘present’,
distinguished by eleven forms, are apprehended

children.text: bhūtaḥ pañcavidhas tatra bhaviṣyaṃś ca caturvidhaḥ
children.translated_text: There, the ‘past’ is fivefold, and the ‘future’ fourfold,
the ‘present’ is declared twofold—thus there are eleven conceptualizations

children.text: kāle nidhāya svaṃ rūpaṃ prajñayā yan nigṛhyate
children.translated_text: Placing its own form in time and grasped by cognition,
entities then are withdrawn, their powers having passed into that (time)

children.text: bhāvināṃ caiva yad rūpaṃ tasya ca pratibimbakam
children.translated_text: And the very form of things-to-be, and its reflection,
is suitably presented in time, as in a well-polished mirror
As a current draws along grasses, leaves, tendrils, and the like,
so time too sets in motion, measure by measure, those that have measures
Entering in, it connects, as the wind connects the motions of those that have motion,
there, as the very self of time, it establishes the form of sequence

children.text: ayanapravibhāgaś ca gatīś ca jyotiṣāṃ dhruvā
children.translated_text: The division of solstitial courses and the fixed motions of the luminaries,
and likewise the cessations and origins of beings, are grounded upon that
The transformations of measures that follow upon the operation of time,

children.text: nakṣatrākhyā pṛthak teṣu cihnamātraṃ tu tārakāḥ
children.translated_text: these, distinct, are called ‘<s>nakṣatra</s>’; but the stars are only marks therein
By the seasons’ marks are determined through the cries of beasts and birds and the behaviors of immovables,
and by transformations such as shadow and the like
This coming of manifestation, which is seen as if sequential,
is the activity of time even of a universe that is without sequence
As the arrangement of far and near is grounded on space (<s>adhvan</s>),
so the arrangement of long and short in seeing-time is grounded on time
For that undivided time, through common usage, three distinctions made by action are established,

children.text: bhedā iva trayaḥ siddhā yāṃl loko nātivartate
children.translated_text: which the world does not transcend
There are three powers of the one time, abiding,
through relation to which, for entities that exist, there is seeing and non-seeing

children.text: dvābhyāṃ sa kila śaktibhyāṃ bhāvānāṃ varaṇātmakaḥ
children.translated_text: By two of those powers indeed, it is of the nature of screening with respect to entities,
but the power called ‘present’ is manifestive of the form of entities
The power named ‘future’ is non-obstructive of the power of birth,

children.text: atītākhyā tu yā śaktis tayā janma virudhyate
children.translated_text: but the power called ‘past’ is that by which birth is opposed
And like darkness and light, these three courses (<s>adhvan</s>) are established,
in them, although they are non-sequential, the sequence of entities is apprehended

children.text: dvau tu tatra tamorūpāv ekasyālokavat sthitiḥ
children.translated_text: There, two are of the nature of darkness, and one has the status of light,

children.text: atītam api keṣāṃ cit punar viparivartate
children.translated_text: and for some, even what is past turns back again
Simultaneous presentness is then attained by its property

children.text: keṣāṃ cid vartamānatvāc caiti tadvad atītatām
children.translated_text: For some, because of presentness, it likewise goes and attains pastness,
Having been impelled into presentness through the assistance of a cause,
when the assisting cause has subsided, it no longer attains manifestation

children.text: dve eva kālasya vibhoḥ keṣāṃ cic chaktivartmanī
children.translated_text: For some, indeed only two pathways of the power of the all-pervading time,
are what effect the opening and closing (unfolding and folding) of entities
Some declare that, by distinct <s>kalā</s> (liminal powers/parts) having separate purposes,

children.text: ke cid buddhyanusaṃhāra- lakṣaṇaṃ taṃ pracakṣate
children.translated_text: that (time) is, by its very nature, divided, and is characterized by the collecting-up of cognitions

children.text: jñānānugataśaktiṃ vā bāhyaṃ vā satyataḥ sthitam
children.translated_text: Whether as a power accompanied by cognition or as something external truly established,
without resorting to the very self of time one cannot transact (make sense of things)

children.text: tisro bhāvasya bhāvasya keṣāṃ cid bhāvaśaktayaḥ
children.translated_text: For some, there are three powers of the being of being,

children.text: tābhiḥ svaśaktibhiḥ sarvaṃ sadaivāsti ca nāsti ca
children.translated_text: by their own powers, everything always both is and is not
And, without difference from existence (being), those three are established,

children.text: kramas tās tadabhedāc ca sadasattvaṃ na bhidyate
children.translated_text: and sequence, due to that non-difference, does not divide being and non-being
By seeing and non-seeing, the very same one is seen and unseen,

children.text: adhvanām ekatā nāsti na ca kiṃ cin nivartate
children.translated_text: there is no oneness of the <s>adhvan</s> (courses), nor does anything truly cease
The perspectives that are of the nature of power, self, and deity make the view of time differ;

children.text: prathamaṃ tad avidyāyāṃ yad vidyāyāṃ na vidyate
children.translated_text: the first is that (view) which exists in ignorance, which does not exist in knowledge
If, despite the non-duality of time, a manifestation of difference is seen in short, long, and protracted (measures),
that is like those who awaken late or quickly
By the recurrence of short, long, and protracted (syllables), in water-clocks and the like,
how could accumulation occur, being caused by mere conceptual construction?
By the accumulation of the condition for manifestation, there is accumulation,
but the true nature of sound, though undivided, is not of the nature of accumulation
Thus, a division of the <s>mātrāturīya</s> (quarter beyond the measures) or of the ten-fold (group),
does not exist, in terms of quantitative distinction, in the self of sound
Those sounds which, by a conception of non-simultaneous production, are as though situated with an interval between,
are means for the cognizers to attain cognition

children.text: viśiṣṭam avadhiṃ taṃ tam upādāya prakalpate
children.translated_text: Time, though one for those who are time-endowed, is conceived—taking this or that specific limit—
as bearing divisions of instant, month, and season
And, due to differences of mental grasp and practical convention, being established in the realm of usage,

children.text: tāvān eva kṣaṇaḥ kālo yugamanvantarāṇi vā
children.translated_text: time is just so much as an instant, or a <s>yuga</s> (age), or the intermediate periods
By obstruction and permission, in the water contained within the aperture of the water-clock,

children.text: yad ambhasi prakṣaraṇaṃ tat kālasyaiva ceṣṭitam
children.translated_text: that outflow which occurs is an operation of time itself

children.text: alpe mahati vā chidre tatsaṃbandhe na bhidyate
children.translated_text: In a small or large hole, in that connection there is no difference,
the operation of time is its very self, and that indeed it (the water) follows

children.text: ākrīḍa iva kālasya dṛśyate yaḥ svaśaktibhiḥ
children.translated_text: As in a play-ground (arena) of sport, the manifestation of time by its own powers is seen,
and, because of the manifoldness of the many-formed in entities, by it time is diversified in many ways

children.text: tvacisārasya vā vṛddhiṃ tṛṇarājasya vā dadhat
children.translated_text: Whether bearing the growth of the essence of skin, or of a blade of grass,
to just that extent, through the connection with that growth, the principle of time is conceptually determined
Even if there is alternation of measures, for it (time) there is no alternation,
nor is there any difference of path due to a difference in the mover’s motion
Through the rise-and-setting recurrence of the luminaries, established for the world,
even though time does not deviate, a property as if belonging to it is observed
Others, moreover, who know time, understand time as differentiated,
by the distinctness of recurrences, according to the quivering of sun, planets, and <s>nakṣatra</s> (asterisms)
That activity which proceeds to delimit another activity, with respect to an activity,
once its measure is ascertained, that is designated ‘time’
In cognition there is a transfer of form, and by cognition itself there is a collecting-up,

children.text: ataḥ kriyāntarābhāve sā kriyā kāla iṣyate
children.translated_text: therefore, in the absence of another activity, that very activity is considered time

children.text: bhūto ghaṭa itīyaṃ ca sattāyā eva bhūtatā
children.translated_text: ‘The pot has become’ and ‘this is’—this ‘has-become-ness’ belongs only to existence,
‘existence has become’ thus, of existence, existence is said to have become

children.text: parato bhidyate sarvam ātmā tu na vikalpyate
children.translated_text: Everything is distinguished by another, but the self is not to be conceptualized,
therefore a state such as a mountain and the like is distinguished by another form
Well-known distinctions are operations, and activities of dissimilar parts;
by association, the activities of similar parts are distinguished
As if it takes on separation, as if it is seen to have ceased,
a complex of actions, such as eating, proceeds with intervals
And even though it has an appearance of being broken, it does not cease, being unbroken,
for every activity is apprehended as mingled with something else
Or, every activity of the parts that is seen in the intervals,

children.text: sādṛśyāt sati bhede tu tadaṅgatvena gṛhyate
children.translated_text: if similarity exists, despite difference, is grasped as a limb of that (whole)

children.text: sad asad vāpi vastu syāt tṛtīyaṃ nāsti kiṃ cana
children.translated_text: A thing is either existent or non-existent; there is no third whatsoever,

children.text: tena bhūtabhaviṣyantau muktvā madhyaṃ na vidyate
children.translated_text: therefore, apart from past and future, there is no middle
A single ‘cessation-form’ does not arise, due to the absence of difference

children.text: sad asad vāpi tenaikaṃ kramarūpaṃ kathaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: How, then, could there be one ‘sequence-form’ of it, whether existent or non-existent,
And because of the non-establishment of many, only one is apprehended,
according to the apprehension there is remembrance, and there indeed it is reasonable
If, in the supposition of the oneness of everything, there were one form, existent-and-non-existent,

children.text: nirvṛttirūpaṃ nirvṛtteḥ sāmānyam atha vā bhavet
children.translated_text: or else, there would be a ‘cessation-form’ as the commonality of cessation

children.text: kāryotpattau samarthaṃ vā svena dharmeṇa tat tathā
children.translated_text: Or, that (time), capable in the production of an effect, by its own property, would similarly be grasped as the principle of self,
and that is the state of ‘presentness’ here
What, as pertaining to the inner domain (adhyātma), is determined as a sequence-complex of actions,
they call that ‘presentness,’ as a form transferred into one locus
‘Exceeding of activity’ is characterized as the non-arising of activity altogether,

children.text: na ca bhūtam anutpannaṃ na bhaviṣyat tathāvidham
children.translated_text: and what has not arisen is not past, nor will there be anything of that sort in the future
Prior to the arising of an opposed activity, or when an opposed (activity) has ceased,
in the operation, by a difference of limit, the object there is divided
When there is irregularity, the fitness of the indicator is not established,

children.text: bhāvy āsīd iti sūtreṇa tat kāle+anyatra śiṣyate
children.translated_text: by the rule ‘it would be’ the intended meaning at that time is left over elsewhere

children.text: svakāla eva sādhutve kālabhede gatiḥ katham
children.translated_text: If the fitness is only in its own time, how could there be conveyance across a difference of time,
from the sentence-meaning, specificity with respect to non-intended objects is not accomplished
If a part is for that meaning, then the arrival of pastness to what is future

children.text: na syād atyantabhūtatvam evaikaṃ tatra saṃbhavet
children.translated_text: would not occur; only absolute pastness, one (thing), would be possible there
Even if there were prior specific temporality, nevertheless, in the qualifier,
because of dependence and because it is more internal, there it will be fit

children.text: āmiśra eva prakrāntaḥ sa padārthas tathāvidhaḥ
children.translated_text: That kind of word-meaning proceeds as unmixed,
and the mixedness of the purely single cannot be accounted for in an eternal object

children.text: śuddhe ca kāle vyākhyātam āmiśre na prasidhyati
children.translated_text: And in pure time this has been explained; in the unmixed, it is not established,
fitness out of keeping with time is taught by that rule
Because, in the meaning denoted by the finite verb and the word, what is to be effected is primary,
the qualifier, being implied by that, is fixed at that time
Either as an imitation of a conception-of-the-present, or simply as the operation of word(s),

children.text: adhyasyate viruddhe+arthe na ca tena virudhyate
children.translated_text: a meaning opposed (to that time) is superimposed, and it is not thereby contradicted

children.text: bhūtaṃ bhaviṣyad ity etau pratyayau vartamānatām
children.translated_text: The two affixes ‘past’ and ‘future’ do not abandon presentness,
and they come to have the form of a contrary substrate
Of the path (adhvan) of the present, by the (shared) object with the future,
in the commentary it is indicated as ‘future-time,’ for a practical purpose
In ‘he wishes, he intends to do,’ its own time is being followed,
‘it will be’—in the primary meaning, that time is not being followed
Because hope depends on what is hoped-for, there is a reversal in the expression of hope,
the speaker’s property is connected to the word-meaning by the words themselves
When, in the conjunction of the seed with the pollinator, the fruit is operative,
then, because the parts are in operation, there is the exclusion of the future
But when the fruit is in the form of manifest ripening, there is past-time-ness,
and that form is superimposed, as conceived, upon other properties
When the operations of the instruments employed are appropriate for the attainment of the result,

children.text: tatra rūpaṃ yad adhyastaṃ tatkālaṃ tat pratīyate
children.translated_text: then the form that is superimposed is apprehended as of that time

children.text: niṣpattāv avadhiḥ kaś cit kaś cit prativivakṣitaḥ
children.translated_text: In completion there is some limit intended, and some (limit) counter-intended,
because of regard for the birth from the cause, it is also said ‘birth of the effect’
Where attainment is intended as dependent upon external means,
there, because of the absence of other means, it is designated ‘accomplished’
Therefore, by a difference of limit, past-ness is primarily established as accomplished,
while futurity and existence are (established) in the regard for the property of the cause
Because for real things, through connection with the senses, that very being is specified,
for transaction rests on difference that is grounded in another entity
Existence is apprehended, by cognition, of mere thinghood,

children.text: yaḥ samāsādanād bhedaḥ sa tatra na vivakṣitaḥ
children.translated_text: the difference that arises from combination is not intended there

children.text: yogād vā strītvapuṃstvābhyāṃ na kiṃ cid avatiṣṭhate
children.translated_text: Nor, from combination with femaleness and maleness, does anything stand firm,

children.text: svasminn ātmani tatrānyad bhūtaṃ bhāvi ca kathyate
children.translated_text: in its own self, there, another—past and future—is spoken of
3.10: <s>puruṣa</s> (Self/Person) topic-introduction
The inward-status and the other-status are also upādhis (limiting adjuncts) of agent and object,
for those two, by a special usage in the <s>Śruti</s>, the middle and the second are the denoters

children.text: sad asad vāpi caitanyam etābhyām avagamyate
children.translated_text: Whether existent or non-existent, consciousness is understood by these two,

children.text: caitanyabhāge prathamaḥ puruṣo na tu vartate
children.translated_text: but in the portion of consciousness, the first person <s>puruṣa</s> does not occur
If the first-person <s>puruṣa</s> existed, (then) with the knowings born of intellect and cognition,
there would be no demonstrated use of consciousness for terms of designation

children.text: saṃbodhanārthaḥ sarvatra madhyame kaiś cid iṣyate
children.translated_text: For the sake of vocative address everywhere, the middle (person) is, by some, accepted

children.text: tathā saṃbodhane sarvāṃ prathamāṃ yuṣmado viduḥ
children.translated_text: Likewise, in vocative address they know the entire first (person) to be of <s>yuṣmad</s> (you),
there is no vocative, in common usage, with any thing that is to be enjoined,

children.text: svāhendraśatrur vardhasva yathā rājā bhaveti ca
children.translated_text: ‘svāhā,’ ‘O slayer of <s>Indra</s>!’ ‘increase!’ and ‘become a king!,’ and the like
Because the object of <s>yuṣmad</s> (you) is already established, and because the initial acute accent is fixed,

children.text: yuṣmadaḥ prathamāntasya paraś cen na padād asau
children.translated_text: if the first-case form of <s>yuṣmad</s> (you) were other (than that), it would not be from the word; that (form) is not (so) from the word
Difference of subordinate-and-principal, and the reversal regarding <s>puruṣa</s> (grammatical person) and the rest,

children.text: nirdeśaś cānyathā śāstre nityatvān na virudhyate
children.translated_text: and designation otherwise in the <s>Śāstra</s> (treatise) does not contradict (it), because of eternality

children.text: yathānirdeśam arthāḥ syur yesāṃ śāstraṃ vidhāyakam
children.translated_text: Objects would be as designated, for which the <s>Śāstra</s> is prescriptive;

children.text: kim cit sāmānyam āśritya sthite tu pratipādanam
children.translated_text: but, relying on some generality, when there is an established basis, there is instruction

children.text: yo+aśve yaḥ pīṭha ity atra bhūtayor aśvapīṭhayoḥ
children.translated_text: In ‘he (who is) on a horse, he (who is) on a seat,’ here, of the two beings—horse and seat—,
just as the purpose is that of indication-by-example, so is the injunction among the objects
3.11: saṃkhyā-topic introduction
An entity endowed with number, being of the nature of existent, indeed is what is denoted in all cases,
for the division into difference and non-difference, in the world, is grounded in number

children.text: sa dharmo vyatirikto vā teṣāṃ ātmaiva vā tathā
children.translated_text: That property is either distinct (from substances), or else, in that way, it is their very self-nature,
taking as its basis the being a cause of difference, it is designated ‘number’

children.text: samavetā paricchedye kva cid anyatra sā sthitā
children.translated_text: Conjoined with the delimited, and in some cases existing elsewhere,
number posits the difference of entities, and likewise of their very self

children.text: paratve cāparatve ca bhede tulyā śrutir yathā
children.translated_text: As, with respect to otherness and non-otherness, the <s>Śruti</s> (scripture) is equal (i.e., treats them alike),
so, being the denotatum of the word ‘number,’ the cause of difference is likewise a quality
As in what is not independent there is the state of independence—(that) being a property of another—in a quality,
so, even in what is non-different, the state of being distinguished is, as a property of substance, in a quality

children.text: svabuddhyā tam apoddhṛtya loko+apy āgamam āśritaḥ
children.translated_text: Abstracting that by his own cognition, the world too, relying on tradition,
expounds one’s own property by means of another’s property, for the sake of comprehension
Speech, which denotes the realities of assistance-to-others, independently,
is drawn away from its own property with respect to all objects

children.text: yathaivāviṣayaṃ jñānaṃ na kiṃ cid avabhāsate
children.translated_text: Just as cognition without an object does not make anything appear,

children.text: tathā bhāvo+apy asaṃsṛṣṭo na kaś cid upalabhyate
children.translated_text: so too, an existent, being unassociated, is not apprehended by anyone

children.text: bhedena tu samākhyātaṃ yal loko+apy anuvartate
children.translated_text: But what has been denominated by means of difference, which the world too follows,
that transaction, from tradition, is described as corresponding to the <s>Śāstra</s> (treatise)

children.text: buddhau sthiteṣu teṣv evam adhyāropo na durlabhaḥ
children.translated_text: When they are thus established in the intellect, superimposition is not difficult,

children.text: paradharmasya na hy atra sadasattvaṃ prayojakam
children.translated_text: for here, the being or non-being of another’s property is not the operative factor
Even in generalities, (there is) a generality; in particularized things, a particularity,

children.text: saṃkhyāsu saṃkhyā liṅgeṣu liṅgam evaṃ prakalpate
children.translated_text: in numbers, a number; in marks (indicators), a mark—thus is posited
Therefore, those who hold a theory of conjunction say that number resides in substance,
which, transcending difference and non-difference, brings about difference-and-non-difference
By which, among distinct selves, the self is indicated as though of that form,
through conjunction with what is not of that form, that is the likeness-to-a-cause

children.text: saṃsṛṣṭeṣv api nirbhāge bhūteṣv arthakriyā yathā
children.translated_text: Just as, even in parts that are conjoined yet partless, there is efficacy for a purpose,

children.text: sattvādiṣu ca mātrāsu sarvāsv evaṃ pratīyate
children.translated_text: so, in the measures called existence and the like, in all of them, it is apprehended thus
Unity is the source of duality and the rest, since differences are preceded by that;

children.text: vinā tena na saṃkhyānām anyāsām asti saṃbhavaḥ
children.translated_text: without that, there is no possibility of any of the other numbers
With unity, accompanied by cognition, there is the cause in the birth of duality;

children.text: ekatvābhyāṃ samutpannam evaṃ vā tat pratīyate
children.translated_text: or, being produced from unity and unity, thus it is apprehended

children.text: ekatvasamudāyo vā sāpekṣe vā pṛthak pṛthak
children.translated_text: Or a collection of unities, or, being relative, separately and separately,

children.text: ekatve dvitvam ity evaṃ tayor dvivacanaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: ‘duality is (based) on unity’—in this way, a dual number would result
Even a single (entity), by difference of qualities, a group, would posit difference,
for the difference of substrate and of what is grounded-on-a-substrate is grounded in that substrate
A group whose number is the number of countables—a group—is spoken of as ‘number,’
in twenties and the like, that (number) is different from others, as the differentiator of a group of substances
The number ‘twenty-one,’ having the form of another number,
in a single (number), by non-repetition in the intellect, is imagined as in the case of fractions
Because of being an aggregate of innumerables, a number-function is enjoined;

children.text: samūhatve tu tan na syāt svāṅgādisamudāyavat
children.translated_text: but if there were mere collectivity, that would not be so—like an aggregate of own-parts and the like
That number which operates in numbers dependent upon other countables,
they know that number—of repetitions and classes of countables—to be of that sort

children.text: na saṃkhyāyāṃ na saṃkhyeye dvau daśety asti saṃbhavaḥ
children.translated_text: There is no possibility of ‘two tens’ either in number or in the countable,

children.text: bhedābhāvān na saṃkhyāyāṃ virodhān na tadāśraye
children.translated_text: because of the absence of difference, not in the number; because of contradiction, not in its substrate
‘These two groups of ten are (a) twenty’—by the number-utterance;
or else, in that very form, the repetition regarding the countable is reckoned

children.text: saṃkhyā nāma na saṃkhyāsti saṃjñaiṣeti yathocyate
children.translated_text: As it is said, ‘number’ is not number—this is a technical term,

children.text: rūpaṃ na rūpam apy evaṃ samjñā sā hi sitādiṣu
children.translated_text: so too ‘form’ is not (mere) form; it is a technical term, indeed, in ‘white’ and the like
But, due to the conjunction of number and the genus of number, it is spoken of as ‘number is number,’

children.text: rūpatvajātiyogāc ca rūpe rūpam iti smṛtam
children.translated_text: and, due to the conjunction of being-form and the genus of form, in regard to form it is remembered as ‘form is form’

children.text: nimittam ekam ity atra vibhaktyā nābhidhīyate
children.translated_text: In the statement ‘the cause is one,’ here, it is not expressed by means of a case-ending,

children.text: tadvatas tu yad ekatvaṃ vibhaktis tatra vartate
children.translated_text: but the oneness that belongs to that (possessor of it)—the case-relation operates there

children.text: ekasya pracayo dṛṣṭaḥ samūhaś ca dvayos tathā
children.translated_text: An accumulation of one is observed, and likewise a collection of two;
therefore, apart from the causal factor, a different number serves as the differentiator

children.text: tad ekam api caikatvaṃ vibhaktiśravaṇād ṛte
children.translated_text: And that very unity—even being ‘one’—is not denoted by that word without the hearing of a case-ending,

children.text: nocyate tena śabdena vibhaktyā tu sahocyate
children.translated_text: but is indeed stated together with a case-ending
And if there were co-presence and co-absence, there would be a distinct expression;

children.text: syātām asati tasmimś ca prakṛtyartho na kalpyate
children.translated_text: and if that were absent, no inherent meaning of the base (prakṛti) is to be imagined
‘Oneness’ in ‘one’ here is a qualifier of a pure substance,
but the inherent meaning (of the base), when possessed of qualities, is distinguished by the meaning of the case-ending
From the indication ‘of two and of one,’ there is possibility even for mere number,
but, by the established usage of ‘one’ and the rest, it is said to have the sense of a countable
3.12: Delineation of the <s>Upagraha</s> (ancillary determiners)

children.text: ya ātmanepadād bhedaḥ kva cid arthasya gamyate
children.translated_text: Whatever difference of an action (or meaning) is apprehended somewhere from the <s>Ātmanepada</s>,

children.text: anyataś cāpi lādeśān manyante tam upagraham
children.translated_text: and also from other substitutions such as the <s>lādeśa</s> (suffixal replacement), they consider that to be an <s>upagraha</s> (ancillary determinant)

children.text: kva cit sādhanam evāsau kva cit tasya viśeṣaṇam
children.translated_text: In some cases, that (upagraha) itself is an instrument; in some cases, a qualifier of that,
there, ‘instrument’ is the action etc., while ‘qualifier’ is that which has explicit expression
An action is differentiated, according to the difference of its object, in matters such as livelihood and the like,

children.text: lādeśaiḥ sa kriyābhedo vākyeṣv api niyamyate
children.translated_text: and by the substitutions like <s>lādeśa</s>, that differentiation of action is also regulated in sentences

children.text: dhātvarthas tadviśeṣaś cāpy uktaḥ kva cid upagrahaḥ
children.translated_text: The meaning of the verbal root and its specification too, in some cases, is said to be an <s>upagraha</s>,
the meaning of the verbal root would be smelling and the like, while variation (vyatihāra) is the qualifier
In the initiation of action by a finite verb, some hold the views of self-meaning and other-meaning,
either absent or present, in any case dependent on the intention to be conveyed

children.text: kesāṃ cit kartrabhiprāye ṇicā saha vikalpate
children.translated_text: According to some, in the agent’s intention, it is optionally used together with the <s>ṇic</s> (causative),
for others, the <s>Ātmanepada</s>; as the base (prakṛti) is for that meaning

children.text: krīṇīṣva vapate dhatte cinoti cinute+api ca
children.translated_text: ‘Buy!’ ‘he sows,’ ‘he takes up,’ ‘he gathers,’ and also ‘he causes to gather’—
authoritative usages are seen in which the meaning of the <s>ṇi</s> (causative) is expressed

children.text: saṃvidhānaṃ pacādināṃ kva cid arthaḥ pratīyate
children.translated_text: A prescribing (or directing) meaning of the ‘cook’-class (verbs like ‘pac-’) is apprehended in some places,
and, as dependent on that, there are also other (meanings) such as the assumption of the action-base, and the like
In the sūtra, ‘the agent’s intention’ is a mark for distinguishing actions,

children.text: tathābhūtā kriyā yā hi tatkartā phalabhāg yataḥ
children.translated_text: for the action being of such a kind is that by which that agent becomes the enjoyer of the result
Just as time is identified by indications such as the sighting of stars,
so a difference of action is exemplified by a distinction of result
When a specification of action is stated, capability is restricted;

children.text: kesāṃ cid anye tu kṛtāḥ svariteto ñitas tathā
children.translated_text: for some, others are formed with the acute accent, and likewise with the <s>ñit</s> (affix bearing ñ-it marker)
And an indicatory marker is attached, with the meaning already accomplished, for the sake of recall,

children.text: tulyārtheṣv api cāvaśyaṃ na sarveṣv ekadharmatā
children.translated_text: and even in meanings that are similar, necessarily there is not a single and same property in all
In the case of ‘seeing’ and ‘knowing,’ though their meaning is similar, there is no identity with what precedes,
therefore those that employ the meaning of <s>ṇi</s> (causative) are not identical in meaning with the ‘cook’-class (pac- etc.)
Since, for ‘do’ existing in the sense of ‘for the sake of’, the properties are different,
therefore, taking up the meaning of <s>ṇi</s>, the powers of words are determinate
Thus, indeed, in the <s>Ātmanepada</s> of ‘do’ in the sense of repeated application,
when the ‘as-before’ inclusion would be obtained, the acute accent presents itself
Even when the action is single as to verbal expression, by the number of instruments or supports,

children.text: bhidyate na tu liṅgākhyo bhedas tatra tadāśritaḥ
children.translated_text: it is differentiated; but the gender-named distinction does not depend thereon

children.text: tasmād avasthite+apy arthe kasya cit pratibadhyate
children.translated_text: Therefore, even though the meaning is established, that of some word is constrained,

children.text: śabdasya śaktiḥ sa tv eṣa śāstre+anvākhyāyate vidhiḥ
children.translated_text: and this is the power of a word; this, in the treatise, is explained as the injunction
That meaning for whose establishment the ‘cook’-class (pac- etc.) is undertaken—

children.text: tat pradhānaṃ phalaṃ teṣāṃ na lābhādi prayojanam
children.translated_text: that is the primary result for them; gain and the like are not the purpose

children.text: yatrobhau svāmidāsau tu prārabhete saha kriyām
children.translated_text: Where both master and servant undertake an action together,

children.text: yugapad dharmabhedena dhātus tatra na vartate
children.translated_text: there, the verbal root does not bear, at the same time, a difference of properties
Where ‘pac-’ is for the purpose of counter-prescription, there the <s>Ātmanepada</s> (is used),
elsewhere, the <s>Parasmaipada</s>, when denoting preparation and the like
And owing to the proximity of the prescriber, the property adheres to the servant,
just as, owing to the proximity of the word ‘plakṣa,’ in the banyan tree there is ‘plakṣa-ness’
And as the designation ‘puroḍāśa’ is established among grains and the like,
and by relation with ‘umbrella-bearer’ there is denotability by the word ‘umbrella-bearer’
Mutual subordination, understood from the context, though not intended to be expressed,

children.text: ity ayaṃ śeṣaviṣayaḥ kaiś cid atrānuvarṇyate
children.translated_text: this domain of residuary implication is here expounded by some

children.text: atha pratividhātā yo halaiḥ kṛṣati pañcabhiḥ
children.translated_text: Now, as for the prescriber who ploughs with five ploughs,
Why, in the <s>Bhāṣya</s>, is it not cited that here the <s>Ātmanepada</s> has been obtained?
If, because that meaning is already established, one were to posit subordination (śeṣatva) for it,
then the optionality, already obtained, would not be; that acute accent would be the preventer

children.text: śuddhe tu saṃvidhānārthe kaiś cid atreṣyate kṛṣiḥ
children.translated_text: But some hold that, in the sense of a pure prescribing (saṃvidhāna), there is here ‘ploughing’,

children.text: taddharmā yajir ity evaṃ na syāt tatrātmanepadam
children.translated_text: thus, “its property is a <s>yajis</s> (yajur-chant/ritual utterer),” and so the <s>Ātmanepada</s> would not (be used) there
But here, by means of the subordinate word (upapada), this difference of meaning is apprehended,
since optionality is (only) made when (it is) already obtained, therefore here there is no <s>Ātmanepada</s>
3.13: <s>liṅga</s>-topic (exposition of gender)
Connection with breasts and hair and the like, or breasts and the like themselves being distinguished,
the genus indicated thereby, the state of a quality, and likewise the qualities—
and also “word-conditioning” (śabda-saṃskāra), whose self is the meaning produced by the word—
these seven alternatives of <s>liṅga</s> (gender) have been shown by those who know the truth of gender
And seven options of taking-up (upādāna) of the <s>liṅgas</s> have been described,
those that are established in words by combination with alternatives and constraints

children.text: tisro jātaya evaitāḥ kesāṃ cit samavasthitāḥ
children.translated_text: These indeed are just three classes, in which, for some, they are co-instantiated,
not incompatible with, and (for others) incompatible with, genera such as cow and buffalo

children.text: hastinyāṃ vaḍavāyāṃ ca strīti buddheḥ samanvayaḥ
children.translated_text: In “she-elephant” and “mare,” there is concord of the notion ‘female’,
therefore they desire that genus which inheres in substance and the rest
As for the gender of what is dependent, when elimination (apoddhāra) is intended,
there that is ‘word-conditioning,’ resorting solely to words

children.text: buddhyā kalpitarūpeṣu liṅgeṣv api ca saṃbhavaḥ
children.translated_text: And there is occurrence even for genders whose forms are constructed by intellect,

children.text: strītvādīnāṃ vyavasthā hi sā liṅgair vyapadiśyate
children.translated_text: for that fixity of femaleness and the like is what is denoted by genders
Just as an appearance of water is produced in mirages,
a cognition, suited to the apprehension of water, arises from a seed, even though water is absent
So too, from causes that are not directly designatable, as in stars and the like,

children.text: mukhyebhya iva liṅgebhyo bhedā loke vyavasthitāḥ
children.translated_text: differences are established in the world, as if from primary genders
Since breasts and the like, having manifest forms, are seen in particulars,
a genus of the unmanifest indicator of an unmanifest is not to be imagined
And for one who, having posited existence, desires constant perception,

children.text: atyantādarśane na syād asattvaṃ prati niścayaḥ
children.translated_text: in absolute non-perception there would not be a determination toward non-existence
Nor is a word, when preceded by non-perception, adequate for inference,

children.text: siddhe hi darśane kiṃ syād anumānaprayojanam
children.translated_text: for when perception is accomplished, what purpose would inference serve?
Emergence and disappearance and persistence—these invariable
properties in all forms are pointed out as genders
For all entities of the nature of forms—such as word and the rest—
the three properties, <s>Sattva</s> (lucidity), and the others (i.e., <s>Rajas</s>, <s>Tamas</s>), are present everywhere in each quality
And of forms and of their bare selves—of white and the like—at every moment,

children.text: kā cit pralīyate kā cit kathaṃ cid abhivardhate
children.translated_text: some part dissolves, some part in some way increases
And like water brought to a boil, their mode of occurrence is unsettled,
unceasing in all entities—this is expounded in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> itself

children.text: pravṛtter ekarūpatvaṃ sāmyaṃ vā sthitir ucyate
children.translated_text: The uniformity of activity, or else equality, is called ‘persistence’,
and it persists by the activity of emergence and disappearance

children.text: guṇā ity eva buddher vā nimittatvaṃ sthitir matā
children.translated_text: Persistence is held to be the cause of the notion ‘qualities alone’,
and, through persistence, ‘all-genderedness’ (assignment to every gender) of all genders is said
When all genders persist, a basis for the regulation of intended expression,

children.text: kasya cic chabdasaṃskāre vyāpāraḥ kva cid iṣyate
children.translated_text: in some cases an operation in some word-conditioning, is admitted

children.text: saṃnidhāne nimittānāṃ kiṃ cid eva pravartakam
children.translated_text: When the causes are present, only something (among them) sets in motion,
just as there is regulation of genders for words like ‘carpenter’ and the like
The learned, observers of the truth of entities, are established regarding word-meanings,

children.text: yad yad dharme+aṅgatām eti liṅgaṃ tat tat pracakṣate
children.translated_text: whatever gender attains accessory-status with respect to some property, that they declare
Just as, by difference of accent, words are correct in another domain,
so, from the difference of gender, correctness is followed as established
Where usage and non-usage are observed in the world,
there the teaching is undertaken, not reversing usage
Owing to a difference of limiting conditions in meanings, the being-a-cause for correctness of some property of a quality,
and the intended expression is fixed
In a snow-forest, femaleness is established on account of greatness,
for a small hut, marked by a short (limiting) condition, there is the capacity for ‘giving birth’ (i.e., ‘producing’)
For understanding of different meanings of different words,
methods have been shown by, as it were, determining unity, for the sake of brevity of meaning

children.text: utpattiḥ prasavo+anyeṣāṃ nāśaḥ saṃstyānam ity api
children.translated_text: For others, ‘origin’ is (so-called), ‘production’ as well, and ‘destruction’, and also ‘stagnation’,

children.text: ātmarūpaṃ tu bhāvānāṃ sthitir ity apadiśyate
children.translated_text: but the self-form of entities is referred to as ‘persistence’

children.text: dṛṣṭaṃ nimittaṃ kesāṃ cij jātyādivad avasthitam
children.translated_text: A perceived cause, for some, is established like <s>jāti</s> (genus) and the rest,
but, like what is perceived, mere ‘word-conditioning’ (<s>śabda-saṃskāra</s>) is imagined
Just as, even where unity is well acknowledged, those clinging to plurality,

children.text: nānātvaṃ janayantīva śabdā liṅge+api sa kramaḥ
children.translated_text: as it were generate plurality; likewise in gender too, that is the procedure with words
“this (neuter), this (feminine), this (masculine)”—a mere ‘word-conditioning’,

children.text: nimittadarśanād arthe kaiś cit sarvatra varṇyate
children.translated_text: on account of observing a cause in the referent, by some, is maintained everywhere
It is not necessary that the cause be fixed as an object,
whatever is observed as the cause of difference—sense-faculty and the like—that is accepted
3.14: Delineation of Functions (<s>vṛtti-samuddeśa</s>)
By censures, praises, and intensifications, the word is properly connected with a completed meaning,
because, beginning from its own sense, all are causes such as censure and the rest
In censure of <s>Devadatta</s> and the like, there occurs an understood ‘censured’,

children.text: kutsitasthā tu yā kutsā tadarthaḥ ko vidhīyate
children.translated_text: but where the censure is situated as censured, what meaning is enjoined there?
‘Excellent’ denotes excellence of white and the like,
and for what is already excellent, ‘more’ and the like (the -tara etc.) are prescribed for intensification

children.text: kutsitatvena kutsyo vā na samyag vāpi kutsitaḥ
children.translated_text: Whether ‘to be censured’ as censured, or not properly censured,
by what is a meaning, denoted by its own word, apprehended as particularized?

children.text: na ca sāṃpratikī kutsā bhedābhāvāt pratīyate
children.translated_text: Nor is present-time censure apprehended, because of absence of difference—
one is honored as censured, and censured as praiseworthy
The relation of qualifier and qualified arises between the two words,
and the nominal-base meaning is not there separated (from it)
The qualified would be what is not yet known; the known entity is the qualifier,
since, as existing for another, the condition of being a remainder belongs to all that render assistance
By rule, there is a distinction of case-endings for the denoters of quality and of that which has quality,
and the establishment of co-reference (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) is for substance-words
When the substance and the genus are not known, the word ‘black’ is employed,
and in the same way, when the quality is not known, the word ‘sesame’ is set in motion
Because universals have no mutual connection, those two are fixed in a particular,

children.text: rūpābhedād viśeṣaṃ tam abhivyaṅktuṃ na śaknutaḥ
children.translated_text: yet, because of non-difference of form, they are not able to manifest that particular
When those very two come together, in presenting by difference,
imposing, as it were, a delimitation, they remove doubt
The substance-nature, because of difference from contact with quality, is separately resorted to,
and because of difference of relation to genus, it is, as it were, grasped as a second
From connections with causes, the similarity to the cause,
by that, even of one thing, plurality is imagined because of difference of forms

children.text: dravyāvasthā tṛtīyā tu yasyāṃ saṃsṛjyate dvayam
children.translated_text: The third condition of substance is that in which the two are compounded,
and because of difference of those two conditions, it is assigned to being a substrate
What is one in cognition is split, and what is split attains unity,

children.text: buddhyāvasthā vibhajyante sā hy arthasya vidhāyikā
