children.translated_text: cognitive conditions are the dividers, for they are the determiners of the object
As in usage, in one thing, plurality is imagined by cognition,
by that, the object-nature, though having a fabricated difference, is designated
Because of difference of action, in things observed, like a stone and so on, again and again,
some seeing is designated by another seeing
From difference of usage of verbal roots, having imagined manifoldness,

children.text: bhedābhedāv upādāya kva cid ekāctvam ucyate
children.translated_text: taking both difference and non-difference, in some cases single-accentedness is stated
By concomitance and its absence, ‘meaningful’ is imagined,
and one (phoneme), through comprehension of the meaning of a root, is metaphorically treated as a letter

children.text: dravyātmānas trayas tasmād buddhau nānā vyavasthitāḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, three substance-natures are variously established in cognition,
as ‘substrate, supporter, and property’—this is the teaching handed down from the elders

children.text: sāmānādhikaraṇyaṃ ca śabdayoḥ kaiś cid iṣyate
children.translated_text: And co-reference (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) between words, some accept,
as also the relation of qualifier and qualified, and name and named
For some, the function in ‘black-sesames’ is desired where genus and quality, inhering in one referent,
with a word that denotes substance
But the substrate of color, taste, and the like is not denoted,
without the denotation of substance; therefore they are in a dual (paired) condition
A denoter of substance, like ‘black’, proceeds with expectancy,
but, because it follows upon a cause, that does not obtain in sesame and the like

children.text: evaṃ jātimati dravye pratyāsanne kriyāṃ prati
children.translated_text: Thus, in a substance possessing a genus, proximate with respect to an action,
the quality-property, with qualities infused, imagines the substance for differentiation
Some desire, among functions, a denotation of mere quality,
because of connection in conventional terms like ‘goat-horse’ and the like, as with established usages by established conventions

children.text: tile pūrvam upātte vā tatraiva matub iṣyate
children.translated_text: In ‘sesame’, when previously taken, or else assumed there, the suffix <s>matup</s> (-mat) is desired,

children.text: sa ca dharmaḥ samāseṣu guṇas tasmād viśeṣaṇam
children.translated_text: and that property, in compounds, is a quality; therefore it is a qualifier
But, in a compound of ‘hard–soft’, although there is, indeed, a functioning-toward-a-single-meaning,

children.text: bhinnam atrādhikaraṇaṃ prāg vṛttes tac ca gṛhyate
children.translated_text: here the locus (adhikaraṇa) is different beforehand in usage, and that is also apprehended
As if woven together by the two differences, a single prominence (repute, presentation as one) arises,
when they call that intended-togetherness (<s>sahavivakṣā</s>) in the <s>dvandva</s> and in the <s>ekaśeṣa</s>
But mutual connection pertains to those that denote an aggregate of distinct members,
and that aggregate, taken individually, is completed among aggregates
Just as, for a complex of operations, in matters like ‘resorting-to’ and the like,

children.text: pratyekaṃ jātivad vṛttis tathā dvandvapadeṣv api
children.translated_text: there is, for each, a functioning like that of a genus, so also in <s>dvandva</s>-words
Here, ‘the half-<s>ṛc</s> of the skilled fellow’, ‘the <s>puroḍāśa</s> (sacrificial cake) [share]’, ‘the umbrella-bearers’ are examples,

children.text: te viṣṇumitrā iti ca bhinneṣu sahacāriṣu
children.translated_text: and ‘they are <s>Viṣṇu</s>-<s>mitra</s>’ too, where companions are distinct
Because they denote a different meaning, and because they reside in a different meaning,

children.text: yābhyāṃ caikam anekārthaṃ tābhyām evāparaṃ padam
children.translated_text: by the two of which one becomes many-meaninged, by those very two another word [arises]
And because it is a different aggregate, such a meaning is not worldly (conventional),
even the scriptural meaning is not seen by concomitance and its absence

children.text: duḥkhā durupapādā ca tasmād bhāṣye+apy udāhṛtā
children.translated_text: Therefore, even in the Bhāṣya, ‘duḥkhā’, ‘durupapādā’ are cited,
but that simultaneous denotability is adopted for the sake of practical usage
Having undertaken the aggregate, a word is employed with respect to it,

children.text: vibhāgena samākhyāne tatas tad dvyartham ucyate
children.translated_text: and, when delineating by division, therefore that is said to be double-meaninged

children.text: vākye+api niyatā dharmāḥ ke cid vṛttau dvayos tathā
children.translated_text: Even in a sentence certain properties are fixed in usage for two (members) as well,

children.text: te tv abhedena sāmarthya- mātra evopavarṇitāḥ
children.translated_text: but these, without distinction, are described merely by capacity (contextual power)
In usage, because of functioning as particular, and in difference, because of denoting the universal,
examples like ‘black’ and the like are given in simile and in compound

children.text: vṛttir anyapadārthe yā tasyā vākyeṣv asaṃbhavaḥ
children.translated_text: That functioning which is toward the meaning of another word—of that there is no possibility in sentences,

children.text: cārthe dvandvapadānāṃ ca bhede vṛttir na vidyate
children.translated_text: and for the meanings of <s>dvandva</s>-words, when there is distinction, there is no functioning
When distinction obtains, for those without prefixes there is no possibility in meanings like ‘crossed’ and the like,

children.text: prāg vṛtter jātivācitvaṃ na ca gaurakharādiṣu
children.translated_text: and prior to usage there is no denotation of genus in ‘cow–donkey’ and the like
Likewise, because play and livelihood are not stated by the sentence,

children.text: na nityagrahaṇaṃ yuktaṃ kauṭilye yaṅvidhau yathā
children.translated_text: a constant taking (of them) is not appropriate, as in the crooked-formation rule of <s>yaṅ</s>
Since dependence is established in the domain of specification and the like,
therefore there is no purpose for prohibitions of compounding
By injunctions and prohibitions, illustration of difference and non-difference
has been effected regarding the one-form-ness of the <s>dvandva</s>, as with the instruction on aggregate-function
Although capacity is stated without distinction, by worldly convention
knowers of usage have distinguished, for the practitioners, between functioning and non-functioning
Because the meaning is removed, there is no conflict with elision and the like,
therefore the very state of being of one meaning is prescribed as the name ‘compound’

children.text: vyavasthitavibhāṣā ca sāmānye kaiś cid iṣyate
children.translated_text: And a settled optionality is accepted by some in common cases,
likewise a sentence when there is dependence, and elsewhere the compound is taught
Because of equal accent, even when the truth (referent) is resorted to like ‘king’ and the rest,
in usage, expectation of a qualifier, being a sign, is dismissed
A relational word is always used as dependent,

children.text: svārthavat sā vyapekṣāsya vṛttāv api na hīyate
children.translated_text: and, having dependence just like its own meaning, it is not diminished even in usage
Those whose relation is with the aggregate, by ‘teacher’s house’ and the like,
touching the parts as well, are joined together with that which possesses it

children.text: abudhān praty upāyāś ca vicitrāḥ pratipattaye
children.translated_text: And various expedients, for the unlearned, are for comprehension,
because of being different words, there is an absolute difference between sentence and compound
Because of non-observation in non-compound and in compound, in ‘cow-chariot’ and the like,
no cessation or following of forms like ‘yukta-’ and the rest has been laid down by the śāstra

children.text: śabdāntaratvād yuktādiḥ kva cid vākye prayujyate
children.translated_text: Because it is a different word, ‘yukta-’ and the like is used somewhere in a sentence,
and ‘gata-’ too in usages like ‘withers-leaves’ and the like
Some accept, for sentence and usage, the relation of qualifier and qualified, and likewise a single substrate,
because, regarding the method, there is insight into the principle (tattva)
Just as a word like ‘tree’ is fixed with respect to a qualified object,

children.text: nīlotpalādy api tathā bhāgābhyāṃ vartate vinā
children.translated_text: so too ‘blue-lotus’ functions even without (explicit) parts
And for ‘having the ear-learning’, ‘having the field’, and the like, there is no apprehension in the world, like ‘of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>’, ‘of <s>Gārgya</s>’,
by reason of non-accord with a uniform form

children.text: saptaparṇādivad bhedo na vṛttau vidyate kva cit
children.translated_text: As with ‘seven-leaved’ and the like, there is no distinction anywhere in usage,
and a division of conventional and non-conventional is made for comprehension

children.text: yā sāmānyāśrayā saṃjñā viśeṣaviṣayā ca yā
children.translated_text: That designation which has the universal as its locus, and that which has the particular as its object—
because of the frequentative-taking, there is no activation (of both) of those two
If, in ‘having very fine matted hair’ and the like, a compound should be in a part,
the sound of the part would, there, because of being internal, be an overrider
And in the functioning of the aggregate, a single part is not optionally allowed,

children.text: bheda eva vibhāṣāyā niyato viṣayo yataḥ
children.translated_text: for the fixed domain of optionality is only difference

children.text: yataś cāviṣayaḥ so+asyās tasmān nāsty akṛtārthatā
children.translated_text: And since that (optional rule) has no scope here, therefore there is no purposelessness,
because, in the procedure of non-difference, differences are entirely set aside

children.text: mahākaṣṭaśritety evaṃ na syād bhedaḥ padatraye
children.translated_text: Thus, in ‘mahā-kaṣṭa-āśrita’ (‘resting on a great log’), there would not be a difference among the three words,
since, in usage, the taking (governance) of a part is not prohibited

children.text: mahāraṇyam atīte tu tripadād bhidyate svaraḥ
children.translated_text: But in ‘mahā-raṇyam atīte’ (‘having passed through the great forest’), the accent differs from that of the triple-word (compound),
because there, being internal, the accent of the part overrides
However, because the <s>śiṣṭa</s> (learned usage) is stronger when a remainder (of conditions) exists, the thāthādi-accent alone,

children.text: dvipade tena yagapat tritayaṃ na samasyate
children.translated_text: applies in a two-word expression; therefore the triad is not compounded at once
For those whose being-honored is absent, since they follow another’s purpose,
even the relation of qualifier and qualified is not posited for them
Even though a specification is heard, whether in primaries or in accessories,

children.text: śabdāntaratvād vākye tu vṛttau nityaṃ na vidyate
children.translated_text: because it is a different word, in a sentence, such functioning is never present
When the relation to a specified action has not been taken up by kṛt-affixes and the like,
another word ‘kṛta’ operates independent of a qualifier

children.text: akarmakatve saty evaṃ ktāntaṃ bhāvābhidhāyi tat
children.translated_text: Thus, when intransitivity is present, the -kta derivative denotes a state (bhāva),

children.text: tataḥ kriyāvatā kartrā yogo bhavati karmaṇām
children.translated_text: therefore there is connection of objects (karmans) with an agent who possesses an action
Just as an indivisible (form) like ‘gata-’ is connected with objects like ‘village’ (grāma) as its karman,
so too the action is connected when it resides in forms like ‘kṛta-pūrva-’ (‘previously done’) and the like
Roots, divided and posited as if endowed with parts that do not exist—like ‘muṇḍi’, ‘sūtrvā’ and the like—
are imagined as having separate selves, like pounding and rubbing

children.text: putrīyatau na putro+asti viśeṣecchā tu tādṛśī
children.translated_text: In the desiderative for ‘having a son’ (putrīyā), there is not (necessarily) a son; rather, there is such a will to the specific (result),
which stands with respect to ‘son’ even without actual accompaniment by a son

children.text: prāṇair vinā yathā dhārir jīvatau prāṇakarmakaḥ
children.translated_text: Just as, without the vital breaths, ‘living’ (jīvati) is one whose action concerns the breaths,

children.text: na cātra dhārir na prāṇā jīvatis tu kriyāntaram
children.translated_text: yet here there is neither a holder nor the breaths; rather, ‘jīvati’ is a different action
So too, in the desiderative regarding ‘to remove’ and ‘son’ (vineṣin, putra), there is a different action in ‘putrīyā’,
and the distinctions, for explanatory repetition, are instructive by means of analogies
And because of presupposition (ākṣepa), when the usage concerns a different domain,

children.text: sad apīcchākyacaḥ karma vākya eva prayujyate
children.translated_text: even though the object exists, the desiderative of ‘icchā’ (wish) is employed only in a sentence
A word established for denigrating a state (bhāva-garhā) has taken over the familiar usage,
and, because of similarity in form in habitual usage, yaṅ-derivatives are not employed

children.text: śabdā yathā vibhajyante bhāgair iva vikalpitaiḥ
children.translated_text: Just as words are divided by parts that are merely posited,
so too the śāstra, being situated very far off, is to be expounded piece by piece
Seeing merely some following of a meaning, one imagines

children.text: padaṃ vākye pade dhātur dhātau bhāgaś ca muṇḍivat
children.translated_text: a ‘word’ in a sentence, a ‘root’ in a word, and a ‘part’ in a root, like a shaven head
Non-variation in correct usage and an unstable derivation—
one should not, as to truth, fancy the methods of apprehension

children.text: yathaiva ḍitthe davatiḥ pācake pacatis tathā
children.translated_text: Just as, in the ḍit-class, ‘ḍavatiḥ’, and for a cook ‘pacati’, so too,

children.text: ḍayatiś ca paciś caiva dvāv apy etāv alaukikau
children.translated_text: both ‘ḍayati’ and ‘paci’ are indeed two non-worldly (forms)

children.text: prakṛtipratyayāv ūhyau padāt tābhyāṃ padaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: The base and affix are to be inferred, and so too the word from them; likewise,

children.text: anubandhasvarādibhyaḥ śiṣṭaiḥ śāstraṃ na tān prati
children.translated_text: because of markers, accents, and the like, the śāstra is not directed toward the learned
But the śāstra’s view is of the śāstra even when attainment is only partial and uncertain,
it coheres by way of adverse consequence: the śāstra is an eye for those who do not see
And because of denoting a different meaning, the order (prior–posterior) is in no way altered
in formations like ‘rāja-danta’, ‘ahita-agni’, etc., compared with ‘rājāśva’, etc.
Those like ‘Garga’, who in usage denote different meanings even without affixes,
being with elision (luk) for them, their correctness is accepted
[If, due to the connection ‘so+ayam’ (‘this very one’), without an affix,
words like ‘Bhṛgu’, etc., were used, there would be no restriction to the filial sense,
in the connection ‘so+ayam’, apart from indication by gender and other hints,
in ‘praṣṭha’, etc., by rule there would not at all be apprehension (of the intended sense)
If, moreover, one accepts a special relation of measurer and measured,
then the incorrectness of ‘prastha’, etc., would result unless with a taddhita affix

children.text: taddhito yogabhedena vākyaṃ vā syād vibhāṣitam
children.translated_text: A taddhita, by difference of construction, would be optionally a sentence,
and, where there is excess of quantity, the nominative is again preserved

children.text: vyatiriktasya sādhutve tad eva ca nidarśanam
children.translated_text: When the distinct (reading) is correct, that itself is the illustration,
and the accepted excess is compatible with all the cases
Because of the display of exception, the omission of ‘matu’ in ‘śukla’ and the like,
is ‘correct’ in order to remove incorrectness, like ‘bidā’, etc.
From the qualifier, upon the increase of ‘being that’ (tad-bhāva) in the qualified sense,

children.text: punaś ca pratisaṃhāre vṛttim eke pracakṣate
children.translated_text: and then again upon re-collection (pratisaṃhāra), some declare the functioning (of compounds)
When there is a cause (nimitta), the affix comes first; it is not subsequently obtained together with the caused entity (nimittin),
and, though there is a cognition in the one who possesses the cause, there is no identity of form with the cause
Because cognitions are accompanied by dispositions (saṃskāra), even memory does not have adhesion (literal fusion),

children.text: vyāpāre tannimittānāṃ na grāhyaṃ syāt tathā sthitam
children.translated_text: in the operation of those whose cause is that, the object would not be graspable—thus it stands
And, when the modification is in the inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa-vṛtti</s>), imagining an external object is futile

children.text: tasmād anupakāre vā grāhyaṃ vā na tathā sthitam
children.translated_text: Therefore, where there is no assistance, or as to what is to be grasped, it is not established in that way
As if threaded together, cognition proceeds toward an object compounded (by factors),
the commentators, dividing the parts of the meaning, state those by way of differentiation
And, while relying on a distinct cognition in that whose nature is undivided,
they suppose, as it were, a division between qualifier and qualified

children.text: abudhān prati vṛttiṃ ca vartayantaḥ prakalpitām
children.translated_text: While they conduct a usage fashioned for the unlearned,
they say that, in speech intended for another’s understanding, there is the property of abandonment and accumulation (i.e., omitting some and adding others)

children.text: anvayād gamyate so+artho virodhī vā nivartate
children.translated_text: By concomitance (anvaya) that meaning is inferred, or, being contradictory, it is excluded,
or, being ambiguous or pertaining to a different meaning, they there call it the subordinate member (upasarjana)

children.text: upāyamātraṃ nānātvaṃ samūhas tv eka eva saḥ
children.translated_text: Multiplicity is merely a means; the aggregate is one and the same,
or, by alternative and accumulation, there is the imagining of combination of difference
Thus, while setting forth the function (vṛtti) for the apprehension of the unlearned,
the means of instruction, being various, are unsettled among persons

children.text: vācikā dyotikā vāpi saṃkhyānāṃ vā vibhaktayaḥ
children.translated_text: Whether verbal, indicative, or numerical, the case-endings,
when the operation is upon that-form as a part, the difference of number ceases
Or, an undifferentiated unity-number arises there,
that undivided is said to be the form of the conjunction (saṃsarga) of numbers
Just as all the potencies of medicinal essences, when placed in honey,

children.text: avibhāgena vartante tāṃ saṃkhyāṃ tādṛśīṃ viduḥ
children.translated_text: operate without division—such is the number they understand there

children.text: bhedānāṃ vā parityāgāt saṃkhyātmā sa tathāvidhaḥ
children.translated_text: Or, by the abandonment of differences, its nature as number is of that sort,
it operates, by the activity of a portion of the <s>jāti</s> (genus), through the exclusion of difference (apoha)
As, with the specific differences not apprehended, by the form ‘form-endowed’ one is made known,

children.text: prakhyāyate na śuklādi- bhedarūpas tu gṛhyate
children.translated_text: but the form constituted by the differences ‘white’, etc., is what is apprehended
When there is inclusion of difference-forms, and yet those are not intended to be expressed,

children.text: bhāgaḥ prakāśitaḥ kaś cic chāstre+aṅgatvena gṛhyate
children.translated_text: some portion, being made manifest in the śāstra, is taken as a limb (constitutive element)
Then, by the general form of number, that portion is cognized,
while the object has many powers, the words, having fixed powers, (pick out that portion)

children.text: avyayānāṃ ca yo dharmo yaś ca bhedavatāṃ kramaḥ
children.translated_text: The property of indeclinables and the sequence belonging to those with difference (i.e., inflected forms)—
the interval suited to an undifferentiated designation lies between these two

children.text: alukaś caikavadbhāvas tasmin sati na śiṣyate
children.translated_text: And the absence of elision (<s>aluk</s>) in the state of oneness is not maintained,
and that is a property, in another expression, of words like ‘<s>goṣucara</s>’ and the like

children.text: jātau dvivacanābhāvāt tad vṛttiṣu na vidyate
children.translated_text: Because there is no dual number in a <s>jāti</s> (genus), that does not occur in its functions,
but, upon the rejection of the <s>yoga</s> (derivational relation), ‘<s>goṣucara</s>’ and the like are (treated as) substances
Because the possession of difference rests on the substrate, there is compatibility with all differences,
yet the view that the word denotes a substance is not found for a term naming a <s>jāti</s>
Thus, the movement to every substance and the ‘one-remainder’ (ekaśeṣa) are not stated,
if the sūtra is otherwise rejected, there would be movement to different substances
The state of ‘being as if connected’ that remains in uses like ‘<s>varaṇa</s>’ and the rest,
does not succeed there, in ‘<s>go-dāu</s>’, for the undifferentiated unity-number

children.text: prāg vṛtter yuktavadbhāve ṣaṣṭhī bhedāśrayā bhavet
children.translated_text: If, before the use, there is the state of ‘being as if connected’, the sixth case (genitive) would rely on difference,
but, in use, because of abandoning distinctions of number, difference ceases

children.text: vidyamānāsu saṃkhyāsu ke cit saṃkhyāntaraṃ viduḥ
children.translated_text: While the numbers exist, some know another number,
called ‘undifferentiated’, which is apprehending; and, in use, that arises

children.text: vyāpāraṃ yāti bhedākhyais tat svair avayavaiḥ kva cit
children.translated_text: It goes into operation with its own parts, called by difference, somewhere,

children.text: ātmā bhedānapekṣo+asya kva cid eti nimittatām
children.translated_text: elsewhere its own nature, not depending on difference, becomes the cause

children.text: dāsyāḥ patir iti vyakto godāv iti ca dṛśyate
children.translated_text: ‘Husband of a slave-woman’ is explicit, and ‘in the two cows’ (<s>go-dāu</s>) is also seen,
therefore the diversity of the operation of number is fixed just so

children.text: dvyādināṃ ca dviputrādau bāhyo bhedo nivartate
children.translated_text: And, for dv- and the like, in ‘two sons’ (<s>dvi-putra</s>) and such, the external difference ceases,
being to be expressed by case-endings, because it has its own sense; but the cause (nimitta) remains established
When ‘two’ is the subordinate member in a collective, the word ‘dvi’ functions there,

children.text: so+ayam ity abhisaṃbandhād ubhaśabde na tat tathā
children.translated_text: but, because of the connection ‘so+ayam’ (‘this very one’), that is not so with the word ‘ubha’ (‘both’)

children.text: ubhayas tatra tulyārtho vṛttau nityaṃ prayujyate
children.translated_text: There ‘both’, being of equal meaning, is always used in the usage,
and in the sūtra too the term ‘nitya’ (constant) is stated for that purpose
And some, because of having a different purpose, say that non-difference does not arise,

children.text: ubhe iti tataḥ svārthe bhede vṛttiḥ prayujyate
children.translated_text: therefore, with ‘ubhe’ in its own sense, in difference, the usage is employed
Even on the view that the word denotes femaleness (<s>strītva</s>), there is a reversal regarding the status of attribute (guṇa-bhāva)

children.text: svabhāvād aparārthatvāt tatra bhedo na hīyate
children.translated_text: Because of its own nature and because it is not for the sake of something else (parārtha), there the difference is not lost
Therefore, from the dual-number, the affix ṭāp is seen for both and elsewhere,

children.text: pratyayaṃ tayapaṃ hitvā nāsty uttarapade punaḥ
children.translated_text: but, abandoning the affix tayap, it does not occur again in the latter member
The attainment of the designation ‘<s>pragṛhya</s>’ would not arise, because of the definition of affix,

children.text: kumāryagāre na hy asti samāso vacanāntare
children.translated_text: for there is no compound, in another number, in ‘<s>kumāry-agāre</s>’ (‘in the maiden’s house’)

children.text: ekadvayor yañādināṃ vibhāṣā luṅ na kalpate
children.translated_text: Optionally, the <s>luṅ</s> (aorist) is not applicable for ‘one’ and ‘two’ and for yañ and the rest,

children.text: yauṣmākas tāvakaś ceti bhedābhāvān na sidhyati
children.translated_text: for ‘yauṣmāka’ and ‘tāvaka’ do not succeed because of the absence of difference

children.text: dṛṣṭo gārgyatare bhedas tathā gargatarā iti
children.translated_text: A difference is observed in ‘<s>gārgy‑atare</s>’, and likewise ‘<s>garga‑tarā</s>’,
and the substitutions ‘<s>yuṣmat‑pitā</s>’ and ‘<s>tvat‑pitā</s>’ are established accordingly
The number which is an incidental qualifier (upādhi), being present in the base,

children.text: ādeśaiḥ samjnayā vāpi vibhaktyā vyajyate vinā
children.translated_text: is manifested by substitutions or by a technical term, even without case-ending
In ‘<s>śaurpika</s>’ and in ‘<s>māsajāta</s>’ the measure is by nature,
relying on the number that is an incidental qualifier, it operates with difference

children.text: vayasvini paricchedaḥ krīte cāpi na gamyate
children.translated_text: In ‘<s>vayasvini</s>’ (mature woman) and in ‘<s>krīta</s>’ (purchased) too, delimitation is not apprehended,
except where non-difference is intended; there, a measure (for number) is useless
Since a term expressing difference is heard, the rule of ‘śa’ (the affix śas) applies to ‘<s>prastha</s>’ and the like,

children.text: taddharmatvād abhedāt tu ghaṭādibhyo na dṛśyate
children.translated_text: but, because there is non-difference as a property of those (measures), it is not seen for ‘<s>ghaṭa</s>’ and the like

children.text: śrūyate vacanaṃ yatra bhāvas tatra viśiṣyate
children.translated_text: Where an injunction is heard, there the state (bhāva) is specified,

children.text: nivartate yad vacanaṃ tasya bhāvo na vidyate
children.translated_text: but where the injunction is withdrawn, the state of that (thing) is not present
Action depends on existence; from the śāstra, non-application is non-perception,

children.text: vākye dṛṣṭaṃ yad atyantam abhāvas tasya vṛttiṣu
children.translated_text: that which is seen as absolute absence in the sentence has no function
Non-perception that is consequent (only) for the sake of specifying the scope of a technical term is remembered,
but an injunction that is heard is apprehended as specified

children.text: abhāvo vā luko yatra rūpavān vā vidhīyate
children.translated_text: Where either absence or <s>luk</s> (elision) is enjoined, or a form with shape (i.e., overt morphology) is enjoined,
because the condition is inconstant, an improper (derivation) would result there
Difference, or a specification of number, has been explained for operations and for rules,

children.text: sarvatraiva viśeṣas tu nāvaśyaṃ tādṛśo bhavet
children.translated_text: yet a specification need not everywhere be of that sort

children.text: āteś ca bhedahetutvān na liṅgena viśeṣyate
children.translated_text: And because the affix (ādeśa/ātta) is a cause of difference, it is not specified by gender,

children.text: pradhānaṃ mṛgadugdhādau gārgīputre na sa kramaḥ
children.translated_text: the head (primary item) is in ‘milk of a deer’ (<s>mṛga‑dugdha</s>) and the like; in ‘son of <s>Gārgī</s>’ that sequence does not hold

children.text: abhede liṅgasaṃkhyābhyāṃ yogāc chuklaṃ paṭā iti
children.translated_text: In non-difference, by gender and number, because of syntactic connection, ‘a white cloth’ (<s>śuklaṃ paṭā</s>) (is formed),
the śāstra is undertaken, when the issue arises, for the accomplishment of gender and number
Whoever, in operations, apprehends the state of being subordinate (śeṣa) as intended for another (parārtha),
that, being a <s>guṇa</s> (attribute) in the capacity of qualifier, is designated in the sūtra

children.text: śabdāntaratvād vākyeṣu viśeṣā yady api śrutāḥ
children.translated_text: Although specifications are heard in sentences because of a different word,

children.text: vṛtter abhinnarūpatvāt teṣu vṛttir na vidyate
children.translated_text: due to the non-difference of form in the operation, there is no operation among them
And because the shaping of the word (śabda‑saṃskāra) is by form and has a universal (sāmānya) as its object,

children.text: tasmāt tadāśrayaṃ liṅgaṃ vacanaṃ ca prasajyate
children.translated_text: therefore gender and number, relying on that, are enjoined

children.text: saliṅgaṃ ca sasaṃkhyaṃ ca tato dravyābhidhāyinā
children.translated_text: And then, a word that denotes a substance, together with gender and number,

children.text: saṃbadhyate padaṃ tatra tayor bhinnā śrutir bhavet
children.translated_text: is connected there; in that case the audition (śruti) of those two will be distinct
Those, by reason of the statement concerning the external (bahiraṅga) of what is to come (future referent), of the substrate,
gender and number, as properties, are set forth by the sūtra
And even though there is a function of specification, because of non-difference of form,

children.text: yasmād viśeṣas tenātra bhedakāryaṃ na kalpate
children.translated_text: the specification is unmarked; therefore here an effect that produces difference is not established

children.text: viśeṣa eva sāmānyaṃ viśesād bhidyate yataḥ
children.translated_text: Specification itself is the universal, since it is from specification that (something) is distinguished,
for non-difference, when relied upon, is what removes specifications

children.text: yad yad āśrīyate tat tad anyasya vinivartakam
children.translated_text: Whatever is relied upon is, each time, the remover of the other,
but the division into difference and non-difference is not determined within the universal
And the universal is ‘extraction’ (<s>apoddhāra</s>); therefore, for that which assists it,
it abides only in the condition of a cause; hence it is grasped by its own property
Because its property is not fixed, only differences are conceptualized,
they are indicated by causes (nimitta), marked by the appellation ‘universal’
But when gender and number are identified by their own nature,

children.text: prayogeṣv eva sādhutvaṃ vākye prakramyate tadā
children.translated_text: then correctness arises only in usages, proceeding within the sentence
There the usage of attributes is not fixed with their substrates,

children.text: sāmānyaṃ yat tad atyantaṃ tatraiva samavasthitam
children.translated_text: the universal, to the utmost, is established right there

children.text: na gotvaṃ śābaleyasya gaur iti vyapadiśyate
children.translated_text: ‘<s>Gotva</s>’ (cowness) of a <s>Śābaleya</s> is not designated by ‘he is a cow’ (<s>gauḥ</s> iti) (i.e., one does not predicate the universal with the individual name),
but ‘whiteness’ of a <s>Bāhuleya</s> is designated by ‘he is white’ (<s>śukla</s> iti)

children.text: vyatireke ca saty evaṃ matupaḥ śravanaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: And when separation (vyatireka) is indeed present thus, the hearing of the affix <s>matup</s> would obtain,

children.text: lug anvākhyāyate tasmād rasādibhyaś ca nāsti saḥ
children.translated_text: but <s>lug</s> (elision) is stated; therefore that (affix) does not occur from ‘<s>rasa</s>’ and the like

children.text: yat so+ayam iti saṃbandhād rūpābhedena vartate
children.translated_text: Because, with the connection ‘this very one’ (so+ayam), it proceeds without difference of form,

children.text: śuklādivat tato lopas tad rasādau na vidyate
children.translated_text: there is deletion like ‘white’ and the rest; therefore it is not present for ‘<s>rasa</s>’ and the like

children.text: āveśo liṅgasaṃkhyābhyāṃ kva cin mañcādivat sthitah
children.translated_text: Assimilation (āveśa) by gender and number is established somewhere, like in ‘bed’ and the like (<s>mañca</s>‑etc.),

children.text: so+ayam ity abhisaṃbandhe sa prasthādau na vidyate
children.translated_text: but, under the connection ‘this very one’ (<s>so+ayam</s>), it is not present at the beginning of a sentence
Gender, when gender is abandoned, the sūtra is the injunction concerning affixes,
because, from the connection ‘this very one’ (<s>so+ayam</s>), in a masculine word one that denotes the feminine is expressed
In the substrate (<s>āśraya</s>), by gender and number, what depends on the substrate (<s>āśrita</s>) is designated,
and this, according to the established doctrine of the śāstra, is that, for qualifiers (<s>viśeṣaṇa</s>), their class-nature (<s>jāti</s>) is not intended
Because the properties that follow their causes (are regulated) by the condition of the cause (<s>nimittānuvidhāyitva</s>), being in the sources of difference,

children.text: ta āśraye+api vidyanta iti buddhir nivartyate
children.translated_text: the notion that they also exist in the substrate is refuted
And it is stated by the śāstra that, by common usage and by nature,
the operation of gender and number is, in cow and the like (<s>go</s>‑etc.), equal to their causes (i.e., conforms to their indicators)
In words like ‘<s>harītakī</s>’ and the like, the individual is denoted; number, in words like ‘<s>khalatika</s>’ and the like,
for subclasses of ‘man’, there is a twofold locus of what is denoted
If, in usage of a class-term (<s>jāti</s>), the qualifier enters into relation with the class,

children.text: viśeṣaṇaṃ tato dharmāñ jātes tat pratipadyate
children.translated_text: then the qualifier apprehends properties belonging to the class from that (relation)
A qualifier other than the class, when it is conjoined with a stem ending in <s>lub</s> (i.e., with taddhita-type base),
since the <s>lub</s>-ending form is primary, is designated by the properties of that (primary member)
The distinctions, according to the Bhāṣya, in negative compounds (<s>nañ</s>-samāsa), <s>bahuvrīhi</s>, dual compounds (<s>dvandva</s>), and in the sense of excess in the feminine,
are to be stated with respect to gender and number
If the comparatives and the like beginning with ‘more’ (<s>tama</s> etc.), built on genitive or accusative forms,

children.text: nyakkāriṇi syur utkṛṣṭe prakṛteḥ syād viliṅgatā
children.translated_text: were abusive when derived from an inferior base and, when from a superior one, would cause absence of the gender of the base

children.text: kālyāṃ kālād dvitīyāntāt kāle kālyās tarab bhavet
children.translated_text: From ‘<s>kālī</s>’ (black) in the genitive ‘of Kālin’ or from the accusative ‘Kālin’, in ‘time’ (<s>kāle</s>), the comparative ‘more Kālin’ (<s>tarap</s>) would occur,

children.text: nyakkāriṇi tathā gārgye gargebhyaḥ pratyayo bhavet
children.translated_text: likewise, being abusive, in the case of <s>Gārgī</s>, the affix would come from ‘the <s>Gargas</s>’ (<s>gargebhyaḥ</s>)

children.text: nyakkartṛṣu ca gargeṣu gārgyāt syāt tac ca neṣyate
children.translated_text: And in ‘the <s>Gargas</s>’ as the agents of abuse, it would come from ‘of <s>Gārgī</s>’ (<s>gārgyāt</s>), and that is not accepted,

children.text: kumāryāḥ svārthike ṅīp syāt prakṛtyartho hi nādhikaḥ
children.translated_text: in ‘of the maiden’ (<s>kumāryāḥ</s>) the affix <s>ṅīp</s> is used for the own sense (feminine formation), for the meaning of the base is not exceeded
Therefore, from a genitive-ending, when there is something additional over (the base), an attribute that abides in its own substrate,
or when an action inheres in something supremely excellent, is enjoined

children.text: upāttaṃ ca prakṛtyartho dravyam evāśrayas tayoḥ
children.translated_text: And the meaning of the base that has been taken up is only substance as the substrate of those two (gender and number),
by the connection ‘this very one’ (<s>so+ayam</s>) it is apprehended as non-different

children.text: rūpābhedāc ca tad dravyam ākāṅkṣāvat pratīyate
children.translated_text: And because of non-difference of form, that substance, being expectancy-bearing (fitting the context), is apprehended,

children.text: viśeṣair bhinnarūpais tad āśrayair iva yujyate
children.translated_text: and with distinct properties of different forms, it is joined as it were with those substrates
The gender that is established among distinct forms in the qualifiers,

children.text: saṃkhyā ca tābhyām dravyātmā so+abhinno vyapadiśyate
children.translated_text: and number—by these two, the substance-nature, being non-different, is designated
The substrate is also the inherent locus, the cause for gender and number,
the passive-stative sense (<s>śeti</s>) which makes abiding in the agent; therefore the Bhāṣya is cited
If the cause were apprehended in the capacity of substrate, as an instrument (of denotation),
then attainment, for gender and number, would occur in what is designated as object (i.e., in the patient)
In the śāstra, being extracted from the aggregate in the capacity of cause (<s>nimitta</s>),

children.text: stryarthas tasyecchayā yogaḥ prakṛtyā pratyayena vā
children.translated_text: the feminine sense has its conjunction by his (speaker’s) intention, either by the base or by the affix
The word ‘woman’ (<s>strī</s>), because it is a word of attribute (<s>guṇa</s>), has properties equal to ‘white’ and the like,
it should be employed in the attribute alone, or when the substrate is present with persistence (i.e., stable possession)

children.text: stryarthaḥ saṃstyānavad dravyaṃ prakṛtyarthaś ca yady asau
children.translated_text: If that feminine sense is substance when there is persistence, and is also the base-meaning,
then the persistence would be for the purpose of indicating the substance

children.text: saṃstyānena kva cid dravyaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ yady upalakṣitam
children.translated_text: If, in some case, a substance is seen as indicated by persistence,
since that persistence is not accepted, the affix would be with reference to what it functions in
When the six named (derivatives) beginning with ‘<s>bhūta</s>’ and the like are delimited by persistence,

children.text: brāhmaṇyādau yadā vṛttās tebhyaḥ syuḥ pratyayās tadā
children.translated_text: then, when they function in ‘<s>brāhmaṇī</s>’ and the like, affixes should be from those
For those possessing that (persistence), being primary, are the activators of affixes,
therefore, even in co-reference (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>), there is possibility of <s>ṭāb</s> and the like
When it is stated, in the word ‘woman’ (<s>strī</s>), that only attribute is denoted,

children.text: prakṛtyarthaś ca saṃstyānaṃ svārthikāḥ pratyayās tadā
children.translated_text: then persistence is the base-meaning, and the affixes are for the own sense

children.text: saṃstyāne kevale vṛttiḥ prakṛtīnām na vidyate
children.translated_text: There is no functioning of bases in bare persistence,
but, when that has entered into a substance, then those that are equally present are apprehended

children.text: upakāri ca saṃstyānaṃ yeṣu śabdeṣv apekṣitam
children.translated_text: And the persistence that is required in certain words as a helper,

children.text: tebhyaṣ ṭābādayas tac ca bhūtādiṣv avivakṣitam
children.translated_text: from those there are <s>ṭāb</s> and the like, and that is not intended in ‘<s>bhūta</s>’ and the like
When persistence, as the meaning of the affix, is purely relied upon,
then the state of dual or multiple affixes does not obtain
If the class (<s>jāti</s>) is ‘womanhood’ (<s>strītvam</s>) itself, then that is the class, and difference elsewhere is not intended,

children.text: yasmād bhinnair api dravyais tad ekaṃ sad viśiṣyate
children.translated_text: because, being one, it is specified even by different substances

children.text: mātrāṇām hi tirobhāve parimāṇam na vidyate
children.translated_text: For when the measures (units) are concealed, there is no magnitude

children.text: kumārya iti tena syāt kumāryāṃ bhedasaṃbhavāt
children.translated_text: By the term ‘young woman’ (<s>kumārya</s>) thus it would be (denoted), because in ‘in the young woman’ (<s>kumāryām</s>) there is the possibility of differentiation
Just as, with class (<s>jāti</s>), number (<s>saṃkhyā</s>), and aggregates (collectives) as concomitants,
actions operate in a substrate (<s>dravya</s>) when unity of essence is expected,
so, from the observation that the properties of form belong to forms,
co-reference (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) and the connection of actions are established
But, when in co-reference the dropping of <s>matup</s> is expected,

children.text: luk taddhitalukīti syāl luk tatrāpy upalakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: there would be elision (<s>luk</s>) by ‘<s>taddhita-luk</s>’; and ‘<s>luk</s>’ even there is to be taken as indicative (i.e., illustrative)

children.text: kesāṃ cit tyaktabhedeṣu dravyeṣv eva vidhīyate
children.translated_text: For some, when distinctions have been abandoned, it is prescribed only in substances,
since, in those lacking persistence, <s>ṭāb</s> and the like, by non-difference, accord with them
The substance-nature, being what is common, with a delimited grasp,
is joined by actions through distinctions, and it stands established part-by-part
In ‘white’ and the like the substrate-substance is denoted primarily,
but ‘womanhood’ (<s>strītva</s>), being the meaning of the affix, is that which is to be denoted by reason of the meaning
By the connection ‘this very one’ (<s>so+ayam</s>) it apprehends the substrate,
and ‘womanhood’ (<s>strītva</s>) is either established as a natural property, or there is a reversal (shift) into the status of attribute
Because it is expectancy-bearing, as an attribute, the universal (<s>sāmānya</s>) too is enjoined,
this being a self-property of individuals, grounded in a presentation as one
And such a state as this, upon the acceptance of division into parts,

children.text: kṛte buddhyaiva bhedānām āśrayatve ca kalpite
children.translated_text: when, by intellect, the statuses of distinctions and of being substrates are posited
then, even when distinctions have been extracted, on the basis of an individual-formed substrate,
by recollection of gender (<s>liṅga</s>) it reaches gender and number
And, without the use of the word ‘and’ (<s>ca</s>) for those that form a dual compound,
the functioning as having an undifferentiated meaning is understood because of non-difference of form
Or else, when there is alternation (option), the function is, upon exclusion or upon combination,
regulated by an indicator (particle), for those whose capacities are unknown
And when the function has a qualified form, the word ‘and’ (<s>ca</s>) is set aside,
and despite difference in meaning, due to similarity of form, that is indicated by the meaning
And if the meaning of ‘and’ (<s>ca</s>), which is of the nature of non-existence (absence), is taken up as that very one,

children.text: taddharmatvaṃ tato dvandve cādiṣv arthakṛtaṃ hi tat
children.translated_text: then, in a copulative compound (<s>dvandva</s>), its being a property is meaning-produced; indeed that (role) is produced by meaning

children.text: cārthaḥ śabde kva cid bhedāt kathaṃ cit samavasthitaḥ
children.translated_text: The meaning of ‘and’ (<s>ca</s>), in the word, is in some places somehow established because of difference,

children.text: dyotakāś cādayas tasya vaktā dvandvas tu tadvatām
children.translated_text: and the indicators, beginning with ‘and’ (<s>ca</s>), are its utterers; the copulative compound (<s>dvandva</s>) is of those that are like that
Since the meaning of ‘and’, which is to be denoted as alternation and the like, would not be capable of being the meaning of another word because it is an indicator,

children.text: dyotakatvān na kalpeta tasmāt sad upalakṣyate
children.translated_text: therefore the existent (meaning) is marked out
There, when a natural gender (<s>liṅga</s>) is expected in the property of the word,

children.text: śabdaḥ kaś cit tam evārthaṃ kathaṃ cit pratipadyate
children.translated_text: some word grasps that very meaning somehow

children.text: śabdād arthāḥ pratāyante sa bhedānāṃ vidhāyakaḥ
children.translated_text: Meanings shine forth from the word; it is the establisher of distinctions,

children.text: anumānaṃ vivakṣāyāḥ śabdād anyan na vidyate
children.translated_text: for intention there is no other inference apart from the word
The meaning of a copulative compound (<s>dvandva</s>) would be a conjunction that is attribute-constituted,
or the conjunction too may be such that the conjunction is attribute-constituted
When the conjunct (members) are primary, gender and number are by nature (of the conjuncts),
when the conjunction itself is primary, the śāstra would be the proclaimer
Some others, however, knowing thus, hold the non-establishment of gender and number,
because, when the meaning has conjunction, there is following of the cause (<s>nimitta</s>)
If the conjunction were the cause (<s>nimitta</s>), then there would be following of the cause,
and by agreement and difference the meaning is grounded in the copulative compound (<s>dvandva</s>)
And when the meaning has conjunction as cause, even if that (meaning) departs,
since gender and number of the copulative compound (<s>dvandva</s>) are established naturally
because of being an indicator of a meaning belonging to another word, it is not fitting,

children.text: nipāto liṅgasaṃkhyābhyāṃ dvandvas tv arthasya vācakaḥ
children.translated_text: the particle does not determine gender and number; the copulative compound (<s>dvandva</s>), however, is the denoter of the meaning
And when there is following of the cause, since there is no expectation of substance-properties,
the connection of action, as attribute and primary, is not established

children.text: yasya nāsti kriyāyogaḥ svatantro+asau na vidyate
children.translated_text: That for which there is no connection with action does not exist independently,

children.text: artho dvandvasya tatra syād upādānam anarthakam
children.translated_text: there, the meaning of the copulative compound (<s>dvandva</s>) would be pointless to employ
The denoter of the meaning that has conjunction does not follow,

children.text: nimittam api cāsyārthaḥ svadharmair yujyate tataḥ
children.translated_text: and its meaning, even as cause, is joined with its own properties; therefore

children.text: bāhyo nāsty āśrayo dvandve viśeṣau tatra hi śrutau
children.translated_text: there is no external substrate in a copulative compound (<s>dvandva</s>); for two specifications are heard there,
the conjunction is the support there, and it is indicated by its properties
The single aggregate, which, as it were, is connected with (both) difference and non-difference through part-and-part distinctions,

children.text: ekaḥ samūho dharmān sa bhāgayoḥ pratipadyate
children.translated_text: that one apprehends the properties in the two parts
And that single meaning is of the nature of two, endowed with both difference and non-difference

children.text: yau bhedāv āśritas tatsthe liṅgasaṃkhye prapadyate
children.translated_text: The two differences that are relied upon, in that which abides in them, adopt gender and number,
Just as, when the meaning of <s>caitra</s> is expressed by its own word, it is not employed,
so too the word <s>caitra</s> would be unfit for use in a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> (exocentric compound)

children.text: yathā gaur iti śuklāder abhidhānaṃ na vidyate
children.translated_text: Just as the expression ‘cow’ (<s>go</s>) does not denote ‘white’ and the like,
so, that one whose relation is with cows is understood only to that extent

children.text: saṃbandhī niyato rūḍhaś citrāṇāṃ na ca vidyate
children.translated_text: And there is no fixed, conventional relatum of the various ‘spotted’ (<s>citra</s>)s,

children.text: gavāṃ yathā vajrapāṇis tryakṣe vā+api vyavasthitaḥ
children.translated_text: as, with respect to cows, <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> or the three-eyed one is established

children.text: śabdāntaratvād vākyeṣu viśeṣā yady api śrutāḥ
children.translated_text: Even if distinctions are heard in sentences because of being different words,
this word ‘function’ (<s>vṛtti</s>) is another, a denoter of the generality
‘Not-cow’ and ‘non-spotted-cow’ are indeed preventers of the differences of forms,

children.text: na citragur viśeṣāṇāṃ rūpābhedāt tu vācakaḥ
children.translated_text: but ‘spotted-cow’ does not denote particulars, because of the non-difference of form

children.text: yathā citragur ity etat prayukte na prayujyate
children.translated_text: Just as, when ‘spotted-cow’ (<s>citragu</s>) is uttered, ‘spotted’ is not separately uttered,

children.text: evaṃ yadi syāt sāmānyaṃ tasya na syāt pratiśrutiḥ
children.translated_text: so, if its generality were like that, there would be no re-utterance (separate mention) of it
But ‘all’ and the like particulars are removers of locales (domains),
just as locales, as generals, are sublators of other locales
And because of the denotation of the sense of the case-ending (<s>vibhakti</s>), the genitive is not re-employed,
but because the substance is not denoted, the pronoun ‘that’ is re-employed
If co-reference (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) were to be contrived from the elision of <s>matu</s> (the -mat affix),
then, since even with <s>matu</s> it has that meaning, an infinite regress would ensue
And also, a relatum of the relation, and a relation distinct (from that), would be entailed,
and when the sense of the case-ending is primary, a connection with the action is not established
Because the sense of the case-ending is primary, therefore the action ‘then, there’ does not occur,
and what is to be seen and the like are fitted to be causes of object, agent, and so on
And how could the relation be included when it is stated as primary?

children.text: sa prātipadikārthaś ca tathābhūtaḥ kathaṃ bhatvet
children.translated_text: and how could it, being thus, be the meaning of the nominal base (<s>prātipadika</s>), O Bhava?
But because of the impossibility, in the case of relation, when accompanied by relation,
there is the possibility of effects such as genus, number, and collection
From the co-reference ‘this is that,’ for words that speak of a qualified substrate,
gender and number will arise, like ‘white’ and the like, from the commencement of the śāstra

children.text: bhedena tu vivakṣāyāṃ sāmānye vā vivakṣite
children.translated_text: But when the intention is by difference, or when the general is intended,
there would be arrival (applicability) of a word-meaning that has gender and has number

children.text: sādhutvaṃ na vibhaktyartha- mātre vṛttasya dṛśyate
children.translated_text: Correctness is not observed for that which functions only for the sense of the case-ending,
the grasping of the meaning ‘correctness is for what functions for the whole meaning’ has been made

children.text: so+ayam ity abhisaṃbandhād dravyavṛttir ayaṃ yadā
children.translated_text: From the co-reference ‘this is that,’ when this has the function of substance,
then correctness is asserted for that which has gender and has number
Just as the genitive is not heard where the sense of the case-ending is included,
so non-hearing would ensue for those that denote gender and number

children.text: sādharmyam avyayena syād bahuvrīhes tathā sati
children.translated_text: There would be similarity with the indeclinable, and, if it were so, with the <s>bahuvrīhi</s>,
because the refinement whose cause is gender and number would be removed
And by relation with what is employed, there would be hearing of <s>Caitra</s> and the like,

children.text: vinā vibhaktyā saṃbandho vibhaktyā vidyate vinā
children.translated_text: the relation, without the case-ending, exists; without the relation, the case-ending exists
Even when number is denoted, the ‘number-ness’ of number is not averted,
but when the genitive’s sense is denoted, there would be being the meaning of the nominal base (<s>prātipadika</s>)
There is no need to posit the sense of the case-ending for the sake of establishing re-employment,

children.text: vastvantaram upakṣiptam iti ke cit pracakṣate
children.translated_text: some declare that another entity has been introduced as a supplement
The causes of relations belonging to the qualified (things) would be the qualificands (relata),

children.text: saṃbandhair vā viśiṣṭānāṃ tadvatāṃ syān nimittatā
children.translated_text: or, by the relations, the causes would be of those qualified by them

children.text: ke cit saṃyogino daṇḍād viṣāṇāt samavāyinaḥ
children.translated_text: Some say that affixes reside, for those having conjunction, in the stick, and, for those having inherence, in the horn,

children.text: tadvati pratyayān āhur bahuvrīhiṃ tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: and likewise in him who has that; and the <s>bahuvrīhi</s> too (is explained) thus
Others know relation as distinct by difference of the relata,
that sense of the case-ending is the cause which is denoted by the compound
The principal (member), being for another’s purpose, is distinct from its own determiners,
the cause is to be expected either as what is to be denoted, or after all the rest

children.text: svāmini vyatirekaś ca vākye yady api dṛśyate
children.translated_text: Although separation from the owner is observed in the sentence,
still, when the <s>bahuvrīhi</s> is intended, its primacy is accepted
When the possessor (tadvat) functions as a qualifier of ‘cows,’

children.text: asyaitā iti tatrārthe bahuvrīhir na vidyate
children.translated_text: the <s>bahuvrīhi</s> is not found for the meaning ‘these are his’

children.text: yadā pratyavamarśas tu tāsāṃ svāmī gavām iti
children.translated_text: But when, rather, there is a reflexive reference ‘their owner is of the cows,’
then the relation with ‘cows’ is contrived to be the cause
while expecting the relation, for the cessation of conventionality
Because it follows upon the cause (nimitta), the purpose of that property arises,

children.text: nānā citrā iti yathā nimittam anurudhyate
children.translated_text: just as, in ‘variegated’ (<s>nānā citrā</s>), the qualifier keeps to (follows) the cause,

children.text: nānābhūte+api vṛttaḥ san bahuvrīhis tathā bhavet
children.translated_text: so too, even though the substrates are diverse, the <s>bahuvrīhi</s> proceeds thus

children.text: saṃbandhini nimitte tu dravyadharmo na hīyate
children.translated_text: But when the cause is in the relatum (saṃbandhin), the property of the substance is not lost,
for the absence of gender functions as an opponent to gender
Number-possessing and gender-possessing are meanings having non-different properties, by reason of the cause,

children.text: āsanna eva dravyatvāt taddharmair na virudhyate
children.translated_text: being proximate to substance, they are not incompatible with its properties

children.text: vibhaktyarthena cāviṣṭaṃ śuddhaṃ ceti dvidhā sthitam
children.translated_text: And it stands in a twofold way: as pervaded by the sense of the case-ending (<s>vibhakti</s>), and as ‘pure’ (i.e., not so pervaded),

children.text: dravyaṃ śuddhasya yo dharmaḥ sa na syād anyadharmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: the property of the pure substance would not belong to what has another property
In the mere designation of substance, this difference is not intended,
but in the text, earlier the difference was indicated at the second stage
And here, the taking of ‘substance’ is as a qualifier of gender and number,

children.text: dravyāśritatvaṃ hi tayos tato+anyasya na sidhyataḥ
children.translated_text: for their being grounded in substance; therefore that of something else is not established
A compound operates, delimited by a relation distinct from the relatum,
in the commonality of substance, not accompanying a meaning that is particularized
Not transgressing the properties of substance, standing in the properties of difference,
it attains gender and number in dependence upon a future locus
Even though there is a difference of <s>śāstra</s>-application, the worldly meaning is not differentiated,

children.text: nañsamase yatas tatra trayaḥ pakṣā vicāritāḥ
children.translated_text: since, in the <s>nañ</s>-compound, three alternatives were examined there
And even under another word too, the inquiry proceeds by relying on unity,

children.text: abrahmaṇādiṣu nañaḥ prayogo na hi vidyate
children.translated_text: for the usage of <s>nañ</s> is not found with ‘non-<s>Brahmaṇa</s>’ and the like

children.text: prāk samāsāt padārthānāṃ nivṛttir dyotyate nañā
children.translated_text: Prior to compounding, the cessation of the word-meanings is indicated by <s>nañ</s>,
but, being by nature ceased, because of non-difference of form, it is unperceived
In sentences where ‘<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>’ and the like stand and are denoted by the finite-verb word,

children.text: kriyayā yasya saṃbandho vṛttis tasya na vidyate
children.translated_text: for that whose connection is with the action, there is no function (of <s>nañ</s>)
If, being in words like ‘cook’ (<s>pācaka</s>) and so on, the action is connected by <s>nañ</s>,
then, because existence is not included there, the threefold view is not tenable
If connection everywhere is to be imagined only with existence,
then in this compound ‘non-being,’ let another existence be imagined

children.text: ktvānte ca tumunante ca nañsamāse na dṛśyate
children.translated_text: And in what ends with -ktvā and what ends with -tumun, the <s>nañ</s>-compound is not seen,
for the state of qualifier–qualificand is asserted by <s>nañ</s>, which denotes non-existence
The <s>nañ</s> is established in the generality of instrument and substrate of action,
therefore it is joined with particular substrates such as ‘<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>’ and the like
As, in usage, taking meanings like ‘gone’ and so on, the privatives are
fitted with instrument and substrate, so too is that procedure in the <s>nañ</s>-compound
There, when the function of <s>nañ</s> is absent, with ‘<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>Kṣatriya</s>,’ and the like,
a qualifier–qualificand relation is imagined, like ‘crooked, lame’

children.text: kāmacāre ca saty evam asataḥ syāt pradhānatā,
children.translated_text: And when free action is present, thus, for the non-existent there would be primacy,

children.text: guṇatvam itareṣāṃ ca teṣāṃ vā syāt pradhānatā
children.translated_text: and the others would be secondary; or else, of those, there would be primacy
Those having general functions, earlier adopted primarily, by usage,
have proceeded only as particulars—‘<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>Kṣatri</s>, trader,’ and the like
Just as delimitation of them is enjoined by ‘cow’ and the like,
so too, even by the non-existent, the identity not yet expressed is made manifest
Just as, for denoting existence, a ‘being’ meaning is imagined,
so too, for denoting non-existence, even the uncharacterized is imagined
Having made ‘<s>Kṣatriya</s>’ and the like the word, the cognition, relying on a different existence,

children.text: jātyā bhinnāṃ tataḥ sattāṃ prasaktām apakarṣati
children.translated_text: then withdraws the existence that would have been admitted as distinct by genus
When ‘absence’ (<s>abhāva</s>) is intended as the negation of a positive entity,
negation is not to be posited without relying on being characterized
Words that express many properties, being denotative of an aggregate,
operate, by their nature alike, with respect to parts
Just as, from doing one part, ‘done’ is said,

children.text: akṛtaś ceti saṃghātaḥ sa evābrāhmaṇe kramaḥ
children.translated_text: and ‘not done’—and that same aggregate is the procedure in ‘non-<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>’
Therefore ‘<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>’ and ‘non-<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>’ would follow from that presentation,
or, if not done, because of non-connection with done, there would be no distinction between done and not done
When the primary sense is not possible there, for the elimination of the primary,
at the time of explanatory supplement to the <s>śāstra</s>, <s>nañ</s> is used as a distinguisher
Without harm to the word-meanings, another specification is seen,

children.text: atha jātimato+arthasya kaś cid dharmo nivartitaḥ
children.translated_text: but if some property of a thing possessing a genus is excluded,

children.text: avaśyaṃ brāhmaṇe kaś cit kva cid dharmo na vidyate
children.translated_text: necessarily, in a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, some property is, somewhere, not present,
therefore, since the particular is not stated there, the utterance of <s>nañ</s> is purposeless
For the unqualified, a periphrasis qualified by <s>nañ</s> (negation) would result,
for by an explanatory supplement (<s>anvākhyāna</s>) the correctness (of usage) in such a case is understood
Even though here the qualification does not injure the word-meanings,
from the standpoint of figurative usage (<s>upacāra</s>), the standing of the meaning is indicated by <s>nañ</s>
Just as the word-meaning, as it truly is, is established in the qualificands,
so too, in the such-like, the such-like absence is inferred by reasons of difference
When the parts have ceased there, how does the word-meaning operate upon that (aggregate)?
for the activation of a word is not reasonable without a cause
If, by nature, the operation of a word extends, like a distant-reaching word, to an opposite meaning,

children.text: śabdasya vṛttir yady asti nañaḥ śrutir anarthikā
children.translated_text: then the utterance of <s>nañ</s> is purposeless
But if, because of a (separate) statement, its own nature is fit to be further explained (<s>anvākhyeya</s>),
that must be stated; since it is not well established, the meaning of <s>nañ</s> is withdrawn

children.text: yady apy ubhayavṛttitvaṃ pradhānaṃ tu pratīyate
children.translated_text: Even if dual operation (on both terms) is possible, nevertheless what is primary is apprehended,

children.text: prasthānaṃ gamyate śuddhe tadarthe+api na tiṣṭhatau
children.translated_text: a starting-point is grasped in the pure meaning, yet even there the two do not stand
For what reason, when the state is not thus and when a primary sense is possible,
is the operation of the word ‘<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>’ admitted in a sense of difference?

children.text: ayaṃ padārtha etasmin kṣatriyādau na vidyate
children.translated_text: “This word-meaning is not present in this one, such as a <s>Kṣatriya</s>,”
thus a word expressing that is employed for the sake of cognition

children.text: buddher viṣayatāṃ prāpte śabdād arthe pratīyate
children.translated_text: When the objecthood of cognition has been attained, the meaning is understood from the word,

children.text: pravṛttir vā nivṛttir vā grutyā hy artho+anusajyate
children.translated_text: and activity or cessation of activity is connected with the meaning according to convention
Or else, because of improper instruction, or because of a (wrong) cause, or because of doubt,

children.text: śabdapravṛttir na tv asti loṣṭādiṣu viparyayāt
children.translated_text: there is no activation of a word with regard to clod and the like, due to reversal (of intention)

children.text: anekasmād asa iti prādhānye sati sidhyati
children.translated_text: From the (mere) non-one (i.e., ‘not one’), multiplicity is established when primacy is present,
and so the dependence of the primaries is appropriate in the procedure concerning the suffix -tvá (<s>tvatal</s>)
And since one (member) is primary, in the presence of a qualifier of that,
there is no exclusion of the primary property; therefore there is no need of another utterance

children.text: pradhānam atra bhedyatvād ekārtho vikṛto nañā
children.translated_text: Here the primary, because it is to be differentiated, is a single meaning modified by <s>nañ</s>,

children.text: hitvā svadharmān vartante dvyādayo+apy ekatāṃ gatāḥ
children.translated_text: and twoness and the rest, having abandoned their own properties, proceed, having attained unity
Just as <s>Kṣatriya</s> and the others, being connected with <s>nañ</s>, have come into the state of ‘<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>-ness,’
so too, in the case of duality and the like, unity is figuratively predicated because of the connection with <s>nañ</s>
Having reached connection with unity, that property is negated,
and with respect to the dual and the rest, the pronoun ‘that’ functions for those, like ‘<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>’ and the like
In a sentence where a number is already present, as it is employed with the dual and the like,

children.text: vṛttau tasya pradhānatvāt sā saṃkhyā na nivartate
children.translated_text: because of its operation being primary, that number is not removed
The thing to be denied, as it truly is, is accordingly connected,
for, when another utterance is yoked, that meaning is not negated
Just as, in ‘not white,’ black and the like are rightly apprehended,
so too here is expressed ‘not one,’ a different number, ‘many’
Since action would extend to all the accepted objects,
even if one is prohibited, another, which is attainable, is understood
And the mention of action, being already underway, in the case of prohibitive negation (<s>prasajya-pratiṣedha</s>),
whereas in counter-assertion (<s>paryudāsa</s>) a different determinate number is stated
The verb-meaning, having objects as its domain, is specified along with its own instruments,
therefore, from the meaning, all the actions, beforehand, are encompassed and established
Where, with the base (substrate) and instruments known, the finite verb is employed,

children.text: aneka iti paścāc ca tiṣṭhatīty anuṣajyate
children.translated_text: ‘not one’ is then subsequently connected, meaning ‘it stands,’

children.text: sādhyatvāt tatra siddhena kriyā dravyeṇa lakṣyate
children.translated_text: Since, there, because it is to be accomplished, the action is marked by an already established substance,

children.text: prāg evāṅgīkṛtaṃ dravyam ataḥ pūrveṇa bhidyate
children.translated_text: the substance has already been accepted earlier; therefore it differs from the previous
By the negation of a number it expects another number,

children.text: vākye+api tena naikatva- mātram eva nivartyate
children.translated_text: and even in the sentence, only unity is negated thereby
From a different unguent (oil) the delimitation, and thus the absence, is understood:

children.text: tailena bhojane+aprāpte na tv anyad upasecanam
children.translated_text: when sesame oil is not available for cooking, there is not, however, some other condiment
When, with ‘non-existent’ and ‘with a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>,’ both employed in a single meaning,
an external different genus, such as <s>Kṣatriya</s> and the like, is indicated,
just as ‘a maiden, indeed dark, armed,’ another (property) is indicated,

children.text: asan brāhmaṇa ity ābhyāṃ tathānye kṣatriyādayaḥ
children.translated_text: so, by these two, ‘non-<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>,’ likewise others—<s>Kṣatriya</s> and the like

children.text: asāsno gaur iti yathā, gavayo vyapadiśyate
children.translated_text: Just as, from ‘cow without dewlap,’ the <s>gavaya</s> is indicated,

children.text: jātyantaraṃ na gor eva sasnābhāvaḥ pratīyate
children.translated_text: the different genus, and not merely a cow with the absence of a dewlap, is understood
As that which is similar in form, as declared, by thorns as causes of difference,
the <s>khadira</s>, by difference of genus, is apprehended apart from the date-palm
A non-existent <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, of the sort that a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> would be,
By an accepted simile (upamāna), likewise another meaning is conveyed
Just as the rains that do not fall, being covered by mist and cloud,

children.text: tadrūpatvāt sa hemanta ity abhinnaḥ pratīyate
children.translated_text: because of being of that form, are apprehended as ‘that is winter,’ as not different
Others declare that, for all terms denoting genera like <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and the rest,
when the substance is intended as another referent, there is conjunction with <s>nañ</s> (the negative particle)

children.text: na caivaṃviṣayaḥ kaś cid bahuvrīhiḥ prakalpate
children.translated_text: And no <s>bahuvrīhi</s> (possessive compound) is to be constructed on such a basis,

children.text: agur aśva iti vyāptir nañsamāsena yasya na
children.translated_text: for the pervasion ‘not heavy,’ ‘not a horse’ does not belong to one whose compound is with <s>nañ</s>
Since the predicate gender of a dual-compound member (dvandva) and of a part-designating member has been stated,
therefore, in cases of ‘no rain,’ etc., non-establishment of the desired gender and number results
When the qualifier like ‘<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>’ pertains to a non-existent connected with an action,
and the topic is distinct, then non-existence in that respect is apprehended

children.text: brāhmaṇatvena cāsattvād ucyate sat tad anyathā
children.translated_text: And because of non-existence as ‘<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>-ness,’ it is said to be existent otherwise;

children.text: asad ity api sattvena sataḥ sattā nivartyate
children.translated_text: and even ‘non-existent,’ by reason of existence, negates the existence of what is existent
Because it subsists in a common substance and follows its occasion (condition),
there would be non-conjunction with gender and number, or else a common property
Previously there is the denotation of non-existence, and in compounding the denotation of substance,
and the following of the occasion; yet these are not everywhere by their very nature
And when there is following of the occasion, a conjunction with an action is not conceived,
and thus, since it is not expressible, the incorporation is pointless
Or, subsisting in the common non-existence, being made distinct by the particulars like <s>Kṣatriya</s> and the rest
that are employed as substrates, it attains their gender and number
For the substrate, kept internal within the principal for the sake of difference beforehand,
upon subsequent recollection appears as if separated

children.text: samāse śrūyate svārtho yena tadvāṃs tadāśrayaḥ
children.translated_text: In a compound, by which one’s own meaning is heard, the possessor of that (quality) and its substrate,
but the substance, like gender and number, is internalized by the non-existent
The two words have a single semantic scope, while, in that, they pertain to another meaning,
but it is precisely by the non-existent that the collection of all differences is encompassed

children.text: te kṣatriyādibhir vācyā vācyā vā sarvanāmabhiḥ
children.translated_text: Those [differences] are to be expressed either by terms like <s>Kṣatriya</s> and the rest, or by pronouns,
as if they were going over to the status of a different referent, because of the indefiniteness of the form of <s>nañ</s>
But when the particular is not employed, gender and number are not established,
and there is a defect in ‘no rain,’ etc., since winter has another substrate
When the form (<s>ākṛti</s>) is apprehended as that which is denoted by all words,

children.text: ekatvād ekaśabdatvaṃ nyāyyaṃ tasyāś ca varṇyate
children.translated_text: its being one, and its being a single word, is rightly stated
In that, the state of being pervaded by gender would obtain, like a village- and cow-herd cluster,
and even if there is a difference of substances, because of unity there, the singular would be appropriate

children.text: āśrayāṇāṃ hi liṅgaiḥ sā niyatair eva yujyate
children.translated_text: For that [form] is connected with fixed genders of substrates alone,
and thus, when a state of being appropriately connected exists, a negation would be pointless
Universal pervasion by gender would result everywhere if worldly gender were adopted,

children.text: virodhitvāt prasajyeta nāśritaṃ tac ca laukikam
children.translated_text: and that, being dependent, is merely conventional

children.text: sāmānyam ākṛtir bhāvo jātir ity atra laukikam
children.translated_text: ‘Universal,’ ‘form,’ ‘state,’ ‘genus’—in this matter, the worldly gender does not at all arise,

children.text: liṅgaṃ na saṃbhavaty eva tenānyat parigṛhyate
children.translated_text: therefore another [account] is adopted

children.text: pravṛttir iti sāmānyaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ tasya kathyate
children.translated_text: As ‘occurrence’ is taught to be the definition of the universal,

children.text: āvirbhāvas tirobhāvaḥ sthitiś cety atha bhidyate
children.translated_text: then it is divided as manifestation, disappearance, and stability
All objects, being endowed with occurrence, and with the three occurrences,

children.text: satataṃ na viyujyante vācaś caivātra saṃbhavaḥ
children.translated_text: are never separated; and the possibility of speech is herewith
And that which, having the import of the property of non-occurrence, is apprehended as a configuration,
as it were, follows upon the occurrences of others, whose supports are everywhere

children.text: tenāsya citirūpaṃ ca citikālaś ca bhidyate
children.translated_text: Therefore, its configuration and the time of configuration are distinguished,

children.text: tasya svarūpabhedas tu na kaś cid api vidyate
children.translated_text: but no difference whatsoever of its own nature is recognized
In non-sentient things, consciousness appears as though transferred,
by the property of being a reflector, in so far as that is bound up with words

children.text: avasthā tādṛśī nāsti yā liṅgena na yujyate
children.translated_text: There is no such state that is not connected with gender,

children.text: kva cit tu śabdasaṃskāro liṅgasyānāśraye sati
children.translated_text: but in some cases there is a verbal conditioning when gender has no substrate
For states denoted by primary and secondary affixes (<s>kṛt</s>, <s>taddhita</s>) this does not conflict,

children.text: śāstre liṅgaṃ guṇāvasthā tathā cākṛtir iṣyate
children.translated_text: in the treatise gender is accepted as a mode of qualities, and so too form (<s>ākṛti</s>)

children.text: liṅgaṃ prati na bhedo+asti dravyapakṣe+api kaś cana
children.translated_text: With regard to gender there is no distinction even on the side of substance,
therefore the seven alternatives—this is precisely the state of being pervaded by gender
Regulation in utterance, on the basis of the treatise, is admitted for the substance,

children.text: yatas tad ākṛtau śāstram anyathaiva samarthyate
children.translated_text: since the treatise is grounded in form (<s>ākṛti</s>); otherwise it would be accounted for differently

children.text: vartate yo bahuṣv artho +abhede tasya vivakṣite
children.translated_text: That meaning which extends over many, when non-difference is intended,
its enunciation in the treatise is said of what is specified by its own substrates

children.text: yadā tv āśrayabhedena bheda eva pratīyate
children.translated_text: But when, due to difference of substrates, a difference itself is cognized,

children.text: ākṛter dravyapakṣena tadā bhedo na vidyate
children.translated_text: then, on the side of substance, there is no difference of the <s>ākṛti</s> (form)

children.text: abhede tv ekaśabdatvāc chāstrāc ca vacane sati
children.translated_text: But when there is non-difference, since there is the state of being a single word, and since there is enunciation according to the treatise,

children.text: ekaśeṣo na vaktavyo vacanānāṃ ca saṃbhavaḥ
children.translated_text: one should not state an ‘ellipsis to one’ (<s>ekaśeṣa</s>), and plurality of words is possible
Objection: If substance is inexpressible, then this assistance of <s>ākṛti</s> (form) which relies upon it,
cannot be posited, because of the absence of substance

children.text: vyapadeśo+abhidheyena na śāstre kaś cid āśritaḥ
children.translated_text: Reply: In the treatise no designation relies upon something that is not denoted;

children.text: dravyaṃ nāma padārtho yo na ca sa pratiṣidhyate
children.translated_text: ‘substance’ is the name of an entity (<s>padārtha</s>), and that is not denied
The state of being a quality (<s>guṇabhāva</s>) is not, as denotability, dependent upon substance;

children.text: upakāri guṇaḥ śeṣaḥ parārtha iti kalpanā
children.translated_text: the quality, being a helper (<s>upakārin</s>), is the remainder (<s>śeṣa</s>), and the view that it is for the sake of another is a construction
In substance there is no state of being a quality without its being expressed by a word as other than substance,

children.text: ākṛtau vā pradhānatvam ata evaṃ samarthyate
children.translated_text: or, the primacy (<s>pradhānatva</s>) is in the <s>ākṛti</s> (form); therefore it is justified thus
By some, the primacy of quality is held, as in the case of the noun and the verb (<s>nāma</s>–<s>ākhyāta</s>),

children.text: na vṛttivat parārthasya guṇabhāvas tu varṇyate
children.translated_text: but the state of being a quality is not described as in the case of an action for the sake of another (<s>vṛtti</s>)
Because of the diversity of that which becomes a quality, there is the state of being a single word for the <s>ākṛti</s> (form),
and a diversity of enunciation is established, in accordance with the diversity of substances
Just as the instrument, being in the state of a quality, differentiates the action,
so the substance is said to be, with regard to verbs, for the single-worded genus
Because of unity there is sameness of form with respect to words in their denotation,
when, due to the cause, there is a particular apprehension of the referent which possesses that

children.text: so+ayam ity abhisaṃbandhād āśrayair ākṛteḥ saha
children.translated_text: Because of the co-reference ‘this-he’ (<s>so ’yam</s>) of the substrates together with the <s>ākṛti</s> (form),
when there is usage with different words, gender and number are sanctioned
And previously, because of co-reference to the genus, pronoun-hood is meant,
the deictics beginning with ‘that’ (<s>tyad</s>) are employed, in the presence of an existent, as an indication of a real thing

children.text: pākau pākā iti yathā bhedakaḥ kaiś cid āśrayaḥ
children.translated_text: As, with ‘cookings’ (<s>pāka</s>), ‘cookings’—by some the substrate is accepted as the differentiator,
and that property, not taken along, is held to belong to words that denote qualities
If, when the substrate is not taken along, one only obtains the general properties of the support,
then the commonness in front was already examined
For words that previously function with respect to the genus, words that denote a genus,
a particular also arises through relation to what is not expressible by a word
Because of the co-reference ‘this-he’ (<s>so ’yam</s>), the property of the genus is metaphorically applied,
and the substance, its substrate, and the difference of the genus are accepted
Just as the word ‘bed’ (<s>mañca</s>), as that which is supported, is confined to beds,

children.text: tattvenāha tathā jāti- śabdo dravyeṣu vartate
children.translated_text: so too the Teacher says that the genus-word in reality operates in substances
There, the status of being the referent of a word for genus is accepted just so,
but genus, once the numbers are released, adheres in the nature of substance

children.text: asyedam iti vā yatra so+ayam ity api vā śrutiḥ
children.translated_text: Where there is the expression ‘this of this’ (<s>asya idam</s>), or also ‘this-he’ (<s>so ’yam</s>),
there, by another’s property, something different is expressed

children.text: yat pradhānaṃ na tasyāsti svarūpam anirūpanāt
children.translated_text: That which is principal has no own-nature, because it is not determined,
