and substance, as the self of the quality, is indicated through its being in that state
But at the time when the quality differentiates, primacy arises,

children.text: saṃsargaśrutir artheṣu sākṣād eva na vartate
children.translated_text: and the conjunction-expression does not operate directly with respect to the things

children.text: jātau vṛtto yadā dravye sa śabdo vartate punaḥ
children.translated_text: When a word, which functions with respect to the genus, functions again in the substance,
then the status of being the referent only of the genus is not accepted
The re-functioning of words already functioning is described as unity,
but in the means of apprehension, the reality is not pursued
When the genus is resorted to for what is denotable by an inseparable word,
then, when there is contact with the substance, there is the status of being the referent of a genus-word

children.text: dravyasya sati saṃsparśe dravyam āśrīyate yadā
children.translated_text: When, there being contact with the substance, the substance is resorted to,
then, by that very word, there is the status of being the referent of a substance-word
Even what is denotable by an inseparable word functions merely in difference,
when the genus is like a relation, then that too has the status of being the referent of a substance-word
Only in the case of two entirely distinct denoters of genus and substance,
does the inexpressible have the role of assistant; but when there is dependence, there is double referentiality
But when one accepts a difference that is made by the substrate, in what is dependent,
then again the single-wordedness is described in the word for genus

children.text: anirjātasya nirjñānaṃ yena tan mānam ucyate
children.translated_text: The cognition of what is not yet known, by means of which that is said to be a measure (<s>māna</s>),
by means of that the nature of what is to be known, like ‘standard’, etc., is ascertained in its entirety
When what is not known is, by what is well-known, its property is inferred,
because the totality is not apprehended, that is called comparison (<s>upamāna</s>)
In the case of two similar things, of the comparator and the compared,
there is a compounding of comparatives by words that denote that
The difference that is due to a difference of substrate, that, in the case of blackness, is unintended; the quality has unity of being-supported, yet a different substrate is apprehended
The quality has unity of being-supported, yet a different substrate is apprehended
Between qualities there is a fixed difference, and likewise there is unity of the quality-genus; when there is unity or an absolute difference, there is no possibility of comparison (<s>upamāna</s>)
When there is regard only to the genus as such, there is no point of comparison at all; one single blackness operates in both qualities

children.text: śyāmatvam ekaṃ guṇayor ubhayor api vartate
yenaiva hetunā śyāmā śastrī tatra pratīyate
children.translated_text: By whatever reason a woman with a sword-belt (<s>śastrī</s>) is apprehended as black, that very reason, in the cognition of <s>Devadattā</s>, is not differentiated

children.text: sa hetur devadattāyāḥ pratyaye na viśiṣyate
āśrayād yo guṇe bhedo jāter yā cāviśiṣṭatā
children.translated_text: By the difference of the substrate with regard to the quality, and by the non-differentiation of the genus, by these two together the substance-nature, along with its activity, is apprehended
Thus this practice, relying on unity-and-multiplicity, proceeds by a reflection on difference-and-non-difference, intermingled
If only the genus as such is intended, one should say simply ‘it is black’; there is then no purpose in adducing ‘woman with a sword-belt’, etc.

children.text: aśabdavācyo yo bhedaḥ śyāmamātre na vartate
children.translated_text: The difference that is inexpressible by a word does not operate in mere blackness; here, that is to be considered whose occurrence is in some blacks

children.text: śyāmeṣu keṣu cid vṛttir yasya so+atra vyapekṣyate
śyāmeṣu keṣu cit kiṃ cit kiṃ cit sarvatra vartate
children.translated_text: In some blacks something or other is present, something is present in all; a certain universal is fixed in one black, a difference

children.text: sāmānyaṃ kaś cid ekasmiñ chyāme bhedo vyavasthitaḥ
tathā hi sati saurabhye bhedo jātyutpalādiṣu
children.translated_text: Thus indeed, when fragrance is present, there is difference among genera such as lotus, etc.; but when there is difference of the smells, similarity is apprehended

children.text: gandhānāṃ sati bhede tu sādṛśyam upalabhyate
guṇānām āśrayād bhedaḥ svato vāpy anugamyate
children.translated_text: The difference of qualities is traced to the substrate, or even to themselves; or to an ineffable particularity, or to a blending with other qualities

children.text: anirdeśyād viśeṣād vā saṃkarād vā guṇāntaraiḥ

children.translated_text: Because it is well-established, comparison (<s>upamāna</s>) is distinguished everywhere; being the upameya-status (status of what is to be compared) does not cease either when there is superiority or when there is equality

children.text: upameyatvam ādhikye sāmye vā na nivartate
anyais tu mānaṃ jātyādi bhedyasyārthasya varṇyate
children.translated_text: But others describe as a measure (<s>māna</s>) the genus, etc., of the thing to be differentiated; for the knowable object, whose own-nature is not ascertained, is measured by that

children.text: mitas tu svena mānena prasiddho yo guṇāśrayaḥ
children.translated_text: But that which, measured by its own measure, is well-known—the quality’s substrate—operates, by its own property, toward the measuring of another substrate
Contact, by means of a different form, of those who possess a different form—this, when belonging to what is to be differentiated, is called comparison (<s>upamāna</s>)

children.text: bhinnena yasya bhedyānām upamānaṃ tad ucyate

children.translated_text: The common property, blackness and the like, of the comparator and the compared, becomes subordinate when what is relied on is primary; by another property it is distinguished

children.text: śastrīkumāryoḥ sadṛśaḥ śyāma ity evam āśrite
children.translated_text: In the case ‘the woman with a sword-belt and the maiden are similar: black’, thus, when what is relied on is given, the designation ‘by means of this it is denoted’—that ground is situated in the qualities
When, because of the grounds, those endowed with them seem to pass into the very nature of that, then the naming, based on the substrate of difference, is of the comparator and the compared

When, for the sake of not violating reality, the differences in which difference ceases are intended, those are called ‘ellipsis-comparisons’ (<s>luptopamāna</s>), because of the common reliance on that property

children.text: śastryāṃ prasiddhaṃ śyāmatvaṃ mānaṃ sā tena mīyate
children.translated_text: The blackness well-known in the woman with a sword-belt is a measure (<s>māna</s>); by that she is measured; but another black woman, though of that form, is not measured by that utterly

children.text: anyā śyāmā tu tadrūpā tenātyantaṃ na mīyate

children.translated_text: Therefore, those who measure the woman with a sword-belt by her own quality to another substrate, call comparison (<s>upamāna</s>) the success of an incomplete quality
A property, being present in the upameya, is heard elsewhere and inferred; or, being heard in the comparator, it is inferred in the upameya
‘They study like a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, they are <s>Kṣatriya</s>-s’—thus it is seen; because the upameya is different, the statement has its basis in <s>Kṣatriya</s>-hood

children.text: sādhāraṇaṃ bruvan dharma kva cid eva vyavasthitam
children.translated_text: One who states a property that is common, but settled only in some locus, is called, in the sūtra, ‘a word that speaks the universal’
A quality is not denoted as hateful either without difference or with difference; of two different properties, one is heard, another is apprehended
What does not measure to the utmost that which resides in the universal, is, because of similarity, conceived as near to the object to be compared

children.text: mānaṃ prati samīpaṃ vā sādṛśyena pratīyate
children.translated_text: Nearness to the measure (<s>māna</s>), too, is apprehended through similarity; for here, by delimitation, there is similarity between measure and comparison
When there is regard to a single genus, it is concluded ‘this very (thing)’; when there is regard to difference, it is understood ‘a different (thing)’
Because being-object and being-instrument are grounded only in difference, there would not be an object of absolute unity; therefore here there is doubt

children.text: bhede+api tulyarūpatvāc chālīmṃ tān iti dṛśyate
children.translated_text: Despite difference, because of similarity of form, it is seen ‘they are like rice-grains’; but because of difference of genus, ‘this very one is this’, thus a different one is denoted

children.text: kathaṃ hy avayavo+anyasya syād anya iti cocyate
children.translated_text: For how could a part of one thing be another’s?—and it is also said thus; where, in absolute difference, there is no reality of plurality

children.text: atyantabhede nānātvaṃ yatra tattvaṃ na vidyate

children.translated_text: When non-difference is intended, oneness of the aggregate and the aggregand (the collection and its members) [is asserted],

children.text: saṅghinor na tv abhedo+asti tathānyatvam udāhṛtam
children.translated_text: but there is not, however, non-difference of the two aggregates; in the same way, otherness is stated
There, when non-difference is the point of view, the meaning of comparison (<s>upamāna</s>) does not obtain,

children.text: yo hi gaur iti vijñāne hetuḥ so+asti gavāntare
children.translated_text: for the reason that functions in the cognition ‘this is a cow’ is present in another cow as well
But when the operation of the distinct differences is what is intended,

children.text: na kaś cid upakāro+asti buddher buddhyantaraṃ prati
children.translated_text: there is no assistance at all of one cognition with respect to another cognition

children.text: kiṃ cid yatrāsti sāmānyaṃ yadi bhedāś ca ke cana
children.translated_text: Where something common exists, and if there are also some differences,

children.text: gotvaṃ goṣv asti sāmānyaṃ bhedāś ca śabalādayaḥ
children.translated_text: cowhood is the common property among cows, and the differences are the piebald and the like

children.text: sāmānyaṃ śyāmatānyaiva tad dhi sādhāraṇaṃ dvayoḥ
children.translated_text: Blackness alone is the common property; for that is what is shared by both,

children.text: tad eva siddhyasiddhibhyāṃ bheda ity apadiśyate
children.translated_text: and that very thing, by success and non-success, is designated ‘difference’

children.text: śyāmatvam eva sāmānyam anyeṣām ubhayoḥ sthitam
children.translated_text: Blackness itself is the common property, present in both of the others,

children.text: saṃpūrnatvāt tad anyasmād viśeṣa iti gamyate
children.translated_text: and because it is complete there, it is understood as a particular different from something else

children.text: ākṛtau vāpi sāmānye kva cid eva vyavasthitāḥ
children.translated_text: Or, even in form (<s>ākṛti</s>) as a universal, they are established only in some cases,
the differences that are determined in blackness and the like are here grounded

children.text: jāter abhede bhede vā sādṛśyaṃ tat pracakṣate
children.translated_text: They call that ‘similarity’ when there is non-difference or difference of the genus,

children.text: kaś cit kadā cit arthātmā tathābhūto+apadiśyate
children.translated_text: and at some time a certain entity, being of such a nature, is designated so

children.text: yatrārthe pratyayābhedo na kadā cid vikalpate
children.translated_text: Where there is never any vacillation of the non-difference of cognitions with respect to an object,
because a difference is not present, it is understood to be one
But that object which has manifoldness based on a substrate, that very one is designated thus,
and there too they acknowledge the operation of a portion of the genus
Where the prominence grounded in a portion of the genus operates as non-different,
there a cognition grounded in a portion of the individuals arises with difference
That cause, which exists elsewhere and is endowed with both difference and non-difference,
is nevertheless grasped elsewhere as if in the mode of manifoldness
Making the placement of words upon substrates, it then reaches that which is supported by them—

children.text: sa sādṛśyasya viṣaya ity anyair apadiśyate
children.translated_text: this is designated by others as the object of similarity
Just as, with reference to another, in the case of being, the designation ‘cause’ operates,
so too they declare comparison (<s>upamāna</s>) to depend upon another mode of apprehension
Just as teacher–student, father–son, actions, times, and the like—
so too transactions as well as similarity are grounded in dependence

children.text: śyāmatvam upamāne ced vṛttaṃ vṛttau prayujyate
children.translated_text: If blackness has occurred in the comparator, it is applied, when it has occurred,
the upameya is summarily indicated as external therein

children.text: ṭābanta eva caitrādau śyāmāśabdas tathā bhavet
children.translated_text: And the word ‘black’ would apply, ending in ṭā, to <s>Caitra</s> and the like,
and, because the nominative is absent in the sūtra, there is no subordination of ‘black’ and the like
But if, because of being in the same case-ending, or because of being a quality, it is held to be subordinate,
not so; for in ‘<s>tittirika</s>-black’ and ‘<s>kalmāṣī</s>-black’ the feminine affix would not be desired

children.text: satiśiṣṭabalīyastvād bāhye ṅiṣi ca saty api
children.translated_text: Because correct-usage is stronger, even when an external ṅis is present,

children.text: upamānasvaro na syāt tasmāt stryantaḥ samasyate
children.translated_text: the accent of comparison (<s>upamāna</s>) would not be present; therefore the compound ends in the feminine
Nor is dependence posited in a quality that is the locus of comparison,

children.text: pradhānasya tathā na syād vyāghrādau liṅgadarśanam
children.translated_text: nor, likewise, would there be the sight of a gender-marker in what is primary, such as ‘tiger’, etc.
Therefore, even when there is quality-hood, predominance, in another type of analysis,
such subordination, of this sort established in grammar, does not occur
Black, existing in the upameya itself, is denoted,
but when it is not specified in the comparator(s), it is understood by implication
Even when only the substance is specified, in ‘moon-faced’ it is followed,
for the quality that abides in the moon is only the qualified one, not blemishes and the like
And this is to be described, even in a compound, with the contemplation of difference,
another word is used with respect to an object that differs by a qualified quality
If, because it is followed from the expression, it is of different substrate,

children.text: mṛgīva capalety atra puṃvadbhāvo na sidhyati
children.translated_text: then in ‘restless like a doe’ the becoming-like-a-masculine does not succeed
But because the prior member is non-feminine, the becoming-like-a-masculine will take place,

children.text: yathaiva mṛgadugdhādau na cet stryartho vivakṣyate
children.translated_text: just as in ‘deer-milk’, etc., if a feminine sense is not intended
‘Like a warrior-woman, black(-complexioned)’—thus indeed <s>Devadatta</s> is spoken of,
therefore, in that very [construction], both are stated in the grammatical analysis
For the sake of establishing the becoming-like-a-masculine, and also of the feminine affix in the case at hand,
much dependence is involved; therefore, in that [construction], both are to be set forth

children.text: śyāmā śastrī yathā śyāmā śastrīkalpeti cocyate
children.translated_text: As ‘black, a warrior-woman’, and likewise ‘black, as-if-a-warrior-woman’, is spoken,
there the expression ‘black’ is to be depended on with respect to the comparator and the compared

children.text: atha śyāmeva śastrīyaṃ śyāmety evaṃ prayujyate
children.translated_text: But if only ‘black’ is intended as ‘warrior-woman-like black’, then ‘black’ is so employed,

children.text: śastrī yatheyam śyāmeti tāvad eva pratīyate
children.translated_text: ‘Warrior-woman-like is this black’—thus far only is apprehended
If the hearing of this quality is only for the sake of indication (secondary signification)

children.text: pṛthag dvayoḥ śruto+apy eṣa neṣṭasvārthasya vācakaḥ
children.translated_text: Even though, taken separately, these two have been heard, this does not serve as an acceptable denoter of its own sense

children.text: upameyaṃ tu yad vācyaṃ tasya cet pratipādane
children.translated_text: But if what is to be expressed is the upameya (the thing compared), then, in its conveying,
the qualities there operate conjointly, and the whole is stated upon a single hearing
Being situated, in the particular case, by the difference of mode and substrate,
how could there be the stating of a generality when there is connection with another word

children.text: sādṛśyamātraṃ sāmānyaṃ dviṣṭhaṃ kaiś cit pratīyate
children.translated_text: Some take mere similarity to be the generality, twofold,

children.text: guṇo bhede+apy abhedena dvivṛttir vā vivakṣitaḥ
children.translated_text: or else a quality, despite difference, is intended as non-different; or a twofold occurrence is intended
The operation of a portion of a class, or of substances, is intended,

children.text: rūpāt sāmānyavācitvaṃ prāg vā vṛtter udāhṛtam
children.translated_text: and the being-a-denoter-of-generality, from form, or else prior to occurrence, has been explained
When the word ‘tiger’ is established, owing to valor, with reference to a man,
then, because the locus is non-different, a compound is possible
But when the word ‘hero’ is employed, the word ‘tiger’ remains in the animal,
and, since the occurrence is in a different locus, there is no possibility there
Even in co-reference (same case-relation), because a difference of quality is possible,
the usage of the word ‘hero’ is to be attached even in a compound

children.text: pūjopādhiś ca yo dṛṣṭaḥ kutsanopādhayaś ca ye
children.translated_text: And the honorific qualifiers that are observed, and the disparaging qualifiers as well—
because these have different conditions (grounds), there is, again, an injunctional statement for restriction

children.text: asaṃbhave+api vā vṛtteḥ syād etal liṅgadarśanam
children.translated_text: Even when an occurrence is not possible, this indication by a mark may obtain,

children.text: acver iti yathā liṅgam abhāve+api bhṛśādiṣu
children.translated_text: as the marker ‘acv’ in ‘acver’—despite absence—applies in words like ‘bhṛśa’, etc.
What likeness is apprehended in a sentence that has an element ending in -vat,
for the prescribing of that affix, in the sūtra, this mention is considered

children.text: kriyety upādhiḥ prāthamyāt prakṛtyarthasya yady api
children.translated_text: Although ‘action’ is, by primacy, the qualifier of the base meaning,
there, a nominal base is not appropriate to be expressed as an action

children.text: sattvavṛttasya śeṣe vā tṛtīyā sādhane+api vā
children.translated_text: Whether in the remainder of what pertains to a continuant-entity, or even as an instrument in the third case-ending,

children.text: tiṅām asattvavācitvād ubhayaṃ tan na vidyate
children.translated_text: because finite verbal endings do not denote entity, neither of the two applies
Cookings and the like, ending in the third case, because of connection with properties of an entity,
are indicated as ‘not action’, just as in the sense-affixes of <s>kṛt</s> (primary suffixes)
And certain indeclinable-derivatives, endowed with properties of action,
their non-denotation of entity is not distinguished by finite-verb forms
And the action that has as its domain the <s>kṛt</s>-suffixes and the <s>sūc</s>-suffix, as in ‘to be slept upon’ and the like,
there, the relation of comparator and compared is utterly impossible

children.text: na kevalau dravyaguṇau tadvān vāpy upamīyate
children.translated_text: Not only substance and quality, nor even a possessor of that, is compared,
with those like ‘to be slept upon’ there is no comparison-meaning at all
When comparator and compared are in substances, and the property-bearer is unexpressed,
then, as grounds, conventional connections—actions and qualities—are understood

children.text: hotavyasadṛśo hotety atrāpy artho na vidyate
children.translated_text: ‘To be offered (hotavya)-like, as “to be offered”’—even here, a meaning does not obtain,
therefore, because of opposition with an action, one endowed with action is not compared
An action is not compared with one of the same class because of its being that (same) state,
for, despite a class-difference, ‘cooking’ and the like are distinct actions by (their) cookings
When the substrate is different, comparison of the comparator is possible,
‘The study of the kings is equal to that of the Brāhmaṇas, by “to be studied”’
Where dependence is apprehended from sense or from context,
by the capacity of what is independent, its application would follow
When equality is intended with ‘oil-cooking’,

children.text: kriyāvad api kāryāṇāṃ darśanāt pratyayo bhavet
children.translated_text: then, because effects are seen to be action-possessing, there would be an affix
Thus, the taking of ‘non-finite’ precludes compounding,

children.text: gamanaṃ kārakasyeti ṇvuly anyasmin na saṃbhavet
children.translated_text: since ‘the going is of the kāraka (participant)’; the ṇvul-affix would not be possible in the other case
For the sake of excluding everything, collective status is adopted,

children.text: śuddhāyāḥ saṃbhavān na syāt kriyāyā brāhmaṇādiṣu
children.translated_text: but because pure action does not occur in ‘Brāhmaṇa’, etc., it would not be so
When comparison is intended, its own property is set aside,

children.text: kriyāyā na śrutād yasmād upamānaṃ samāpyate
children.translated_text: because the comparator is not completed from the mere hearing of an action

children.text: tṛtīyo+apy āśrito bhedo dharmaḥ sādhāraṇo dvayoḥ
children.translated_text: Even a third, adopted distinction is a property common to both,

children.text: vyāpāravān na kṛtsnasya sāmyaṃ kṛtsnena vidyate
children.translated_text: being operative, there is no equality of the whole with the whole

children.text: dravye vāpi kriyāyāṃ vā nimittāt tat prakalpate
children.translated_text: Whether in a substance or in an action, from a ground that is established, that is posited,

children.text: kriyāṇāṃ vidyamānatvād vṛttir na syād gavādiṣu
children.translated_text: but since actions exist, the application would not be in ‘cow’ and the like

children.text: abhāvāt kevalāyās tu tadvān arthaḥ pratīyate
children.translated_text: But in the absence of a mere (isolated) action, a possessor of that is understood,
and when what is primary is not possible, the hearing of the action is fitting for the sake of indication (secondary signification)
Action-words, being dependent upon other actions,
are taken, in regard to a different action, for the sake of assistance, just like ‘Brāhmaṇa’, etc.
Just as excellence everywhere is produced by a different condition,
so, in a quality-word, as in a substance, it requires a ground

children.text: yo ya uccāryate śabdaḥ sa svarūpanibandhanaḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever word is uttered is bound to its own form (intrinsic nature),
just so, in comparators, the expectation (mutual reference) does not cease
When there is a third-case-ending pertaining to the action-occurrence, and likewise when such (an occurrence) is not possible,
the procedure accepted as established by authoritative reasoning, in the Bhāṣya, the root <s>yuj</s> (“to yoke, join”) is cited

children.text: antarbhūte tu karaṇe prayogo na punar bhavet
children.translated_text: But when the instrument is included (subsumed), usage should not occur again,
for, as being improper by the principle, in the case at hand it is like ‘alive’ with ‘the action of breath’

children.text: śāstrābhyāsāc ca bhedo+ayam ayuktam iti varṇyate
children.translated_text: And from study of the śāstra, this difference is described as improper,
‘unbecoming, not connected’—thus the established convention is fixed

children.text: vivibhaktiḥ prakṛtyarthaṃ praty upādhiḥ kathaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: If there is a splitting of case for the base meaning, how would there be a qualifier in each case?
And when there is a transformation of case, a different domain must be posited
For that to which there is connection with another case, is (understood to be) in a different domain,
the connection with another case is inferred from semantic capacity

children.text: sārūpyāt tu tad evedam iti tatropacaryate
children.translated_text: But because of similarity, ‘this very (thing) is that’—thus, in that (context) there is figurative application,

children.text: śabdāntaraṃ vibhaktyā tu yuktaṃ śāstre tad aśrutam
children.translated_text: whereas a different word with a (different) case is proper in the śāstra; that (very) (use) has not been heard (authorized)

children.text: prakṛtiś cet tṛtīyāntā tenety asmāt pratīyate
children.translated_text: If the base is ‘with third-case-ending’, then from that (form) ‘by that (instrument/means)’ is understood,

children.text: kriyeti prathamāntā sā kathaṃ bhavitum arhati
children.translated_text: but ‘action’, being nominative, how could it be (so) intended?

children.text: kriyayeti tṛtīyā ca prayoge kasya kalpyatām
children.translated_text: And if (one says) ‘by the action’ with a third-case-ending, in what (slot) should that be posited in usage?

children.text: tenety asya hi saṃbandhaḥ sūtrasthena na vidyate
children.translated_text: for the connection of ‘by that’ with what stands in the sūtra does not exist
In sūtras that include (implied) supplements, the remainder of the sentence is empowered,

children.text: tena yat tat tṛtīyāntaṃ kriyā cet seti gamyate
children.translated_text: thereby, whatever is in the third case—if ‘action’, then ‘with a suffix having <s>seṭ</s> (iṭ augment)’—is understood

children.text: upādheḥ kasya cid vākye prayoga upalabhyate
children.translated_text: In some sentence the usage of a qualifier is observed,
but what is merely an inferred property of another is never used

children.text: nīlam utpalam ity atra na viśeṣye na bhedake
children.translated_text: In ‘a blue lotus’ (nīlam utpalam), in regard neither to the qualified nor to the differentiator,

children.text: kaś cit taddharmavacano vākye śabdaḥ prayujyate
children.translated_text: is any word used that states ‘that property’

children.text: atyantānugamāt tatra na sūtre na ca vigrahe
children.translated_text: Because of thorough co-occurrence there, neither in the sūtra nor in the analysis (vigraha)
is there any purpose for transformation of case

children.text: tṛtīyāntaṃ kriyety etad vigrahe na prayujyate
children.translated_text: ‘Action with a third case-ending’—this is not employed in the analytic resolution,

children.text: yathā daṇḍaḥ praharaṇaṃ krīḍāyām iti dṛśyate
children.translated_text: just as ‘a stick is an instrument in play’ is seen (as such)

children.text: ghavidhau yac ca saṃjñāyām iti sūtra udāhṛtam
children.translated_text: And the sūtra cited as ‘and in the <s>ghu</s>-paradigm, in a name’—
its bringing-into-use (upādāna) is not absolute (unchanging) in usages
Those by which, though not (otherwise) used, the refinement (saṃskāra) is apprehended in primaries,
these, even with a difference of case-endings, are indicated as qualifiers
In aggregates, there occur words of accompanying entities,
and when non-intention (to express them) obtains, (they serve) for coordination and alternation
Coordination is made in those (cases) where the operations are toward respective objects (praty-artha-vṛtti),
their union, grounded on difference, occurs with number

children.text: sarvair viśiṣṭās tair arthair janyante sahacāribhiḥ
children.translated_text: The cognitions of the understanders are generated, distinguished by all those co-occurring meanings,

children.text: buddhayaḥ pratipattṝṇāṃ śabdārthāṃs tān ato viduḥ
children.translated_text: therefore they know those components of word-meaning
The meanings that are combined in affixes are all helpful,
for them, by the form of the affix, there is utterability by words of them all

children.text: kevalānāṃ tu bhāvānāṃ na rūpam avadhāryate
children.translated_text: But for bare processes/entities (<s>bhāva</s>), no determinate form is ascertained,
and where forms are undetermined, there the word does not function
And from the prior word-usage, the aggregate is not set aside,

children.text: vartate+avayave nāpi nopāttaṃ tyajate kva cit
children.translated_text: nor does it apply to a part, nor does it anywhere abandon what has been taken up
And if one who denotes an aggregate were to specify a difference,
then there would be non-uniformity of case-endings there, as with ‘fore-body’, etc.

children.text: samūhe ca pradeśe ca pañcālā iti dṛśyate
children.translated_text: ‘Pañcāla-s’ is observed both for an aggregate and for a region,

children.text: tathā viśeṣaṇaṃ sarva ity etad upapadyate
children.translated_text: thus the qualifier ‘all’ is appropriate
Likewise, in ‘half-<s>pippalī</s>’ (long pepper), for the cessation of another species,

children.text: ardhaṃ ca pippalī ceti khande śabdaḥ pratīyate
children.translated_text: ‘half’ and ‘<s>pippalī</s>’—in the partial (analysis) the word is understood
And the region of the Pañcālas, too, is distinct from another country,

children.text: tatrānyasya nivṛttyarthe śabde bhedo na gamyate
children.translated_text: there, for the purpose of excluding something else, difference is not apprehended in the word
But those well-known ones, established specifically in an aggregate,
their referential showing in a region is (determined) by sense, context, and the like

children.text: yad upavyañjanaṃ jāteḥ sahacāri ca karmasu
children.translated_text: Whatever is an accessory manifestation of a genus and accompanies actions,
there the conventional relation, which is mostly observed, obtains

children.text: samudāyaḥ pradeśo vety evaṃ tasminn anāśrite
children.translated_text: Whether ‘aggregate’ or ‘region’—thus, when that (distinction) is not relied upon,
the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>-s and the like function, without distinction, in the sense-essence (of the word)

children.text: yaś ca tulyaśrutir dṛṣṭaḥ samudāye vyavasthitaḥ
children.translated_text: And that which is seen as homophonous (tulya-śruti), established in an aggregate,
by that, a figurative unity is observed also in a region
From refinement or from impairment, in what functions with a measured amount of an act,
in ‘oil’ and the like, here the class-term is ascertained by semantic capacity
In words denoting <s>jāti</s> (genus) and <s>guṇa</s> (quality), a difference of concrete form (mūrti) is not intended,
they rest solely upon a difference of the relation to <s>jāti</s> and <s>guṇa</s>
And the designation ‘black’, etc., with qualities that operate with respect to all parts,
even though they are situated in a single part, serve as differentiators of cloth and the like
But when ‘cloth’, etc., are employed with respect to the parts of the cloth,
then, as with ‘oil’ and the like, for them the status of a genus-word is asserted

children.text: nivṛttyarthā śrutir yeṣāṃ bhedas teṣv anapekṣitaḥ
children.translated_text: For those whose wording is for the purpose of exclusion (nivṛtti), in them difference is not attended to,
in a place or in an aggregate, a quality is the factor that excludes others
In ‘study of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>’ there, the wording ‘<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>’ functions,
for resemblance is observed there with ‘study of the <s>Kṣatriya</s>’, etc.
If the functioning of the word ‘<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>’ were in ‘study of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>’,

children.text: vaktavyaṃ kena dharmeṇa tulyatvaṃ kriyayor iti
children.translated_text: one would have to state by what property the equality of the two actions holds
When the functioning of the wording ‘<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>’ is said to be in the student,
then it takes on the role of occasion (cause), while the action itself resides in the student
If, with the word ‘lion’, there is a connection of what merely denotes lion-ness (gauryamātra, i.e., leonine quality),

children.text: caitrāt ṣaṣṭhī prasajyeta yoge śattryādibhir yathā
children.translated_text: then the genitive from ‘<s>Caitra</s>’ would ensue under the relation, as with <s>śatṛ</s>, etc.
In such expressions as ‘it must be given to the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> alone’, ‘to the <s>Vaiśya</s> alone’, and the like,
the syntactic relation of recipient (and the like) does not apply to a bare action
And because in indeclinables the suffix <s>vati</s> denotes only an action,

children.text: pāṭhaḥ kadā cit kartavyas tulyau pakṣāv ubhau yataḥ
children.translated_text: a reading should never be made; for both positions are equivalent

children.text: jahāti jātiṃ dravyaṃ vā tasmān nāvayave sthitaḥ
children.translated_text: It (the wording) abandons either the genus or the substance; therefore it is not fixed in a part,

children.text: kriyāyās tu śrutir yasmāt tadvaty arthe+avatiṣṭhate
children.translated_text: but since the wording is of an action, it settles upon an entity that possesses that (action)
Because they are for the purpose of excluding non-actions, and because here there is wording for an action,
therefore, in what is signified through the action, the action-word is apprehended
And because, in ‘is to be offered’, etc., an action distinct (from the agent) is to be attended to, as with ‘<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>’, etc.,

children.text: apekṣaṇīyā śuddhe+arthe tasmād vṛttir na kasya cit
children.translated_text: therefore, in the pure object, there is no functioning of any (agentive assignment)

children.text: sarvaṃ vāpy ekadeśo vā yasminn āśriyate kva cit
children.translated_text: Whatever whole or single part is in which something is relied upon at some point,

children.text: viśeṣavṛttiṃ taṃ sarvam āhur bhede vyavasthitam
children.translated_text: that entire thing is said to have a function of differentiation, being established in difference

children.text: samuccayo vikalpo vā prakārāḥ sarva eva vā
children.translated_text: Conjunction or alternation, or all modes whatsoever,
are described as specifications, or as an unpartitioned generality

children.text: na hi brāhmaṇa ity atra bhedaḥ kaś cid apāśritaḥ
children.translated_text: For in the expression ‘<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>’, no particular difference is relied upon,
nor is one removed by it; hence it is established in the aggregate

children.text: kriyā tv āśrīyate yasmin sa bhedo +adhyavasīyate
children.translated_text: But that in which an action is relied upon—that difference is ascertained,

children.text: tathānyathā sarvathā cety aprayoge na vidyate
children.translated_text: namely, ‘thus’, ‘otherwise’, ‘in every way’; when there is no usage, it is not known
The functioning of the action in the standard (upamāna) and the wording of action in the compared (upameya),
by making one realize the difference, as it were, produce the status of a word-meaning
When resemblance is solely by operation, and operation is intended,
the cognition is conveyed by a word that speaks as ‘having an action’
Even when resemblance is to something that has an action, if one wishes to speak with ‘having an action’,

children.text: adhyetā brāhmaṇa iva pratyayo na nivartate
children.translated_text: ‘the student is like a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>’—the cognition does not cease

children.text: adhīte tulya ity evaṃ puṃlliṅgena viśeṣaṇam
children.translated_text: ‘He studies, equal’—thus, with a masculine qualifier,
but when the equality is in an action that has an action, the word ‘equal’ is neuter
Even when the base-meaning is specified, since the suffixal meaning is not to be specified,

children.text: putreṇa tulyaḥ kapila iti vṛttiḥ prasajyate
children.translated_text: the usage ‘equal with the son is <s>Kapila</s>’ results

children.text: yāḥ putre rūḍhasaṃbandhāḥ kriyā loke vivakṣitāḥ
children.translated_text: Those actions that have an established relation with ‘son’ and are intended in common usage,

children.text: tābhiḥ kriyāvataḥ putrād guṇatulye vatir bhavet
children.translated_text: with those, from ‘son’ possessing an action, the suffix <s>vati</s> occurs, as in equality of qualities

children.text: antarbhūtaṃ nimittaṃ ca rūḍhiśabdeṣu yady api
children.translated_text: Even though the cause and inclusion are internal in conventional words,

children.text: kriyās tu sahacāriṇyo rūḍhāḥ santi padārthavat
children.translated_text: the actions that accompany them are conventionally established, like word-meanings
But if, setting aside sequence, the specification of the suffixal meaning,
by favoring the principal (member), stands firm owing to similarity and to the separation (vibhakti),
Then, because the base is not to be specified, equality is predicated with respect to the action,
for words of quality, from ‘son’, etc., in the reverse of what was said before
‘He goes equal with the stout one’—here the wording of action is external (secondary),

children.text: animittaṃ vates tulyaṃ yātīty atreṣyate vatiḥ
children.translated_text: but in ‘he goes equal’ without a cause, the suffix <s>vati</s> is approved

children.text: dvayaṃ viśeṣyate tena yad ekatra viśeṣaṇaṃ
children.translated_text: By that, two things are qualified, since in one locus there is a qualifier,

children.text: tulyaśabdo hi taṃ dharmam ubhayastham apekṣate
children.translated_text: for the word ‘equal’ expects that property to be in both
If one single property is common to the standard and the compared,
then ‘equal’ is justified there, as measured by a balance

children.text: sūtre śrutaś ca dviṣṭho+asāv abhedena pratīyate
children.translated_text: And this ‘twofold’ heard in the sūtra is understood as non-different,

children.text: na ca sāmānyaśabdatvād aśrutā gamyate kriyā
children.translated_text: nor is an unexpressed action inferred from it because it is a general term
And unexpressed (elements) are apprehended—such as the stay in the injunction—

children.text: ye dharmā niyatās teṣāṃ putrādiṣu na vidyate
children.translated_text: but the properties that are fixed for those are not found in ‘son’, etc.
Therefore, one who is without a relied-upon action is not equal to one who possesses an action,
and when there is hearing of an action, that (entity) too is understood as ‘having an action’
And because of the provisioning for both, superiority is stated,
since, as the denoter of a perpetual non-existence, it functions as a qualifier of the suffix-meaning
Because the operation, as mere (operation), is of the nature of non-existence in the suffix,
therefore there is the status of being an indicator (lakṣaṇārtha), and there is no (direct) hearing of an action from it
But when there is apprehension of ‘one having an action’, as a qualifier of the base-meaning,
then, in equality through mere action, the denoting of a fixed non-existence is achieved

children.text: yadā kriyānimittaṃ tu sādṛśyaṃ syāt kriyāvatoḥ
children.translated_text: However, when the resemblance of two who have an action is due to an action as the cause,
then, because a possessor of action is what is denoted, there is the denotation of a substance

children.text: avyayeṣu vateḥ pāṭhaḥ kāryas tatra svarādivat
children.translated_text: In indeclinables, the recitation of the suffix <s>vati</s> is to be done—there, it has the function of an effect, as with accent, etc.,

children.text: brāhmaṇena samo+adhyetety atra ca pratyayo bhavet
children.translated_text: and in ‘let him study equal with a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>’, here too the suffix should occur
And co-reference (sāmānādhikaraṇya) is indicated by the meaning of <s>vati</s>,

children.text: tulyam ity anyathā kalpyo vākyaśeṣo+aśruto bhavet
children.translated_text: otherwise, if one were to construe ‘equal’ differently, the remainder of the sentence would be unheard (i.e., unexpressed)
And when there is resemblance between two who have an action, with the suffix-meaning as qualifier,

children.text: adhyetrā sadṛśo+adhyetety atra nāsti vater vidhiḥ
children.translated_text: in ‘the student studies, similar (to a student)’, there is no prescription of <s>vati</s>

children.text: tulyārthair iti yā tasyās tṛtīyāyā na bhidyate
children.translated_text: The locution ‘with equal properties’—its instrumental does not differ,
for though there is difference of meaning, it is expressed by all the other cases as well

children.text: bhojyate brāhmaṇa iva tulyaṃ bhuktaṃ dvijātinā
children.translated_text: ‘He eats, as a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> (does); equal is what was eaten by the twice-born’,

children.text: paśyati brāhmaṇam iva tulyaṃ vipreṇa paśyati
children.translated_text: ‘He sees, as (he would see) a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>; he sees equally with the <s>Vipra</s>’
‘It was understood as by a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>; equal is what was known by the twice-born’,
‘Let it be given just as to a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>; let it be given equally by the <s>Vipra</s>’

children.text: brāhmaṇād iva vaiśyāt tvam adhīṣvādhyayanaṃ bahu
children.translated_text: ‘Study much—just as from a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, so from a <s>Vaiśya</s>’—and with such examples,

children.text: ity evamādibhir bhedas tṛtīyāyā na kaś cana
children.translated_text: there is no difference in the instrumental

children.text: tulyaṃ madhurayādhīye mātrā tulyaṃ smarāmi tām
children.translated_text: ‘I study equal with the sweet one by the measure; I remember her equally,’

children.text: madhurāyāś ca mātuś ca kathaṃ sādṛśyakalpanā
children.translated_text: and how is resemblance to be construed between ‘sweet (woman)’ and ‘mother’?
The reading concerns the domain of ‘sweet one’, the remembering is an action of the mother,
and by the words ‘sweet (woman)’ and ‘mother’, without difference, it is denoted
As, in mouths equal to those of a camel, there is the hearing (use) of ‘camel’,
so, in a palace that is equal to a house, there is the hearing (use) of ‘sweet (woman)’
Just as equality of study for two students is indicated,
so, by properties that reside in action, (things) dependent on the instruments (means) are spoken of

children.text: ivārthe yac ca vacanaṃ pūrvasūtre ca yo vidhiḥ
children.translated_text: And what wording is for the sense of ‘like’ and what prescription was in the previous sūtra—

children.text: kriyāśabdaśrutau bhedo na kaś cid vidyate tayoḥ
children.translated_text: there is no difference between those two when there is hearing of an action-word

children.text: yady apy upādhir anyatra niyato na prayujyate
children.translated_text: Even though a condition (upādhi) fixed elsewhere is not employed,

children.text: rūpābhedāt tv anirjñātā kriyātra śrūyate punaḥ
children.translated_text: because the form is not different, an action is again heard here
As ‘tail-possessed’ and the like at the end of <s>kyaṅ</s> in ‘puccha’ (tail) are cited,
although they have a suffixal meaning, since there is no difference (of form)

children.text: evaṃ ca sati pūrveṇa siddho+atrāpi vater vidhiḥ
children.translated_text: Thus, with this being so, by what preceded, here too the prescription of <s>vati</s> is established,

children.text: niyame vābhidhāne vā bhidyate na kriyāśrutiḥ
children.translated_text: and whether in restriction or in denotation, the hearing of the action does not differ
Again, the suffix is said (to apply) in the domain of substance, etc., as with ‘like’,
whereas in the previous sūtra it is prescribed only for resemblances of actions
In ‘the houses are as in <s>Madhurā</s>; the garments are as of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>’—

children.text: ity atra dravyaguṇayoḥ pūrveṇa na vatir bhavet
children.translated_text: in these, for substance and quality, by the preceding (rule) the suffix <s>vati</s> should not occur
When the undertaking is not for the sake of an action, there is no purpose attained by the compound,
except when ‘action’ is grasped; by the prior connection it is accomplished
The usage in a part of <s>Madhurā</s> has been explained with ‘the hearing (use) of “Madhurā”’,
‘he will speak of teeth, parts of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>’, because of the hearing (use) of ‘<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>’

children.text: na kā cid ivayoge tu bāhyāt saṃbandhino
children.translated_text: But when there is ‘like’-connection, no genitive is prescribed for an external relatum,

children.text: ṣaṣṭhī vidhīyate tatra pūrveṇa pratyayo bhavet
children.translated_text: there the suffix should occur by the prior (rule)
By the word ‘equal’, predominance and relation are produced;

children.text: ṣaṣṭhītṛtīye tatra stas tulyaśabdo hi vācakaḥ
children.translated_text: there the genitive and the instrumental both occur, for the word ‘equal’ indeed is expressive (of relation)
But when the word ‘like’ is employed, without an external relatum,
there is no predominance in the standard; it is employed as an indicator
And the exclusion that is here with ‘like’ is caused by palace, etc.,
in equality, predominance arises with reference to its (the standard’s) domain

children.text: gavayena samo+anadvān iti vṛttis tathā bhavet
children.translated_text: ‘He who is without cattle is equal with a <s>gavaya</s>’—in such a case the usage should be thus,

children.text: na tv asti gaur ivety atra vyatireka ivāśrayaḥ
children.translated_text: but in ‘as a cow (gaur iva)’, there is no basis for exclusion with ‘like’
From relation with the compared (upameya) first, when the exclusion is caused by palace, etc.,
there is the occurrence of <s>vati</s> in exclusion, not when the cause is equality of meaning
When relation is by the word ‘like’, the instrumental is not prescribed,

children.text: prakṛtāṃ tām atas tyaktvā vibhaktyantaraṃ āśritam
children.translated_text: therefore, abandoning that (instrumental) which is at issue, another case-ending is resorted to

children.text: saptamy api na tatrāsti jñāpakārthā tu sā kṛtā
children.translated_text: Nor does the locative (seventh case) occur there either; but that (locative) has been made for the purpose of indicating (as a) jñāpaka (indicatory device),
that (locative) is desired in the domain of the remainder (śeṣa), among case-endings that are fixed
But if, in this domain, the case-endings were to operate by way of exclusion (vyatireka),
then the instrumental alone would display irregularity (vyabhicāra)
When such irregularity is thus established without (explicit) mention of the locative,

children.text: saptamy evocyate sarvā na santy anyā vibhaktayaḥ
children.translated_text: one would state the locative alone everywhere; there are no other case-endings
Here, in this domain, the genitive that was absolutely overridden by the locative whose purpose is indication (as jñāpaka),

children.text: bādhitā vinivarteta ṣaṣṭhī sā gṛhyate punaḥ
children.translated_text: would turn back (i.e., be reinstated); that genitive is taken up again
From the two prior connections (yogas) themselves, since an alternative analytic paraphrase is imagined,

children.text: arhārthe+api vatiḥ siddhaḥ sa tv ekena nidarśyate
children.translated_text: the suffix <s>vati</s> is established also in the sense of ‘worthy/fit’ (<s>arhārtha</s>); but that is illustrated by a single (sūtra)

children.text: tena tulyam iti prāpte kriyopādhiḥ prasidhyati
children.translated_text: Thus, when ‘equal to that’ would be obtained, an action-qualification (kriyopādhi) becomes established:

children.text: rājavad vartate rājety atra bhede vivakṣite
children.translated_text: ‘He behaves like a king (rājavat vartate)’ and ‘he (is) a king’ (rājā iti) in a case where difference is intended
Those kings beginning with <s>Pṛthu</s> who are renowned by ‘kinghood’ (rājatvena),
up to <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, they become the standard of comparison for other rulers of the earth
The difference between the standard (upamāna) and the compared (upameya) is made by success and non-success (siddhi-asiddhi),
for everywhere that which is not established is compared with what is established

children.text: rājavad rūpam asyeti rājany eva vivakṣite
children.translated_text: ‘His form is like a king’s’—when only ‘king’ is intended,
through a connection whose sense is non-actional, it will be with the accusative (dvitīyā)
When there is no intention of a (specific) standard (upamāna), this is stated as a rule of restriction,
‘the property is the agent of the worthiness-action (arhati-kriyā)’—for that purpose the statement is again made

children.text: kṛtahastavad ity etat prasiddheṣv eva dṛśyate
children.translated_text: The expression ‘like one with a made-hand (kṛtahastavat)’ is seen only where there is what is well-known,

children.text: rājatvena prasiddhe ca rājñi rājavad ity api
children.translated_text: and ‘like a king’ (rājavad) also, when the king is established by ‘kinghood’ (rājatvena)
The properties for which an absolute impossibility is observed in a non-king,
those are restricted to a king; the irregular ones are rejected

children.text: arhateś ca kriyā kartrī yā tasyāṃ vatir iṣyate
children.translated_text: And the action of ‘deserving’ (arhateḥ) takes a verb as its agent; in that (construction) the suffix <s>vati</s> is approved,

children.text: rājānam arhati cchattram iti na tv evamādiṣu
children.translated_text: as in ‘A parasol befits the king’ (rājānam arhati chattram), but not in expressions like that (i.e., not otherwise formed)
For the usage of words employed by the good is followed by the treatise (śāstra),

children.text: chattrādyarthe tu vacane pratyākhyānaṃ na saṃbhavet
children.translated_text: but when there is an utterance with the sense of ‘parasol’, etc., rejection is not possible
The sūtra ‘fit for that’ (tad-arham) is not begun in another grammar,
because even by mere comparison the imagining of difference is possible
From the ascertaining of one effect (kārya) in a different domain where (it is) established,
when there is an intention of ‘having that property’ (tad-dharmatva), difference is posited by intellect
Nor, on account of the beginning of the sūtra, is there usage of the word ‘like’ (iva) from this (source),

children.text: prayogaḥ so+api caitasya viṣaye vidyate vateḥ
children.translated_text: and yet its usage is found in this domain of <s>vati</s>
The expression ‘like Indra among the bandits’ (dasyuhendra iva) is employed in the <s>Aindra</s> mantra,
elsewhere, when ‘Indra in respect of a seen action’ (dṛṣṭakarma-indra) is intended, (one says) ‘as such’ (yathā)
When a (present) state is designated with reference to a prior state,
‘You are similar; you are your very self’—thus it is expressed there
Where there is no other standard of comparison for an already-known difference,
there the self of the compared object is partitioned by one’s own cognition
Even the difference that is natural (svābhāvika) is nevertheless founded upon cognition,

children.text: tenāsmin viṣaye bhinnam abhinnaṃ vā na vidyate
children.translated_text: therefore, in this domain, neither the different nor the non-different is (intrinsically) found
Saying ‘wearing armlets, wearing earrings’ (aṅgadī, kuṇḍalī), showing by causes of difference,
he says ‘<s>Caitra</s> is of this sort’, owing to the grasping of a state in intellect
By these words, a cognition whose nature is ‘as it really is’ arises,
and by imitation of that cognition, the domain (of usage) is justified
By the partition of states in intellect, an effect of difference is apprehended,

children.text: janyanta iva śabdānām arthāḥ sarve vivakṣayā
children.translated_text: as though the meanings of words are generated entirely by intention
Even where the external object is of such a sort, if cognitions are divided,

children.text: na tatra kaś cit sādṛśyaṃ sad api pratipadyate
children.translated_text: then no one apprehends similarity there, even though it exists

children.text: atyantaṃ viṣaye bhinne yāvat prakhyā na bhidyate
children.translated_text: So long as renown (prakhyā) is not divided, even when the domain is entirely different,

children.text: na tāvat pratyabhijñānaṃ kasya cid vinivartate
children.translated_text: so long recognition is not removed for anyone

children.text: ayam eva tu sūtreṇa bhedo bhedena darśitaḥ
children.translated_text: But this very difference has been shown in the sūtra by means of difference,
so that even what is well-known yet difficult to know is grasped by the unlearned
He speaks like a grammarian, yet he is not always a grammarian; therefore,
‘Speak like a grammarian!’—on that account he too is so designated

children.text: ke cit pumāṃso bhāṣante strīvat puṃvac ca yoṣitaḥ
children.translated_text: Some men speak like women, and women speak like men,
in irregularity, one’s own property is again enjoined by that (very device)

children.text: sadṛśas tvaṃ tavaiveti loke yad abhidhīyate
children.translated_text: When in the world one says ‘You are similar; you are your very self’,
there any other standard of comparison that has become relevant is set aside

children.text: yuktam aupayikaṃ rājña ity arthasya nidarśane
children.translated_text: This is appropriate as an illustration of the meaning ‘fitting for a king’ (yuktam aupayikaṃ rājñaḥ)
When similarity is not intended to be expressed, ‘fit for that’ (tad-arham) is taught
But the remainder pertaining to <s>vati</s> is stated as ‘entailed’ and ‘entailed-upon’ (prasakta and anuprasakta),
since, owing to relation with the upamāna (standard of comparison), <s>vati</s> is illustrated here
Because, in the absence of positing a primary (sense), the use of the word ‘attribute’ (<s>guṇa</s>) is observed,
from the preverb, with <s>vati</s>, there is established, with regard to the verbal root, a supposition of the verb-meaning

children.text: svaṃ rūpam iti caitasminn arthasyāpi parigrahaḥ
children.translated_text: And the (rule) ‘its own form’ (svaṃ rūpam) here includes even the meaning,
therefore, since the meaning is indicated as ‘like a form’, a meaning that is proximate will be grasped
What is produced by the verb-meaning functions as an instrument, in the capacity of an instrument,

children.text: dhātunā kṛtam ity evam asmin sūtre pratīyate
children.translated_text: thus, ‘made by the verbal root’—in this sūtra it is understood

children.text: yaḥ śabdaś caritārthatvād atyantaṃ na prayujyate
children.translated_text: A word which, because its purpose has been fulfilled, is not employed at all,
in such a case, because it is not seen in usage, its elision is prescribed

children.text: kriyāyāṃ sādhane dravye prādayo ye vyavasthitāḥ
children.translated_text: For those preverbs such as pra-, etc., which are fixed in action, instrument, and substance,
from those, which denote being (existence), <s>vati</s> is enjoined in its own sense

children.text: pratyayena vinā prādis tatrārthe na prayujyate
children.translated_text: Without an affix, a preverb is not employed in that sense,
but, in the designation by distinction, a partition is imagined
However, if an instrument were to be taken with being (existence) not acknowledged,
the assignment would be by case-endings, just as indeed in tasil and the like
For those who, from the textual reading, infer the absence of case-inflection in words ending in <s>vati</s>,

children.text: teṣām udvata ity atra vaktavyā savibhaktitā
children.translated_text: for them, in the instance ud-vati, one should state that case-inflection is present

children.text: vatyarthaṃ nāvagāhete puṃvad ity asya darśanāt
children.translated_text: They do not apprehend the meaning of <s>vati</s>, because of the observation of ‘like a masculine’ (puṃvad),
therefore that convention is established as a blocker (bādhaka) of the exception constituted by nañ and snañ

children.text: etam utkrāmato nūnaṃ vatyarthaṃ nañsnañāv iti
children.translated_text: ‘Surely as he departs from this, nañ and snañ denote the meaning of <s>vati</s>’—if so,
then, when those two operate, the general rule would not be reasonably blocked

children.text: nañsnañau vihitau yena sa yogo nāvagāhate
children.translated_text: By whomsoever nañ and snañ are enjoined, that combination (with <s>vati</s>) is not understood,

children.text: vatiprakaraṇaṃ tad dhi liṅgam evaṃ samarthyate
children.translated_text: for the topic on <s>vati</s> is precisely the sign; thus it is justified
Because the upamāna (standard of comparison) is introduced with a different meaning while the similarity is of a single (kind),
therefore, conjectural adjustment (ūha) of upamānas, like that of ancillary parts (aṅga), is not admissible
In the verbs gā, vedh, and car, singular number is observed for go-vikartā and akṣa-vāpā,

children.text: paśū rudra iva hy etāv ity ekavacanaśrutiḥ
children.translated_text: ‘These two are animals like <s>Rudra</s>’—thus is the hearing of the singular

children.text: upamānasya bhedāc ca bahuṣu syād año vidhiḥ
children.translated_text: And because of the difference of the upamāna, in the plural there would be a different prescription,

children.text: kāśyapā iti lopaḥ syāt tathā pratikṛtiṣv api
children.translated_text: ‘descendants of <s>Kāśyapa</s>’—thus there would be elision, and likewise in replicas (pratikṛti)
But in this way, because there is the state ‘as if connected’ (yuktavat-bhāva), the singular should occur here,

children.text: lum manuṣye tathoktaṃ syāl liṅgasyaikasya siddhaye
children.translated_text: ‘lum manuṣye’—thus it would be stated, for the accomplishment of a single gender

children.text: upameyeṣu bhinneṣu kiṃ cid ekaṃ pravartate
children.translated_text: When, among the upameyas (objects compared), something single operates, though they are different,

children.text: pratyayasya vidhau tatra nityaṃ yuktavad iṣyate
children.translated_text: then, in the enjoinment of the affix, the ‘as if connected’ (yuktavat) is consistently accepted

children.text: yadā pratyupameyaṃ tu tad ekaikam avasthitam
children.translated_text: But when, in each case, the upameya stands separately,
then, by reason of external difference of meanings, a taddhita-formation is accumulated
As, in the accumulation of a group, there is different number for dvigu-compounds,
so, in pañca-pūla and the like, there would be accumulation of forms ending in lum

children.text: pracaye bhidyamāne tu saṃkhyā pūleṣu bhidyate
children.translated_text: But when, in the accumulation, difference occurs, number differs in the pūlas,

children.text: arthabhedo lubanteṣu naivaṃ kaś cana dṛśyate
children.translated_text: no such difference of meaning is seen in lum-final forms
Where, in regard to the upameya, another word is not employed,
there a difference of number for the upamāna is accepted by others
Just as, from the usage of guḍa, tila, and the like, there is single number,
but when pakā and the like are not used, a different number is expressed

children.text: yaḥ saṃbandhigato bhedaḥ sa prayoge pratīyate
children.translated_text: A difference that belongs to the relatum (saṃbandhin) is apprehended in usage,

children.text: saṃbandhinām ato bheda upameye na gamyate
children.translated_text: therefore, the difference of the relata (saṃbandhin) is not inferred in the upameya
Therefore, in order to avert the consequence of being a general term,
a difference that belongs to the upameya is observed in the upamānas

children.text: upamānaṃ samastānām abhinnam śrūyate kva cit
children.translated_text: The upamāna of all (collectively) is heard as undivided in some cases,
or each one of the distinct upameyas is compared

children.text: yathā garuḍa ity etad vyūhāpekṣaṃ prayujyate
children.translated_text: As the term ‘<s>Garuḍa</s>’ is employed with reference to an array (vyūha),
where there is similarity of the elephants with one <s>Vainateya</s>
Even with respect to a single (prototype), a different replica is apprehended together (with it),
‘of <s>Kāśyapa</s>’—therefore this stands individually

children.text: meghāḥ śaila ivety ukte samastānāṃ pratīyate
children.translated_text: When one says ‘the clouds are like a mountain’, similarity of all (clouds) with a single mountain is apprehended,
therefore, individually, it is distinguished by that one mountain
Because it presupposes a tail (chā) and pertains to that domain, its being something to be enjoined is not inferred,

children.text: kākatālīyam ity atra prasiddham hy upalakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: for in ‘kāka-tālīyam’ (crow-and-palm-nut) the indication (upalakṣaṇa) is indeed well-known

children.text: rājāśvādiś ca viṣayaḥ syād anyo vety aniścitam
children.translated_text: And the domain such as ‘king-horse’ may be different—or not; it is indeterminate,

children.text: tena cchasya vidhānāt prāg vyapadeśo na vidyate
children.translated_text: therefore, since ch is enjoined, prior designation does not exist
Here, as with two meanings ‘as if’, a causal basis is apprehended,
one part is connected with one, and the affix is connected with the other
The arrival of <s>Caitra</s> there is like the arrival of a crow,

children.text: dasyor abhinipātas tu tālasya patanaṃ yathā
children.translated_text: but the sudden fall upon (someone) by a bandit is like the falling of a palm-nut
When, upon their coming together, another action arises there,
then, in the upameya (the thing compared) and in the sense such as ‘killing’, the prescription of ch is accepted
When an action is what is conjointly present, a substance-word is established;
thus, for falling and arriving, the words ‘crow’ and ‘palm’ are likewise fixed

children.text: yad anvākhyāyakaṃ vākyaṃ tad evaṃ parikalpyate
children.translated_text: Whatever sentence is an explanatory reiteration (anvākhyāyaka), that is construed thus,

children.text: prayogavākvaṃ yal loke tad evaṃ na prayujyate
children.translated_text: but whatever sentence is current in the world as usage, that is not employed thus
Where the occurrence of two (events) unforeseen is seen, as in the crow-and-palm (<s>kākatāla</s>),
there the functioning of the compound-basis (samāsa-prakṛti) is admitted

children.text: kākasya tālena yathā vadho yasya tu dasyunā
children.translated_text: Just as the crow’s (coming) with the palm(-nut’s falling), so, wherever someone’s killing is by a bandit,
there, when another upameya is made vivid, ch is accepted
‘Flickering-mode’, ‘flickerish’, and ‘great-rayed’—so say others,
they designate jewels, frogs, and fireflies by similarity
There, by opening and shutting of the eyes, the firefly is compared,
by the patterns of breathing the frog, and the jewel by its quivering radiance
Where, though small, one is apprehended as having a vastly spreading radiance,

children.text: bṛhatka iti tatraiṣa maṇau śabdaḥ prayujyate
children.translated_text: there, with reference to the jewel, the word ‘great-rayed’ is employed

children.text: sādṛśyam eva sarvatra prakāraḥ kaiś cid iṣyate
children.translated_text: Some hold that everywhere ‘mode’ (prakāra) is nothing but similarity,

children.text: bhede+api tu prakārākhyā kaiś cid abhyupagamyate
children.translated_text: while others admit the name ‘mode’ even amid difference
One speaker of ‘mode’ remains with what possesses a mode,

children.text: prakāramātre vartitvā kaś cit tadvati vartate
children.translated_text: another, having dealt only with mode-as-such, proceeds to what has that (mode)
The taking of ‘similarity’ in the sūtra is an indicator of ‘similar’,
and in an avyayībhāva-compound of two equals the word ‘together’ (saha) is the denoter
The function, with respect to distribution (vipsā) and similarity, of those that denote the appropriate meaning,

children.text: sa cāyam avyayībhāve bhedo bhedena darśitaḥ
children.translated_text: and this difference, in the avyayībhāva, has been shown by a difference (of form)

children.text: sādṛśyaṃ yogyatā kaiś cid anāv abhyupagamyate
children.translated_text: Similarity and fitness (yogyatā) are, by some, admitted not (to be expressed) by ‘with’ (anā),

children.text: yat tu mūrtigataṃ sāmyaṃ tat sahenābhidhīyate
children.translated_text: but whatever equality inheres in form (mūrti) is expressed by ‘with’ (saha)
Even in the itthaṃbhāva (‘suchness’) construction, similarity depends upon a determinate cognition,
yet, in the apprehension of mere difference, there another (expression) is employed

children.text: gaur vāhīka iti dvitve sādṛśyaṃ pratyudāhṛtam
children.translated_text: ‘A white (cow), a <s>Vāhīka</s>’—in this duality, similarity was cited; but

children.text: śuklādau sati niṣpanne vāhīko na dvir ucyate
children.translated_text: when whiteness and the like are established, ‘Vāhīka’ is not said twice
Thus is completed the <s>Vākyapadīya</s> composed by <s>Bhartṛhari</s>
